nodes.label: 01-spot-exchange
Curve
F1 a Stableswap pool quotes a swap off A*n^n*Sum(xi) + D = A*D*n^n + D^(n
nodes.text: a Stableswap pool quotes a swap off A*n^n*Sum(xi) + D = A*D*n^n + D^(n+1)/(n^n*Prod(xi)), obtained by scaling the constant-sum leg of chi*D^(n-1)*Sum(xi) + Prod(xi) = chi*D^n + (D/n)^n by chi = A*Prod(xi)/(D/n)^n so the curve degrades toward constant product as the pool goes out of balance, with D and xj recovered by iterative convergence in integer arithmetic inside the contract
nodes.note: THE POOL INVARIANT, first of two. St fits: constant-sum near a FIXED parity, degrading to constant product with imbalance. The whitepaper's own simulation over DAI/USDC/USDT, May-Oct 2019 at $30,000 liquidity, reports optimal A = 85 and fee 0.06%. A is stored scaled by A_PRECISION = 100.

nodes.label: F2 a Cryptoswap pool quotes off the IDENTICAL algebraic form with a diffe
nodes.text: a Cryptoswap pool quotes off the IDENTICAL algebraic form with a different leverage term — K*D^(N-1)*Sum(xi) + Prod(xi) = K*D^N + (D/N)^N with K0 = Prod(xi)*N^N/D^N and K = A*K0*gamma^2/(gamma+1-K0)^2 — solved by Newton's method first for D then for xj at about 35k gas, with balances first transformed by a price vector so the invariant is always evaluated near equilibrium: liquidity is concentrated around a MOVING internal price_scale rather than around parity
nodes.note: RESIDUE — THE POOL INVARIANT, second answer. St names constant-sum near a FIXED parity; Cl names user-chosen static ticks; Pm names an EXTERNALLY quoted price. None applies. But stage 1's sharper finding is that the corpus's cut is wrong in shape: stableswap and cryptoswap are ONE PARAMETERISED FAMILY differing only in whether the leverage term is chi = A*Prod(xi)/(D/n)^n or K = A*K0*gamma^2/(gamma+1-K0)^2, so the repair is a parameterised invariant, not a second symbol beside St. The published convergence limits are 0.1 <= D <= 1e15 USD, 5e-3 < xi/D < 200 and 1e-8 <= gamma <= 1e-2.

nodes.label: F3 the pool moves its own centre of concentration only when TWO condition
nodes.text: the pool moves its own centre of concentration only when TWO conditions hold: an exponential moving average of the pool's own price has moved past the adjustment_step, AND the loss of value of X_cp = (Prod D/(N*pi))^(1/N) 'doesn't exceed half the profit we've made', tracked as a monotone accumulator (xcp_profit) of that same functional
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and three separable objects need naming rather than one: (i) a SELF-REFERENTIAL PRICE — the pool's own EMA is its own oracle and the input to its own state transition; (ii) a PROFIT FUNCTIONAL — a named scalar of the pool state that only ratchets up; (iii) a RATIO-BOUNDED STATE TRANSITION conditioned on it. The corpus paraphrases the gate as 'repeg if profitable', which is weaker than the whitepaper's condition and admits behaviours Curve forbids. Verbatim condition at https://docs.curve.finance/pdf/whitepapers/whitepaper_cryptoswap.pdf (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F4 the protocol runs several mutually incompatible implementations of tha
nodes.text: the protocol runs several mutually incompatible implementations of that repeg gate in production at once, and they cannot be distinguished by the version string the contracts publish: the deployed and the repository implementations both report version 'v2.1.0' while testing mathematically different predicates
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a CITATION HAZARD for every other obligation that depends on the gate (F2, F3, F5). BYTECODE-LEVEL EVIDENCE, run by this lane 2026-08-04 and not taken from the version string. (a) Deployed: of the 80 largest mainnet twocrypto pools (source list https://api.curve.finance/api/getPools/ethereum/factory-twocrypto), eth_call of version() 0x54fd4d50 against ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com returns FIVE live strings — v2.0.0 (13 pools), v2.1.0 (48), v2.1.0d (9), v2.1.1 (1), v3.0.0 (9). All 48 v2.1.0 pools share one implementation: eth_getCode returns an 18,355-byte runtime whose non-immutable prefix hashes identically across all 48. Its Blockscout-verified source (Vyper 0.3.10, TwoKittyOptimized, e.g. 0xec977F46467a3021785Cff88894886E617abd65b) declares version 'v2.1.0' at line 188 and gates the repeg LINEARLY at line 925: 'if virtual_price * 2 - 10**18 > xcp_profit + 2 * rebalancing_params[0]:', with the accept check at line 982 '2 * old_virtual_price - 10**18 > xcp_profit'. (b) Repository: curvefi/twocrypto-ng main, contracts/main/Twocrypto.vy, declares version 'v2.1.0' at line 110 and gates it QUADRATICALLY at line 799: 'if (virtual_price - rebalancing_params[0])**2 > xcp_profit * 10**18:', with line 848 'new_virtual_price ** 2 > xcp_profit * 10**18'. Since (1+e)^2 = 1 + 2e + e^2, the deployed linear form is exactly the first-order expansion of the repository's quadratic form about unit virtual price: the two agree near unit profit and diverge as profit compounds, the quadratic being strictly the more permissive as profit grows. Repository source at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/curvefi/twocrypto-ng/main/contracts/main/Twocrypto.vy (2026-08-04). The vocabulary has no way to record that an artefact is ambiguous at its own version string, and a construction citing 'twocrypto v2.1.0' names two different mechanisms.

nodes.label: F5 the safety property in F3 has a documented deadlock: when the market p
nodes.text: the safety property in F3 has a documented deadlock: when the market price moves far from the last rebalance price the available liquidity falls, volume and fees fall with it, and 'without enough profit from fees, the pool cannot afford to rebalance and follow the price, leaving its liquidity stranded' — for which the protocol's own documented remedy includes wash-trading the pool with flash loans 'at a loss with no guarantee of a lasting fix'
nodes.note: RESIDUE — a protocol whose recovery procedure is an intentional loss-making trade by an unrelated third party. This is not a bug report; it is in the official documentation with a remedy list. A formalism that reproduces Cryptoswap and cannot exhibit the stuck state has not reproduced Cryptoswap, and no symbol in the 58 can even state that a mechanism has a reachable absorbing state.

nodes.label: F6 a liquidity provider holds a FUNGIBLE LP token — a pro-rata claim on t
nodes.text: a liquidity provider holds a FUNGIBLE LP token — a pro-rata claim on the whole reserve — may deposit any subset of the coins unbalanced, and may exit either balanced or into a single coin, paying an imbalance fee calibrated so that 'a swap between USDC and USDT would pay roughly the same amount of fees as depositing USDC into the pool and then withdrawing USDT'
nodes.note: FUNGIBILITY OF THE POSITION. Sh fits exactly, and Curve is the ONLY one of the five with no non-fungible position anywhere in its DEX — the polar answer to Uniswap and PancakeSwap, which is what makes the fungible/non-fungible split a real axis rather than a detail. RESIDUE for the arbitrage-equivalence pricing of the imbalance fee: a fee calibrated so that two different action sequences cost the same has no expression.

nodes.label: F7 the fee is a function of pool imbalance, not a constant: 'Cryptoswap a
nodes.text: the fee is a function of pool imbalance, not a constant: 'Cryptoswap and all new Stableswap pools feature dynamic fees that adjust to increase returns for LPs when their liquidity is in high demand', governed by mid_fee, out_fee and fee_gamma
nodes.note: RESIDUE — no symbol names a fee that is a function of the pool state. Note the consequence for the corpus: 'Curve charges a flat fee' is false for the current generation, and this also weakens St as a description of Stableswap-NG, since a state-dependent fee is not implied by a constant-sum-near-parity invariant.

nodes.label: F8 which asset the fee is taken in is fixed by pool type: stableswap take
nodes.text: which asset the fee is taken in is fixed by pool type: stableswap takes it in the OUTPUT coin, cryptoswap takes it in the pool's own LP token
nodes.note: RESIDUE — no symbol distinguishes which leg a fee is skimmed from, and the choice changes the quoting equation by direction. The same gap appears on Raydium as an immutable per-pool CollectFeeOn setting (raydium.json F7), so it is a category-level gap, not a Curve quirk.

nodes.label: F9 the invariant's own parameter moves on a RAMP rather than a step: A is
nodes.text: the invariant's own parameter moves on a RAMP rather than a step: A is changed by ramp_A with a minimum ramp time of 86,400 seconds, so the curve is time-varying by construction and a swap quoted at t and the same swap quoted at t+dt are priced by different invariants
nodes.note: RESIDUE — Tg names a DELAY BEFORE a change takes effect; this is a change CONTINUOUSLY INTERPOLATED over time, which is a different object, and it means the pool invariant is a function of block timestamp.

nodes.label: F10 the protocol publishes a PRICE, not an accumulator: Cryptoswap's price
nodes.text: the protocol publishes a PRICE, not an accumulator: Cryptoswap's price_oracle is an internal exponential moving average parameterised by ma_exp_time, and Stableswap-NG exposes an EMA oracle with _ma_exp_time set as time_in_seconds / ln(2); a consumer reads a number and uses it, performing no integration
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and THE PRICE-SERIES QUESTION answered the OPPOSITE way to Uniswap and Raydium, which publish accumulators the consumer must difference (uniswap.json F7, raydium.json F12). Tp collapses that distinction, and it also misses the load-bearing fact: this price is not merely exported, it is an INPUT TO THE POOL'S OWN STATE TRANSITION (F3), so manipulating it manipulates the pool's geometry rather than a downstream consumer. It is also an exponential rather than an arithmetic time weighting, which no symbol registers. Factory bounds 86 < ma_exp_time < 872542.

nodes.label: F11 settlement is atomic and per-pool — each pool holds its own coins and
nodes.text: settlement is atomic and per-pool — each pool holds its own coins and there is no netting layer — and a metapool composes by making one of its coins another pool's LP TOKEN, tradeable through to the base coins but not depositable in them because of the contract size limit
nodes.note: RESIDUE, twice. (i) THE SETTLEMENT DISCIPLINE: per-pool transfers, no deferred netting anywhere in Curve, and no symbol names either discipline — the vocabulary cannot state the difference between this and Uniswap v4. (ii) A pool whose inventory is another pool's CLAIM is a containment relation between mechanisms, and composition in this corpus is modelled as union of element sets between peers. Same gap the intents and yield lanes reported.

nodes.label: F12 anyone may deploy a pool, but only the DAO may register the implementa
nodes.text: anyone may deploy a pool, but only the DAO may register the implementation it is deployed FROM: per-generation factories (CurveStableSwapFactoryNG, TwocryptoFactory, CurveTricryptoFactory, CurveL2TricryptoFactory) take the full parameter vector under asserted bounds (0 < adjustment_step < 1e18+1, allowed_extra_profit < 1e18+1, fee_max = 10*1e9, 86 < ma_exp_time < 872542), only set_pool_implementation is DAO-gated, and 'Pools created through the Factory are owned by the factory admin (DAO)'
nodes.note: RESIDUE — free instantiation over a GOVERNED SET OF TYPES: a two-level permission structure the corpus records only half of (it records permissionless deployment and not the gated registry). The same two-level shape recurs three times in this lane — Uniswap's monotone enableFeeAmount (uniswap.json F14) and Fluid's governance-approved pool list plus 'infinite DEX types' (fluid.json F18, F19). Parameter bounds cross-checked at https://docs.curve.finance/developer/amm/factory/tricrypto-ng/deployer-api (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F13 pools deployed by different factory generations are discovered through
nodes.text: pools deployed by different factory generations are discovered through one interface, a MetaRegistry sitting behind an AddressProvider, and the protocol's own router constructs multi-pool routes across those generations within Curve
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Ag says MULTI-VENUE and this router is single-venue. Stage 1 sharpens the corpus's marker: the object solved here is REGISTRY UNIFICATION ACROSS GENERATIONS of a protocol's own code, not route construction across venues, and the two problems have nothing in common but the word routing.

nodes.label: F14 CRV is minted weekly by the Minter against integrals reported by liqui
nodes.text: CRV is minted weekly by the Minter against integrals reported by liquidity gauges, and the DAO may kill a gauge, ending its emissions without touching anyone's deposits
nodes.note: Em fits the issuance.

nodes.label: F15 WHERE those emissions go is decided by a vote: veCRV holders vote a we
nodes.text: WHERE those emissions go is decided by a vote: veCRV holders vote a weight vector over gauges in the GaugeController, and that vector parameterises the emission function
nodes.note: RESIDUE — Em says tokens are emitted and is silent on direction; the contested Ve names the lock and is silent on the vote. Note the object is identical to PancakeSwap's MasterChef allocation table (pancakeswap.json F19) with an admin in place of the vote — the same unnameable weight vector under two different authorities.

nodes.label: F16 voting power is a non-transferable, non-reversible time-decaying lock:
nodes.text: voting power is a non-transferable, non-reversible time-decaying lock: VotingEscrow.vy (Vyper 0.2.4, 0x5f3b5DfEb7B28CDbD7FAba78963EE202a494e2A2) with MAXTIME = 4*365*86400, a one-week minimum, unlock times rounded down to whole weeks, one lock per user, and power stored as a (bias, slope) piecewise-linear function with scheduled slope_changes so decay needs no user action
nodes.note: RESIDUE BY RULE. Only the CONTESTED-register symbol Ve names this and it is outside the 58, so under the decomposition contract it is recorded as residue rather than used. The corpus uses Ve under offVocabulary with a note arguing it is load-bearing; stage 2 agrees it is load-bearing and disagrees that one symbol covers it — Curve runs FOUR separable mechanisms on this one lock (the lock, the gauge vote F15, the boost F17, the external vote market F23), three of which are residue in their own right.

nodes.label: F17 the lock also multiplies an LP's own emission rate, RIVALROUSLY: Liqui
nodes.text: the lock also multiplies an LP's own emission rate, RIVALROUSLY: LiquidityGaugeV6._update_liquidity_limit sets working_balance = min(l, l*40/100 + L*voting_balance/voting_total*60/100) and the reward rate is working_balance/working_supply, so an unboosted LP earns 40% of their nominal share, a fully boosted LP earns 100%, and one LP's boost lowers every other LP's yield through the shared denominator
nodes.note: RESIDUE — the widely quoted '2.5x' is the RATIO between the floor (0.4) and the cap (1.0), not a multiplier on an independent quantity, and the mechanism is dilutive: it reallocates a fixed emission rather than increasing one. No symbol names a rivalrous multiplier over a shared denominator.

nodes.label: F18 THE VALUE-RETURN CHANNEL IS DISTRIBUTION TO A CLAIM CLASS: 50% of ever
nodes.text: THE VALUE-RETURN CHANNEL IS DISTRIBUTION TO A CLAIM CLASS: 50% of every trading fee is an admin fee, routed FeeCollector -> CowSwapBurner -> Hooker -> FeeAllocator (which may divert at most 5,000 bps, 'the remaining portion (at least 50%) always flows to the FeeDistributor') -> FeeDistributor -> veCRV claimants, paid in crvUSD
nodes.note: Fd fits, and this is THE ONLY GENUINE DISTRIBUTION TO A CLAIM CLASS among the five applications in this category — Uniswap and PancakeSwap destroy, Raydium accumulates, Fluid's channel is unestablished. Fd is a candidate-register symbol and is used as such. DEPARTURE from the corpus in detail: the reward token is crvUSD, not 3CRV — 'There are actually two FeeDistributors deployed, as rewards were distributed in 3CRV tokens, before a DAO vote changed the reward token to crvUSD' — so a construction assuming the 3CRV route describes a retired system. Allocator cap at https://docs.curve.finance/developer/fees/fee-allocator (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F19 the protocol does not price its own fee stream: admin fees arriving in
nodes.text: the protocol does not price its own fee stream: admin fees arriving in arbitrary tokens are converted by posting CoW Protocol CONDITIONAL ORDERS through CowSwapBurner (Ethereum 0xC0fC3dDfec95ca45A0D2393F518D3EA1ccF44f8b, Gnosis 0x566b9F24200A9B51b76792D4e81B569AF27eda83), and on chains without CoW the superseded route still runs — burn to MIM, bridge to mainnet, burn MIM to 3CRV
nodes.note: RESIDUE — Ba names batch-auction clearing but belongs to the OTHER protocol; nothing says 'this protocol's fee plumbing is a client of that protocol's clearing mechanism'. This is the containment relation again (F11, F23), here across a protocol boundary rather than within Curve.

nodes.label: F20 authority is split across TWO governance bodies with different thresho
nodes.text: authority is split across TWO governance bodies with different thresholds over disjoint action sets: the OWNERSHIP DAO (agent 0x40907540d8a6C65c637785e8f8B742ae6b0b9968, quorum 30%, support 51%) and the PARAMETER DAO (agent 0x4eeb3ba4f221ca16ed4a0cc7254e2e32df948c5f, quorum 15%, support 60%), both voting with veCRV and executing Aragon EVM scripts
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Tg treats governance as ONE delayed authority. There are two, over disjoint action sets, with different thresholds, and Tg names neither the partition nor the thresholds. The bridges lane's finding applies here too: the control elements name the facility and not the holder.

nodes.label: F21 a third body may act quickly but only in one DIRECTION: a 5-of-9 Emerg
nodes.text: a third body may act quickly but only in one DIRECTION: a 5-of-9 Emergency DAO (0x467947EE34aF926cF1DCac093870f613C96B1E0c on Ethereum, 0x6d447e544D01a59cb0774763bf15526574CffFeD elsewhere) that 'cannot move or withdraw any user funds', may pause the Peg Stability Reserve, may REDUCE but never increase debt ceilings, may adjust Llamalend AMM fees and monetary policy 'without triggering liquidation for any users', and may set lending-vault deposit limits; pools themselves additionally expose kill_me / is_killed
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and Gp is ADDED relative to the corpus, which records no emergency element for Curve at all. RESIDUE for the shape: a MONOTONE-RESTRICTED authority — may lower a bound, may never raise it — is neither a pause (Gp) nor a delay (Tg), and the constraint 'may act only where the act cannot cause a liquidation' is a restriction stated over the mechanism's own effects, which nothing in the 58 can express. Its nine members are named publicly, which is itself unrecordable.

nodes.label: F22 the reference path for exercising that governance runs through another
nodes.text: the reference path for exercising that governance runs through another protocol: Curve's own voting library creates DAO votes through the Convex voter proxy 0x989AEB4D175E16225E39E87D0D97A3360524AD80
nodes.note: RESIDUE — the vocabulary has no way to say that the effective controller of a mechanism is a third-party protocol. Stage 1 upgrades this from an observation about the ecosystem (Convex/Votium vote markets) to a fact about the protocol's own tooling, which is a stronger claim than the corpus's residue entry. Note also the reproduction constraint on any construction claiming to reimplement this AMM: the current-generation pool repositories are all-rights-reserved by Swiss Stake AG, 'published for informational purposes only', so the construction must be built from the whitepapers (F1, F2), not the code.

nodes.label: Fluid
F1 a DEX v1 pool quotes off x*y=k CONTRACTED INTO A RANGE — 'The DEX uses
nodes.text: a DEX v1 pool quotes off x*y=k CONTRACTED INTO A RANGE — 'The DEX uses the x*y=k curve, but the liquidity is contracted within a range that is set by governance upon pool creation' — which Fluid describes as 'a combination of Uniswap v2 & Uniswap v3, otherwise known as a single auto rebalancing range order'
nodes.note: THE POOL INVARIANT, v1 answer. Cp is exact. Cl is APPROXIMATE here and this is where the corpus's forced marker is correct: there is exactly ONE range, it is a pool-level parameter set by governance, and no user chooses ticks — so 'range positions, ticks' names the geometry and misnames the ownership. Cp is ADDED relative to the corpus, which records Cl alone and therefore loses the fact that the curve inside the range is constant product.

nodes.label: F2 a DEX v2 pool has ticks, a current tick and per-range positions: the s
nodes.text: a DEX v2 pool has ticks, a current tick and per-range positions: the singleton's DexKey is {token0, token1, fee, tickSpacing, controller}, pool state exposes currentTick, currentSqrtPriceX96, activeLiquidity and lpFee, and types 3 and 4 are explicitly range orders — 'Like Uniswap v3 range orders, but enhanced: the liquidity earns lending APR by default and can be used as collateral' (D3) and 'Create range orders on the debt side by borrowing assets' (D4)
nodes.note: THE CORRECTION THE CORPUS RECORD NEEDS. The corpus marks Cl FORCED with the reason 'Fluid's curve is a single self-rebalancing moderate-width range ... Cl names user-owned static ticks, which Fluid does not have — there are no per-user ranges to name'. That describes DEX v1. DEX v2 was announced 2026-05-09 and IS DEPLOYED, with tick spacing in the pool key, a current tick in pool state and per-range positions on both the collateral and the debt side, so for D3/D4 pools Cl is a GOOD fit and the forced marker is wrong as recorded. The forced reading survives only for v1 / Type-1 / Type-2 pools (F1). Announcement and type list at https://fluid.io/blog/protocol-introducing-fluid-dex-v2 (2026-08-04). Caveat for stage 3: DEX v2 is NOT in the public repository — at HEAD a9949b48ba1247d4f478cd0acb40896b5c8bf3f8 (2026-03-04) contracts/protocols/dex/ holds only poolT1 and smartLending, while the docs reference contracts/periphery/dexV2/router/main.sol and publish a live FluidDexV2Router on Polygon at 0x713fD04a47Db41AB5684AEC2A2063d5278A53616 — so every v2 claim here rests on documentation, not on source.

nodes.label: F3 the pool moves its own centre without an owner action and without a pr
nodes.text: the pool moves its own centre without an owner action and without a profit test: the Center Price is 'the price at which the Pool rebalances itself once the Upper or Lower bounds are breached by the pool price', the move takes place over a Shift Time rather than instantaneously, and the centre may never leave [Center Min Price, Center Max Price]
nodes.note: RESIDUE — a PROFIT-INDEPENDENT, GOVERNANCE-BOUNDED, TIME-SMEARED recentering. Cl presumes user-chosen static ticks; Pm presumes an externally quoted price. And critically it is NOT Curve's profit-gated repeg (curve.json F3): Curve gates on a running profit ledger and may deadlock, Fluid gates on a bound breach and interpolates over a fixed duration under hard governance limits. So RECENTERING IS A FAMILY WITH AT LEAST TWO MEMBERS whose failure modes differ, and the vocabulary collapses both to nothing. Mechanism names corroborated by the DexLite resolver structs CenterPriceShift, RangeShift and ThresholdShift at https://docs.fluid.instadapp.io/ (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F4 one unit of capital occupies three roles simultaneously: Smart Collate
nodes.text: one unit of capital occupies three roles simultaneously: Smart Collateral 'is a single range order' that is lent into the Liquidity Layer earning supply yield, is borrowable against, AND is deployed as AMM inventory quoting swaps
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the reason the protocol exists — Fluid claims up to $39 of quoted liquidity per $1 of TVL. The vocabulary partitions Pool pricing (G02) and Credit (G05) into DISJOINT REGISTERS and provides no way to say that one position occupies both. 100% residue, exactly as the corpus records.

nodes.label: F5 Smart Debt inverts it: the BORROWED PRINCIPAL is the AMM's inventory,
nodes.text: Smart Debt inverts it: the BORROWED PRINCIPAL is the AMM's inventory, so a swapper trades against someone else's liability and the trading fees pay that liability down — 'the first time debt can be transformed into a productive asset by using it as liquidity for the DEX', with borrowers 'even having the possibility of getting paid to borrow'
nodes.note: RESIDUE, two distinct gaps. (i) No symbol names a trade whose COUNTERPARTY INVENTORY IS A LIABILITY. (ii) No symbol names a FEE NETTING AGAINST AN INTEREST EXPENSE INSIDE ONE ACCOUNTING UNIT. Stage 1 strengthens the corpus's Pl marker here: the swapper is not merely transacting against the debt, the trade AMORTISES it. The vault taxonomy makes the product of the two choices explicit — Type 1 normal/normal, Type 2 smart collateral/normal debt, Type 3 normal collateral/smart debt, Type 4 smart/smart — and nothing in the 58 can be indexed by which leg it applies to.

nodes.label: F6 the two sides carry different claim instruments: a lender receives a F
nodes.text: the two sides carry different claim instruments: a lender receives a FUNGIBLE ERC-4626 fToken, while a borrower's vault position is an NFT that 'can be moved freely if needed. Each NFT comprises the Vault including its debt and collateral assets'
nodes.note: FUNGIBILITY OF THE POSITION, and Fluid answers it differently on each side. Sh discharges the fToken's pro-rata claim. RESIDUE for the other side: a TRANSFERABLE INSTRUMENT BUNDLING A COLLATERAL LEG AND A DEBT LEG is not a pro-rata claim on anything — selling it transfers an obligation, not just an asset — and neither Sh nor any credit symbol names an instrument with negative components. Vault taxonomy verbatim in the repo README at https://github.com/Instadapp/fluid-contracts-public (contracts/protocols/vault/README.md, 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F7 one ledger serves several independent products: 'The Liquidity Layer s
nodes.text: one ledger serves several independent products: 'The Liquidity Layer serves as the foundation of Fluid upon which various protocols can be built. It acts as a singular layer that consolidates liquidity across protocols built on Fluid, eliminating the need for each protocol to independently attract liquidity' — the DEX, the vaults and the lending market all draw balances from it
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Pl names a shared pool where LENDERS AND BORROWERS meet. What is shared here is a ledger that several distinct PRODUCT TYPES register against, which is structurally the SAME OBJECT as PancakeSwap Infinity's Vault (pancakeswap.json F10). One missing symbol, two independent appearances in this lane on protocols with no shared lineage — the strongest evidence in the category that this gap is real. Pl is retained because the debt side of the DEX is literally this pool's debt, but it is carrying two jobs.

nodes.label: F8 capacity is a bound that RELAXES ON A SCHEDULE rather than a fixed cap
nodes.text: capacity is a bound that RELAXES ON A SCHEDULE rather than a fixed cap: borrowing is governed by Base Limit, Current Limit, Max Limit, Expand Percentage ('the rate at which Limits would increase or decrease over the given duration') and Expand Duration, withdrawal by the same four plus Withdrawable, and the docs state the ceilings adjust 'in real-time based on utilization rates'
nodes.note: RESIDUE — a RATE-LIMITED CAPABILITY, not a cap. Gp is a switch and Tg is a delay; neither is a continuously-relaxing bound whose current value is a function of utilisation and elapsed time. Parameter glossary at https://fluid.guides.instadapp.io/dex-protocol/protocol-details.md (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F9 a portion of the pool is reserved for an operation that has not happen
nodes.text: a portion of the pool is reserved for an operation that has not happened yet: the Withdrawal Gap is a 'safety non-withdrawable amount to guarantee liquidations'
nodes.note: RESIDUE — reserved capacity for a FUTURE operation, which is neither a queue (Wq, which orders claims that have been made) nor a backstop (Bs, which is capital posted by a party and slashable). Nothing names 'this liquidity is unavailable so that a mechanism can still run'.

nodes.label: F10 a position's solvency is tested by its debt-to-collateral ratio agains
nodes.text: a position's solvency is tested by its debt-to-collateral ratio against the vault's liquidation threshold, with LTVs up to 95%, and there is an additional Max Liquidation Threshold above which 'a vault ... is liquidated automatically'
nodes.note: DEPARTURE from the corpus, which lists Ct as DERIVED rather than as part of the canonical form. It is a first-class, per-vault parameterised test with TWO thresholds — one admitting partial liquidation, one forcing it — and it should be first-class in the construction. This is the same demotion error stage 1 found on the options lane (Aevo, Panoptic), which suggests the derivation rule itself is what is wrong, not the two decompositions.

nodes.label: F11 the unit liquidated is an EQUIVALENCE CLASS, not a position: each posi
nodes.text: the unit liquidated is an EQUIVALENCE CLASS, not a position: each position is assigned to a slot keyed by its ratio ('Drawing inspiration from Uniswap v3's slot-based liquidity'), and when a slot crosses the threshold 'the protocol aggregates all vaults in that slot for liquidation in a single transaction. Afterward, the system recalibrates the remaining vaults, adjusting their debt ratio positions down to the next slot' — taking only the minimum needed to restore health
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Li names third parties paid to close POSITIONS and the unit here is a slot; Ad's 'rank-ordered forced close' is close in spirit and wrong in mechanism, because there is no ranking — there is a QUANTISED KEY, and every member of a bucket is treated identically regardless of its position within the bucket. The user docs confirm the consequence: 'your position is not individually liquidated but instead a portion of all at risk positions is liquidated, all at once in one transaction' (https://fluid.guides.instadapp.io/vault-protocol/advanced-liquidation-mechanism/vault-liquidation.md, 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F12 the liquidator is an ordinary trader who does not know they are one: l
nodes.text: the liquidator is an ordinary trader who does not know they are one: liquidatable collateral is exposed at a discount inside DEX aggregator routes (1inch, Paraswap and 0x are named) so that 'traders participate in the liquidation process indirectly by completing normal swaps', making Fluid 'less reliant on Keepers'
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and only the weakest half of Li survives: a third party closes the position. There is NO BOUNTY — the incentive is delivered as PRICE IMPROVEMENT TO AN UNAWARE COUNTERPARTY on an unrelated trade — and no symbol expresses an incentive paid as execution quality to a party who has not opted in. The penalty figure needs a qualifier in any paper text: the Liquidity Layer page says 'as low as 0.1%' while the user docs put the ETH/USDC vault, the most common borrowing vault, at 1%, so 0.1% is a floor claim and not a typical value.

nodes.label: F13 vault pricing reads an external stack arranged as a CHECKED FALLBACK L
nodes.text: vault pricing reads an external stack arranged as a CHECKED FALLBACK LATTICE: ChainlinkOracleImpl, RedstoneOracleImpl, UniV3OracleImpl, PegOracleImpl, FallbackOracleImpl and UniV3CheckCLRSOracle (a Uniswap-v3-checked Chainlink/Redstone fallback), plus fluidCappedRate* and fluidCenterPrice* families and DEX-specific oracles — while at least one vault deliberately uses no market price at all: 'the weETH/wstETH Vault uses Contract Backing for the liquidation oracle'
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and stage 1 says Ex should be STRENGTHENED rather than weakened. Ex names 'push/pull/medianizer'; a lattice in which one source CHECKS another and a named fallback fires on failure is a different object, with a different failure model — and Ex cannot say that a price source is deliberately not a market price. The contract-backed leaf at https://fluid.guides.instadapp.io/vault-protocol/advanced-liquidation-mechanism/vault-liquidation.md (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F14 the DEX publishes its OWN price series, as a price rather than an accu
nodes.text: the DEX publishes its OWN price series, as a price rather than an accumulator, and publishes more than a price: 'Fluid's DEX has an inbuilt most optimized TWAP oracle. It allows you to fetch the last 5 min data in <15k gas; Last 15 min data in <30k gas', and it 'returns additional data like: maxima & minima during that time frame'
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and Tp is ADDED relative to the corpus, which records no price element for Fluid. THE PRICE-SERIES QUESTION: like Curve and unlike Uniswap and Raydium, the consumer reads a finished time-weighted price and integrates nothing. RESIDUE for the extrema: publishing the maximum and minimum over the window is STRICTLY MORE than Tp names, and it is the part a consumer needs to bound manipulation, so the symbol names the weaker of the two things the protocol supplies.

nodes.label: F15 settlement is atomic on-chain against the shared Liquidity Layer rathe
nodes.text: settlement is atomic on-chain against the shared Liquidity Layer rather than against per-pool inventory, and DEX v2 additionally advertises 'Flash Accounting (inspired by Uniswap v4)' alongside on-chain dynamic fees and on-chain limit orders that 'earn lending APR while waiting to be filled'
nodes.note: RESIDUE — THE SETTLEMENT DISCIPLINE, and a third protocol in this lane whose settlement regime has no symbol. Fl is NOT assigned: the deferred-net-settlement claim rests on an announcement blog alone because DEX v2 is absent from the public repository (F2), and the run's cite-or-drop invariant will not carry a mechanism symbol on a marketing page. Stage 3 should treat this obligation as UNVERIFIED rather than as residue proper. A resting order that earns lending yield while unfilled is separately unnameable and is F4's three-roles gap appearing on the execution side.

nodes.label: F16 the extension point is a CONTROLLER named per pool: the DexKey carries
nodes.text: the extension point is a CONTROLLER named per pool: the DexKey carries a controller address alongside tickSpacing, and the feature is documented as Hooks
nodes.note: RESIDUE — EXTENSION POINT, permission-binding convention #3 of three in this lane, and the corpus records NO hook residue for Fluid at all. The three conventions are genuinely different objects: Uniswap MINES the permission set into the hook contract's address so it belongs to the code and is frozen at pool initialization; PancakeSwap packs a 16-bit permission bitmap into the pool key's parameters so it belongs to the pool and one hook may hold different powers in different pools; Fluid names a single controller in the DexKey and publishes NO PERMISSION BITMAP AT ALL, so the scope of what a controller may do is not expressed in the pool's identity. Nothing in the 58 names third-party code executing inside the settlement path, and a single symbol for it would make three different security models look identical.

nodes.label: F17 which pools may exist is decided by governance: 'DEX v2 operates with
nodes.text: which pools may exist is decided by governance: 'DEX v2 operates with pools that are permissioned and listed on the Fluid Money Market ... Each pool has been approved through Fluid governance', discoverable through getD3PermissionedDexes() and getD4PermissionedDexes(), with a stated future transition to permissionless pools discovered from LogInitialize(dexType, dexId, dexKey, sqrtPriceX96)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Aw was considered and REJECTED: Aw gates a PARTY's access to a mechanism, whereas this gates a MECHANISM'S EXISTENCE, and conflating them would make a permissioned pool list look like a KYC'd pool. Same two-level structure as Curve's DAO-gated implementation registry (curve.json F12) and Uniswap's monotone fee-tier ratchet (uniswap.json F14), approached from the restrictive end — third appearance in the lane.

nodes.label: F18 governance can create new PRICING ENGINES, not merely new pools: 'At i
nodes.text: governance can create new PRICING ENGINES, not merely new pools: 'At its core, Fluid DEX v2 runs on a singleton contract built atop the Fluid Liquidity Layer ... Governance can deploy infinite DEX types, each with its own logic and math', with four types at launch (v1 Smart Collateral, v1 Smart Debt, Smart Collateral Range Orders, Smart Debt Range Orders)
nodes.note: RESIDUE — an authority over the SPACE OF ADMISSIBLE INVARIANTS. This is strictly stronger than F17: F17 governs which instances exist, this governs which kinds can. It also breaks the closure assumption behind any fixed decomposition of Fluid, because the set of pool-pricing obligations the protocol discharges is itself mutable by vote.

nodes.label: F19 governance is a Compound GovernorBravo fork: the fluid-governance repo
nodes.text: governance is a Compound GovernorBravo fork: the fluid-governance repository states 'Forked from Compound Governance' and ships GovernorBravoDelegate.sol, GovernorBravoDelegator.sol, Timelock.sol, TokenDelegate.sol, TokenDelegator.sol and a payloads/ directory
nodes.note: Tg is retained on the presence of Timelock.sol and the Bravo lineage, NOT on a parameter: stage 1 could not confirm the proposal threshold, the quorum, the timelock delay, or the identity of any team multisig at a primary source, so no numeric governance claim may enter the paper for Fluid.

nodes.label: F20 the implementation is mutable and configuration is delegated per-param
nodes.text: the implementation is mutable and configuration is delegated per-parameter: contracts/infiniteProxy/ implements an 'InfiniteProxy' with AdminInternals and CoreInternals, vault configuration is routed 'through the fallback which directs the call to adminModule', and authority is fanned out to named Auth contracts (LimitsAuth, LimitsAuthDex, WithdrawLimitAuth, WithdrawLimitAuthDex, RangeAuthDex, DexFeeAuth, RatesAuth, LiquidityTokenAuth, CollectRevenueAuth, VaultFeeRewardsAuth) plus AUTO-CONFIG HANDLERS (ExpandPercentHandler, MaxBorrowHandler, BufferRateHandler, EthenaRateHandler, DexFeeHandler with a DynamicFee abstract)
nodes.note: Up fits and the corpus understates it — the repo ships a contract literally named infiniteProxy. RESIDUE for two further things. (i) Authority is partitioned BY PARAMETER rather than by delay or by holder, which the control register cannot express. (ii) The auto-config handlers are the yield and CDP lanes' BOUNDED DELEGATE MANDATE schema — named agent, bounded quantity, cap, step limit, revocation — appearing in a spot DEX, bounding a rate or an expansion percentage instead of an allocation. That is a third independent lane arriving at the same schema, which is the strongest cross-lane evidence in the run for a LEVEL above the element. Tree confirmed at https://github.com/Instadapp/fluid-contracts-public (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F21 a guardian sits at the liquidity layer: the admin module's abstracts a
nodes.text: a guardian sits at the liquidity layer: the admin module's abstracts are GovernanceModule, GuardianModule, AuthModule and AuthInternals
nodes.note: Gp fits by name. Its scope, its holder and whether its powers are directional (as Curve's are, curve.json F21) were not established at a primary source.

nodes.label: F22 value return runs through a governance-toggled Revenue Cut into an on-
nodes.text: value return runs through a governance-toggled Revenue Cut into an on-chain buyback: 'Revenue Cuts can be turned on through governance voting and could consist of a cut from trading fees and/or a fee from any Smart Vault', and the deployed contract index carries Periphery/Buyback/{FluidBuyback, FluidBuybackProxy, FluidBuybackCore}
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and an HONEST GAP rather than a symbol. The corpus records NO value-return element for Fluid at all; a buyback contract is deployed, which puts Fluid in the same family as the other four. But WHICH CHANNEL it uses — destruction (Uniswap, PancakeSwap), accumulation (Raydium) or distribution to a claim class (Curve) — is not stated at any primary source reached by stage 1, nor is whether the buyback is currently running, so no element is assigned and the ambiguity is recorded instead of guessed. Note the shape of the failure: the ONE symbol the vocabulary offers here, Fd, would have been assigned by default in a decomposition that did not ask which channel, and it would have been wrong for three of the five and unproven for the fourth. Buyback contract index at https://docs.fluid.instadapp.io/ (2026-08-04); trading fees are themselves 'set to any trading fee by governance voting'.

nodes.label: PancakeSwap
F1 a v2 pool quotes a swap off the constant-product invariant on its own
nodes.text: a v2 pool quotes a swap off the constant-product invariant on its own two reserves, charging a total swap fee of 0.25% of which 0.17% is added back to the liquidity pool
nodes.note: THE POOL INVARIANT, first of four this protocol runs simultaneously. Cp fits exactly. The residual 0.08% is documented only as non-LP: the widely repeated 0.03% treasury / 0.05% burn split could NOT be confirmed at a PancakeSwap primary source by stage 1 and must not be carried further.

nodes.label: F2 a v3 or Infinity CLAMM pool applies the constant-product curve inside
nodes.text: a v3 or Infinity CLAMM pool applies the constant-product curve inside a tick range — 'CLAMM operates on the constant product formula (X * Y = K)' — with tick spacing carried in the pool's parameters
nodes.note: THE POOL INVARIANT, second answer. Cl and Cp together fit well, as for Uniswap.

nodes.label: F3 an Infinity LBAMM ('Liquidity Book') pool prices instead on DISCRETE B
nodes.text: an Infinity LBAMM ('Liquidity Book') pool prices instead on DISCRETE BINS: liquidity sits in a bin at a fixed price, the invariant WITHIN a bin is constant sum — 'LBAMM follows the constant sum formula (X + Y = K)' — so a trade inside one bin has zero price impact, and the bin step rather than a tick spacing is carried in the pool key
nodes.note: RESIDUE — THE POOL INVARIANT, third answer, and unnameable. St was considered and REJECTED: St is constant-sum NEAR PARITY over a whole pool as a limiting behaviour, whereas a bin is EXACTLY constant-sum over a quantised price cell, and vocab.md itself declares constant sum (CSM) 'a limit of St, not an element'. Cl was also rejected: bins are not ranges and carry no per-position index. This is a live, named, deployed pool type whose curve the vocabulary cannot state, and the corpus does not record it.

nodes.label: F4 a StableSwap pool type is deployed and routed to by the SmartRouter, w
nodes.text: a StableSwap pool type is deployed and routed to by the SmartRouter, which is documented as 'Able to route to v3, v2 and stable pool'
nodes.note: THE POOL INVARIANT, fourth answer. St fits by kind but the pool's parameterisation was not established at a primary source by stage 1, and the type carries only $3.7M of a $2,059.6M protocol (DefiLlama, 2026-08-04), so the symbol is carried on thin evidence and is the weakest member of this construction. SmartRouter 0x13f4EA83D0bd40E75C8222255bc855a974568Dd4.

nodes.label: F5 a v2 liquidity provider holds a fungible ERC-20 LP token: a pro-rata c
nodes.text: a v2 liquidity provider holds a fungible ERC-20 LP token: a pro-rata claim on the whole reserve
nodes.note: FUNGIBILITY OF THE POSITION, first of three answers this one protocol gives.

nodes.label: F6 a v3 or CLAMM liquidity provider holds a per-range NON-FUNGIBLE positi
nodes.text: a v3 or CLAMM liquidity provider holds a per-range NON-FUNGIBLE position, wrapped as an ERC-721 by the NonfungiblePositionManager
nodes.note: RESIDUE — FUNGIBILITY OF THE POSITION, second answer, and the same gap as Uniswap F4. NonfungiblePositionManager 0x46A15B0b27311cedF172AB29E4f4766fbE7F4364.

nodes.label: F7 an LBAMM liquidity provider holds a claim that is FUNGIBLE PER BIN — a
nodes.text: an LBAMM liquidity provider holds a claim that is FUNGIBLE PER BIN — an ERC-20 for the bin — so within one protocol the claim shape is a property of the pool type, not of the protocol
nodes.note: FUNGIBILITY OF THE POSITION, third answer. Sh discharges the per-bin claim. RESIDUE for the indexing: a decomposition assigns Sh to 'PancakeSwap' as a whole and thereby asserts something false about its v3 pools and something true about its bins. No element in the 58 is indexed by pool type, which is the resolution failure this protocol exhibits most cleanly.

nodes.label: F8 fees accrue to a v3/CLAMM position against a fee-growth index snapshot
nodes.text: fees accrue to a v3/CLAMM position against a fee-growth index snapshotted when the position was opened, and are collected rather than paid
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE for the same reason as Uniswap F5: the index is range-local, not global. Ix is ADDED relative to the corpus.

nodes.label: F9 settlement in Infinity is deferred and net against an immutable ledger
nodes.text: settlement in Infinity is deferred and net against an immutable ledger: vault.lock() then lockAcquired(data), operations run against a pool manager which calls vault.accountAppBalanceDelta(...), and the caller reconciles with take / settle / mint / burn (plus clear() for dust and the three-step sync-transfer-settle), with unsettled deltas counted in transient storage by SettlementGuard through UNSETTLED_DELTAS_COUNT and CURRENCY_DELTA
nodes.note: RESIDUE — THE SETTLEMENT DISCIPLINE. Same object as Uniswap v4 (uniswap.json F10) and the same failure: Fl names borrow-and-repay, not 'run arbitrary operations then settle the net', and no symbol states the zero-delta conservation law. Note the counter-based encoding here (a count of unsettled currencies) rather than Uniswap's vector-of-deltas encoding — a difference in mechanism that no construction can register because neither is nameable.

nodes.label: F10 custody and pricing are SPLIT ACROSS CONTRACTS: an immutable Vault hol
nodes.text: custody and pricing are SPLIT ACROSS CONTRACTS: an immutable Vault holds all balances and the accounting, while pricing lives in independent singleton pool managers (CLPoolManager and BinPoolManager) that register against it, so two AMM families share one ledger and tokens are transferred to the Vault rather than to the pool manager
nodes.note: RESIDUE — a settlement ledger that several independent pricing engines register against. This is the single largest architectural difference from Uniswap v4, which fuses the two, and it is structurally the SAME OBJECT as Fluid's Liquidity Layer (fluid.json F8). One missing symbol, two appearances in this lane — which is the strongest evidence in the category that the gap is real rather than an artefact of one protocol. PoolKey is (currency0, currency1, hooks, poolManager, fee, parameters), so the pricing engine is named IN the pool's identity; PoolId = keccak256(abi.encode(poolKey)). Cross-check https://developer.pancakeswap.finance/contracts/infinity/overview/amm-layer-poolmanager (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F11 a caller may take assets before paying inside one lock scope, with the
nodes.text: a caller may take assets before paying inside one lock scope, with the balance check deferred to reconciliation
nodes.note: Fl fits the take-before-settle capability. Distinguish from F9 as in Uniswap: the flash capability and the net-settlement discipline are different obligations that happen to be implemented by the same machinery.

nodes.label: F12 a pool may name a hook, and WHICH callbacks fire is carried in the POO
nodes.text: a pool may name a hook, and WHICH callbacks fire is carried in the POOL'S OWN KEY: the first 16 bits of the bytes32 parameters field are the hook registration bitmap and the next field is tick spacing (CL) or bin step (Bin) — the docs decode 0x...0a00c2 as permission bits 0000 0000 1100 0010 (afterInitialize, beforeSwap, afterSwap) with tick spacing 10 — so one hook contract may be registered with DIFFERENT permission sets by different pools and no address mining is required
nodes.note: RESIDUE — EXTENSION POINT, permission-binding convention #2 of three in this lane. The semantics match Uniswap's but the BINDING is opposite: here the permission set belongs to the POOL, there it belongs to the CODE. Any symbol that names 'hook' must choose one, and these two protocols answer differently, so a single symbol would make them look identical when their security and deployment models differ. Nothing in the 58 names third-party code in the settlement path at all. CertiK published 'PancakeSwap Infinity: Hooks Security Considerations' for this surface.

nodes.label: F13 the current generation publishes no protocol-level price series: Infin
nodes.text: the current generation publishes no protocol-level price series: Infinity ships no oracle in the core and a custom oracle is an advertised hook use case
nodes.note: RESIDUE — THE PRICE-SERIES QUESTION, answered by relocation rather than by a mechanism, as in Uniswap v4 (uniswap.json F8). Tp is NOT assigned: the v3 fork presumably inherits Uniswap v3's observation ring buffer but stage 1 did not verify this at a primary source, so under the run's cite-or-drop invariant no price element enters this construction. The corpus likewise carries no Tp for PancakeSwap.

nodes.label: F14 the protocol's share of the fee is set by a swappable controller: Prot
nodes.text: the protocol's share of the fee is set by a swappable controller: ProtocolFeeController is Ownable2Step with protocolFeeSplitRatio = 33 * 1e4 (33% of the total fee in hundredths of a bip) and defaultProtocolFeeForDynamicFeePool = 300, rejects a dynamic-pool default greater than 0.4%, and exposes owner-only setProtocolFeeSplitRatio, setDefaultProtocolFeeForDynamicFeePool, per-pool setProtocolFee and collectProtocolFee
nodes.note: RESIDUE — the whole controller is replaceable wholesale by setProtocolFeeController, which is the same privilege/policy split as Uniswap's V4FeePolicy (uniswap.json F20): not Up (no proxy, no delegatecall) and not Tg (the swap is not the delay). This is the mechanism the corpus mislabels as Up.

nodes.label: F15 the swap fee is split THREE WAYS at the protocol level, per tier, with
nodes.text: the swap fee is split THREE WAYS at the protocol level, per tier, with the burn as one of the three legs: EVM v3 tiers pay LP 67 / burn 15 / treasury 18 at 0.01%, 66 / 15 / 19 at 0.05%, and 68 / 23 / 9 at both 0.25% and 1%, while Solana pools pay a uniform 84 / 8 / 8
nodes.note: RESIDUE — Fd is DROPPED from this construction. Fd names distribution of surplus to a claim class; here the split is a PRIMITIVE OF THE FEE ACCOUNTING computed per tier, and one of its three destinations is destruction and another is a treasury, neither of which is a claim class. After Tokenomics 3.0 there is no revenue share to any class at all.

nodes.label: F16 THE VALUE-RETURN CHANNEL IS SUPPLY DESTRUCTION, funded from five named
nodes.text: THE VALUE-RETURN CHANNEL IS SUPPLY DESTRUCTION, funded from five named sources: spot trading 15-23% of trading fees, perpetual trading 20% of all profits, CAKE.PADs 100% of fees, Prediction 3% of each round and Lottery 20% of CAKE played, targeting 'an annual deflation rate of at least ~4% per year and a total CAKE supply reduction of ~20% by 2030'
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Destruction, like Uniswap and UNLIKE Raydium, which buys and holds (raydium.json F11) — the corpus's three-way grouping of these protocols is invalid. Note the mechanism differs from Uniswap's even within the destruction family: PancakeSwap burns at source from an enumerated set of revenue lines, whereas Uniswap burns a searcher's premium paid to redeem an inventory. One symbol for 'burn' would erase that too.

nodes.label: F17 the terminal bound on supply is itself governable: the CAKE hard cap w
nodes.text: the terminal bound on supply is itself governable: the CAKE hard cap was lowered from 450M to 400M by a proposal that passed 2026-01-16
nodes.note: RESIDUE — Em covers issuance and says nothing about a ceiling; nothing covers a governance-mutable terminal bound on supply.

nodes.label: F18 liquidity providers may stake their LP tokens or position NFTs into fa
nodes.text: liquidity providers may stake their LP tokens or position NFTs into farms and receive CAKE emissions, directed to 'multichain farms, lottery, and ecosystem growth'
nodes.note: Em fits the issuance. MasterChefV3 0x556B9306565093C855AEA9AE92A594704c2Cd59e per https://developer.pancakeswap.finance/contracts/v3/addresses (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F19 the emission is directed across pools by an admin-mutable allocation-p
nodes.text: the emission is directed across pools by an admin-mutable allocation-point vector, and the docs do not name the authority that sets it, calling it only 'the Chefs'
nodes.note: RESIDUE — Em says tokens are emitted and is silent on DIRECTION. Confirms the corpus's first residue item. Note this is the same shape as Curve's gauge-weight vote (curve.json F16) with the vote replaced by an admin: the object is a weight vector over pools parameterising the emission function, and the vocabulary can name neither the vector nor who sets it.

nodes.label: F20 the AMM layer can be stopped, by an authority strictly weaker than own
nodes.text: the AMM layer can be stopped, by an authority strictly weaker than ownership: CLPoolManagerOwner is PausableRole and exposes pausePoolManager() onlyPausableRoleOrOwner while unpausePoolManager() is onlyOwner
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and Gp is ADDED relative to the corpus, which records no pause for PancakeSwap at all — stage 1 calls this the single most consequential delta in its section. RESIDUE for the shape: the authority is ONE-DIRECTIONAL, a delegate may stop but only the owner may restart. Gp names a pause as a symmetric switch. Compare Curve's Emergency DAO, which is monotone in the other register (may reduce a ceiling, may never raise it) — curve.json F22.

nodes.label: F21 the core is not upgradeable — the Vault is stated immutable and the do
nodes.text: the core is not upgradeable — the Vault is stated immutable and the docs assert 'The non-upgradeable core ensures stability' — while ownership of the pool-manager owner and of the fee controller moves by 2-step transfer, and the identity of the owner and of the pausable role is not published
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and TWO DEPARTURES from the corpus. Up is DROPPED: the corpus assigns it on the strength of 'a mutable admin', but at the Infinity generation there is no proxy and no delegatecall — what exists is a wholesale-swappable policy object (F14) and a pause (F20). Tg is DROPPED for want of evidence, not refuted: stage 1 could not establish at any primary source whether the owner is a multisig, a timelock, or an EOA, or what delay applies, so under the run's cite-or-drop invariant no delayed-governance symbol may be asserted. The vocabulary's control elements name the FACILITY without naming the holder — the same gap the bridges lane found on three bridges.

nodes.label: F22 the protocol RETIRED a whole mechanism and settled the holders of a th
nodes.text: the protocol RETIRED a whole mechanism and settled the holders of a third party's derivative of it: veCAKE, gauge voting, farm boosting and the 5% revenue share ended on 2025-04-23 (final gauge vote Epoch 37), Epoch 38 ran 2025-04-25 to 05-06, accrual and revenue share stopped 2025-05-07, a 6-month redemption window for directly staked CAKE closed 2025-10-23, third-party locker protocols were handled by whitelisting delegator addresses for 1:1 redemption, and the freed revenue-share allocation was 'redirected to the CAKE burn mechanism, increasing the burn rate for these pools from 10% to 15%'
nodes.note: RESIDUE, twice. (i) The vocabulary is a predicate on a protocol at an instant: it can record the absence of a vote-escrow mechanism but not a TRANSITION out of one, and every construction in this lane is therefore timeless in a way the protocols are not. (ii) It cannot record that a protocol assumed a liability to a derivative built on its own mechanism by a third party — the mirror image of Curve's finding that a third party effectively controls its governance path (curve.json F23).

nodes.label: Raydium
F1 an AMM v4 or CPMM pool quotes a swap off x*y=k on its two vault reserv
nodes.text: an AMM v4 or CPMM pool quotes a swap off x*y=k on its two vault reserves, consulting no external oracle during a swap, deposit or withdrawal — 'Raydium's core products don't depend on external oracles for pricing: the pool state IS the oracle'
nodes.note: THE POOL INVARIANT, first of three live answers. Cp fits exactly. Program IDs: AMM v4 675kPX9MHTjS2zt1qfr1NYHuzeLXfQM9H24wFSUt1Mp8, CPMM CPMMoo8L3F4NbTegBCKVNunggL7H1ZpdTHKxQB5qKP1C, per https://docs.raydium.io/reference/program-addresses (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F2 a CLMM pool quotes off sqrt-price and tick arithmetic with price(i) =
nodes.text: a CLMM pool quotes off sqrt-price and tick arithmetic with price(i) = 1.0001^i and MIN/MAX_TICK = -/+443636, carrying sqrt_price_x64, a current tick, fee-growth globals, an inline bitmap covering +/-1,024 tick arrays, and Uniswap v3's liquidity_gross / liquidity_net accounting
nodes.note: THE POOL INVARIANT, second answer. Cl and Cp fit together as for Uniswap. CLMM program CAMMCzo5YL8w4VFF8KVHrK22GGUsp5VTaW7grrKgrWqK.

nodes.label: F3 a Stable AMM program is deployed and live at 5quBtoiQqxF9Jv6KYKctB59NT
nodes.text: a Stable AMM program is deployed and live at 5quBtoiQqxF9Jv6KYKctB59NT3gtJD2Y65kdnB1Uev3h, and no invariant for it is stated at any primary source: the program is closed source and publishes no IDL
nodes.note: RESIDUE OF A DIFFERENT KIND — not unnameable, UNVERIFIABLE. St was considered and rejected: assigning it would be an inference from the product's name, and the run's cite-or-drop invariant forbids that. Only three of Raydium's nine programs are open source (raydium-amm, raydium-cp-swap, raydium-clmm); Stable AMM, AMM Routing, Burn&Earn/LP Lock and the three Farm programs have no public source, and four of those have no IDL either, so any construction claiming to reproduce 'Raydium' reproduces a prose description for a substantial part of it.

nodes.label: F4 an AMM v4 or CPMM liquidity provider holds a FUNGIBLE SPL LP token and
nodes.text: an AMM v4 or CPMM liquidity provider holds a FUNGIBLE SPL LP token and exits by burning it for a pro-rata slice of both vaults; there is no collect-fees instruction on either program, so fees remain in the vaults, inflate k, and are realised only implicitly at exit
nodes.note: FUNGIBILITY OF THE POSITION, first answer. Sh names the pro-rata claim. RESIDUE for the ABSENCE OF A CLAIM STEP: an LP earning that can only be realised by exiting is a different instrument from one with a callable accrual, and no symbol registers the difference.

nodes.label: F5 a CLMM liquidity provider instead holds a POSITION NFT — a supply-1 mi
nodes.text: a CLMM liquidity provider instead holds a POSITION NFT — a supply-1 mint whose mint authority is the program — against a chosen price range, claims fees explicitly, and closes by decreasing liquidity to zero, collecting, then burning the NFT
nodes.note: RESIDUE — FUNGIBILITY OF THE POSITION, second answer, and the same gap as Uniswap F4 and PancakeSwap F6. Third protocol in this lane holding both instrument shapes at once with no way to index a symbol by pool type.

nodes.label: F6 fees accrue to a CLMM position against the pool's fee-growth globals,
nodes.text: fees accrue to a CLMM position against the pool's fee-growth globals, differenced against the position's own PersonalPositionState checkpoint
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE for the same reason as Uniswap F5 — the effective index is range-local. Ix is ADDED relative to the corpus.

nodes.label: F7 which leg the fee is taken from is fixed at pool creation and can neve
nodes.text: which leg the fee is taken from is fixed at pool creation and can never change: CLMM's CollectFeeOn is one of FromInput, Token0Only or Token1Only, so a pool may take its fee out of swap OUTPUT rather than input, changing the quoting equation by direction
nodes.note: RESIDUE — no symbol distinguishes which leg a fee is skimmed from. The same gap appears on Curve as a pool-type property (curve.json F8), so this is category-level. CLMM also supports an optional dynamic volatility-surcharge fee, which is Curve's dynamic-fee residue (curve.json F7) appearing on a second protocol.

nodes.label: F8 a pool's fee tier is a reference to an immutable AmmConfig chosen at c
nodes.text: a pool's fee tier is a reference to an immutable AmmConfig chosen at creation and can NEVER be changed for that pool, with 19 live CPMM configs spanning 0.005%-4% and 18 live CLMM configs spanning 0.01%-4%
nodes.note: RESIDUE — a pool-parameter registry, the same shape as Uniswap's tier ratchet (uniswap.json F14) with the mutability moved: Uniswap's registry grows monotonically and the pool follows it, Raydium's pool is frozen to the config it was born with. Neither is nameable. The commonly circulated '0.01/0.25/1%' triple is wrong; CLMM config list at https://api-v3.raydium.io/main/clmm-config (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F9 the trading fee is split at the protocol level: CLMM and CPMM pay 84%
nodes.text: the trading fee is split at the protocol level: CLMM and CPMM pay 84% to LPs, 12% to buyback and 4% to treasury, while AMM v4 pays 88/12 with no treasury slice — verified against every live config, all of which carry protocolFeeRate 120000 and fundFeeRate 40000 on a 1,000,000 denominator, whereas AMM v4 uses a 10,000 denominator on which 25 means 0.25%
nodes.note: RESIDUE — Fd is DROPPED from this construction (see F11). A three-way protocol-level split has no symbol, as on PancakeSwap (pancakeswap.json F15). Rates verified live against https://api-v3.raydium.io/main/cpmm-config and /clmm-config (2026-08-04) rather than the docs, because the docs contradict themselves here: /reference/fee-comparison claims CPMM is '100% LP (protocol share currently 0%)' and that AMM v4/CLMM's 12% goes '100% to treasury', both refuted by all 37 live configs and by /ray/protocol-fees on the same site.

nodes.label: F10 CPMM additionally charges a CREATOR fee that is not a slice of the tra
nodes.text: CPMM additionally charges a CREATOR fee that is not a slice of the trade fee at all — live configs show creatorFeeRate from 500 to 14,950 — plus a flat createPoolFee of 150,000,000 lamports (0.15 SOL) on CPMM and AMM v4
nodes.note: RESIDUE — an additive fee accruing to a party who is neither the LP nor the protocol, sitting outside the fee split entirely. Nothing in the 58 names a third fee beneficiary, and nothing names a fee charged for the act of creating a mechanism.

nodes.label: F11 THE VALUE-RETURN CHANNEL IS ACCUMULATION: the 12% buys RAY on the open
nodes.text: THE VALUE-RETURN CHANNEL IS ACCUMULATION: the 12% buys RAY on the open market and HOLDS it in a protocol-controlled account, DdHDoz94o2WJmD9myRobHCwtx1bESpHTd4SSPe6VEZaz, which holds about 83.54M RAY across six token accounts, while RAY total supply stands at 554,997,631.209468 against a 555,000,000 maximum — on the order of 2,400 RAY has ever been destroyed
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and THE CORRECTION THAT INVALIDATES THE CORPUS'S GROUPING. The corpus files Raydium with Uniswap and PancakeSwap under a shared 'burn/buyback ambiguity'. Uniswap DESTROYS UNI, PancakeSwap DESTROYS CAKE, Raydium BUYS AND HOLDS — the docs' own row label is 'Bought-back RAY accumulation' and the chain agrees. Three channels, three different effects on the supply model, and the vocabulary names only the fourth (Fd, distribution to a claim class) which none of the three uses. Fd is therefore DROPPED from this construction. Supply and balances re-run against the Solana RPC by stage 1; buyback rate at https://docs.raydium.io/ray/ray-buybacks (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F12 CPMM and CLMM each maintain an on-chain price series as a 100-entry ri
nodes.text: CPMM and CLMM each maintain an on-chain price series as a 100-entry ring in an ObservationState PDA — CPMM storing (block_timestamp, cumulative price), CLMM storing cumulative TICK — which downstream protocols consume; AMM v4, which holds the largest share of the TVL, has no observation account at all and publishes nothing
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and Tp is ADDED relative to the corpus, which records no price element for Raydium. THE PRICE-SERIES QUESTION: this is an ACCUMULATOR the consumer must difference and divide, as on Uniswap and unlike Curve — and CLMM accumulates TICK rather than price, so the consumer must also exponentiate, which no symbol registers. RESIDUE for the scoping: a decomposition assigns Tp to 'Raydium' and thereby asserts it of a program that does not have it.

nodes.label: F13 settlement is atomic within one Solana instruction against per-pool va
nodes.text: settlement is atomic within one Solana instruction against per-pool vaults, and multi-hop is bounded: the AMM Routing program CPIs across at most two pools in a transaction
nodes.note: RESIDUE — THE SETTLEMENT DISCIPLINE: per-pool transfers, no deferred netting, and no symbol names either regime. Ag was considered and REJECTED: the router is single-venue, capped at two hops, closed source and without an IDL, so 'multi-venue route construction' is false of it on three counts. Routing program routeUGWgWzqBWFcrCfv8tritsqukccJPu3q5GPP3xS.

nodes.label: F14 the protocol's on-chain state footprint can only GROW: CLMM TickArrayS
nodes.text: the protocol's on-chain state footprint can only GROW: CLMM TickArrayState accounts (60 ticks each, lazily initialised) can never be closed and their rent is permanently locked even when no tick in them is initialised, and CPMM pools and their PDAs are never closed even at zero liquidity
nodes.note: RESIDUE — nothing names state that can only be created, and it is a design commitment with a monetary cost, not an implementation detail.

nodes.label: F15 AMM v4 retains a FOSSILISED INTERFACE for a mechanism that no longer e
nodes.text: AMM v4 retains a FOSSILISED INTERFACE for a mechanism that no longer exists: the 2026-07-22 upgrade removed the OpenBook/Serum dependency, all related CPIs and seven instructions (Initialize(0), MonitorStep(2), MigrateToOpenBook(5), WithdrawSrm(8), PreInitialize(10), SimulateInfo(12), AdminCancelOrders(13)), yet AmmInfo/StateData remain byte-compatible with inline open_orders / market / market_program fields as inert references and v1 swaps still demand 17-18 accounts of which several are never validated, with SwapBaseInV2/SwapBaseOutV2 (tags 16/17, 8 accounts) as the recommended path
nodes.note: RESIDUE — the on-chain TYPE is provably wider than the on-chain SEMANTICS, and the width is load-bearing for integrators. The corpus's residue reads 'a mechanism that exists in the bytecode but is switched off'; that is now superseded by a datable event, verified at bytecode level by stage 1: a scan of the deployed 1,406,384-byte ELF at ProgramData A7ZG7ByDi8DpzT9Ab7CiXhvgYTJQmaDPJkMDoPitaCQV found zero 'serum' strings and neither OpenBook program ID as a 32-byte constant, with the SPL Token ID present as a positive control. The residue changed register from DEAD CODE to DEAD INTERFACE, which is the harder thing to name. Ob remains correctly unused. Repo HEAD 27f461dd439086c774055f771b253fb0fbc52008, 'Remove openbook dependency (#69)'.

nodes.label: F16 LaunchLab issues a new token against a bonding curve with NO pre-seede
nodes.text: LaunchLab issues a new token against a bonding curve with NO pre-seeded liquidity, with curve_type fixed at Initialize: 0 = constant product on VIRTUAL reserves, (V_q + dq)(V_b + b_rem - b_out) = V_q*V_b, 1 = fixed price, 2 = linear price
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Cp was considered and REJECTED even for curve_type 0: Cp presumes a pool of reserves someone deposited and holds a claim on, whereas the curve here prices ISSUANCE against reserves that do not exist, with no LP and no claim. Only the contested-register Bc is near this and it is outside the 58. LaunchLab program LanMV9sAd7wArD4vJFi2qDdfnVhFxYSUg6eADduJ3uj.

nodes.label: F17 the launch GRADUATES into a pool price-continuously and permissionless
nodes.text: the launch GRADUATES into a pool price-continuously and permissionlessly: base_supply_graduation is typically 0.8 x base_supply_max with the remaining 20% seeding the pool, so the pre-graduation invariant is literally the post-graduation CPMM invariant; graduation fires when quote_vault.balance >= quote_reserve_target, and 'Graduate is permissionless' — anyone may call it — whereupon the program CPIs CPMM CreatePool, revokes the base mint authority and sets LaunchState.status to Graduated
nodes.note: RESIDUE, three separable pieces and no symbol for any: the threshold gate on a vault balance, the price-continuous handoff between two different mechanisms, and the fact that firing the transition is a PUBLIC GOOD anyone may perform. The failure mode is likewise unnameable: a curve that never reaches its threshold leaves buyers 'stuck with tokens they can only sell back to the curve (at worse prices)'.

nodes.label: F18 the graduated pool's LP is split three ways by PlatformConfig under st
nodes.text: the graduated pool's LP is split three ways by PlatformConfig under strict equality, platform_scale + creator_scale + burn_scale = 1,000,000 checked by MigrateNftInfo::check, where the leg named 'burn' routes to the Lock program with is_burn = true and the docs concede 'Despite the name, the LP tokens / position NFT are LOCKED in a program-owned escrow, not destroyed', while Burn&Earn mints a transferable Raydium Fee Key NFT carrying the perpetual right to collectFees
nodes.note: RESIDUE — a TRANSFERABLE PERPETUAL CLAIM ON A LOCKED POSITION'S FEE STREAM, which is a security manufactured out of an LP position and is neither Sh (it is not a claim on the inventory) nor Py (there is no principal leg to separate). Note also that a leg named 'burn' is an escrow: the value-return vocabulary problem (F11) recurs inside a single instruction, where even the protocol's own naming is wrong. Split parameters at https://docs.raydium.io/products/launchlab/platform-config (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F19 ecosystem farms emit rewards against escrowed LP tokens in a separate
nodes.text: ecosystem farms emit rewards against escrowed LP tokens in a separate MasterChef-style program (Farm v6, FarmqiPv5eAj3j1GMdMCMUGXqPUvmquZtMy86QH6rzhG) that escrows the LP token against PRE-FUNDED emissions and never calls the pool
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Em names PROTOCOL-FUNDED emissions, and here the reward vault is funded at farm creation, so the funder may be a third-party project rather than the protocol; the three farm programs are closed source with no IDL (F3), so the funding party could not be established at a primary source. Em is retained because RAY emissions to farms are documented, but it is the weakest member of this construction.

nodes.label: F20 every program's code can be replaced wholesale by ONE authority: all e
nodes.text: every program's code can be replaced wholesale by ONE authority: all eight queried programs use BPF Loader Upgradeable and share the single upgrade authority FytDrVzDybM1TwFQPGb8qaxZR7dBCzNeqT3vtQsceZQK, none is immutable, and the docs concede 'Raydium has not set any program's upgrade authority to null'
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and the corpus is right to mark it forced. Up names a proxy delegating to a swappable implementation; here the bytecode at the SAME ADDRESS is replaced entirely, with no delegatecall, no implementation slot, and no way for an integrator to diff what changed. RESIDUE also for the holder: the docs claim a 3/4 Squads multisig with a 24-hour timelock for upgrades and a separate 3/5 with NO timelock for treasury (which also holds program-admin powers and is described as 'an interim arrangement'), but stage 1 found the authority address to be a System-Program-owned zero-data account, consistent with a Squads vault PDA and NOT with a settings account, so the threshold and the delay are docs-only and Tg cannot be asserted. There is no on-chain token voting anywhere in Raydium.

nodes.label: F21 pools can be stopped and creation disabled by that same admin: AMM v4
nodes.text: pools can be stopped and creation disabled by that same admin: AMM v4 exposes SetParams(param=Status), CPMM exposes UpdatePoolStatus, and an AmmConfig carries disable_create_pool
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and Gp is ADDED relative to the corpus. Gp names an EMERGENCY guardian; this is a routine per-pool status word held by the same authority that sweeps protocol fees, so the emergency framing is wrong and the concentration is the risk. The 2022-12-16 exploit was executed THROUGH this surface with a compromised pool-owner key — SetParams combined with AmmParams::SyncNeedTake to inflate need_take_pc/need_take_coin, then withdrawPNL (the same instruction that collects the 12%) drained the vaults — for a loss of $4,417,202.04 across nine pairs by the protocol's own published Total Loss Per Vault.csv, against a postmortem that says eight pools. SyncNeedTake was subsequently removed. https://github.com/raydium-io/dec_16_exploit (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F22 no registry attests that any deployed program matches any published so
nodes.text: no registry attests that any deployed program matches any published source: OtterSec reports is_verified false for AMM v4, CPMM, CLMM and LaunchLab, CPMM's record carries an empty executable_hash, and the docs' stated mitigation — expected hashes per deploy in the repositories' releases — does not exist, because all three program repos have zero tags and zero releases
nodes.note: RESIDUE — VERIFIABILITY IS A PROPERTY OF THE DEPLOYMENT, NOT OF THE CODE, and the vocabulary has no way to record its absence. This is not proof of divergence, only that nothing attests to a match. It compounds F3: a construction of 'Raydium' is a construction of three published programs plus six prose descriptions, none of which is attested to be what is running.

nodes.label: Uniswap
F1 a v2 pool quotes a swap off the constant-product invariant on its own
nodes.text: a v2 pool quotes a swap off the constant-product invariant on its own two reserves: the swapper's marginal price moves monotonically against size, the LP fee is skimmed from the input, and the pair asserts that k is non-decreasing across the swap after fees
nodes.note: Cp fits exactly. THE POOL INVARIANT, first of two answers this protocol gives — the fungible-reserve answer.

nodes.label: F2 a v3 or v4 pool applies the same constant-product curve to VIRTUAL res
nodes.text: a v3 or v4 pool applies the same constant-product curve to VIRTUAL reserves inside the active tick range, carrying sqrtPriceX96, a current tick, a tick bitmap, per-tick liquidityNet/liquidityGross and a pool-level active liquidity, so that liquidity is a step function of price rather than a constant
nodes.note: THE POOL INVARIANT, second answer. Cl and Cp together are a genuinely good fit and this is the strongest case in the lane for the vocabulary's pool-pricing resolution being real: the pair states both the curve and its restriction to a range. Cross-checked against the v4 PoolKey (currency0, currency1, fee, tickSpacing, hooks) at https://github.com/Uniswap/v4-core/blob/v4.0.0/README.md (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F3 a v2 liquidity provider holds a FUNGIBLE ERC-20 LP token representing
nodes.text: a v2 liquidity provider holds a FUNGIBLE ERC-20 LP token representing a pro-rata claim on the entire reserve, redeemable at any time for its share of both assets
nodes.note: FUNGIBILITY OF THE POSITION, first answer. Sh fits exactly.

nodes.label: F4 a v3 or v4 liquidity provider instead holds a position bounded by a lo
nodes.text: a v3 or v4 liquidity provider instead holds a position bounded by a lower and an upper tick which is NOT fungible: two providers in the same pool with different ranges hold economically different instruments, and the v3 periphery wraps each position in its own ERC-721
nodes.note: RESIDUE — the per-range non-fungible instrument. FUNGIBILITY OF THE POSITION, second answer, and the vocabulary can only express the first. Cl names the curve shape and Sh names a pro-rata pool claim; neither names an individually owned position whose identity is (owner, tickLower, tickUpper). This confirms the corpus's third residue item verbatim.

nodes.label: F5 fees accrue to a v3/v4 position as the difference between a range-loca
nodes.text: fees accrue to a v3/v4 position as the difference between a range-local fee-growth index and the snapshot of that index taken when the position was opened, so the position is settled against an index rather than paid
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Ix names a GLOBAL index that changes claim value. Here feeGrowthInside is range-local, reconstructed as feeGrowthGlobal minus the outside-values recorded at both boundary ticks, so the index a position accrues against depends on the position's own bounds. Ix is ADDED relative to the corpus decomposition, which carries no accrual element for Uniswap at all.

nodes.label: F6 the LP fee is taken out of the swap INPUT and left inside the pool rat
nodes.text: the LP fee is taken out of the swap INPUT and left inside the pool rather than paid out, so a v2 provider realises it as appreciation of a fungible share and a v3/v4 provider realises it by collecting against the index
nodes.note: Both symbols discharge the accounting; neither says which leg of the trade the fee is skimmed from, which is a free parameter other protocols in this lane set differently (Curve takes stableswap fees in the output token, Raydium fixes the leg per pool at creation).

nodes.label: F7 v2 and v3 publish an ACCUMULATOR, not a price: v2 stores price0Cumulat
nodes.text: v2 and v3 publish an ACCUMULATOR, not a price: v2 stores price0CumulativeLast/price1CumulativeLast, described as 'a sum of the Uniswap price for every second in the entire history of the contract', and v3 stores a ring buffer of observations, so a consumer must read two points, difference them and divide by elapsed time to obtain a time-weighted price
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and this is THE PRICE-SERIES QUESTION. The protocol supplies the integral; the consumer performs the differentiation and chooses the window. Tp names 'on-chain time-weighted price' and therefore names the consumer's output, not the protocol's obligation. Curve answers the same question the other way (it publishes a price directly), so the accumulator/price distinction is a real axis the single symbol Tp collapses.

nodes.label: F8 v4 ships NO built-in price series at all: the observation machinery wa
nodes.text: v4 ships NO built-in price series at all: the observation machinery was removed from the core and a TWAP is now something a hook must implement
nodes.note: RESIDUE — the deliberate removal of a mechanism into third-party code. The vocabulary can record the presence of Tp and its absence, but not that the absence is a design decision that relocates the obligation to an extension point.

nodes.label: F9 in v2 and v3 settlement is per-pool: each swap moves both tokens at th
nodes.text: in v2 and v3 settlement is per-pool: each swap moves both tokens at the pool contract itself inside the transaction, so an n-hop route performs 2n token transfers and each pool must hold its own inventory
