nodes.note: RESIDUE — THE SETTLEMENT DISCIPLINE, first answer. No element in the 58 names a settlement discipline at all; it is smuggled in as an unstated assumption of the pool-pricing symbols, which is why F10 cannot be distinguished from this obligation by any construction.

nodes.label: F10 in v4 settlement is deferred and net: an integrator calls unlock, the
nodes.text: in v4 settlement is deferred and net: an integrator calls unlock, the PoolManager calls back, any number of swap / modifyLiquidity / donate / take / settle / mint / burn operations run against the singleton, signed per-currency deltas are accumulated in EIP-1153 transient storage, and the only enforced condition is that every delta is zero when the unlock is released, so only the net moves
nodes.note: RESIDUE — THE SETTLEMENT DISCIPLINE, second answer, and the corpus's second residue item confirmed at the source. Fl names borrow-and-repay in one scope and does not fit: nothing is borrowed and nothing is repaid. The repo's own statement of the invariant — 'Any number of actions can be run on the pools, as long as the deltas accumulated during the unlock reach 0 by the unlock's release' — is a CONSERVATION LAW OVER A TRANSACTION, and no symbol in the 58 states a conservation law. Delta-zero wording cross-checked at https://developers.uniswap.org/llms.mdx/docs/protocols/v4/concepts/flash-accounting (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F11 a caller may take assets out of a pool before paying for them within o
nodes.text: a caller may take assets out of a pool before paying for them within one settlement scope — v2/v3 flash swaps transfer out optimistically and call back before checking k, and v4 permits take() before settle() inside the unlock
nodes.note: Fl fits: borrow-and-repay inside one settlement scope, with the invariant check deferred to the end. This is the obligation Fl was cut for, and it is DIFFERENT from F10 — conflating them is the error the corpus's residue note warns against.

nodes.label: F12 a v4 pool may name a hook contract at initialization, and WHICH of the
nodes.text: a v4 pool may name a hook contract at initialization, and WHICH of the fourteen lifecycle callbacks fire is encoded in the low fourteen bits of that contract's ADDRESS (ALL_HOOK_MASK = (1<<14)-1), so the permission set is chosen by mining the deployment address and is frozen: 'which callbacks are executed on a pool cannot change after pool initialization'
nodes.note: RESIDUE — EXTENSION POINT, permission-binding convention #1 of three in this lane. The permission set belongs to the CODE (its address) and is therefore a property of the hook, identical across every pool that names it. Nothing in the 58 names third-party code executing inside the settlement path, and nothing names a capability vector fixed at instantiation. Contrast PancakeSwap (bitmap in the pool key) and Fluid (a controller field in the pool key).

nodes.label: F13 four of the fourteen hook bits — BEFORE_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA, AFTER_SWAP
nodes.text: four of the fourteen hook bits — BEFORE_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA, AFTER_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA, AFTER_ADD_LIQUIDITY_RETURNS_DELTA, AFTER_REMOVE_LIQUIDITY_RETURNS_DELTA — let the hook alter the accounting outcome of the operation rather than observe it, i.e. supply a custom curve in place of the pool's
nodes.note: RESIDUE — and the sharpest instance of it. This is the boundary between 'a v4 pool' and 'an arbitrary AMM wearing a v4 costume': with a RETURNS_DELTA bit set, F2's invariant is no longer the pool's invariant. Any vocabulary that acquires a hook symbol will still miss the observer/pricer distinction unless the symbol is typed. Uniswap ships docs/security/Known_Effects_of_Hook_Permissions.pdf precisely because this code is untrusted and in the settlement path.

nodes.label: F14 which curves may exist is itself a governed, MONOTONE registry: the v3
nodes.text: which curves may exist is itself a governed, MONOTONE registry: the v3 factory owner calls enableFeeAmount to add a (fee, tickSpacing) pair — seeded at 500/10, 3000/60 and 10000/200 — and a tier once added can never be removed
nodes.note: RESIDUE — a pool-parameter registry acting as a ratchet on the space of admissible pools. Tg names the delay in front of the owner, not the registry, and cannot express one-directional growth of an admissible set. The same shape recurs three times in this lane (Curve's DAO-gated implementation registry, Fluid's governance-approved pool list).

nodes.label: F15 a live parameter surface is held behind a delay: UNI holders propose a
nodes.text: a live parameter surface is held behind a delay: UNI holders propose at a 1M threshold, vote after a 2-day delay for 7 days against a 40M quorum, and execution passes a 2-day Timelock which is v2's feeToSetter, is (through the fee adapter) v3's factory owner, and is the PoolManager's Owned.owner in v4
nodes.note: DEPARTURE from the corpus marker, which reads 'the core pool contracts are immutable ... the mechanism is beyond authority'. That is too strong and stage 1 refutes it: the fee switch, the tier registry and the per-pool protocol-fee fraction are all owner-gated and all three were exercised on 2025-12-28. The accurate statement is no upgrade path, no pause, and a live owner-gated parameter surface — and Tg names only the delay, not the code/parameter split that is the actual design. Timelock 0x1a9C8182C09F50C8318d769245beA52c32BE35BC.

nodes.label: F16 there is no pause anywhere in the v4 core: PoolManager.sol and Protoco
nodes.text: there is no pause anywhere in the v4 core: PoolManager.sol and ProtocolFees.sol at tag v4.0.0 contain no occurrence of 'pause', so no party can stop a pool
nodes.note: RESIDUE — the absence is the design. Gp names the presence of a guardian or pause; the vocabulary has no way to state that an obligation is DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION because the facility deliberately does not exist. This is the options lane's stage-1 formalism finding appearing in a DEX, from the control plane rather than the solvency plane.

nodes.label: F17 since December 2025 a protocol fee is skimmed off the LP fee on all th
nodes.text: since December 2025 a protocol fee is skimmed off the LP fee on all three generations — v2 fixed in the pair at 1/6 of the swap fee (0.05% of the 0.30%), v3 at a per-tier 1/4 or 1/6, v4 resolved by an adapter — and accumulates in a per-chain immutable TokenJar exposing exactly one privileged role, a releaser that 'can atomically transfer the full balance of specified assets to a recipient'
nodes.note: RESIDUE — an immutable value sink with a single privileged role. Fd is DROPPED from this construction (see F18) and does not fit here either: accrual into a jar is not distribution to a claim class. Mainnet TokenJar 0xf38521f130fcCF29dB1961597bc5d2B60F995f85. Fee rates cross-checked at https://developers.uniswap.org/llms.mdx/docs/protocols/protocol-fee/overview (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F18 THE VALUE-RETURN CHANNEL IS SUPPLY DESTRUCTION, exercised by a third p
nodes.text: THE VALUE-RETURN CHANNEL IS SUPPLY DESTRUCTION, exercised by a third party at a fixed price: Firepit.release() takes a fixed quantity of UNI from a searcher, releases the Jar's full balance of the named assets to that searcher's recipient, and sends the UNI to 0xdead; the protocol never places a market order and never holds the bought asset
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the reason Fd is DROPPED from this construction relative to the corpus. The corpus marker calls this a 'UNI buy-and-burn' and files it with PancakeSwap and Raydium; stage 1 shows no buying happens on-protocol, and Raydium is not in this family at all (it accumulates — see raydium.json R11). Three separable things need naming and none is named: the sink (F17), the exercise (a standing, immutable, fixed-price call option on the fee inventory, exercisable by anyone, whose premium is the governance token), and the destruction. Fd names distribution to a claim class; nobody is distributed to. Mainnet Firepit 0x0D5Cd355e2aBEB8fb1552F56c965B867346d6721; architecture at https://github.com/Uniswap/protocol-fees (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F19 on OP-Stack L2s the same channel completes on another domain: a search
nodes.text: on OP-Stack L2s the same channel completes on another domain: a searcher pays bridged UNI on the L2 above a 2000 UNI threshold, the Jar releases locally, and a bridge withdrawal is queued whose effect — L1 UNI sent to 0xdead — lands only after the 7-day challenge period
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. Xf discharges only the transfer leg. RESIDUE for the shape: an economic act that begins on one domain and completes on another after a challenge window, with the two halves not atomic. Xf is ADDED relative to the corpus. A Wormhole NTT path (SyntheticNttUni) covers non-OP chains, and the chain surface includes a Robinhood-operated chain, id 4663.

nodes.label: F20 fee policy is a replaceable object held behind a non-replaceable adapt
nodes.text: fee policy is a replaceable object held behind a non-replaceable adapter: V4FeeAdapter is registered permanently as the PoolManager's protocolFeeController, while V4FeePolicy is swappable by an owner, so governance can change fee strategy without ever re-handing the PoolManager privilege
nodes.note: RESIDUE — a deliberate split of PRIVILEGE from POLICY. This is neither Up (there is no proxy and no delegatecall; a whole contract is exchanged by reference) nor Tg (the swap is not the delay). PancakeSwap's setProtocolFeeController has the same shape (pancakeswap.json P14, P21), which is why Up is dropped there too. V4FeeAdapter 0x89A5D5bF00a27D55c02951E49078a5C5771051dB, V4FeePolicy 0x1cd822b70a0591420F65E94b9B3A0D0b0fB3a314.

nodes.label: F21 the fee owed by a pool is resolved by an on-chain classifier over thir
nodes.text: the fee owed by a pool is resolved by an on-chain classifier over third-party code: the policy checks a per-pool override, else resolves a family by hookFamilyId[hook], else static-pool 255 ('native math'), else protocolFeeFlags plus flagRules, else 0, then applies pairClassFees then familyDefaults then defaultFee, with native-math pools priced on a piecewise-linear bucket schedule alpha + beta x (lpFee - floor)/1e6 capped at 16 buckets
nodes.note: RESIDUE — a governance-maintained on-chain TAXONOMY OF THIRD-PARTY CODE, keyed by hook address. Nothing in the 58 is close. Two roles govern it: owner (swap the policy, set the fee-setter) and feeSetter (everything else).

nodes.label: F22 the whole arrangement was installed in one governance act: proposal 93
nodes.text: the whole arrangement was installed in one governance act: proposal 93 executed 2025-12-28 17:55 with 125,342,017 FOR and 742 AGAINST, in eight on-chain actions including burning 100M UNI, handing v3 factory ownership to the fee controller, setting v2's feeToSetter to the Timelock and turning feeTo on, approving 40M UNI into UNIVester, and anchoring three legal agreements via AgreementAnchor
nodes.note: Tg discharges only the delayed execution of the batch. RESIDUE for two of the eight actions: a retroactive one-off supply destruction of 100M UNI, and the on-chain anchoring of an off-chain legal agreement, neither of which any symbol names.

nodes.label: 02-lending
Aave V3
F1 a supplier deposits an ERC-20 into a single shared reserve and receive
nodes.text: a supplier deposits an ERC-20 into a single shared reserve and receives a transferable claim token one-for-one, and every supplier of that reserve holds the same undifferentiated claim on it
nodes.note: Pl is exact. FLAG FOR STAGE 3: law L2 (Pl implies a claim form plus an exit-liquidity term drawn from Sl, Ad, Bs, Tr, Cv, Wq, Rd, Ps, Sv, Im, Of) is discharged on its first term by Ix and Rb at F2 and is NOT discharged on its second by anything this lane can cite. The corpus discharged it with Im, Sl and Bs; this lane drops all three (Im at F12, Bs and Sl for want of any source read in stage 1 -- the Umbrella/Safety Module contracts were not fetched and stage 1 records Bs as UNCONFIRMED, not confirmed). Aave's real exit guarantee is that a withdrawal reverts when the reserve's available liquidity is short and the rate curve then pays borrowers to repay; that is an incentive, not a mechanism, and no element names it. A resulting INADMISSIBLE verdict is a statement about the evidence base and about L2's term list, not about Aave.

nodes.label: F2 interest is capitalised into a per-reserve index recomputed on every s
nodes.text: interest is capitalised into a per-reserve index recomputed on every state-changing interaction rather than billed, and the claim token's nominal balance grows with that index so a holder's displayed balance changes without a transfer
nodes.note: Two symbols for one mechanism, and the corpus marker for Rb (FORCED) is retained and sharpened: an aToken is a scaled balance multiplied by the reserve's liquidity index, so Ix is the internal object and Rb is the external presentation of the same object. The vocabulary charges twice and has no way to state that the two symbols denote one thing viewed from two sides. Confirms the corpus residue verbatim.

nodes.label: F3 a borrower designates supplied reserves as collateral and draws an ope
nodes.text: a borrower designates supplied reserves as collateral and draws an open-ended loan from the same shared reserve, with no maturity and no schedule, recorded as a debt token that accrues by the same index mechanism
nodes.note: setUserUseReserveAsCollateral then borrow then repay. Ft is deliberately NOT emitted: there is no maturity date anywhere in the position, which is the axis on which Aave and Maple differ most and which the vocabulary does record.

nodes.label: F4 solvency is a single scalar computed on chain from the oracle value of
nodes.text: solvency is a single scalar computed on chain from the oracle value of each collateral times that asset's liquidation threshold against the oracle value of the debt, and the position is closable when the scalar falls below one
nodes.note: Ct is exact and, contrary to the corpus, first-class rather than derived: the health factor is a named quantity the protocol computes and stores intent against, not something a reader infers from other elements. The per-asset liquidation threshold and LTV are separate configuration fields (LIQUIDATION_THRESHOLD_MASK, LTV_MASK, both MAX_VALID 65535) at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/main/src/contracts/protocol/libraries/configuration/ReserveConfiguration.sol (accessed 2026-08-04); Ct names the test and not that the test has two thresholds per asset.

nodes.label: F5 a liquid-staking-token feed is wrapped in an adapter that rejects any
nodes.text: a liquid-staking-token feed is wrapped in an adapter that rejects any published value implying growth faster than a governance-set maximum yearly ratio, live example 10.64 per cent for wstETH
nodes.note: RESIDUE. maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent: 10_64 on the wstETH price cap adapter, with updateLstPriceCaps and updateStablePriceCaps as steward domains. Ex names a feed and Tp names a time-weighted price; neither reaches A PREDICATE ON THE FEED'S DERIVATIVE. This is not oracle freshness validation in the sense of L13 -- the value may be fresh and still rejected -- it is a bound on how fast a truth may move, which is the same shape as the mandate's slot 4 applied to an oracle rather than to an agent. Whether these adapters are attached to every live reserve is UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F6 a third party may repay part of a borrower's debt and seize the borrow
nodes.text: a third party may repay part of a borrower's debt and seize the borrower's collateral at a bonus, in one permissionless transaction, with no authorisation and no queue
nodes.note: Li is exact here and this is the lane's positive control for it: the clause 'third parties paid to close positions' is true in both halves, which it is not at Maple (see maple.json F13). The per-asset LIQUIDATION_BONUS_MASK is a configuration field (ReserveConfiguration.sol, accessed 2026-08-04); Li names the incentive and not that its size is a governed per-asset parameter.

nodes.label: F7 how much of a position one liquidation may take is itself a computed q
nodes.text: how much of a position one liquidation may take is itself a computed quantity: at most half the debt when the health factor is above 0.95 and both the collateral and the debt exceed 2000 units of base currency, otherwise all of it, and in no case may the call leave less than 1000 base units of either side standing
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and it re-sites a corpus residue. DEFAULT_LIQUIDATION_CLOSE_FACTOR = 0.5e4, CLOSE_FACTOR_HF_THRESHOLD = 0.95e18, MIN_BASE_MAX_CLOSE_FACTOR_THRESHOLD = 2000e8, MIN_LEFTOVER_BASE = that over two. The corpus files 'no element for the close factor' under JustLend with the gloss 'every Compound descendant has it', which implies Aave has none. Aave has one and a more elaborate one: JustLend's is a constant inside [5 per cent, 90 per cent] while Aave's is a FUNCTION OF HOW UNDERWATER THE POSITION IS AND OF ITS SIZE. Two distinct residues live in this one obligation: (a) a liquidation allowance with its own state, which Li treats as unbounded; (b) a dust floor, which is a constraint on the SHAPE of a permitted partial close and not on the incentive to perform it. The gap is category-wide with two shapes, not JustLend-specific.

nodes.label: F8 the protocol withholds a fraction of borrower interest from suppliers
nodes.text: the protocol withholds a fraction of borrower interest from suppliers and diverts a further share of the liquidator's bonus, both accruing to a treasury address
nodes.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fd), retained from the corpus and extended. The reserve factor appears in the strategy's own output as liquidityRate = borrowRate * U_s * (1 - reserveFactor); RESERVE_FACTOR_MASK and LIQUIDATION_PROTOCOL_FEE_MASK (MAX_VALID 65535 each) are both live per-reserve fields at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/main/src/contracts/protocol/libraries/configuration/ReserveConfiguration.sol (accessed 2026-08-04). DEPARTURE from the corpus, which files the liquidation protocol fee as residue: Fd does reach 'a share of a flow is routed to the protocol'. What Fd does not reach is that this particular share is CARVED OUT OF A THIRD PARTY'S INCENTIVE, so raising it weakens the liquidation guarantee -- a fee that is also a risk parameter. That much remains residue.

nodes.label: F9 anyone may borrow any amount of an enabled reserve with no collateral
nodes.text: anyone may borrow any amount of an enabled reserve with no collateral provided it is returned inside the same transaction
nodes.note: Fl is exact. The facility is per-reserve switchable: FLASHLOAN_ENABLED_MASK at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/main/src/contracts/protocol/libraries/configuration/ReserveConfiguration.sol (accessed 2026-08-04). Conditional prohibition X2 (Fl present with a manipulable pool price and Pl) is armed by construction; Aave prices from Ex rather than from a pool invariant, so the antecedent's second conjunct is not met inside this application.

nodes.label: F10 borrowing power is raised above the ordinary per-asset limits when the
nodes.text: borrowing power is raised above the ordinary per-asset limits when the collateral and the debt belong to one governance-declared category of assets expected to track each other
nodes.note: RESIDUE, confirming the corpus. setUserEMode is a user-facing Pool function (https://aave.com/docs/developers/smart-contracts/pool, accessed 2026-08-04) and updateEModeCategories is one of the steward's enumerated domains. No element names correlated-asset margin relief. Note what it is structurally: a SECOND Ct with different constants selected by a declared equivalence class over assets, and the vocabulary has one Ct with no notion of a regime.

nodes.label: F11 each reserve carries a supply cap and a borrow cap that bound aggregat
nodes.text: each reserve carries a supply cap and a borrow cap that bound aggregate exposure to the asset independently of whether any individual position is solvent
nodes.note: RESIDUE, confirming the corpus. SUPPLY_CAP_MASK and BORROW_CAP_MASK, both MAX_VALID 68719476735; updateCaps is a steward domain. A cap is a bound on a POPULATION and Ct is a test on an INDIVIDUAL, so no composition of Ct instances yields it. NEW DELTA, and it removes an element the corpus carries: the same bitmap contains NO debt-ceiling field, and its own comment records 'an unoccupied hole of 40 bits from 212 to 251 left from pre 3.7 debtCeiling'. Isolation mode's debt ceiling has been removed from the reserve configuration in the current main tree. The corpus assigns Aave Im with the marker 'FORCED ... the position stays inside the one shared pool'; on this evidence Im is not merely forced but unsupported, and it is DROPPED from the construction. Stage 3 should re-check against a pinned SHA before the paper repeats it.

nodes.label: F12 the borrow rate is a memoryless two-slope function of the reserve's cu
nodes.text: the borrow rate is a memoryless two-slope function of the reserve's current utilisation alone -- base rate, a first slope up to a kink, a steeper second slope beyond it -- and the supply rate is that borrow rate scaled by supply utilisation and by one minus the reserve factor
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and it is FINDING 1's first row. THE FUNCTIONAL FORM. Ix says an index accrues and is silent on the rate at which it accrues, which is the product. Note the property that distinguishes this row from Morpho's: the rate is a pure function of the CURRENT state, with no memory. A construction that names Ix at Aave and Ix at Morpho asserts they price credit the same way, and they do not -- one is a function, the other a controller (morpho.json F11).

nodes.label: F13 those rate parameters live in a mutable per-reserve struct that only t
nodes.text: those rate parameters live in a mutable per-reserve struct that only the pool configurator may write, and the configurator's own callers are addresses enumerated in an on-chain role registry that a default admin may add to and remove from
nodes.note: FINDING 1: THE SETTER LOCUS -- a mutable parameter inside the protocol. Aw is APPROXIMATE and this lane emits it uniformly for address-keyed administrative gates, following the corpus's own FORCED use of Aw for role structure at Morpho and the 06-yield lane's use of it for mandate slot 1. DEPARTURE: the corpus does not carry Aw for Aave. What Aw names: the call is gated by address and the gate is mutable (POOL_ADMIN_ROLE, RISK_ADMIN_ROLE, EMERGENCY_ADMIN_ROLE, FLASH_BORROWER_ROLE, BRIDGE_ROLE, ASSET_LISTING_ADMIN_ROLE over OpenZeppelin AccessControl, with add/remove per role and setRoleAdmin under onlyRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE)). What Aw does not name: that the gated thing is a DISCRETIONARY ECONOMIC AUTHORITY rather than a right to participate; and who holds each role, or how many of them there are, which stage 1 records as UNKNOWN for all five targets and the 07-bridges lane records as the party-sort gap. An architectural fact the corpus record predates: earlier Aave V3 deployed one strategy contract per reserve with immutable parameters, so this locus is itself a design that changed.

nodes.label: F14 whatever curve is written must satisfy hard bounds checked at write ti
nodes.text: whatever curve is written must satisfy hard bounds checked at write time: the sum of base rate and both slopes may not exceed 1000 per cent, the kink must lie between 1 and 99 per cent, and the first slope may never exceed the second
nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE BOUND. MAX_BORROW_RATE = 1000_00 bps, MIN_OPTIMAL_POINT = 1_00, MAX_OPTIMAL_POINT = 99_00, and the shape constraint variableRateSlope1 <= variableRateSlope2 which forbids a concave curve, all as requires in _setInterestRateParams. The corpus records Aave's rate model as residue but does not record that the rate is a BOUNDED parameter, and the bounding is the same structure as F17. Nothing in the vocabulary states 'this parameter has a permitted interval'.

nodes.label: F15 inside the strategy contract a permitted caller moves the entire curve
nodes.text: inside the strategy contract a permitted caller moves the entire curve in one transaction: there is no delay before the change takes effect and no limit on how far it may move
nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE LATENCY, at the core layer. Tg is the wrong symbol: nothing here is delayed. The delay and the step limit exist one layer up and in a different repository (F16 to F20), which is why a lane reading only aave-v3-origin would conclude Aave's rate is unbounded in time, and a lane reading only aave-v3-risk-stewards would conclude it is bounded. Both are true of different callers, and the vocabulary cannot hold two authorities over one parameter.

nodes.label: F16 a single named address, held immutably by the contract, may change ris
nodes.text: a single named address, held immutably by the contract, may change risk parameters directly without a governance vote
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 1 (named agent). Aw APPROXIMATE, same reading as F13. address public immutable RISK_COUNCIL with modifier onlyRiskCouncil reverting InvalidCaller. Two things Aw does not carry and neither does anything else. (a) THE AGENT MAY BE AN AUTOMATON: AaveStewardInjectorRates, ...Caps, ...EMode and ...DiscountRate read a recommendation from RiskOracle.sol and inject it inside the same envelope under Chainlink or Gelato automation (https://api.github.com/repos/aave-dao/aave-v3-risk-stewards/git/trees/main?recursive=1, accessed 2026-08-04), so 'named agent' must admit a machine acting on an oracle's advice. (b) MANDATE SLOT 6 (agent stake): EMPTY. The Risk Council posts no bond and is not paid by this contract; its only sanction is F20. Contrast Maple (maple.json F19), where the slot is filled and the cross-lane phrase 'accountable only reputationally' is refuted in code.

nodes.label: F17 that address may act only within an enumerated set of parameter famili
nodes.text: that address may act only within an enumerated set of parameter families -- caps, rates, the collateral side, e-mode categories, and three kinds of oracle price cap -- and any individual asset or e-mode may be fenced out of its reach entirely
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 2 (domain whitelist). RESIDUE. Three layers, all in code: (a) the only entry points that exist are updateCaps, updateRates, updateCollateralSide, updateEModeCategories, updateLstPriceCaps, updateStablePriceCaps and updatePendleDiscountRates; (b) _restrictedAddresses[asset] reverts AssetIsRestricted and _restrictedEModes[id] reverts EModeIsRestricted, both written onlyOwner; (c) the EdgeRiskStewardRates, ...Caps, ...EMode and ...DiscountRate variants exist so that a deployment can expose exactly one domain. No element restricts a delegated decision to a domain. Aw is deliberately NOT re-used here: an enumerated set of PERMITTED ACTIONS over PERMITTED SUBJECTS is not an identity gate, and stretching Aw across both would erase the distinction between who may act and what they may touch.

nodes.label: F18 each parameter carries its own maximum change per update, expressed ei
nodes.text: each parameter carries its own maximum change per update, expressed either as a percentage of the current value or as an absolute step, and an update outside that range reverts
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 3 (magnitude cap). RESIDUE. struct RiskParamConfig { uint40 minDelay; uint256 maxPercentChange; }, checked by _updateWithinAllowedRange with an isChangeRelative flag, with separate configs per family (Config{CollateralConfig, EmodeConfig, RateConfig, CapConfig, PriceCapConfig}). Ct is a solvency test, not a parameter envelope; no element expresses a numeric domain restriction on a delegated decision.

nodes.label: F19 no parameter may be moved again until a minimum interval has passed si
nodes.text: no parameter may be moved again until a minimum interval has passed since that same parameter was last moved on that same asset, each pair carrying its own timestamp
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 4 (rate-of-change limit or delay). RESIDUE. riskConfig.minDelay checked against a per-(asset, parameter) lastUpdated -- the contract keeps supplyCapLastUpdated, borrowCapLastUpdated, optimalUsageRatioLastUpdated, baseVariableRateLastUpdated, variableRateSlope1LastUpdated, variableRateSlope2LastUpdated, ltvLastUpdated, liquidationThresholdLastUpdated, liquidationBonusLastUpdated and e-mode equivalents. THE MECHANISM IS A DEBOUNCE AND Tg IS THE WRONG SYMBOL: this is a cooldown SINCE the last change, not a delay BEFORE execution, and the steward's own change is immediate. This is one of four distinct mechanisms occupying this slot across the lane -- debounce here, queue-and-accept timelock at MetaMorpho, one-sided cooldown at Spark's CapAutomator, continuously refilling token bucket at Spark's ALM. A formalism with one field called 'rate-of-change limit' conflates a limit on HOW OFTEN with a limit on HOW MUCH PER UNIT TIME.

nodes.label: F20 the principal may zero the envelope or fence any asset at any time, bu
nodes.text: the principal may zero the envelope or fence any asset at any time, but cannot remove the agent: the agent's address is fixed at deployment and this contract holds no way to change it
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 5 (revocation). RESIDUE, and it is the sharpest of the five parts here. setRiskConfig, setAddressRestricted and setEModeCategoryRestricted are all onlyOwner (the governance executor), so the owner can reduce the mandate to nothing without touching the council; but RISK_COUNCIL is immutable, so WHAT IS REVOCABLE IS THE MANDATE'S CONTENTS AND NOT ITS HOLDER. Revoking the agent means retiring the whole steward instance (or removing its role at the ACLManager, F13) -- a different act at a different contract. Aw is NOT emitted: a mutable membership set is not the claim 'a principal may withdraw a delegated economic authority', and here the membership is not even mutable. Across the corpus stage 4 has counted ZERO revocation obligations; this is one of five added by this lane.

nodes.label: F21 any reserve may be frozen or paused individually, and a distinct emerg
nodes.text: any reserve may be frozen or paused individually, and a distinct emergency role exists whose purpose is to do so
nodes.note: Gp is supported. ACTIVE_MASK, FROZEN_MASK and PAUSED_MASK are per-reserve configuration bits, and EMERGENCY_ADMIN_ROLE is a declared role at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/main/src/contracts/protocol/configuration/ACLManager.sol (accessed 2026-08-04). Gp names one halt; it does not name that there are THREE graduated states here (active, frozen -- no new positions but existing ones may be closed -- and paused), which is a lattice of degrees of stop and reads as a single boolean. Who holds the role is UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F22 the pool and its configurator sit behind admin-upgradeable proxies who
nodes.text: the pool and its configurator sit behind admin-upgradeable proxies whose implementations may be replaced by an owner the source names as the governance
nodes.note: Up is exact. setPoolImpl, setPoolConfiguratorImpl, setAddressAsProxy and _updateImpl, all external override onlyOwner over Ownable, deploying InitializableImmutableAdminUpgradeabilityProxy; the contract's own comment reads 'Owned by the Aave Governance'. Law L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is discharged by F23, subject to the caveat there. Prohibition X9 (Up with immediate single-key control) is NOT armed on this evidence and is not disarmed either: the owner's identity and quorum are UNKNOWN, which is exactly the 07-bridges lane's finding that the risk is a property of the holder and the vocabulary has no party sort.

nodes.label: F23 a governance action arrives as a payload bridged from a separate gover
nodes.text: a governance action arrives as a payload bridged from a separate governance chain, is queued on receipt, becomes executable by anyone only after a per-executor delay of between one and ten days, and expires if left unexecuted through a grace period
nodes.note: Tg and Xm both supported, and both were carried by the corpus without a source; this lane supplies one. MIN_EXECUTION_DELAY 1 day, MAX_EXECUTION_DELAY 10 days, EXPIRATION_DELAY 35 days, GRACE_PERIOD 7 days; executionTime = payload.queuedAt + payload.delay and executePayload has no caller restriction beyond state validation. Xm is warranted by the payload arriving from the governance chain, not by any user asset movement -- so Aave's cross-domain element is a CONTROL-PLANE object, which the vocabulary places in the same group as bridged value and cannot distinguish. Two things Tg does not say and both matter here: that the delay is per-executor and configurable, and that it protects only THIS path -- the steward (F16 to F20) reaches the same parameters with no delay at all.

nodes.label: JustLend V1
F1 a supplier deposits into a per-asset market and receives a token repre
nodes.text: a supplier deposits into a per-asset market and receives a token representing a pro-rata claim on it, whose redemption value rises through a growing exchange rate rather than through a growing balance
nodes.note: CErc20, CEther and CTokenERC777 in the tree; a Compound V2 fork on TRON, confirmed file-by-file across 52 Solidity files at pragma ^0.5.12. The corpus marker for Sh (FORCED) is retained and inverted in emphasis: the MECHANISM is Ix and the USER-FACING OBJECT is Sh, so the vocabulary again charges two symbols for one design -- the mirror image of Aave, where the same duality appears as Ix plus Rb (aave-v3.json F2). Three protocols in this lane express one accrual in three symbol pairs and no element says they are the same idea. FLAG FOR STAGE 3: law L2's exit-liquidity term is not discharged by any element this lane can cite; a redemption simply fails when the market has no cash, which is the same unnameable conditional exit recorded at Morpho (morpho.json F8).

nodes.label: F2 interest accrues into a per-market borrow index that is advanced every
nodes.text: interest accrues into a per-market borrow index that is advanced every block a transaction touches the market
nodes.note: Ix is exact -- borrowIndex is an explicit named accumulator, more literally Ix than either Morpho's totals or Maple's per-loan accounting.

nodes.label: F3 the rate is quoted and accrued per block rather than per second or per
nodes.text: the rate is quoted and accrued per block rather than per second or per year, with a hard-coded 10,512,000 blocks per year matching a three-second chain, so the realised annual rate depends on how fast the chain produces blocks
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a kind of gap no other target in the lane exhibits. blocksPerYear = 10_512_000 is the TRON adaptation of Compound's Ethereum constant. A CONSENSUS PROPERTY LEAKS INTO A CREDIT PARAMETER: if block production drifts, every quoted rate in the protocol is wrong by the same factor, and the fix is a redeployment. No element in the vocabulary touches block time, and the four other targets in this lane all denominate in seconds or years, so the vocabulary records five rate mechanisms with one time base when they have two.

nodes.label: F4 a borrower enters markets explicitly and a controller contract compute
nodes.text: a borrower enters markets explicitly and a controller contract computes account liquidity from each entered collateral's collateral factor against the value of every borrow, refusing any action that would leave a shortfall
nodes.note: Ct is exact and first-class, not derived. One threshold per asset (collateralFactorMantissa), so as at Morpho and unlike Compound V3 there is no separate opening and closing line.

nodes.label: F5 collateral and debt are valued by a push oracle whose price is written
nodes.text: collateral and debt are valued by a push oracle whose price is written by a permitted party rather than pulled from a feed
nodes.note: Ex APPROXIMATE. The tree carries PriceOracle.sol, PriceOracleProxy.sol, PriceOracle/PriceOracleV1.sol, PriceOracle/DSValue.sol and SimplePriceOracle.sol; DSValue is a Maker-lineage SINGLE-WRITER PUSH oracle, which is a materially different trust object from a medianised feed, and WHICH OF THE FIVE IS LIVE IS UNKNOWN. Ex bundles push, pull and medianizer into one symbol, so a protocol whose price is one address's assertion and a protocol whose price is an aggregate of many reporters decompose identically -- the 07-bridges lane's party-sort gap, here on the truth axis rather than the control axis. Law L13 (Ex implies freshness validation) is NOT evidenced.

nodes.label: F6 a liquidator repays part of an underwater borrow and seizes collateral
nodes.text: a liquidator repays part of an underwater borrow and seizes collateral worth the repayment times a multiplicative premium, priced from the same oracle
nodes.note: Li is exact. Seize amount = repayAmount * liquidationIncentive * priceBorrowed / priceCollateral, the Compound-family form.

nodes.label: F7 one liquidation may repay at most a fixed fraction of the outstanding

The corpus files this residue under JustLend with the gloss 'every Compound descendant has it', which reads as though it were JustLend-specific and as though Aave lacked one. IT IS CATEGORY-WIDE WITH TWO DISTINCT SHAPES: JustLend's close factor is a CONSTANT, Aave's is a FUNCTION of health factor and position size (aave-v3.json F7), and Morpho's liquidation incentive is a FUNCTION of the market's loan-to-value (morpho.json F6). A multiplicative seize premium with an explicit permitted interval has no symbol, and neither does a permitted interval on any other governed parameter. Note especially the SPLIT this protocol makes and the corpus does not record: RISK parameters are bounded here while RATE parameters are not bounded at all (F11). A vocabulary that cannot see either bound cannot see that a protocol drew the line between them.

nodes.label: F9 the borrow rate is a memoryless two-slope jump-rate function of curren

nodes.text: the whole rate curve -- base rate, both multipliers and the kink -- may be rewritten in one call by a single owner address, guarded by exactly one equality check

That is the 07-bridges lane's finding -- QUORUM VERSUS SINGLE KEY, not delay versus upgrade -- reproduced in lending. WHETHER THE OWNER IS ACTUALLY THE TIMELOCK ON THE LIVE TRON DEPLOYMENT IS UNKNOWN: the file's comments say so and no on-chain read was performed in this run.

nodes.label: F11 nothing bounds what that curve may become: there is no maximum rate, n

nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE BOUND -- NONE, the fifth and last distinct answer in this lane after Aave's parameter bounds, Morpho's output clamp, SparkLend's inherited bound and Maple's absence of any instrument. This is the entire risk statement about JustLend's rate and it is invisible: the vocabulary can record that Tg is present and cannot record that THE TIMELOCK IS THE ONLY PROTECTION. An absent bound and a present bound produce the same decomposition, which is the strongest single argument in the lane for a bound-valued field rather than a new element. Prohibition X16 (unbounded delegated authority) is arguably armed here in a way the corpus does not record.

nodes.label: F12 the only protection on that rewrite is timing: the owner is a delay co
nodes.text: the only protection on that rewrite is timing: the owner is a delay contract, so the change is visible before it can take effect

Tg is emitted on the presence of Timelock.sol in the tree together with the rate model's own comment identifying the owner as 'the Timelock contract, which can update parameters directly'. THE DELAY'S VALUE WAS NOT READ AND THE LIVE OWNERSHIP WAS NOT VERIFIED. nodes.label: F13 every risk and every rate parameter in the protocol is set directly by
nodes.text: every risk and every rate parameter in the protocol is set directly by one administrative address, with no per-parameter envelope, no step limit, no cooldown and no delegate of any kind
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and this obligation is the LANE'S CONTROL. MANDATE ABSENT: zero of the five parts. No curator, no steward, no keeper, no bounded operator; _setCloseFactor and its siblings are guarded by msg.sender != admin and nothing more. Its importance is chronological. Aave's RiskSteward, MetaMorpho's curator, SparkLend's CapAutomator and SparkLend's ALM RateLimits are ALL in separate repositories from their protocol cores and are ALL later than the code they bound; JustLend is a 2020-era Compound V2 fork at pragma ^0.5.12 and has none. THE BOUNDED DELEGATE MANDATE IS NOT A LENDING PRIMITIVE -- IT IS A LAYER THAT GREW ON TOP OF LENDING PRIMITIVES, and its absence from a 58-element vocabulary is a vintage problem rather than an oversight. One protocol in five having none is also what makes the other five instances measurable rather than universal.

nodes.label: F14 the controller and every individual market sit behind delegate-call pr

Law L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is discharged by F12, with the same UNKNOWN attached.

nodes.label: F18 no contract in this repository rents chain execution resources, so the
nodes.text: no contract in this repository rents chain execution resources, so the resource-rental business the corpus attributes to this protocol is not part of the artefact decomposed here
nodes.note: RESIDUE, recorded as UNCONFIRMED IN-REPO rather than refuted. IF IT IS REAL the corpus's own gloss is the right one and worth carrying: it would be Pl over a NON-FUNGIBLE PER-ACCOUNT EXECUTION ALLOWANCE, and Pl assumes the lent thing is fungible value. A REPRODUCTION CONSTRAINT belongs on this record too: the repository declares NO LICENCE AT ALL (https://api.github.com/repos/justlend/justlend-protocol, accessed 2026-08-04, license null), where Compound V2's own code is BSD-3-Clause, so under default copyright there is no grant of reproduction rights and no JustLend source may be quoted in the paper. That is the same class of constraint the 01-spot-exchange lane found at Curve.

nodes.label: Maple
F1 a lender deposits a single asset into a pool contract implementing the

CROSS-LANE NOTE: this application is decomposed twice in the run. 09-rwa/02-decomp/maple-finance.json decomposes Maple Finance from published documentation and live measurement; this file decomposes it from repository source. Where they disagree the disagreement is recorded rather than reconciled -- see F12.

nodes.label: F3 the money is lent as dated loan contracts with a payment schedule, a g

RESIDUE INSIDE A NAMED OBLIGATION, agreeing with the 09-rwa lane: the LENDER's claim is perpetual and open-ended while the ASSET is dated, and the maturity mismatch between the two sides is the actual mechanism -- it is why F15 exists -- and no element states it.

nodes.label: F4 a loan may require the borrower to post collateral into the loan contr
nodes.text: a loan may require the borrower to post collateral into the loan contract itself, recorded as a required amount against a delivered amount
nodes.note: Ct FORCED, and the corpus marker is retained with its reason sharpened. _collateralRequired and _collateral are loan fields, so a threshold exists on chain; what does not exist on chain is the MONITORING -- there is no oracle in the pool layer (F25) and the 09-rwa lane established that the margin call is computed and issued off chain by the delegate's operations team. Ct names an on-chain margin computation and here the computation is a drawdown check, not a solvency test. DEPARTURE: Uc is DROPPED. The corpus carries it FORCED 'in the other direction', and the 09-rwa lane measured the book at 147.72 per cent collateralisation, so emitting Uc asserts something false about the loans while law L3's warrants would then demand a structure Maple does not have. The identity, underwriting and recourse dimension that Uc bundles is real and is residue at F6 and F26.

nodes.label: F5 the price of credit is a term of a bilateral contract, not an output o
nodes.text: the price of credit is a term of a bilateral contract, not an output of the protocol: a fixed annualised rate written into the loan at origination, alongside a closing rate, a late-fee rate and a premium that raises the interest rate once a payment is overdue past the grace period
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and FINDING 1's fifth row -- the one the CDP lane never saw. THE FUNCTIONAL FORM IS A BOND INDENTURE: _interestRate ('The annualized interest rate of the loan'), _closingRate, _lateFeeRate, _lateInterestPremiumRate, on a _paymentInterval schedule with _gracePeriod and _endingPrincipal. No utilisation curve exists anywhere in the pool layer, and MaplePoolManager holds no rate parameter at all -- the only rate-like quantity it carries is the fee at F16. Two residues in one object. (a) A PRICE DETERMINED OUTSIDE THE PROTOCOL AND MERELY STORED: every other target in this lane has a curve, Maple has a negotiation, and the vocabulary cannot record that a quantity is not the protocol's. (b) A STATE-DEPENDENT PENALTY RATE: the rate a borrower pays depends on whether they are late, so the instrument has two regimes and the vocabulary has no rate at all, let alone two.

nodes.label: F6 the rate is agreed by the delegate and the borrower, and a loan cannot
nodes.text: the rate is agreed by the delegate and the borrower, and a loan cannot be funded until the borrower has accepted the terms
nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE SETTER LOCUS -- A COUNTERPARTY, the fifth of five distinct loci in this lane and one no in-protocol repair can reach. _loanTermsAccepted gates funding; _borrower, _lender, _pendingBorrower and _pendingLender make BOTH SIDES NAMED AND TRANSFERABLE. This is not the CDP lane's borrower-chosen rate: a rate one party POSTS is a unilateral offer, a rate two parties AGREE is a contract, and the difference is exactly the acceptance flag. Who proposes the number and by what process is UNKNOWN -- MapleLoan.sol and MapleLoanInitializer.sol were not read, and the 09-rwa lane found only that it is 'determined by the loan terms set by Maple's credit underwriting and risk management', which is a description of an off-chain committee.

nodes.label: F7 nothing in the loan contract bounds that rate: there is no maximum, no
nodes.text: nothing in the loan contract bounds that rate: there is no maximum, no minimum and no permitted interval on any of the four rate fields
nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE BOUND -- NONE, as at JustLend, and for an entirely different reason: JustLend leaves a governed parameter unbounded, Maple has no governed parameter to bound because the number is a contractual term. TWO PROTOCOLS WITH NO BOUND AND NOTHING IN COMMON, which is precisely what a single boolean 'bounded' field would flatten.

nodes.label: F8 the rate does not move until both parties agree a new one: a change of
nodes.text: the rate does not move until both parties agree a new one: a change of terms is proposed as a hash commitment and takes effect only when the counterparty accepts it
nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE LATENCY -- BILATERAL CONSENT. _refinanceCommitment holds the keccak256 of proposed terms and _refinanceInterest the interest accrued to the switch; maple-core-v2 ships a RefinanceScenario end-to-end test (https://api.github.com/repos/maple-labs/maple-core-v2/git/trees/main?recursive=1, accessed 2026-08-04). Tg is wrong (no delay), Ep is wrong (no period), Sv is wrong (a refinance is not a determination). A COMMIT-THEN-ACCEPT PROTOCOL BETWEEN TWO NAMED PARTIES over the terms of an existing obligation has no symbol, and it is the same queue-and-accept shape as MetaMorpho's cap increase (morpho.json F20) with the acceptor being a counterparty instead of the clock.

nodes.label: F9 closing a bad loan is an authorised act by a named party rather than a
nodes.text: closing a bad loan is an authorised act by a named party rather than a race: the delegate or a protocol admin triggers a default, no third party is paid to do it, and the process may span several transactions and be finished later by a second authorised call
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and Li is REFUTED IN BOTH CLAUSES OF ITS OWN DEFINITION. triggerDefault(loan_, liquidatorFactory_) is onlyPoolDelegateOrProtocolAdmins and requires isInstanceOf('LIQUIDATOR_FACTORY', liquidatorFactory_); it may return with liquidationComplete_ == false, emitting CollateralLiquidationTriggered, and be closed later by finishCollateralLiquidation, also onlyPoolDelegateOrProtocolAdmins. Li reads 'third parties paid to close positions': there is no third party and there is no payment. The corpus marks Li FORCED for Maple; the source supports something stronger than forced. This is the 10-options lane's DISCHARGE BY CONSTRUCTION in mirror image -- not an obligation closed by construction, but an element ASSERTED WHERE THE MECHANISM IS ABSENT -- and it is very likely the whole of why the corpus records satisfiesRequirementsAndWarrants false for Maple. With Li dropped, law L1d is discharged by Bs and Sl at F12 instead.

nodes.label: F10 whether a loan has defaulted, and when, is a judgement the delegate ma
nodes.text: whether a loan has defaulted, and when, is a judgement the delegate makes and executes
nodes.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Sv), and this is its INTENDED sense -- servicing and determination discretion over a loan -- which is why it fits here and does not fit the Morpho curator (morpho.json F24), where the corpus emits it over an allocation decision. Sv covers the determination. It does not cover that the determination is conditioned on the delegate's own stake (F13), and the 09-rwa lane found a further power at the same object that Sv also misses: a reversible provisional impairment that immediately reduces what an exiting lender receives, used explicitly to discourage exit.

nodes.label: F11 the delegate may act only through instances the protocol registry reco
nodes.text: the delegate may act only through instances the protocol registry recognises by kind -- a strategy, a liquidator factory, a withdrawal manager, a permission manager -- rather than through an enumerated list of addresses
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 2 (domain whitelist). RESIDUE. isStrategy[msg.sender] plus IGlobalsLike(globals()).isInstanceOf('STRATEGY_FACTORY' / 'LIQUIDATOR_FACTORY' / 'WITHDRAWAL_MANAGER_FACTORY' / 'POOL_PERMISSION_MANAGER', x). A WHITELIST BY TYPE RATHER THAN BY ADDRESS is a distinct object from the four other domain mechanisms in this lane, all of which enumerate: it is open-ended forward in time, since any future instance of a registered kind is automatically in the domain. Aw names an identity gate over users and cannot express a gate over KINDS, and a schema whose domain field is a set of addresses cannot hold a set whose membership is decided by a registry elsewhere.

nodes.label: F12 a loss draws down the delegate's own posted capital first, up to a gov
nodes.text: a loss draws down the delegate's own posted capital first, up to a governed fraction of it, splitting the proceeds between the protocol treasury and the pool, and whatever remains is a straight reduction of the pool's assets borne by every remaining lender
nodes.note: Bs and Sl, both DEPARTURES from the corpus, which carries neither for Maple. _handleCover(losses_, platformFees_) draws from poolDelegateCover up to balanceOf(poolDelegateCover) * maxCoverLiquidationPercent / HUNDRED_PERCENT. Bs is 'slashable first-loss capital' and MaplePoolDelegateCover is exactly that, with the loss waterfall in code. CROSS-LANE CONFLICT, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED, AND IT MATTERS FOR THE STAKE FINDING: 09-rwa/02-decomp/maple-finance.json F8 REFUTES and DROPS Bs on documentation evidence -- Maple's own docs head the section 'First-Loss Capital (Unused)', noting the cover is unused because most pools are managed by Maple Direct, and stSYRUP was never slashable. The two lanes are looking at different things and both are right: THE MECHANISM IS PRESENT AND ENFORCED IN CODE, AND ITS LIVE BALANCE MAY BE ZERO. This lane performed no on-chain read, so the value of minCoverAmount on any live pool is UNKNOWN. Stage 3 should treat Bs here as CODE-LEVEL and stage 6 must not write that Maple's delegate is bonded in practice without a live figure. Sl is straightforward and is the only unconditional loss-absorption mechanism the protocol has.

nodes.label: F13 the delegate cannot originate a loan while its own posted capital is b
nodes.text: the delegate cannot originate a loan while its own posted capital is below the protocol's floor, and cannot withdraw that capital below the same floor
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 6 (agent stake): FILLED -- the only one of the five instances in this lane, and the refutation the lane brief asks to carry. requestFunds requires the caller be a registered STRATEGY_FACTORY instance with isStrategy[msg.sender], that pool supply be non-zero, and _hasSufficientCover(globals, asset); withdrawCover asserts balanceOf(poolDelegateCover) >= globals.minCoverAmount(this). THE CROSS-LANE CHARACTERISATION 'ACCOUNTABLE ONLY REPUTATIONALLY' IS FALSE HERE AND FALSE IN CODE: at Aave, Morpho and both SparkLend instances the agent is unbonded and the only sanction is revocation; here the sanction is financial, automatic, and prior -- the authority does not exist while the stake is short. RESIDUE, and the residue is the COUPLING rather than either half: Bs names the capital (F12) and Sv names the discretion (F10), and neither carries AUTHORITY WHOSE PRECONDITION IS STAKE. The schema needs a sixth slot whose default value is empty, and 'reputational' should be read as that default rather than as part of the definition. Live enforcement is subject to the caveat at F12.

nodes.label: F14 a named delegate holds the pool's origination, default, servicing and
nodes.text: a named delegate holds the pool's origination, default, servicing and refinancing authority, and succession is a two-step handover the delegate or a protocol admin may begin
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 1 (named agent), the fifth instance in this lane counting SparkLend's two. Aw APPROXIMATE, uniform reading (see aave-v3.json F13). poolDelegate with onlyPoolDelegate and onlyPoolDelegateOrProtocolAdmins; setPendingPoolDelegate then acceptPoolDelegate. Note what is bounded here that is bounded nowhere else in the lane: ORIGINATION -- the act of creating an asset -- rather than a parameter, an allocation or a transfer. Six different bounded quantities across five instances in one category is the evidence that this is a schema over elements and not an element.

nodes.label: F15 a lender leaves through a queue rather than on demand, and a loan may
nodes.text: a lender leaves through a queue rather than on demand, and a loan may not be funded if doing so would leave the pool unable to serve the exits already queued
nodes.note: Wq is exact. The org ships both a queue and a cyclical implementation (withdrawal-manager-queue, withdrawal-manager-cyclical), so WHICH SEMANTICS A GIVEN POOL HAS IS A DEPLOYMENT CHOICE and Wq names only one of the two -- the cyclical variant is window-based and closer to Ep, a distinction the 09-rwa lane drew against Centrifuge and which one symbol cannot hold. requestFunds additionally enforces balanceOf(pool) >= lockedLiquidity_ after the transfer, which is the queue REACHING BACK INTO THE ORIGINATION DECISION: the exit mechanism is also a constraint on the mandate, and nothing composes the two.

nodes.label: F16 the pool charges a management fee to its operator's account, bounded b
nodes.text: the pool charges a management fee to its operator's account, bounded by a hundred per cent at four-decimal precision, and after configuration it is the protocol's admins and not the operator who set it
nodes.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fd). setDelegateManagementFeeRate is onlyProtocolAdminsOrNotConfigured, bounded by HUNDRED_PERCENT = 100_0000. CORRECTION OF FACT to the corpus, whose residue reads 'no element for management and performance fees charged on a lending pool BY ITS OPERATOR': the residue stands -- no element names the fee as the price of a mandate -- and the implied agency does not. THE OPERATOR DOES NOT SET ITS OWN FEE. The identical correction lands at MetaMorpho (morpho.json F24), where setFee is onlyOwner and not the curator, so in both protocols the delegate's compensation is the principal's decision, and a schema field 'performance fee' must record WHO SETS IT, not merely that it exists. The 09-rwa lane measured delegateManagementFeeRate() = 0 on the flagship syrupUSDC pool, so the flow may currently be zero.

nodes.label: F17 the pool has a maximum size it may accept, and after configuration it
nodes.text: the pool has a maximum size it may accept, and after configuration it is the protocol's admins and not the delegate who set it
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 3 (magnitude cap). RESIDUE, and the slot is filled ODDLY: setLiquidityCap is onlyProtocolAdminsOrNotConfigured, so the cap exists and the agent does not choose it, which is what a mandate should look like and is not what the corpus assumed. It is also a cap on the POOL rather than on any exposure inside it: there is no per-borrower concentration limit anywhere in the pool manager, the globals or the documentation, which the 09-rwa lane confirmed independently. The magnitude slot is therefore satisfied at the wrong granularity -- the mandate bounds how much money the agent may be given and not how much of it may go to one place -- and a schema with one cap field cannot record that mismatch.

nodes.label: F18 nothing limits how fast the delegate may lend: within the cap it may o
nodes.text: nothing limits how fast the delegate may lend: within the cap it may originate at will, with no cooldown, no step limit and no throughput budget
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 4 (rate-of-change limit or delay): ABSENT for the bounded quantity. This is the ONLY one of the five instances in this lane where the fourth slot is empty over the thing the agent actually does. A delay exists at this contract but over a different act -- the delegate may call upgrade solely through globals.isValidScheduledCall(sender, this, 'PM:UPGRADE', msg.data), which is F23 -- and withdrawals are separately queued (F15), which bounds the pool's outflow and not the delegate's origination. Recording this instance as 'has a delay' because a delay exists somewhere in the contract would be the error the schema most invites.

nodes.label: F19 the protocol's admins may replace the delegate, the registry alone may
nodes.text: the protocol's admins may replace the delegate, the registry alone may deactivate the pool, and every function in the pool manager stops while the protocol is paused
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 5 (revocation). RESIDUE, on the same reading applied at all five instances. setPendingPoolDelegate is onlyPoolDelegateOrProtocolAdmins so the admins can begin a replacement; setActive requires msg.sender == globals(); every function carries whenNotPaused; and securityAdmin can force an upgrade past the delegate. THREE DIFFERENT REVOCATIONS OF THREE DIFFERENT SCOPES live here -- replace the agent, deactivate the mandate's object, halt everything -- and the schema has one field. Gp is emitted for the pause at F23 and is not emitted for the revocation: a halt suspends an authority and a replacement ends it, and only one of them returns the principal's money.

nodes.label: F20 several powers exist only until the pool is configured and then move t
nodes.text: several powers exist only until the pool is configured and then move to a different party or vanish
nodes.note: RESIDUE. onlyIfNotConfigured (setWithdrawalManager) and onlyProtocolAdminsOrNotConfigured (setLiquidityCap, setDelegateManagementFeeRate, setPoolPermissionManager). A PERMISSION THAT EXPIRES AT A LIFECYCLE BOUNDARY has no symbol: Ep names an epoch-gated TRANSITION, not an epoch-gated AUTHORITY, and Aw is a state predicate with no time index. This is why F16 and F17 read as they do -- the delegate DID set its own fee and its own cap, once, before completeConfiguration, and never again -- so a decomposition that reports the steady state misdescribes the protocol's history, and one that reports the initial state misdescribes its present.

nodes.label: F21 there is no permissionless action anywhere on the credit side of this
nodes.text: there is no permissionless action anywhere on the credit side of this protocol: depositing is gated, originating is delegated, defaulting is authorised, and the only act anyone may take unbidden is to leave, which is queued
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and it is the most useful single sentence about how Maple differs from the other four. Every element in this construction is also carried by protocols where the corresponding act is open to anyone, so the construction cannot state the property that most determines what a Maple lender owns. The category's own defining question -- how do you let anonymous strangers borrow with no underwriting and no recourse -- IS NOT THE QUESTION THIS PROTOCOL ANSWERS, and a vocabulary calibrated on that question resolves Maple to roughly the same string as protocols that do answer it.

nodes.label: F22 no price source exists in the pool layer at all: the pool manager hold
nodes.text: no price source exists in the pool layer at all: the pool manager holds no oracle, and where the secured book's collateral is valued is not established on chain
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE: the corpus carries Ex for Maple and this lane drops it. Law L1a (a credit element implies a truth element) therefore has an OPEN TERM at Maple, which is a true statement about the protocol and not an artefact -- valuation is a human act performed off chain, and the 09-rwa lane established from documentation that an operations team watches feeds and issues margin calls by agreement. The vocabulary has no way to record SOLVENCY ACCOUNTED ON CHAIN AND ENFORCED OFF CHAIN, so the honest decomposition leaves the term open and the checker will read that as incompleteness. Also unreachable from source and left UNKNOWN rather than asserted: custodian identities, the governing law of the loan agreements, and any perfected security interest -- all four corpus residues in that family stand, and none of them is reachable from code, which is itself the finding.

nodes.label: F23 the pool's contracts may be upgraded, by the delegate only through a c
nodes.text: the pool's contracts may be upgraded, by the delegate only through a call the registry has scheduled in advance and otherwise by a security administrator directly, and the whole protocol can be paused from one registry
nodes.note: All three supported. upgrade is gated by globals_.isValidScheduledCall(..., 'PM:UPGRADE', msg.data) for the delegate and by globals_.securityAdmin() otherwise; setImplementation requires msg.sender == _factory(); whenNotPaused is protocol-wide from MapleGlobals. Law L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is discharged NOMINALLY ONLY: the 09-rwa lane established from Maple's own documentation that timelock parameters are set by the Governor, can be changed at any time, and take RETROACTIVE effect on calls already scheduled, so a pending scheduled call becomes immediately executable the moment the Governor shortens the delay. Tg asserts delayed execution and cannot express A DELAY THE DELAYED PARTY CONTROLS, so the symbol reads as a protection that is nominal. THE GOVERNOR, SECURITY ADMIN AND OPERATIONAL ADMIN KEYS ARE UNKNOWN -- no on-chain read was performed, the same gap recorded for all five targets. LICENCE, a reproduction constraint on the paper: the GitHub API reports NOASSERTION across the product because the licence files are custom, and reading the source resolves it -- MapleLoanStorage.sol carries SPDX-License-Identifier BUSL-1.1, so the loan core is not open source and may not be reproduced in atlas.tex. Repo metadata alone gets this wrong; the SPDX header is the authority.

nodes.label: Morpho
F1 credit is organised as many independent markets inside one contract, e
nodes.text: credit is organised as many independent markets inside one contract, each fixed at creation by five parameters -- loan asset, collateral asset, oracle, interest-rate model and liquidation loan-to-value -- with no netting between them, so a bad debt in one market cannot reach another
nodes.note: Im is exact and it is the design claim rather than a fence bolted onto a shared pool, which is what distinguishes it from the corpus's FORCED Im at Aave and SparkLend. SCOPE NOTE for the whole file: Morpho is two layers and they must not be conflated. F1 to F16 are Morpho Blue, the singleton primitive; F17 to F24 are Morpho Vaults (MetaMorpho), where most depositor capital actually sits. Elements true of one layer are routinely false of the other -- see F15 and F24 -- and the corpus record does not separate them.

nodes.label: F2 anyone may create a market from any combination whose interest-rate mo
nodes.text: anyone may create a market from any combination whose interest-rate model and loan-to-value are on governance's enabled lists, and nobody may edit it afterwards
nodes.note: RESIDUE, confirming the corpus. Im names the fence and says nothing about who may build one. A PERMISSIONLESS FACTORY OVER A FROZEN TEMPLATE is a different object from either a governed market list or an open pool: the template's degrees of freedom are governance's, the instantiation is anyone's, and the result is immutable. Aw is deliberately not emitted -- createMarket has no caller gate at all, so what would be gated is the SHAPE of the argument, not the identity of the caller.

nodes.label: F3 a lender supplies to a chosen market and receives shares of that marke
nodes.text: a lender supplies to a chosen market and receives shares of that market alone, whose value rises as accrued interest is added to that market's totals against a share supply that does not change
nodes.note: The corpus marker for Pl (FORCED) is retained: each market IS a shared pool of many lenders in one asset, so Pl is literally true, while the protocol's entire design claim is that it is not pooled. Emitting Im and Pl together states the fact and loses the claim, and the vocabulary offers no way to say 'pooled within a fence'. Ix is APPROXIMATE: the accrual is implemented as growth of totalSupplyAssets against fixed totalSupplyShares rather than as a published global index object, so what Ix names here is the effect, not the artefact. DEPARTURE: the corpus carries Fl for Morpho; stage 1 read Morpho.sol and recorded no flash-loan facility, so this lane declines to assert it and DROPS Fl. If Morpho.flashLoan exists on a pinned SHA, stage 3 should restore it -- an element restored on evidence is a better outcome than one carried on memory.

nodes.label: F4 a borrower posts the market's collateral asset and every borrow and wi
nodes.text: a borrower posts the market's collateral asset and every borrow and withdrawal is checked against that market's single fixed loan-to-value using the price reported by the oracle address named at the market's creation
nodes.note: Ct is exact (_isHealthy) and, as at Aave, first-class rather than derived. One threshold, not two: Morpho has no separate borrow-side and liquidation-side factor, so a position is opened and closed at the same line, which Ct cannot distinguish from Aave's two-threshold arrangement or from Compound V3's. enableLltv requires lltv < WAD, the only validation governance performs on the number.

nodes.label: F5 the protocol checks nothing whatever about that oracle -- not its sour
nodes.text: the protocol checks nothing whatever about that oracle -- not its source, not its decimals, not its liveness -- and the address can never be changed for the life of the market
nodes.note: RESIDUE, confirming the corpus. Ex names a feed. It cannot say 'the feed is whatever the market creator wrote and the protocol never looks at it', and it cannot say the choice is irrevocable. Law L13 (Ex implies freshness validation, Gp preferred for high-value obligations) is NOT discharged at the protocol layer and CANNOT BE, by design: there is no pause (F15) and no validation. The risk is relocated rather than removed -- it lands on the curator's whitelist (F20), which is the only filter in the system and is unverifiable on chain.

nodes.label: F6 a liquidator repays an unhealthy position's debt and seizes collateral
nodes.text: a liquidator repays an unhealthy position's debt and seizes collateral at an incentive the protocol computes from that market's own loan-to-value rather than accepting as a parameter, hard-capped at 1.15 times
nodes.note: Li is exact on the incentive. RESIDUE INSIDE A NAMED OBLIGATION: LIQUIDATION_CURSOR = 0.3e18 and MAX_LIQUIDATION_INCENTIVE_FACTOR = 1.15e18 make the bonus A FUNCTION OF THE LLTV, so a market creator who picks a loan-to-value has thereby picked a liquidation bonus and cannot pick them independently. Li treats the incentive as given. This is the third distinct shape of the liquidation-allowance gap in this lane -- Aave computes the close factor from health and size, JustLend fixes it as a constant in an interval, Morpho derives the bonus from the LLTV -- and one residue line covers all three in the corpus.

nodes.label: F7 a debt that survives liquidation with no collateral behind it is writt
nodes.text: a debt that survives liquidation with no collateral behind it is written down against that market's own suppliers and cannot touch any other market
nodes.note: Sl names the allocation of a loss to a claim class; Im names the boundary of that class. What neither names is that the boundary is the LOSS-CONTAINMENT DESIGN rather than a risk-management preference -- isolation here exists so that socialisation has a small and knowable domain, and the two symbols are emitted independently as though they were unrelated facts about the protocol.

nodes.label: F8 a borrow or a withdrawal is refused whenever it would leave the market
nodes.text: a borrow or a withdrawal is refused whenever it would leave the market's borrowed assets above its supplied assets, and that is the whole of a lender's exit guarantee -- there is no queue, no ordering, no buffer and no reserve
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and it names the open term in law L2 (Pl implies a claim form plus exit liquidity). Wq is wrong -- there is no queue and no order. Rd is wrong -- redemption is not guaranteed at par or at all. What the protocol actually offers is a SOLVENCY-PRESERVING REFUSAL: the invariant totalBorrowAssets <= totalSupplyAssets, enforced on both borrow and withdraw, which protects the accounting and gives the lender no timing guarantee at all. No element expresses 'the exit right is conditional on someone else's behaviour, with no mechanism to make it happen'.

nodes.label: F9 the borrow rate is produced by a closed-loop controller: a static curv
nodes.text: the borrow rate is produced by a closed-loop controller: a static curve of steepness four around a target rate, and that target rate itself drifts continuously toward whatever level drives utilisation to ninety per cent
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and FINDING 1's second row and its most consequential distinction. CURVE_STEEPNESS 4 ether, TARGET_UTILIZATION 0.9 ether, ADJUSTMENT_SPEED 50 ether / 365 days, INITIAL_RATE_AT_TARGET 0.04 ether / 365 days (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/morpho-org/morpho-blue-irm/main/src/adaptive-curve-irm/libraries/ConstantsLib.sol, accessed 2026-08-04). THE FUNCTIONAL FORM IS A CONTROLLER, NOT A FUNCTION: Aave, SparkLend and JustLend price from CURRENT utilisation and are memoryless; Morpho prices from the HISTORY of utilisation through a stateful rateAtTarget that compounds at ADJUSTMENT_SPEED times the normalised utilisation error per second. Ix cannot distinguish a memoryless price from a stateful one and the difference is the whole design. The CDP lane found a closed-loop controller on PEG error; this is the same shape on UTILISATION error, which shows the controller is not specific to stablecoins.

nodes.label: F10 no party may change any parameter of that controller: the steepness, t
nodes.text: no party may change any parameter of that controller: the steepness, the target, the adjustment speed and the bounds are compile-time constants in a contract with no setter and no admin
nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE SETTER LOCUS -- a compile-time constant, and this is the only one of the five loci in the lane where the answer is NOBODY. Not the owner, not the market creator, not the curator. This is a different risk object from Aave's mutable-parameter-with-bounds and from JustLend's mutable-parameter-with-no-bounds, and all three decompose to the same Ix. The vocabulary cannot record the absence of an authority as a positive property, which is the same defect as F15.

nodes.label: F11 the controller's output is clamped in code: the target rate may never
nodes.text: the controller's output is clamped in code: the target rate may never leave the band from one tenth of one per cent to two hundred per cent a year, so the realised borrow rate lies between 0.025 and 800 per cent a year
nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE BOUND. MIN_RATE_AT_TARGET = 0.001 ether / 365 days, MAX_RATE_AT_TARGET = 2.0 ether / 365 days, and the source's own comments record the implied realised band. Note the type of bound: Aave bounds the PARAMETERS a setter may write, Morpho bounds the OUTPUT a controller may reach with no setter in the picture. Both are 'a bound', both are residue, and a single repair that names only one of them would misdescribe the other.

nodes.label: F12 the only rate decision anyone ever makes is which interest-rate-model
nodes.text: the only rate decision anyone ever makes is which interest-rate-model address a market is created with, and that address is then part of the market's identity and frozen for its life
nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE LATENCY -- never. Rate policy at Morpho is not a governance action at all; it is a deployment choice made once per market by whoever created it, out of a set governance pre-approved through enableIrm. Tg is meaningless here: there is nothing to delay because there is nothing to change. Whether any live market uses an interest-rate model other than AdaptiveCurveIrm is UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F13 one owner address may transfer its own ownership, add interest-rate mo
nodes.text: one owner address may transfer its own ownership, add interest-rate models and loan-to-value values to the permitted lists, set a per-market protocol fee of at most twenty-five per cent, and name the recipient of that fee
nodes.note: CORPUS DELTA, and the one the lane brief asks to carry: MORPHO BLUE IS NOT ADMIN-LESS. The corpus records 'Morpho Blue has no admin and cannot be upgraded' as a single residue; the second clause is confirmed at F15 and the first is FALSE. Morpho.sol declares owner, an onlyOwner modifier and exactly five owner functions: setOwner, enableIrm, enableLltv (requiring lltv < WAD), setFee bounded by MAX_FEE = 0.25e18, and setFeeRecipient. Aw is APPROXIMATE, emitted on this lane's uniform reading for address-keyed administrative gates (see aave-v3.json F13) and following the corpus's own FORCED use of Aw for Morpho's role structure. The accurate claim is GOVERNANCE-MINIMISED AND NON-UPGRADEABLE WITH A LIVE OWNER WHOSE AUTHORITY IS MONOTONIC AND CANNOT REACH AN EXISTING MARKET -- which is a more interesting statement than 'no admin' and which no element or combination of elements can make.

nodes.label: F14 no owner function can alter an existing market's oracle, model or loan
nodes.text: no owner function can alter an existing market's oracle, model or loan-to-value, there is no proxy and no pause anywhere in the singleton, and the permitted lists may only be widened -- an enabled model or loan-to-value can never be disabled
nodes.note: RESIDUE, three distinct ones fused because they are one commitment. (a) IMMUTABILITY AS A POSITIVE COMMITMENT: the vocabulary can only record this as the absence of Up and Gp, and absence of a symbol means 'I did not observe it', not 'it cannot exist'. (b) MONOTONIC AUTHORITY: enableIrm and enableLltv set a flag true and there is no disable, so governance can widen the permitted set forever and never narrow it, and can never retract a market already created. No element expresses a one-way authority. (c) IRREVOCABILITY OF AN INSTANTIATION. DEPARTURE: the corpus lists Gp for Morpho; Morpho Blue has no pause function, so Gp is REFUTED at this layer and is emitted only at the vault layer (F24), where its meaning is also wrong in a different way. The corpus record does not separate the layers and therefore attributes a vault power to the primitive.

nodes.label: F15 a passive depositor deposits a single asset into a vault and receives
nodes.text: a passive depositor deposits a single asset into a vault and receives vault shares, and the vault -- not the depositor -- is the lender of record in the markets the money reaches
nodes.note: Sh is exact for the ERC-4626 claim. Most depositor capital reaches Blue through a vault rather than directly, which is why the curator (F17 to F22) is the economic centre of the protocol even though it is no part of the base primitive.

nodes.label: F16 the vault is itself a depositor in markets it does not control, so wha
nodes.text: the vault is itself a depositor in markets it does not control, so what a vault shareholder holds is a claim on a lender rather than a claim on a loan
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the third independent sighting of the run's CONTAINMENT gap after 08-intents (a meta-aggregator routing to routers) and 06-yield (a curator allocating over protocols). Composition in this corpus is modelled as UNION OF ELEMENT SETS BETWEEN PEERS; there is no relation for one protocol consuming another, and the union of MetaMorpho's elements with Blue's asserts a single flat system that does not exist. Lending exhibits the same relation three further times: SparkLend's rate IS Sky's rate (sparklend.json F10), Spark ships MorphoUpgradableOracle into Morpho markets (sparklend.json F22), and Maple runs reward programmes on Morpho Blue (https://api.github.com/orgs/maple-labs/repos?per_page=100&sort=pushed, accessed 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F17 two named agents with different powers act over the vault's money: a c
nodes.text: two named agents with different powers act over the vault's money: a curator who sets the envelope of markets and sizes, and one or more allocators who move the money inside it
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 1 (named agent). Aw APPROXIMATE, uniform reading. setCurator and setIsAllocator are both onlyOwner. THE SLOT IS NOT SCALAR: this instance splits the mandate between an agent who may widen the envelope and an agent who may only act within it, and a schema with one 'named agent' field cannot express a two-tier delegation. MANDATE SLOT 6 (agent stake): EMPTY -- the curator posts no bond, and what is genuinely reputational at Morpho is precisely and only the JUDGEMENT INSIDE THE ENVELOPE. Blue validates neither oracle (F5) nor collateral, so the curator's whitelist is the only risk filter in the system. The five parts bound the magnitude of a mistake; nothing bounds its direction.

nodes.label: F18 the money may enter only markets the curator has admitted, and a marke
nodes.text: the money may enter only markets the curator has admitted, and a market may not be admitted at all unless its loan asset is the vault's own asset and it already exists on the singleton, with at most thirty markets in the queue
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 2 (domain whitelist).
