RESIDUE. reallocate reverts UnauthorizedMarket(id) whenever config[id].cap == 0; submitCap rejects any market whose loanToken != asset() or which is not yet created on Blue; MAX_QUEUE_LENGTH = 30 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/morpho-org/metamorpho/main/src/libraries/ConstantsLib.sol, accessed 2026-08-04). Note the identity the code makes between slots 2 and 3: THE DOMAIN IS THE SET OF MARKETS WITH A NON-ZERO CAP, so admitting a market and sizing it are the same act, and a schema that separates the two fields will not fit this instance without collapsing them.

nodes.label: F19 no market may hold more of the vault's money than its own supply cap,
nodes.text: no market may hold more of the vault's money than its own supply cap, checked on every allocation
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 3 (magnitude cap). RESIDUE. if (supplyAssets + suppliedAssets > supplyCap) revert SupplyCapExceeded(id). Ct is a solvency test and not a parameter envelope; nothing in the vocabulary states a per-destination allowance on a delegated allocation.

nodes.label: F20 lowering a cap takes effect at once while raising one must be queued a
nodes.text: lowering a cap takes effect at once while raising one must be queued and accepted only after a delay of between one day and two weeks, and removing a market from the vault is queued the same way
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 4 (rate-of-change limit or delay), and THE ONLY ONE OF THE FIVE INSTANCES IN THIS LANE THAT ANY ELEMENT REACHES. Tg is emitted as APPROXIMATE: a queue-and-accept timelock is literally a delayed execution, so Tg names the delay on increases. Two things it cannot say, and both are the point. (a) THE ASYMMETRY: a decrease calls _setCap inline while an increase writes pendingCap[id].update(newSupplyCap, timelock) and waits for acceptCap; MIN_TIMELOCK = 1 days, MAX_TIMELOCK = 2 weeks. Tg is a single scalar delay and cannot express 'instant to tighten, slow to loosen'. SparkLend's CapAutomator reached the same asymmetry independently in a different organisation over a different quantity, which is evidence that it is structural rather than idiomatic. (b) THE PARTY: Tg reads 'delayed-GOVERNANCE execution' and the delayed party here is a delegate, not governance. Compare the other three mechanisms in this slot across the lane -- debounce (Aave), one-sided cooldown (Spark caps), token bucket (Spark ALM) -- none of which Tg reaches at all, so the slot is one-fifth named and four-fifths residue.

nodes.label: F21 the owner may remove the curator or any allocator at any moment, immed
nodes.text: the owner may remove the curator or any allocator at any moment, immediately and without a delay
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 5 (revocation). RESIDUE. setCurator(address(0)) and setIsAllocator(x, false), both onlyOwner. Aw is NOT emitted for this slot anywhere in this lane: a mutable membership set is a state predicate over who may call, and the obligation here is that A PRINCIPAL MAY WITHDRAW A DELEGATED ECONOMIC AUTHORITY UNILATERALLY AND WITHOUT NOTICE, which is a relation between two parties and not a property of a gate. Note the asymmetry the code creates with F20: revoking the agent is instant while the agent's own loosening is delayed -- the principal is faster than the agent in one direction and slower in the other, and nothing states it. Stage 4 has counted ZERO revocation obligations across the corpus; this is one of five added by this lane.

nodes.label: F22 a separate guardian may cancel any queued change -- a pending cap, a p
nodes.text: a separate guardian may cancel any queued change -- a pending cap, a pending market removal, a pending timelock, a pending guardian -- without being able to initiate one
nodes.note: Gp is APPROXIMATE and defensible ONLY at this layer. revokePendingCap and revokePendingMarketRemoval (curator or guardian), revokePendingTimelock and revokePendingGuardian (guardian). Gp names an emergency stop over user funds; this guardian cannot stop anything users do and cannot touch the money -- its whole power is a VETO OVER QUEUED CHANGES. That is the 12-prediction lane's PREVENTIVE versus COMPENSATORY distinction, arrived at independently: a party who can only cancel a pending change holds a preventive power, and the vocabulary has one symbol for both kinds. The design point Gp also misses is the SEPARATION -- the right to veto is deliberately held by a different party from the right to act, which is the whole accountability structure and reads as a single boolean.

nodes.label: F23 an allocation must end where it began: the total withdrawn across mark
nodes.text: an allocation must end where it began: the total withdrawn across markets in one call must equal the total supplied, so the allocator may permute the deposit and can never move value out of the vault
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and it is the constraint the other four mandate sightings in this lane lack. reallocate ends with if (totalWithdrawn != totalSupplied) revert InconsistentReallocation(). This is a CONSERVATION LAW ON A DELEGATED ACTION, which is a categorically stronger protection than any bound on magnitude: caps limit how much damage an allocation can do, conservation makes theft-by-allocation impossible. The five-part schema has no slot for it, and a formalism that models the mandate purely as an envelope will price Morpho's allocator and Spark's ALM controller as the same risk when one cannot remove value and the other exists precisely to move it out.

nodes.label: F24 the vault charges a performance fee, capped at half the yield, and the
nodes.text: the vault charges a performance fee, capped at half the yield, and the party who sets it is the owner and not the curator who earns the return
nodes.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fd). setFee is onlyOwner with MAX_FEE = 0.5e18 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/morpho-org/metamorpho/main/src/libraries/ConstantsLib.sol, accessed 2026-08-04). DEPARTURE: the corpus files 'a curator ... takes a performance fee' as part of its largest residue and does not record that the agent DOES NOT SET ITS OWN FEE. The same correction lands at Maple (maple.json F16), so it is a category-level fact and not a Morpho detail: in both protocols the delegate's compensation is set by the principal. Fd reaches 'a fee accrues and is distributed'; it does not reach that the fee is the PRICE OF A MANDATE, which is the seventh field the schema would need. DEPARTURE: the corpus carries Sv for Morpho with its own marker conceding Sv 'is still wrong' -- Sv names servicing and determination discretion over a loan, and a curator never touches a loan. This lane DROPS Sv rather than carry a symbol the corpus itself refutes; the curator's discretion is over allocation and caps exercised before anything goes wrong, and it is residue at F17 to F21. The corpus also carries Em for Morpho, uncited in stage 1 and therefore also dropped.

nodes.label: SparkLend
F1 a supplier deposits an asset into a single shared reserve and receives
nodes.text: a supplier deposits an asset into a single shared reserve and receives an interest-bearing claim token whose nominal balance grows as a per-reserve index accrues
nodes.note: Inherited verbatim from Aave V3 and the fork is confirmed structurally rather than asserted: the tree carries contracts/protocol/pool/DefaultReserveInterestRateStrategy.sol, the Aave-V3 PoolConfigurator and ACLManager layout, AToken, StableDebtToken and VariableDebtToken, flashloan/, and the Aave certora/ harness set. REPOSITORY DELTA: the org is sparkdotfi, not the corpus-era marsfoundation, and the core's default branch is dev, not main or master (https://api.github.com/repos/sparkdotfi/sparklend-v1-core, accessed 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F2 a borrower marks supplied reserves as collateral, draws an open-ended
nodes.text: a borrower marks supplied reserves as collateral, draws an open-ended loan with no maturity, and is monitored by a single on-chain health factor computed from oracle-priced collateral against oracle-priced debt
nodes.note: Ex is warranted by a purpose-built oracle estate rather than by the fork alone: WSTETHExchangeRateOracle, RETHExchangeRateOracle, WEETHExchangeRateOracle, EZETHExchangeRateOracle, RSETHExchangeRateOracle, SPETHExchangeRateOracle, CBBTCRatioOracle, FixedPriceOracle, CappedOracle and MorphoUpgradableOracle all sit in https://github.com/sparkdotfi/sparklend-advanced (accessed 2026-08-04). Two of those names are themselves residue: an EXCHANGE-RATE oracle reports a redemption ratio rather than a market price, and a CappedOracle bounds what a feed may report -- the same predicate-on-a-feed gap recorded at Aave (aave-v3.json F5). Ex names one undifferentiated feed for all of them.

nodes.label: F3 a third party may repay part of an unhealthy borrower's debt and seize
nodes.text: a third party may repay part of an unhealthy borrower's debt and seize collateral at a bonus, permissionlessly
nodes.note: Li is exact, inherited. The close-factor machinery is inherited too and carries the same residue as Aave's (aave-v3.json F7); this lane did not read SparkLend's LiquidationLogic to establish whether the fork tracks Aave's current dynamic close factor or an earlier constant one, so WHICH OF THE TWO SHAPES SparkLend runs is UNKNOWN. That question is unaskable in the vocabulary, which is the point.

nodes.label: F4 anyone may borrow and repay within a single transaction with no collat
nodes.text: anyone may borrow and repay within a single transaction with no collateral
nodes.note: Inherited; the tree carries a flashloan/ directory. Conditional prohibition X2 is armed by construction and not met inside this application, as at Aave.

nodes.label: F5 the borrow rate has the same two-slope kinked form as Aave's, but its
nodes.text: the borrow rate has the same two-slope kinked form as Aave's, but its base rate and its rate at the kink are not stored numbers -- they are read live, on every call, as a fixed spread over another protocol's savings rate
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and FINDING 1's third row. RateTargetBaseInterestRateStrategy sets _getBaseVariableBorrowRate() = RATE_SOURCE.getAPR() * 10^(27-dec) + _baseVariableBorrowRateSpread; RateTargetKinkInterestRateStrategy sets _getVariableRateSlope1() = max(0, RATE_SOURCE.getAPR() * 10^(27-dec) + _variableRateSlope1Spread - _baseVariableBorrowRate). THE FUNCTIONAL FORM IS THE SAME AS AAVE'S AND THE INSTRUMENT IS NOT, which refutes the corpus's own identity claim -- see F24. The slope-1 spread is a SIGNED int256, so SparkLend can deliberately price its kink BELOW the rate it tracks, a sign convention that carries the whole commercial policy and that no element could hold.

nodes.label: F6 the quantity the rate tracks is fetched by a direct call into another
nodes.text: the quantity the rate tracks is fetched by a direct call into another protocol's own accumulator, not from any feed, medianizer or reporter
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the sharpest one for this target. PotRateSource.getAPR() = (pot.dsr() - 1e27) * 365 days and SSRRateSource.getAPR() = (susds.ssr() - 1e27) * 365 days (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sparkdotfi/sparklend-advanced/master/src/PotRateSource.sol, accessed 2026-08-04). This is NOT Ex: there is no oracle, no feed, no publisher, no staleness, nothing to be wrong -- it is a staticcall into a live state variable of a contract in another system. It is not Ix either. The vocabulary has no way to say THIS PROTOCOL'S PRICE IS A FUNCTION OF THAT PROTOCOL'S PRICE, which is the containment gap (morpho.json F16) appearing on the rate axis rather than the allocation axis. A CappedFallbackRateSource also exists, so even the fallback is a rate source rather than a feed.

nodes.label: F7 no party sets the rate in place: the spreads are fixed in the strategy
nodes.text: no party sets the rate in place: the spreads are fixed in the strategy contract's constructor and can only be changed by deploying a new strategy contract and repointing the reserve at it
nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE SETTER LOCUS -- another protocol's state variable for the level, and a redeployment for the spread. _baseVariableBorrowRateSpread and _variableRateSlope1Spread are immutable; the change path is a governance spell (https://api.github.com/orgs/sparkdotfi/repos?per_page=100, accessed 2026-08-04, spark-spells, AGPL-3.0, last push 2026-08-04T08:18:54Z). Up is the WRONG symbol and instructively so: Up names a mutable implementation behind a fixed address, and this is the exact opposite -- an IMMUTABLE IMPLEMENTATION BEHIND A MUTABLE POINTER. The two have different risk objects (an upgrade rewrites history for existing users; a repoint applies only forward) and the vocabulary has one symbol and it is the wrong one.

nodes.label: F8 nothing bounds the rate on SparkLend's own side: there is no maximum o
nodes.text: nothing bounds the rate on SparkLend's own side: there is no maximum on the spread and no maximum on the level, which is whatever the tracked protocol sets
nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE BOUND -- INHERITED, which is a fourth distinct answer after Aave's in-code parameter bounds, Morpho's in-code output clamp and JustLend's nothing at all. SparkLend's safety on the level is entirely a property of a governance process in a different organisation. No element expresses a bound held by a third party, and none expresses that a protocol has DELEGATED ITS RISK LIMIT TO ANOTHER PROTOCOL'S GOVERNANCE.

nodes.label: F9 when the tracked protocol changes its savings rate, SparkLend's kink r
nodes.text: when the tracked protocol changes its savings rate, SparkLend's kink rate moves on the next interaction with no transaction on SparkLend at all
nodes.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE LATENCY -- instantaneous and automatic in one direction, a deployment cycle in the other. This is NOT the CDP lane's 'administered rate keyed to external benchmarks': an administered rate is written by a party who reads a benchmark, and this is a LIVE FUNCTIONAL DEPENDENCY with no writer in the loop. Tg names a delay and there is none; Ep names a period and there is none; the change happens because someone touched the reserve for an unrelated reason.

nodes.label: F10 the lender of last resort is not a depositor: liquidity issued by anot
nodes.text: the lender of last resort is not a depositor: liquidity issued by another protocol is moved into SparkLend and into other venues by an operator acting on that other protocol's behalf
nodes.note: RESIDUE, confirming the corpus verbatim and extending it. The subsystem is real and separately engineered: ALMProxy.sol, ALMProxyFreezable.sol, MainnetController.sol, ForeignController.sol, OTCBuffer.sol, RateLimits.sol, RateLimitHelpers.sol, plus venue libraries for Aave, Curve, Uniswap V4, CCTP, LayerZero, ERC-4626 and the peg-swap module. Not Pl (there is no depositor and no claim), not Em (nothing is emitted), not Ps (no one-for-one reserve swap), not Cd (no per-position collateral). What the corpus did not record and this lane adds is that THE LINE IS ITSELF A BOUNDED DELEGATE MANDATE (F16 to F21), which converts the finding from 'an unnameable facility' into 'an unnameable facility governed by the same five-part shape found in three other categories'. The D3M's rate-targeting objective and which venues are live remain UNKNOWN -- MainnetController.sol was not read.

nodes.label: F11 a named keeper role may move the protocol's supply and borrow caps wit
nodes.text: a named keeper role may move the protocol's supply and borrow caps without a governance vote, and a separate admin role sets the envelope it moves inside
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 1 (named agent), instance (a) of two at this target. Aw APPROXIMATE, uniform reading (see aave-v3.json F13). OpenZeppelin AccessControlEnumerable with UPDATE_ROLE for the keeper and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE for governance, both required non-zero at construction. THIS IS THE LIMIT CASE OF THE SHAPE AND WORTH RECORDING AS SUCH: the target cap is a pure function of observed usage, so the UPDATE_ROLE holder exercises no discretion at all and chooses only WHEN to call. The mandate has been narrowed until the agent is a crank. A schema that treats 'named agent' as a party with judgement will misdescribe this instance, and Aave's automaton variant (aave-v3.json F16) reaches the same place from the other direction. MANDATE SLOT 6 (agent stake): EMPTY. Performance fee: absent -- the keeper is not paid by this contract.

nodes.label: F12 the keeper may act only on assets that have been given a configuration
nodes.text: the keeper may act only on assets that have been given a configuration, and an asset with none is inert -- the computation returns its cap unchanged
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 2 (domain whitelist). RESIDUE. Per-asset supplyCapConfigs and borrowCapConfigs; _calculateNewCap returns the current value when max == 0. Note the default: THE DOMAIN FAILS CLOSED, an unconfigured asset being untouchable rather than unlimited. The 09-rwa lane found a gate at the same organisation's competitor that fails OPEN. A gate that fails open and a gate that fails closed are different security objects and no element distinguishes them.

nodes.label: F13 each configured cap has a ceiling it may never exceed and a headroom i
nodes.text: each configured cap has a ceiling it may never exceed and a headroom it maintains above current usage, so the new cap is the lesser of current usage plus headroom and that ceiling
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 3 (magnitude cap). RESIDUE. max, further bounded by ReserveConfiguration.MAX_VALID_SUPPLY_CAP and MAX_VALID_BORROW_CAP, with gap <= max enforced. Two bounds of different kinds live in one slot here: an ABSOLUTE ceiling (max) and a RELATIVE headroom (gap) which makes the cap track usage. A single 'magnitude cap' field cannot hold both, and the relative one is the interesting half -- it is a cap that follows the thing it caps.

nodes.label: F14 a cap may be lowered whenever the keeper likes but may not be raised a
nodes.text: a cap may be lowered whenever the keeper likes but may not be raised again until a cooldown has passed since it was last raised, and no cap may be touched twice in one block
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 4 (rate-of-change limit or delay). RESIDUE. increaseCooldown seconds tracked in lastIncreaseTime and applied to increases only -- the source comment reads 'Cap cannot be increased before cooldown passes, but can be decreased' -- plus a lastUpdateBlock == block.number guard. Tg does NOT reach this: a cooldown SINCE the last change is not a delay BEFORE execution, and the keeper's call executes immediately. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE SECOND INDEPENDENT REDISCOVERY: MetaMorpho reached instant-to-tighten and slow-to-loosen in a different organisation over a different quantity by a different mechanism (morpho.json F20). Two independent arrivals at the same asymmetry is evidence it is structural, and it is the property the current one-field schema most obviously cannot hold.

nodes.label: F15 the admin may delete any asset's configuration and may remove the keep
nodes.text: the admin may delete any asset's configuration and may remove the keeper's role outright
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 5 (revocation). RESIDUE. removeSupplyCapConfig and removeBorrowCapConfig under DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, plus revokeRole(UPDATE_ROLE, ...) from AccessControlEnumerable. Aw is not emitted, for the reason given at morpho.json F21. Note that here the two revocations are of DIFFERENT KINDS -- removing the domain leaves the agent in place with nothing to do, removing the role leaves the domain in place with no one to act -- and a single revocation field cannot express which of the two a principal used, though the recovery paths differ.

nodes.label: F16 a named controller contract, driven by an off-chain relayer, may move
nodes.text: a named controller contract, driven by an off-chain relayer, may move another protocol's liquidity across a set of external venues, and a separate admin role sets the budget it moves inside
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 1 (named agent), instance (b) of two at this target and the FIFTH instance in this lane. Aw APPROXIMATE, uniform reading. CONTROLLER role held by MainnetController / ForeignController; DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE sets the envelope. MANDATE SLOT 6 (agent stake): EMPTY. Performance fee: absent. The agent here is a CONTRACT DRIVEN BY AN OFF-CHAIN PROCESS, which is a third kind of holder after a human council and an on-chain automaton, and 'named agent' as a single field cannot distinguish an address that decides from an address that relays a decision made elsewhere -- which is precisely where the accountability sits.

nodes.label: F17 every permitted action is identified by a key naming an action and a v
nodes.text: every permitted action is identified by a key naming an action and a venue together, and a key with no budget cannot be used at all
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 2 (domain whitelist). RESIDUE. Budgets are keyed by bytes32, constructed by RateLimitHelpers.sol, with venue libraries (AaveLib, CurveLib, UniswapV4Lib, PSMLib, CCTPLib, LayerZeroLib, ERC4626Lib) enumerating what may be done at all; a key with maxAmount == 0 reverts RateLimits/zero-maxAmount. The domain here is a PRODUCT OF TWO AXES -- what may be done and where -- and it is expressed as a hash, so the whitelist is not enumerable from the contract's own state. A formalism with a set-valued domain field would model this as a set of opaque atoms and lose the structure that makes it auditable.

nodes.label: F18 each key carries a ceiling that is the most the agent can move in any
nodes.text: each key carries a ceiling that is the most the agent can move in any one action
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 3 (magnitude cap). RESIDUE. maxAmount in struct RateLimitData { uint256 maxAmount; uint256 slope; uint256 lastAmount; uint256 lastUpdated; }.

nodes.label: F19 spent budget refills continuously with elapsed time at a per-key rate,
nodes.text: spent budget refills continuously with elapsed time at a per-key rate, so what bounds the agent is not how often it acts but how much it may move per unit of time
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 4 (rate-of-change limit or delay). RESIDUE, and the FOURTH DISTINCT MECHANISM occupying this one slot in this one lane. getCurrentRateLimit returns _min(d.slope * (block.timestamp - d.lastUpdated) + d.lastAmount, d.maxAmount); triggerRateLimitDecrease consumes it under onlyRole(CONTROLLER) and requires amountToDecrease <= currentRateLimit. THIS IS A TRUE FLOW LIMIT, NOT A DELAY: it bounds THROUGHPUT where Aave's debounce and Spark's own cooldown bound FREQUENCY and MetaMorpho's timelock bounds LATENCY. A formalism that writes 'rate-of-change limit' as a single field conflates three different guarantees, and only the throughput form composes with itself -- two calls under a token bucket are bounded, two calls under a debounce are not.

nodes.label: F20 the admin may zero any budget, remove the controller's role, or freeze
nodes.text: the admin may zero any budget, remove the controller's role, or freeze the proxy that holds every deployed fund through purpose-built freezer and kill-switch contracts
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 5 (revocation). Gp is APPROXIMATE and emitted only for the freeze half: ALMProxyFreezable.sol in the same tree, plus sparklend-freezer and sparklend-kill-switch as separate audited AGPL-3.0 repositories (https://api.github.com/orgs/sparkdotfi/repos?per_page=100, accessed 2026-08-04). The revocation half -- setRateLimitData(key, 0, 0) and revokeRole(CONTROLLER, ...) -- is RESIDUE on the same reading as elsewhere in this lane. Gp names a halt and cannot say that halting and de-authorising are different acts with different blast radii, nor that this protocol has THREE separate stop mechanisms in three separate repositories, which is a control-plane estate Aave has no analogue for.

nodes.label: F21 the admin may also switch the bound off entirely for any single key in
nodes.text: the admin may also switch the bound off entirely for any single key in one transaction with no delay, after which the agent's budget is unlimited and the checks short-circuit
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and it is the sharpest control-plane detail in the lane. setUnlimitedRateLimitData(bytes32 key) sets maxAmount = type(uint256).max, and both trigger functions then return type(uint256).max immediately. THE BOUND IS REVOCABLE UPWARD AS WELL AS DOWNWARD. The five-part schema has a slot for revoking the AGENT and none for revoking the BOUND, and the second is the more dangerous: revoking an agent removes an authority, revoking a bound converts a bounded agent into an unbounded one while every element and every role assignment in the decomposition stays exactly as it was. No other of the five instances in this lane has this property. Prohibition X16 (unbounded delegated authority) is reachable from a bounded configuration in one admin transaction, which means the prohibition is a predicate on STATE and the risk is a predicate on REACHABLE state.

nodes.label: F22 an oracle written and maintained in this protocol's own repository is
nodes.text: an oracle written and maintained in this protocol's own repository is supplied as the price source for markets in a different lending protocol
nodes.note: RESIDUE. MorphoUpgradableOracle sits in sparklend-advanced/src/ alongside Spark's own oracles, so one target in this lane is a price input to another target in the same lane (see morpho.json F5, where Morpho Blue validates no oracle whatsoever). This is the CONTAINMENT gap again and in its most awkward direction -- not a protocol consuming another, but a protocol SUPPLYING A SAFETY-CRITICAL COMPONENT TO A COMPETITOR. Union of element sets between peers cannot state it, and a decomposition of Morpho that emits Ex is silently emitting a dependency on SparkLend's engineering.

nodes.label: F23 reserves and the whole market can be frozen or killed, the pool sits b
nodes.text: reserves and the whole market can be frozen or killed, the pool sits behind a replaceable implementation, and governance acts by deploying executable payload contracts
nodes.note: All three inherited or purpose-built, and all three thin. The org carries sparklend-freezer, sparklend-kill-switch, sparklend-health-checker, spark-gov-relay (cross-chain governance), spark-spells (executable governance payloads), upgradeable-proxy and mainnet-invariants, all AGPL-3.0. Tg is emitted on the spell process; THE DELAY'S VALUE WAS NOT READ IN THIS RUN and is Sky's rather than SparkLend's, so law L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is discharged only nominally and stage 3 should treat it as UNKNOWN rather than as satisfied. Xm is NOT emitted despite spark-gov-relay: the evidence is a repository name in an org listing, and this lane does not assert a verification mechanism it has not read. Who holds any of these keys is UNKNOWN, as for all five targets.

nodes.label: F24 the protocol's code is a fork of one protocol and the price of its cre
nodes.text: the protocol's code is a fork of one protocol and the price of its credit is a function of a second protocol's state, so it depends on two upstreams for two different things
nodes.note: RESIDUE, confirming the corpus and adding its second half. THE CORPUS'S IDENTITY CLAIM IS REFUTED HERE: identicalClaimedByLane records [Aave V3, SparkLend], and the two are not the same instrument on the one axis the corpus itself says matters most. Aave runs a mutable-parameter, bounded, governed kinked curve (aave-v3.json F12 to F15); SparkLend runs an immutable-spread curve pegged live to an external protocol's savings rate (F5 to F9). Same functional form, different setter, different bound, different latency, different party in control. The identity survives only because the vocabulary cannot see rates, which is the corpus's own thesis -- now demonstrated rather than asserted. A second corpus statement is also qualified: SparkLend's element set IS close to a subset of Aave's, and SparkLend nonetheless carries a control-plane estate Aave has no analogue for (three separate stop mechanisms, a cap automator, a health checker, a liquidity controller, each an independently audited repository). Subset in symbols, superset in control machinery. DEPARTURES: Im is dropped (inherited from Aave, whose debt ceiling is absent from the current reserve configuration -- aave-v3.json F11) and Em is dropped (uncited in stage 1).

nodes.label: 03-cdp-stablecoins
Ethena (USDe / sUSDe)
F1 only counterparties on a whitelist may create or destroy the unit; eve
nodes.text: only counterparties on a whitelist may create or destroy the unit; everyone else may only buy and sell it on a secondary market
nodes.note: PARTIAL FIT, and the corpus files this as residue while also carrying Aw. Both are right about different halves. Aw names the gate; it does not name that the gated action is ISSUANCE ITSELF, so that the peg is a right for a named few and an arbitrage outcome for everyone else. In V2 the whitelist moved on-chain and benefactors whitelist their own beneficiaries by contract call (https://docs.ethena.fi/technical-design/minting-usde/mint-and-redeem-contract-v2.md, accessed 2026-08-04), which makes the gate a delegable authority as well as a list — a second thing Aw does not say.

nodes.label: F2 creation is an atomic exchange against a signed order quoting a price
nodes.text: creation is an atomic exchange against a signed order quoting a price the protocol computed, carrying its own request identifier, executable by contract wallets as well as keys, and priced so that the issuer earns no spread on it
nodes.note: DEPARTURE: the corpus carries no execution element for Ethena. The mint is a request-for-quote in the precise sense of the symbol — a signed maker quote settled atomically — with the RFQ id moved on-chain as order_id inside the signature and signature_type defaulting to EIP712 with EIP-1271 support (https://docs.ethena.fi/technical-design/minting-usde/mint-and-redeem-contract-v2.md, accessed 2026-08-04). What Rf does not carry is that the quote is the ISSUANCE PRICE OF A LIABILITY rather than a trade in an existing asset, and that slippage and execution cost are priced into it so 'Ethena earns no profit from the minting or redeeming of USDe'.

nodes.label: F3 a whitelisted holder may redeem the unit for backing assets at one dol
nodes.text: a whitelisted holder may redeem the unit for backing assets at one dollar at any time, served from about half a percent of backing held as stablecoins inside the minting contract and replenished from about four percent held across custodians
nodes.note: FORCED: Rd as written implies a general right. Law L7's discharge for this application is a redemption right restricted to a whitelist plus a 0.5% on-demand reserve — a par exit for named parties over a fractional buffer, which is a materially weaker guarantee than Rd asserts.

nodes.label: F4 the right to create or destroy the unit is suspended automatically whe
nodes.text: the right to create or destroy the unit is suspended automatically whenever the unit's price diverges unfavourably from its stablecoin reference beyond a configured threshold
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and one of the sharpest in the lane. The V2 mandate delta limit is aimed explicitly at 'blackswan events like stablecoin collateral de-pegging'. Gp names a pause held by an authority; Rd names a right. Neither names a right that voids ITSELF, by rule and with no actor, precisely in the price region where it would be exercised — which is the entire content of this control and inverts the guarantee in F3 exactly when it matters.

nodes.label: F5 creation and destruction are capped per block, separately for stableco
nodes.text: creation and destruction are capped per block, separately for stablecoin and non-stablecoin assets, under a global cap adjustable by a development multisig
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A quantitative speed limit on creating the unit, differentiated by asset class, and the main defence against a compromised minter key. As is quantity adjustment TOWARD A PEG; this is a quantity ceiling per unit time FOR SAFETY, which is a different instrument with a different objective. CROSS-PROTOCOL: the same object is Sky's Hole/hole liquidation throughput cap (sky.json F11), Lista's 500,000/day redemption quota (lista-cdp.json F10) and Spark's regenerating allowance (spark-savings.json F19). Four independent instances of a magnitude-per-time envelope on a permitted action, and no symbol.

nodes.label: F6 the backing is a book of six strategy families — crypto basis, non-cry
nodes.text: the backing is a book of six strategy families — crypto basis, non-crypto basis, DeFi lending, institutional lending, tokenised real-world assets and liquid stablecoins — whose allocation across categories is changed continuously at the operator's discretion
nodes.note: RESIDUE. At attests to a reserve's existence and value; nothing names 'the reserve's composition is a discretionary investment decision taken continuously'. Sv (servicing & determination discretion) is REJECTED after consideration: Sv names discretion in determining and servicing a CLAIM — calling a default, applying a waterfall — not discretion in choosing what the reserve owns. CORRECTION TO THE CORPUS: the corpus record describes the 2024 design ('long staked ETH and liquid restaking collateral, short an equivalent notional of ETH perpetual futures'). Against the current documentation the crypto basis trade is one family of six, so the corpus's ~20% coverage score for Dp is an overstatement measured against the 2026 mechanism.

nodes.label: F7 the composition and value of the backing, and the balance of the reser
nodes.text: the composition and value of the backing, and the balance of the reserve fund, are published on a dashboard and supported by custodian attestations rather than by an on-chain object
nodes.note: FORCED, the same way At is forced for Sky's RWA vaults: At implies an on-chain attestation object and this is a web page plus a custodian's letter. L27 requires named attester, independence, stated assurance, staleness bound and recourse; the custodians are named (Copper, Ceffu, Fireblocks) and the staleness bound and recourse are not stated anywhere I can cite. UNKNOWN on three of five limbs.

nodes.label: F8 volatile holdings are paired with a short futures position of approxim
nodes.text: volatile holdings are paired with a short futures position of approximately the same notional so that a move in the spot leg is offset by the hedge, and that pairing is re-established continuously as prices move, margin is rebalanced and positions are rolled
nodes.note: CANDIDATE and FORCED. Dp reads 'directional position & hedge maintenance'; the defining property here is that the book is deliberately NON-directional, and the hedge is not an overlay protecting some other exposure — the hedge IS the reserve asset. Dp is silent on where the position lives (a centralised venue), who maintains it (an off-chain operator), why it exists (to make the backing price-invariant), what it earns (funding), and what happens when the venue fails. The maintained-neutrality invariant is an operational obligation on an off-chain program, checked by no contract, and it is the single largest unnamed object in a $3.9bn protocol.

nodes.label: F9 the protocol's revenue is the funding payment of perpetual markets it
nodes.text: the protocol's revenue is the funding payment of perpetual markets it does not operate and does not govern, received as an ordinary external participant
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Pf is NOT USED, deliberately: Pf is the transfer a perp exchange implements between its own longs and shorts. Ethena implements no such transfer; it takes one from Binance (50%), Bybit (25%), OKX (15%), Deribit (5%) and Bitget (5%). Using Pf here would assert that Ethena runs a perpetual market, which is false. This is a clean DIRECTIONAL gap: every risk-transfer symbol in the vocabulary is written from the issuer's side and there is no way to name being the counterparty to someone else's mechanism.

nodes.label: F10 the backing never sits on the venue that holds the hedge: it is held b
nodes.text: the backing never sits on the venue that holds the hedge: it is held by named third-party settlement providers in bankruptcy-remote structures and only delegated to derivatives venues as margin on a rolling four-hour cycle, so that on a venue's failure positions are treated as closed and exposure is limited to unsettled profit and loss between cycles
nodes.note: RESIDUE, confirmed verbatim against the current docs. Copper (Clearloop), Ceffu and Fireblocks; 'in the event of Copper's failure, users' funds are not a part of the Copper estate'; Copper settles PnL daily; the protocol 'is reliant upon the cooperation and legal behavior of our Off-Exchange Settlement provider partners'. Two unnamed objects in one obligation: off-exchange settlement and custody mirroring, and venue/counterparty concentration as a risk the design deliberately trades against custodial risk. The vocabulary has no custody sort at all — Xf moves an asset between domains, and there is nothing for an asset that stays put while its economic effect is mirrored somewhere else.

nodes.label: F11 the prices used to quote creation and redemption are computed by an of
nodes.text: the prices used to quote creation and redemption are computed by an off-chain service that ingests six centralised venues plus two oracle networks, normalises and validates them, and publishes the result; no contract reads a price feed to test solvency
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE: the corpus carries Ex for Ethena and this construction drops it. Ex names an on-chain oracle with an on-chain consumer. Here the price service, the order router, the position reconciliation service and the monitoring systems are a private program run by a company (https://docs.ethena.fi/technical-design/hedging-system.md, accessed 2026-08-04), and the on-chain mandate delta limit of F4 compares the order's own implied price against its reference rather than reading a feed. The largest synthetic dollar in the category has no on-chain price oracle, which is a stronger statement than the corpus's Ex records and changes which laws even apply.

nodes.label: F12 holding the unit pays nothing; staking it mints a share whose price ri
nodes.text: holding the unit pays nothing; staking it mints a share whose price rises as an off-chain distributor transfers realised revenue into the vault
nodes.note: StakedUSDeV2 (0x9d39a5de30e57443bff2a8307a4256c8797a3497) is ERC-4626 and the staking contract IS the share token. Ix is FORCED in the way the corpus records: the index moves because an operator transferred realised profit in, not because an on-chain accrual computed it. 'Two instruments the vocabulary treats as one' — the unstaked unit and the staked share have different economics and Sh + Ix cannot say that one of them pays nothing by design.

nodes.label: F13 revenue is transferred in periodically and vests linearly across the i
nodes.text: revenue is transferred in periodically and vests linearly across the interval rather than landing at once, so that a deposit made just before a transfer cannot capture it
nodes.note: FLAGGED rather than claimed, following stage 1. Transfers every 8 hours vesting linearly over 8 hours, and the Foundation deliberately pays in several smaller instalments through the week to deny arbitrage (https://docs.ethena.fi/protocol-overview/rewards-mechanism.md, accessed 2026-08-04). Sr names the shape exactly and gets the reason wrong: here streaming is an MEV defence, not a product feature. Same shape, different justification, and the vocabulary cannot record the difference — which matters because removing the stream would not remove a feature, it would open an attack.

nodes.label: F14 the share price can only rise or stay flat: periods in which the cost
nodes.text: the share price can only rise or stay flat: periods in which the cost of maintaining positions exceeds revenue are absorbed by a reserve fund, and the share of ongoing revenue directed to that fund is a governance parameter currently set to zero, with all revenue going to incentive rewards and promotional distributions instead
nodes.note: Bs is FORCED: the reserve absorbs the loss first, so it is first-loss, but it is protocol-owned treasury rather than staked third-party capital exposed to slashing, and 'slashable' is the operative word in Bs. SHARPENING THE CORPUS: a first-loss buffer with a zero accrual rate is a different object from a first-loss buffer, and the vocabulary cannot say that a backstop is not being funded. Em covers the destination of the revenue.

nodes.label: F15 the staked class stands ahead of the unstaked class in the declared lo
nodes.text: the staked class stands ahead of the unstaked class in the declared loss order, so that the unit's holders bear a shortfall the share's holders do not
nodes.note: FORCED: a two-class waterfall in substance, with no attachment points, no separately priced tranche instruments, and a seniority asserted in documentation rather than enforced by a settlement contract. L6 requires (Sv | mechanical trigger) + declared seniority + dispute forum + recovery-timing assumption; only declared seniority is present, and the dispute forum is a company.

nodes.label: F16 the level of the payout is decided off-chain: a foundation subsidiary
nodes.text: the level of the payout is decided off-chain: a foundation subsidiary calculates an annual percentage yield weekly as part of internal accounting and executes it as a transfer, and no rate anywhere in the system is set to defend the peg
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the finding this obligation exists to record. Ethena is the one protocol of the five with NO price-of-credit instrument at all: the peg is defended purely by primary-market arbitrage between whitelisted parties (F1, F3), and the payout is a distribution of realised profit rather than a price set to move supply or demand. Written beside the other four — Sky's bounded delegate (sky.json F5-F10), USDD's external-benchmark reaction function (usdd.json F6), Lista's closed-loop controller (lista-cdp.json F6) and Liquity's borrower-chosen rate (liquity.json F5) — this makes five species, not one gap. It also refines the corpus's category residue, which asserts that the price of credit is 'the instrument all five actually use': four of five use it, and the largest by TVL does not.

nodes.label: F17 an unwhitelisted holder exits by unstaking through a cooldown that par
nodes.text: an unwhitelisted holder exits by unstaking through a cooldown that parks the unit in a separate contract for a period the administrator may set to anything up to ninety days
nodes.note: USDeSilo holds the parked balance; setCooldownDuration admits values up to 90 days at admin discretion. Wq names the queue and not that ITS LENGTH IS A LEVER THE OPERATOR MAY PULL — the difference between a queue that reflects backing illiquidity and a queue that can be extended to ninety days by a transaction is the whole of L14's content, and the symbol carries neither.

nodes.label: F18 two multisigs hold the constructive authority — one may change the sup
nodes.text: two multisigs hold the constructive authority — one may change the supported collateral set and the custodian set, the other may grant and revoke every operational role — and no delay applies to either
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE twice over. (a) The corpus carries Tg for Ethena; the multisig/timelock matrix specifies NO TIMELOCK DELAY FOR ANY ROLE, so Tg is dropped. (b) The corpus carries Up; the V1-to-V2 transition was a redeployment to a new address (V1 0x2cc440b721d2cafd6d64908d6d8c4acc57f8afc3, V2 0xe3490297a08d6fC8Da46Edb7B6142E4F461b62D3, https://docs.ethena.fi/technical-design/key-addresses.md, accessed 2026-08-04), i.e. migration by moving the whitelist and the roles, not upgrade in place, so Up is dropped. What remains has no symbol: an authority whose risk is entirely a property of its holder — two multisigs of undisclosed threshold, immediately. The vocabulary names facilities and not holders, which is exactly the gap lane 07 exhibited on the three largest bridges.

nodes.label: F19 twenty minter keys and twenty redeemer keys exist because concurrent t
nodes.text: twenty minter keys and twenty redeemer keys exist because concurrent throughput demands them, and at least three further keys, held partly by external organisations that are not governors, can disable creation and destruction and strip the operational roles without being able to use them
nodes.note: FORCED, and two unnamed objects. (a) The NUMBER of keys is a capacity parameter — the Redeemer set is deliberately the same twenty addresses as the Minter set 'for handling concurrent load' — so key count is an operational-throughput decision with a security cost, and no symbol carries it. (b) An outsider holds a purely destructive power: Gatekeepers can kill but never mint. Gp names a pause and cannot express that the right to halt is deliberately held by parties who hold no right to act, which is the same accountability split the yield lane found at Spark (spark-savings.json F20). Gatekeeper monitoring runs 'in separate AWS accounts' (https://docs.ethena.fi/technical-design/overview/github-overview.md, accessed 2026-08-04). Governance itself is a rotating committee structure whose docs state that 'fully on-chain governance is not a practical or viable option at present' (https://docs.ethena.fi/protocol-overview/governance.md, accessed 2026-08-04) — so there is no on-chain franchise, no quorum and no delay to decompose.

nodes.label: F20 a named role may mark a holder fully restricted, after which they cann
nodes.text: a named role may mark a holder fully restricted, after which they cannot receive the share, and may move the locked balance of a restricted address to a segregated protocol wallet
nodes.note: CANDIDATE, and an unusually exact fit — one of the few candidate symbols in this lane that needed no stretching. CORRECTION: the corpus names the role FULL_RESTRICTED_STAKER_ROLE; the docs name it FULL_RESTRICTED_STAKING_ROLE, and record that SOFT_RESTRICTED_STAKING_ROLE exists and has never been used. redistributeLockedAmounts is a documented function rather than an inferred capability, so the fit is tighter than the corpus records. L28 wants named authority + enumerated triggers + appeal path + holder disclosure; only the named authority is present.

nodes.label: F21 the administrator may remove any token except the protocol's own unit
nodes.text: the administrator may remove any token except the protocol's own unit from the contract to an address the protocol controls
nodes.note: RESIDUE. rescueTokens is a standing administrative sweep: a permanent claim on everything that lands in the contract other than the unit itself. Fz covers freeze and forced transfer of the protocol's OWN unit; this is the complement and has no symbol.

nodes.label: F22 the unit, the share and the governance token are issued on many domain
nodes.text: the unit, the share and the governance token are issued on many domains, sharing one address triple across most rollups and carrying distinct deployments on non-EVM chains
nodes.note: ENA 0x58538e6A, USDe 0x5d3a1Ff2, sUSDe 0x211Cc4DD on most L2s, with separate deployments on Solana, ZKSync, Zircuit, Aptos and TON. As at USDD (usdd.json F15), Xf asserts a transfer with L9's debit-equals-credit; a shared vanity address across domains is not evidence of a transfer relation, and stage 1 did not establish the bridging path. Carried because multi-domain issuance is real; flagged because the symbol asserts more than the evidence.

nodes.label: Liquity (V1 + V2)
F1 a user deposits a single collateral asset into a position and draws th
nodes.text: a user deposits a single collateral asset into a position and draws the stablecoin against it, in V1 against ether alone and in V2 against one of three assets on the branch that matches it, subject to a minimum draw and a refundable gas reserve
nodes.note: V1: ether into a Trove, LUSD out, plus a refundable 200 LUSD Liquidation Reserve. V2: WETH, wstETH or rETH into a branch Trove, at least 2,000 BOLD out, plus a refundable 0.0375 ETH gas reserve. Per branch the contracts are AddressesRegistry, BorrowerOperations, TroveManager, TroveNFT, StabilityPool, SortedTroves, ActivePool, DefaultPool, CollSurplusPool, GasPool and a PriceFeed, above which sit CollateralRegistry and BoldToken. Confirmed against contracts/src at liquity/bold main c8a5a4ee2e9dc024905856b6698a77d849c68c7e (2026-07-13).

nodes.label: F2 the position must stay above a minimum collateral ratio which differs
nodes.text: the position must stay above a minimum collateral ratio which differs by branch, and which is tighter for liquid-staking collateral than for ether
nodes.note: V1: a single 110% minimum. V2: maximum loan-to-value 90.91% on WETH and 83.33% on wstETH and rETH. Ct names the test and not that its parameter is per-market, which is the difference between V1's one number and V2's three.

nodes.label: F3 each branch reads its own price feed, and the liquid-staking branches
nodes.text: each branch reads its own price feed, and the liquid-staking branches read a composed one: an ether price multiplied by an exchange rate for the staking receipt
nodes.note: WETHPriceFeed, WSTETHPriceFeed and RETHPriceFeed over CompositePriceFeed and MainnetPriceFeedBase — five feed contracts for three branches. A single Ex cannot distinguish a direct feed from a composed one, and composition is exactly where the LST branches' risk lives: the composite has two failure sources and one symbol. The V2 known-issues register devotes several of its twenty-six entries to oracle frontrunning and stale prices, with branch shutdown (F15) as the terminal mitigation — a documented, enumerated risk register that no element and no law records.

nodes.label: F4 in V1 the borrower pays a one-time fee at origination whose level rise
nodes.text: in V1 the borrower pays a one-time fee at origination whose level rises with recent redemption activity and decays back, floored at half a per cent and capped at five, and pays no interest at all thereafter
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a fifth species of the price of credit that the lane's four-instrument taxonomy should record. V1 prices credit as a STOCK, not a flow: there is no rate at all, only a one-off charge whose level is a decaying function of how much redemption pressure the system has recently absorbed. That is a price set by a state variable of the system rather than by a vote, a controller, a benchmark or a borrower — and it is priced in the wrong dimension for any rate symbol to reach even if one existed.

nodes.label: F5 in V2 each borrower chooses their own annual interest rate and may cha
nodes.text: in V2 each borrower chooses their own annual interest rate and may change it whenever they like, and that same rate fixes their place in the redemption queue: redemptions consume the lowest-rate positions in a branch first, ties broken last-in-first-redeemed
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the fourth of the four rate instruments this lane was sent to separate — the strangest of them, because IT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT THE PROTOCOL HOLDS AT ALL. The rate is simultaneously a cost and a queue position, so the borrower is buying insurance against redemption with the interest they volunteer to pay. Nothing in 58 symbols touches a price mechanism for redemption priority. Contrast the other three: Sky's bounded delegate writes one number for everyone (sky.json F5-F10), USDD's formula reads the outside world (usdd.json F6), Lista's controller reads the peg (lista-cdp.json F6). Here there is no number for the protocol to write, so a repair that adds 'a rate the protocol sets' would name three of the four and miss this one entirely.

nodes.label: F6 interest on each position is computed simply on its own recorded debt
nodes.text: interest on each position is computed simply on its own recorded debt at its own rate and compounded only when the position is touched, while the branch keeps two running aggregates so that pending interest for the whole branch can be computed without iterating positions
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a direct failure of Ix that the corpus does not record. accrued = recorded_debt x annual_rate x elapsed; the branch keeps weightedRecordedDebtSum and aggRecordedDebt. Ix reads 'a global index changes claim value', and there IS NO GLOBAL INDEX HERE — rates are heterogeneous across positions, so no single accumulator can value a claim, and the aggregates are a bookkeeping device for computing a total rather than an index that prices anybody's claim. Every other CDP in this category discharges accrual with Ix; Liquity V2 cannot, and the reason is F5. Stated invariant: 'Aggregate total debt of a branch always equals the sum of individual entire Trove debts.'

nodes.label: F7 anyone may exchange the stablecoin for collateral at face value at any
nodes.text: anyone may exchange the stablecoin for collateral at face value at any time, served from the riskiest positions first
nodes.note: EXACT for V1, and noted for contrast: this is the one protocol in the lane where Rd fits with no stretching, which suggests the symbol was written from it. But V1 and V2 are one corpus row under one Rd, and that hides the most interesting fact in the lane — see F5, F8 and F9. Same symbol, three different instruments.

nodes.label: F8 in V2 redemption volume is allocated across branches in proportion to
nodes.text: in V2 redemption volume is allocated across branches in proportion to each branch's debt minus that branch's own stability-pool deposits, so the least self-insured market absorbs the most redemption pressure
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A cross-market risk-allocation rule computed from an insurance-coverage statistic. Rd names a right against a system; Im names an isolated market; neither names a rule that routes pressure BETWEEN markets according to how well each has insured itself. CollateralRegistry holds the routing. This is the sharpening of the corpus's queue residue: the rate buys queue position within a branch (F5) and the branch's own self-insurance buys queue position across branches, so there are two priority mechanisms stacked and the vocabulary reaches neither.

nodes.label: F9 redemption carries a fee equal to half a per cent plus a base rate tha
nodes.text: redemption carries a fee equal to half a per cent plus a base rate that rises with redemption volume and decays on a six-hour half-life, and in V2 that fee is retained inside the redeemed borrower's collateral rather than paid to anyone
nodes.note: RESIDUE, new. min(0.5% + baseRate, 100%). Fd names surplus and fee DISTRIBUTION and presumes a recipient. Here the fee has NO RESIDUAL CLAIMANT AT ALL: it exists purely to make redemption unprofitable at the margin, and it lands back on the borrower it was charged against. In V1 the same fee went to stakers. A fee that is a deterrent rather than revenue is a different object from a fee that is revenue, and the vocabulary has one word for both. L29's demand for a declared residual claimant is discharged here by there being none.

nodes.label: F10 an opt-in pool of stablecoin depositors absorbs liquidated debt first:
nodes.text: an opt-in pool of stablecoin depositors absorbs liquidated debt first: the pool burns stablecoin equal to the debt and receives the collateral, so in normal conditions depositors profit from the event rather than losing by it
nodes.note: FORCED, and the mis-fit is instructive. The docs' worked example gives a depositor $21,800 of collateral against $20,000 of debt cancelled. Bs says 'slashable first-loss capital' and the word SLASHABLE INVERTS THE INCENTIVE: this is first-loss capital that is compensated rather than penalised, so it must be recruited by a return rather than bonded by a threat. V2 sharpens the mis-fit further — the pool now also receives a share of interest revenue (F20), so it earns a running yield ON TOP of the liquidation discount. A paid, yielding, opt-in first-loss class.

nodes.label: F11 if that pool cannot absorb the position, its debt and its collateral a
nodes.text: if that pool cannot absorb the position, its debt and its collateral are redistributed pro rata to every remaining borrower in the branch, who never opted in
nodes.note: FORCED. Sl names the socialisation and cannot distinguish OPT-IN loss absorption (F10) from CONSCRIPTED loss absorption (this), which are the two halves of Liquity's solvency design and carry opposite consent. V2 bounds the conscripted loss explicitly: up to 9.09% on the ether branch and 16.67% on the LST branches.

nodes.label: F12 the party who triggers a liquidation is paid the position's refundable
nodes.text: the party who triggers a liquidation is paid the position's refundable reserve plus a fixed fraction of its collateral
nodes.note: V1: the 200 LUSD reserve plus 0.5% of the collateral. Li fits the incentive. Liquity uses NO AUCTION anywhere — the only protocol of the five without one — so the Dutch-auction residue that Sky, USDD and Lista all carry is absent here by construction, and that absence is a positive fact about the design rather than a missing observation.

nodes.label: F13 in V2 liquidation is attempted in three ordered tiers with different p
nodes.text: in V2 liquidation is attempted in three ordered tiers with different payers and different penalties: offset against the stability pool at five per cent, then a just-in-time liquidation in which a liquidator supplies the stablecoin for a hundred and five per cent of the collateral value, then redistribution
nodes.note: RESIDUE, new. Li presumes ONE path paid to a third party. Here three paths are tried in a fixed order, the payer changes at each step (pooled depositors, then an outside liquidator, then every other borrower), and the penalty changes with the payer (5%, then a 5% spread to the liquidator, then up to 9.09%/16.67%). A liquidation WATERFALL is not a liquidation, and Tr — the only waterfall symbol — is about seniority over a loss event among claim classes, not about an ordered sequence of settlement attempts.

nodes.label: F14 in V1, when the system-wide total collateral ratio falls below one hun
nodes.text: in V1, when the system-wide total collateral ratio falls below one hundred and fifty per cent the whole system changes regime: positions under 150% become liquidatable, any transaction that would worsen the aggregate ratio is blocked, and the origination fee drops to zero to pull collateral in
nodes.note: RESIDUE, confirmed. Ct names a threshold test with a fixed parameter; nothing names THE PARAMETER ITSELF SWITCHING on an aggregate statistic, nor a transaction filter that admits an action only if it improves a global quantity, nor a fee that goes to zero as a countercyclical measure. Three mechanisms fire off one trigger and the vocabulary reaches none of them.

nodes.label: F15 in V2 each branch degrades on its own: below a critical ratio it block
nodes.text: in V2 each branch degrades on its own: below a critical ratio it blocks withdrawals, new debt and premature rate changes, and below a lower shutdown ratio it closes permanently to new borrowing and switches redemption to zero fee with a two per cent collateral bonus
nodes.note: RESIDUE, new. Critical ratio 150% ether / 160% LST; shutdown ratio 110% ether / 120% LST. Gp is REJECTED and the rejection is the finding: Gp names an emergency guardian or pause and PRESUMES A HOLDER, and this has none — the shutdown is a pure function of state, triggered by a measured ratio, with no key and no vote. It is also per-market rather than global, and it IMPROVES the redeemer's terms: where Sky's global settlement freezes the system (sky.json is silent on End, which its own docs now file under archive), this pays people to unwind the branch. A terminal state that is an incentive rather than a halt.

nodes.label: F16 a borrower may delegate the choice of their own interest rate to a reg
nodes.text: a borrower may delegate the choice of their own interest rate to a registered manager who declares a minimum and maximum band, may do nothing else whatsoever, and reprices the whole delegated set in one operation
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and THE SECOND INSTANCE OF THE FIVE-PART MANDATE IN THIS CATEGORY, with the principal changed. Slot 1 named agent: registered batch managers, live ones named in the docs (Summerstone, Trove Zero 0xe707784292289be3aa0fb6f9d33d420291f98695, Bolder Cash). Slot 2 bounded quantity: the interest rate and nothing else — 'delegates can do nothing else but set the interest rate in a predetermined range'. Slot 3 magnitude bounds: the declared min/max band, plus a Buffer Collateral Ratio adding margin above the minimum for batch members. Slots 4 and 5: see F17. Au is REJECTED under L17 — no expiry, no nonce, no domain separation. THE DIFFERENCE THAT MATTERS FOR STAGE 4: at Sky and Spark the principal is governance and the mandate is granted downward; here THE PRINCIPAL IS THE INDIVIDUAL BORROWER and the mandate is granted sideways, by one user over their own position. Same five slots, opposite direction of authority, and the vocabulary has no party sort to tell them apart. The batch is modelled as a virtual shared Trove for accrual, so one delegation also merges accounting.

nodes.label: F17 the option to reprice is itself priced: opening or changing a rate cos
nodes.text: the option to reprice is itself priced: opening or changing a rate costs seven days of the borrower's own chosen interest, changing it again within seven days costs a further fee, switching manager costs an upfront fee, and a manager's own annual fee can be lowered but never raised
nodes.note: RESIDUE, two new objects. (a) A commitment device denominated in the very parameter it governs: the cost of choosing a rate is seven days of that rate, so the fee scales with the choice. (b) A MONOTONE DELEGATED PARAMETER — the manager's fee is a one-way ratchet. Au bounds a delegated scope; nothing names a bound that can only tighten. These are mandate slots 4 and 5 in a form neither Sky nor Spark exhibits: the rate-of-change limit is a PRICE rather than a cap, and revocation is available always but PRICED, rather than free and held by a guardian. That the same five slots admit both a bound and a price is the strongest evidence in this lane that the repair belongs at a level above the element.

nodes.label: F18 a position redeemed below the minimum debt is not closed: it enters a
nodes.text: a position redeemed below the minimum debt is not closed: it enters a state in which it can no longer be redeemed against but still exists and still accrues interest
nodes.note: RESIDUE, new. Redemptions no longer close positions in V2, and a position redeemed to dust becomes a 'Zombie'. No symbol admits a terminal-but-not-closed position — a liability with no exit path that keeps growing. The nearest neighbours all presume a position is open or settled; this is a third state, and it is reachable by an action a third party takes without the owner's participation.

nodes.label: F19 the debt position is a transferable non-fungible token, so one address
nodes.text: the debt position is a transferable non-fungible token, so one address may hold many of them and any of them may be sold
nodes.note: RESIDUE, new. TroveNFT and NFTMetadata are shipped contracts. Nothing in the vocabulary says a LIABILITY IS ITSELF A TRADABLE OBJECT. Every credit symbol is written as a relation between a protocol and a borrower, with the borrower an address; here the borrower is a token holder, the position is an asset with a market, and liquidation risk can be sold. Contrast Sky, where the Staking Engine position is deliberately non-transferable (sky.json F24) — two protocols making opposite choices about the same property, decomposing identically.

nodes.label: F20 V1 emitted its governance token to stability-pool depositors and liqui
nodes.text: V1 emitted its governance token to stability-pool depositors and liquidity providers; V2 emits nothing and instead splits interest revenue between the stability pool and a router that funds liquidity for the stablecoin
nodes.note: Fd is CANDIDATE. DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS, which carries Em for the combined V1+V2 entity: V2's Protocol Incentivized Liquidity is funded from PROTOCOL REVENUE, not from token issuance, which is Fd-shaped, and carrying Em across both versions blurs a real change of funding source. Both symbols are carried here because the entity spans both versions, and the note is the finding: the same incentive with two different funding sources is two different sustainability claims.

nodes.label: F21 the contracts cannot be changed: V1 has no administrative key, no gove
nodes.text: the contracts cannot be changed: V1 has no administrative key, no governance and no upgrade path, and V2's core contracts are immutable and non-upgradeable while a governance system exists that can do exactly one thing
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and it needs THREE VALUES, not two. V1: 'no admin key... non-custodial, immutable, and governance-free'. V2: 'Governance has no other functions or powers, as Liquity V2's smart contracts are immutable and not upgradeable' — a strictly bounded mandate (direct incentives, nothing else) over contracts nobody can change. Recording either as the absence of Up, Tg and Gp is indistinguishable from 'I did not look', and recording both the same way erases the difference between genuine ungovernability and a governance system with one power. This is the same shortfall as Sky's 'fees cannot be enabled in the future' (sky.json F16): the vocabulary cannot state a FORECLOSED POWER, only an unobserved one. A CONTROL-PLANE FACT THE CORPUS HAS NO FIELD FOR: V2's core is Business Source License 1.1, licensor Liquity AG, change date 2027-09-01 to GPL-2.0-or-later, so it is source-available and not open source until then, while V1 is GPL-3.0 and V2-gov is MIT (gh api repos/liquity/bold/contents/LICENSE, accessed 2026-08-05). If any construction in the paper asserts permissionless forkability as a property of this category, this is the counterexample.

nodes.label: F22 the one governable quantity — a quarter of protocol revenue — is direc
nodes.text: the one governable quantity — a quarter of protocol revenue — is directed by stakers voting in weekly epochs, where voting power is the product of stake and staking age, new stake starts at zero power, withdrawal destroys power immediately, only downvotes are admitted in the last day, registering a recipient costs a fee and a fraction of total voting power, and a recipient must clear a threshold of votes to receive anything
nodes.note: Ep names the weekly Thursday-to-Wednesday epoch and the claim-in-the-same-week rule. Everything else is RESIDUE. (a) VOTING POWER = STAKE x STAKING AGE is a franchise that accrues with time held rather than with time locked, and it is a flash-loan defence rather than an alignment device; contested Ve is REJECTED because there is no escrow and no chosen lock duration. (b) A 2% eligibility threshold, a 100 BOLD registration fee and a 0.01%-of-total-voting-power registration cost are three distinct anti-spam prices on the franchise itself. (c) Voters may receive bribes from recipients, disclosed and expected. (d) 25% of revenue is the mandate's magnitude bound — mandate slot 3 again, this time bounding what a VOTE may direct rather than what an agent may write. Contracts: Governance.sol, BribeInitiative.sol, CurveV2GaugeRewards.sol, UniV4MerklRewards.sol, UserProxy.sol (github.com/liquity/V2-gov, MIT, accessed 2026-08-05). In 58 symbols this whole control plane is Ep, which is the lane's control-plane finding in its most extreme form.

nodes.label: Lista CDP
F1 a user deposits one of eight accepted collateral assets through a sing
nodes.text: a user deposits one of eight accepted collateral assets through a single front contract which routes it into the ledger and records the position, then borrows the stablecoin against it
nodes.note: A MakerDAO DSS fork behind a Helio-era front contract on BSC. Interaction is 'a proxy for MakerDAO contracts'; GemJoin is the collateral treasury; HayJoin mints and burns lisUSD; ListaDistributor snapshots debt for reward accounting. Live core: VAT 0x33A34eAB3ee892D40420507B820347b1cA2201c4, JUG 0x787BdEaa29A253e40feB35026c3d05C18CbCA7B3, DOG 0xd57E7b53a1572d27A04d9c1De2c4D423f1926d0B, CLIP 0x2dcFb02CE33955b6Cc0aF34033189DE3ac4C0292, lisUSD 0x0782b6d8c4551B9760e74c0545a9bCD90bdc41E5. Accepted collateral: BNB, ETH, slisBNB, wBETH, BTCB, FDUSD, wstETH, USDT, with per-collateral modules deployed for eleven assets.

nodes.label: F2 the position must remain above a per-collateral ratio, and each collat
nodes.text: the position must remain above a per-collateral ratio, and each collateral type carries a debt cap set by vote
nodes.note: The DSS test with spot written from the oracle of F3. Collateral rates and debt caps are named as governable in the governance page (https://docs.bsc.lista.org/governance/lista/governance.md, accessed 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F3 each collateral is priced by an external oracle contract deployed on t
nodes.text: each collateral is priced by an external oracle contract deployed on two chains
nodes.note: Resilient Oracle at 0xf3afD82A4071f272F403dC176916141f44E6c750 (BNB Chain) and 0xA64FE284EB8279B9b63946DD51813b0116099301 (Ethereum).

nodes.label: F4 that price is taken from an ordered chain of providers — a main source
nodes.text: that price is taken from an ordered chain of providers — a main source, a pivot and a fallback, drawn from four independent networks and differing per asset — and is then checked against a hard per-asset band and rejected outright if it falls outside it
nodes.note: RESIDUE, new and not in the corpus. Chainlink, RedStone (including OEV feeds), Atlas and the Binance Oracle; BNB is RedStone OEV main, Atlas pivot, Chainlink fallback; a BoundValidator enforces per-asset upper and lower bounds, typically 1.01 and 0.99. Ex names 'external data oracle (push/pull/medianizer)'. Nothing names an ORDERED FALLBACK CHAIN — which is a failover policy with a defined degradation order, not an aggregation — and nothing names a PREDICATE THAT REJECTS A PRICE rather than incorporating it. L13 asks for freshness validation and gets validity validation, which is a different check with a different failure mode: a medianiser degrades gracefully under a bad feed and a rejecting validator halts.

nodes.label: F5 debt accrues by a per-collateral accumulator folded across the ledger
nodes.text: debt accrues by a per-collateral accumulator folded across the ledger
nodes.note: JUG 0x787BdEaa29A253e40feB35026c3d05C18CbCA7B3, the DSS accumulator unchanged. Ix names the accrual and is blind to the level, which at Lista is set by F6.

nodes.label: F6 the borrow rate is recomputed every fifteen minutes, and on any user i
nodes.text: the borrow rate is recomputed every fifteen minutes, and on any user interaction, as an exponential function of the deviation of the stablecoin's price from one dollar read from an exchange oracle, parameterised per collateral by a base rate and an amplification factor, and clipped at twenty per cent
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the third of the four rate instruments this lane was sent to separate: a CLOSED-LOOP CONTROLLER ON PEG ERROR. Explicitly modelled on Curve's MonetaryPolicy. Worked example in the docs: at $0.98 with r0 = 8% and Beta = 2% the rate becomes about 21.746%, then clipped by the 20% cap; r0 itself is capped at 200%. REFUTATION, with evidence, of a recorded corpus residue: the corpus assigns Lista 'the same interest-rate-as-policy gap' as Sky. NO ONE VOTES ON THIS RATE. The gap Lista arms is the crvUSD gap the corpus records one row later — 'no element for a rate controller that reads the peg and sets the borrow rate automatically' — not the Sky gap. Nothing discharges it: As is quantity toward a peg rather than price; Ex supplies the input and does not name the feedback law; Ix names the accrual and not the level. Initial parameters were set by the core team with future changes routed to governance, so the CONTROLLER'S GAINS are governed while its OUTPUT is not — a two-level structure no symbol reaches.

nodes.label: F7 anyone, including the borrower, may trigger a liquidation; the trigger
nodes.text: anyone, including the borrower, may trigger a liquidation; the trigger is paid a fixed reward of five units of the stablecoin plus a proportional reward set by governance, paid both for the initial trigger and for each restart, and the debt to be covered is grossed up by a ten per cent penalty
nodes.note: REFUTATION, with evidence, of a recorded corpus residue. The corpus records 'no element for gas-compensation-only liquidation incentives (the liquidator's reward is a gas rebate, not a collateral discount, which changes who shows up)'. THE DOCS SPECIFY A FIXED tip OF 5 lisUSD PLUS A GOVERNANCE-SET PROPORTIONAL chip, WITH A 10% PENALTY ON THE DEBT — the standard DSS chip/tip structure Sky uses, with the docs' own worked example grossing $13.2 of debt to a $14.52 auction target. The claim that Lista's liquidator receives only a gas rebate is not supported and the residue should be struck. The corpus's marker 'Li FORCED twice over' should accordingly be reduced to the single Dutch-auction objection recorded at F8.

nodes.label: F8 the seized collateral is sold by an auction that opens at the unit pri
nodes.text: the seized collateral is sold by an auction that opens at the unit price times 1.02 and declines linearly toward zero over a fixed horizon, pauses when it has run past a time bound or fallen about forty per cent, and must then be restarted by someone who is paid for restarting it
nodes.note: RESIDUE. top = unit price x 1.02, top x ((tau - dur)/tau), paused at tail or cusp (~40%). Reachable only through the contested symbol Da, which this lane declines to use. CROSS-PROTOCOL: the same engine as sky.json F12 and usdd.json F10 — same descent, same tail/cusp reset, same restart reward. Three of the five protocols in this category run one settlement implementation, which is a stronger argument for promoting Da than a usage count: promoting it would let the algebra see a shared engine rather than a shared style. Lista's Abaci is deployed twice (0xc1359eD77E6B0CBF9a8130a4C28FBbB87B9501b7 and a separate CLASSIC 0xbaf8b40a), so even the descent curve is per-vintage.

nodes.label: F9 the stablecoin is minted one-for-one against two named reserve stablec
nodes.text: the stablecoin is minted one-for-one against two named reserve stablecoins out of a pre-minted facility
nodes.note: USDT and USDC; launch cap 5M lisUSD pre-minted into the PSM contract. The only par exit: Rd is correctly ABSENT, so L7 is discharged through Ps alone — and F10 shows how much weight that single discharge is carrying.

nodes.label: F10 that swap is free in one direction and taxed two per cent in the other
nodes.text: that swap is free in one direction and taxed two per cent in the other, is capped in size, is subject to a daily redemption ceiling of five hundred thousand units, and is documented as taxed on exit in order to push exit onto a third-party automated market maker
nodes.note: RESIDUE, new and not in the corpus. Ps names a 1:1 reserve-backed swap. A gate that is free one way, taxed the other, capped per day, and designed to EXTERNALISE ITS OWN EXIT LIQUIDITY onto PancakeSwap is a materially different instrument, and the asymmetry is the instrument: it prices the exit and outsources it. The mint fee is 0% 'at launch' with the docs stating it may be introduced in 0.01% increments if the unit trades at a premium — a second administered price, discretionary and unbounded in the documentation. The daily ceiling is the same magnitude-per-time envelope as ethena.json F5 and sky.json F11. Against L7 this is the sharpest stress in the lane: the only par exit for a $324M unit is fee-gated at 2% and quota'd at 500k/day.

nodes.label: F11 the protocol mints its stablecoin unbacked, directly into two third-pa
nodes.text: the protocol mints its stablecoin unbacked, directly into two third-party lending markets, to seed liquidity there, and takes the returns into its own treasury
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and a DEPARTURE: the corpus carries neither As nor Cd for this behaviour. The docs call it 'credit-based minting' into Venus Core Pool and Aave. As is 'algorithmic supply adjustment' and this is supply created by rule rather than against collateral, so the fit is real; but everywhere else in the corpus As is read as rebase or seigniorage against holder balances, and this is one-sided unbacked minting into a venue. Flagged rather than asserted. The corpus's own note that the D3M is 'closer to As than to Cd' is followed here.

nodes.label: F12 the solvency of that minted supply then depends on two lending markets
nodes.text: the solvency of that minted supply then depends on two lending markets the protocol neither operates nor governs, and the rates its unit earns on those markets are themselves managed by its own controller
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The corpus records this gap only for Sky/Spark; it appears here too, in a protocol an order of magnitude smaller, against venues (Venus, Aave) that Lista neither operates nor governs. This is the containment relation the intents and yield lanes independently found: a protocol whose balance sheet is a position in another protocol. Composition in this corpus is the union of element sets between peers, and there is no relation for one protocol consuming another — so 'Lista mints into Aave' and 'Lista and Aave both use Ix' are the same statement in the carrier.

nodes.label: F13 a holder may deposit the stablecoin into a savings pool that compounds
nodes.text: a holder may deposit the stablecoin into a savings pool that compounds per block, capped at thirty million units
nodes.note: Jar 0x0a1Fd12F73432928C190CAF0810b3B767A59717e manages staking and interest distribution. The 30M pool cap is another magnitude envelope, this time on a savings product.

nodes.label: F14 the rate that pool pays is a fixed number adjusted by hand, inside the
nodes.text: the rate that pool pays is a fixed number adjusted by hand, inside the same protocol whose borrow rate is set by a closed-loop controller
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a refinement of the lane's central finding that stage 4 should not lose. THE FOUR RATE INSTRUMENTS ARE NOT ONE PER PROTOCOL. Lista runs a controller on the borrow side (F6) and an administered number on the savings side, simultaneously, on the two sides of the same balance sheet. Sky does the same in reverse — one bounded delegate writing all three of its rates (sky.json F6-F10). So the taxonomy is a property of the INSTRUMENT, not of the protocol, and a repair that attaches one rate mechanism to one application will get Lista wrong.

nodes.label: F15 a saver withdraws immediately if pool liquidity allows and otherwise w
nodes.text: a saver withdraws immediately if pool liquidity allows and otherwise within fourteen days
nodes.note: DEPARTURE: the corpus carries no queue element for Lista. Wq names the deferred exit; L14 (illiquid backing -> Wq | bounded liquidity reserve) is discharged. What Wq does not name is the CONDITIONAL structure — immediate when liquid, queued when not — which is two different products under one deposit.

nodes.label: F16 borrowers are paid the protocol's governance token for holding debt
nodes.text: borrowers are paid the protocol's governance token for holding debt
