nodes.note: 'Claim rewards in LISTA for borrowing lisUSD' — an emission paid for taking on a liability, which inverts the sign of the borrow rate of F6 for anyone who values the token. The two prices are set by different mechanisms and the vocabulary cannot net them: Em and the missing rate element do not compose.

nodes.label: F17 parameters are changed by an off-chain vote on a hosted platform in wh
nodes.text: parameters are changed by an off-chain vote on a hosted platform in which only core team members may submit a proposal, voting runs three days, a proposal passes on more than half of the tokens cast, and implementation follows by hand one to two weeks later
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE: the corpus carries Tg for Lista and this construction drops it. Snapshot at snapshot.org/#/listavote.eth. NO TIMELOCK IS DOCUMENTED AND NO VOTE IS ON-CHAIN. In the 58 symbols this whole arrangement decomposes to Gp and nothing else, which makes it indistinguishable from a timelocked on-chain DAO with an emergency pause. The absence of Tg reads as 'no timelock found' rather than 'governance is not on-chain at all', and those are opposite epistemic states. Governable per the same page: withdrawal and unlock fees, new collateral, collateral rates and debt caps, protocol fee sharing, and emission allocation — note that this list does NOT include the borrow rate, which F6 sets mechanically.

nodes.label: F18 the core team retains a right to pause contracts and to reject unsafe
nodes.text: the core team retains a right to pause contracts and to reject unsafe gauges without a poll, subject only to an obligation to explain
nodes.note: FORCED. Gp names an emergency pause. It does not name a VETO — a standing right to overrule the outcome of the franchise of F17 — which is a different authority with a different holder and a different justification. Combined with core-team-only proposal rights, the franchise is bounded on both ends by the same party, and the vocabulary records one bit. UNKNOWN, flagged for stage 3: the upgradeability and proxy structure of the CDP contracts is not documented at any page reached, although the archived source repository contains an upgrade/ directory. The corpus carries Up for Lista; it is dropped here for want of a citation, not because a proxy is believed absent.

nodes.label: F19 the protocol accepts its own liquid-staking receipt as one of the asse
nodes.text: the protocol accepts its own liquid-staking receipt as one of the assets backing its own stablecoin, so that one of its products' liabilities is another of its products' collateral
nodes.note: RESIDUE, confirmed but NARROWER than the corpus records. slisBNB is one of eight accepted collaterals, not 'the primary collateral'; per-collateral modules exist for eleven assets, and the weight slisBNB actually carries is not established by anything in the record. The reflexivity is real and its magnitude is UNKNOWN. Cd names the mint and nothing names the correlation between the collateral's solvency and the issuer's, so the risk is invisible rather than mis-stated. Prohibition X3 (protocol token as collateral AND oracle market AND backstop) is NOT armed — slisBNB is a staking receipt on BNB, not the governance token.

nodes.label: F20 a shortfall the auction did not cover is booked against the system's s
nodes.text: a shortfall the auction did not cover is booked against the system's surplus and deficit account
nodes.note: FORCED and thinly evidenced, as at USDD. The only citation is the deployed VOW at 0x2078A1969Ea581D618FDBEa2C0Dc13Fc15CB9fa7 in the published address table; no Lista page describes deficit handling, surplus auctions or debt auctions. Carried because the DSS skeleton cannot function without it; flagged so stage 3 weighs it below Sky's identically shaped obligation. NOTE ON THE REPOSITORY, which the corpus has no field for: the source of this live $324M system is lista-dao/lista-dao-contracts, ARCHIVED, carrying NO LICENCE, with a README that still opens '# HELIO' and describes borrowing DAI against a MakerDAO vault, while all current engineering happens in repositories that do not contain the CDP (gh api repos/lista-dao/lista-dao-contracts, accessed 2026-08-05).

nodes.label: Sky (Sky Lending, ex-MakerDAO)
F1 a user locks an approved collateral asset under a named collateral typ
nodes.text: a user locks an approved collateral asset under a named collateral type and draws a newly issued stablecoin liability against it, recorded as normalised debt in one global ledger whose stated invariant is that the stablecoin cannot exist without collateral
nodes.note: Vat holds ilks(Art, rate, spot, line, dust) and urns(ink, art); frob adjusts a position, fork splits it, grab confiscates it, fold advances the accumulator, suck/heal create and cancel unbacked stablecoin. Documented invariant: total debt = vice + sum over ilks of (Art x rate). Collateral enters through Join adapters.

nodes.label: F2 a position may not be adjusted into a state where its debt exceeds its
nodes.text: a position may not be adjusted into a state where its debt exceeds its collateral valued at a safety-margined price, and its size is additionally bounded by a per-position debt floor, a per-collateral-type ceiling and a global ceiling
nodes.note: Ct names the ratio test (art x rate <= ink x spot). It does not name dust, line or Line. Those ceilings are the instrument Sky actually uses to size a market, and the same object reappears as the Star credit line in F20 and as the liquidation throughput cap in F11. A quantity envelope on a permitted action recurs four times in this lane and has no symbol.

nodes.label: F3 the safety-margined price of each collateral type is written from a pe
nodes.text: the safety-margined price of each collateral type is written from a per-collateral oracle that publishes a current and a queued next price one hour apart, readable only by whitelisted contracts, writable only by whitelisted feeds, and stoppable
nodes.note: hop = 3600s, peek()/peep()/poke(), a wards mapping for admin and a buds whitelist for readers, with stop() and void() as kill switches; Spot reads the OSM and writes ilk.spot. Tp is REJECTED: a queued next price is a one-hour delay, not a time-weighted average, and the two have different manipulation profiles. The docs disclose a timing weakness the symbol cannot carry: poke() becomes callable when block.timestamp/hop increments, not a full hop after the last call. DEPARTURE: the corpus carries At for RWA vault backing, marked FORCED because 'the attestation is a PDF and a legal entity'. Stage 1 confirms PIP_* RWA keys in the ChainLog but records no on-chain attestation object, so At is not carried here; L27 (named attester, independence, stated assurance, staleness bound, recourse) cannot be checked from the evidence in hand. UNKNOWN, flagged for stage 3.

nodes.label: F4 debt accrues continuously by a per-second compounding rate accumulator
nodes.text: debt accrues continuously by a per-second compounding rate accumulator that is advanced by a permissionless call and folded across every position of a collateral type at once, so no per-position interest is ever written
nodes.note: Jug.drip(ilk) computes base + duty and calls Vat.fold. The docs warn that rate(base + duty) != rate(base) + rate(duty), i.e. the two components do not compose additively — a fact about the accumulator that Ix, which names only 'a global index changes claim value', cannot state. Read on-chain 2026-08-04: Jug.base = 0, so the whole fee is the per-ilk duty.

nodes.label: F5 the level of the borrow rate, of the savings rate and of the savings-r
nodes.text: the level of the borrow rate, of the savings rate and of the savings-reserve rate is a written number: no utilisation curve, market, auction, target or measured quantity derives it anywhere in the system
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and this is the category's headline gap in its Sky form. The Stability register holds Rd, Ps and As — a redemption right, a 1:1 swap and quantity adjustment. There is no price-of-credit instrument at all, and the price of credit is Sky's primary peg lever in both directions: raise the fee to contract supply, raise the savings rate to create demand. Ix names the accrual and is blind to the level; As names the wrong instrument (quantity, not price). Read on-chain 2026-08-04 via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com against ChainLog addresses: Pot.dsr = 1000000000393915525145987602 ray (~1.25%/yr), sUSDS.ssr = 1000000001096988989836188433 ray (~3.52%/yr), stUSDS rate = 1000000001940295800728849590 ray (~6.31%/yr). Three simultaneous administered prices for the same issuer's liabilities.

nodes.label: F6 an agent named in an on-chain permission set, which governance may add
nodes.text: an agent named in an on-chain permission set, which governance may add to or remove from at any time, may write those rates directly and in batches, with no executive vote and no governance delay
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 1 — the named agent. PARTIAL FIT. MCD_SPBEAM (0x36B072ed8AFE665E3Aa6DaBa79Decbec63752b22), the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module, deployed by the 2025-04-17 executive spell (archive/2025-04-17-DssSpell/dependencies/sp-beam/SPBEAMInit.sol in sky-ecosystem/spells-mainnet). Aw names the caller enumeration and its mutability; it does not name that what is granted is a discretionary economic authority rather than a right to participate. Au is REJECTED: L17 requires bounded scope + revocation + expiry + nonce/domain separation, i.e. a session key over the principal's own assets; a facilitator has no expiry, no nonce, and acts over the whole system's economics. This is the same slot the yield lane found at Spark (spark-savings.json F5) and at MetaMorpho, bounding an allocation instead of a rate.

nodes.label: F7 that agent may write only parameters drawn from an enumerated set of r
nodes.text: that agent may write only parameters drawn from an enumerated set of rate identifiers, each with its own configuration record, and cannot touch debt ceilings, collateral onboarding, liquidation parameters or anything else
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 2 — the bounded quantity. RESIDUE. The bounded quantity here is a rate: per-ilk duty, the DSR and the SSR. Live ids include 'SSR', 'DSR' and per-ilk stability fees. No symbol restricts a delegated decision to a domain. In the yield lane the identical slot bounded a venue list (spark-savings.json F18, twenty-nine enumerated actions) and a collateral list (MetaMorpho). Same slot, different quantity — which is the evidence that this is a schema over elements, not an element.

nodes.label: F8 each value the agent writes must lie between a governance-set floor an
nodes.text: each value the agent writes must lie between a governance-set floor and ceiling for that identifier, and a write outside the band reverts
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call cfgs('SSR') on 0x36B072ed8AFE665E3Aa6DaBa79Decbec63752b22 = {min 200, max 3000, step 400}, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 3 — the magnitude bounds. RESIDUE. Live band for the savings rate is 2% to 30%. Ct is a solvency test, not a parameter envelope; there is no symbol for a numeric domain restriction on a delegated decision. INHERITED READ: the live cfgs tuple was read by lane 06 and is recorded at C:\defiformal-work\06-yield-vaults\02-decomp\spark-savings.json F8; this lane did not re-read it. Stage 1 for this lane establishes the min/max/step structure from the repository README (https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/sp-beam, accessed 2026-08-05) without the numeric values.

nodes.label: F9 a single update may move a rate by at most a governance-set step, and
nodes.text: a single update may move a rate by at most a governance-set step, and no update may occur within a cooldown of the previous one; the update then takes effect immediately
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 4 — the rate-of-change limit. RESIDUE. Live step for the savings rate is 4 percentage points; live tau is 16 hours. Tg is wrong twice over: tau is a cooldown SINCE the last change, not a delay BEFORE execution, and the agent's write does not pass the governance pause that gates governance's own actions (F22). Ep is wrong: there are no periods, only a minimum spacing. INHERITED READ, as F8.

nodes.label: F10 the whole rate-setting module can be disabled by a dedicated contract
nodes.text: the whole rate-setting module can be disabled by a dedicated contract and by a pre-deployed emergency transaction, neither of which waits for the governance delay, after which no agent may write anything
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 5 — revocation. PARTIAL FIT. SPBEAM_MOM disables the module without the GSM delay; EMSP_SPBEAM_HALT (src/spbeam-halt/SPBEAMHaltSpell.sol) is the pre-deployed circuit breaker. Gp names the kill switch and not the mandate it kills, and it cannot express that the right to halt is deliberately held by a different party from the right to act — the accountability design. Five slots, five obligations, one element and two partial fits: F6 Aw and F10 Gp. F7, F8 and F9 are empty. That is the measurement this lane was asked for.

nodes.label: F11 any party may confiscate an unsafe position by a permissionless call w
nodes.text: any party may confiscate an unsafe position by a permissionless call which books the debt to the balance sheet and starts a settlement, is paid a flat fee plus a proportion of the debt for doing so, and charges the position owner a penalty
nodes.note: Dog.bark(); keeper paid tip (flat) + chip (proportional) from the Vow; owner charged chop. The docs explicitly warn that mis-calibration of tip and chip enables farming attacks — an incentive-design hazard Li cannot carry. SECOND RESIDUE INSIDE THIS OBLIGATION: simultaneous auction exposure is capped globally (Hole) and per collateral type (hole) against running totals (Dirt, dirt), so liquidation throughput is bounded independently of solvency. That is a magnitude cap on a safety-critical action — mandate slot 3 with no agent — and it has no symbol. It is the same object as Ethena's per-block issuance ceiling (ethena.json F5) and Spark's regenerating allowance (spark-savings.json F19). Stated invariants: sum of per-ilk dirt = global Dirt; auction collateral <= Vat gem balances.

nodes.label: F12 settlement clears by a descending price: the auction opens above the o
nodes.text: settlement clears by a descending price: the auction opens above the oracle price, falls along a chosen curve, is bought atomically at the current price with an optional callback so the buyer needs no capital of their own, and is reset by anyone once it has run past a time bound or fallen below a price bound
nodes.note: RESIDUE. One Clipper per ilk: kick() at OSM price x buf, take() with a clipperCallee callback, redo() past tail or below cusp, chost = ilk.dust x ilk.chop to prevent dust remainders, descent by LinearDecrease / StairstepExponentialDecrease / ExponentialDecrease. Reachable only through the contested symbol Da, which the corpus declined to use and which this lane also declines to use, recording the behaviour here instead. CROSS-PROTOCOL: this is the same implementation, down to the parameter names buf/tail/cusp/chip/tip/chost/chop and the kick/take/redo interface, at USDD (usdd.json F10) and Lista (lista-cdp.json F8). Three of the five share a settlement engine, not merely a settlement style — which is a stronger argument for promoting Da than the 3-of-5 usage count the corpus recorded.

nodes.label: F13 debt a settlement did not cover is queued against the balance sheet fo
nodes.text: debt a settlement did not cover is queued against the balance sheet for a fixed waiting period and then charged against the protocol's surplus
nodes.note: FORCED. Vow queues bad debt as sin[timestamp] for wait seconds, released by flog; heal and kiss cancel surplus against debt. Sl reads 'loss assigned to a claim class'. Here the loss lands first on the issuer's own balance sheet, which is not a claim class, and only reaches a class if the surplus is exhausted and the debt auction of F14 fires. Sl cannot distinguish a loss absorbed by the issuer from a loss allocated to holders.

nodes.label: F14 the balance sheet mechanically converts imbalance into an auction in b
nodes.text: the balance sheet mechanically converts imbalance into an auction in both directions: surplus above a high-water mark is sold off in fixed lots, and a deficit beyond a fixed lot triggers an auction of newly issued governance tokens for the stablecoin
nodes.note: RESIDUE, two distinct gaps in one mechanism. (a) A buffer with a high-water mark (hump) and a fixed lot (bump) that mechanically triggers an auction has no symbol. (b) Recapitalisation by governance-token dilution has no symbol: Sl assigns a loss to a class, Bs pre-stakes capital to be slashed, and neither says new equity is issued against the loss after the fact, which is a materially different promise to token holders. Both auction paths are deployed: MCD_FLAP 0x374D9c3d5134052Bc558F432Afa1df6575f07407 and MCD_FLOP 0xA41B6EF151E06da0e34B009B86E828308986736D. UNKNOWN, and it matters: the Vow page still says flop mints MKR and that dump is 'the starting amount of MKR offered', but MCD_ADM is Chief V3 on SKY and MKR converts one-way to SKY at 1:24,000. Which token a debt auction actually mints must be read on-chain before either is asserted.

nodes.label: F15 the surplus lot is split by a fixed fraction between a leg that buys t
nodes.text: the surplus lot is split by a fixed fraction between a leg that buys the governance token on an external AMM and redeposits both sides as protocol-owned liquidity, and a leg that funds a rewards contract, with acceptable slippage bounded against a reference oracle
nodes.note: Fd is CANDIDATE and FORCED: MCD_SPLIT withdraws vow.bump every hop seconds and divides it by burn; FlapperUniV2 swaps the stablecoin for the gem and then deposits BOTH sides back as LP to a receiver, so the 'burn' leg becomes protocol-owned liquidity rather than destroyed supply, while FlapperUniV2SwapOnly buys and forwards. Fd cannot distinguish burn, distribute and become-an-LP — three different claims on the same surplus with three different effects on float. Em covers the farm leg. want bounds slippage against FLAP_SKY_ORACLE 0xc2ffbb; SPLITTER_MOM and EMSP_SPLITTER_STOP can stop the whole route without governance delay.

nodes.label: F16 a holder may deposit the stablecoin into a share token whose nominal b
nodes.text: a holder may deposit the stablecoin into a share token whose nominal balance never changes and whose redemption value rises by its own per-second accumulator, with no fee, and with fees that cannot be enabled later
nodes.note: sUSDS is ERC-4626 with real-time share/asset conversion even between drips. DEPARTURE: the corpus carries Ix for Sky but not Sh, while carrying Sh for the identically shaped sUSDe. 'Fees cannot be enabled on this route in the future' is a negative commitment written into the contract; the vocabulary has no way to record a foreclosed power, which is the same shortfall the options lane hit as discharge-by-construction and Liquity hits as immutability (liquity.json F21).

nodes.label: F17 the stablecoin swaps one-for-one against a named reserve stablecoin th
nodes.text: the stablecoin swaps one-for-one against a named reserve stablecoin through a module holding pre-minted inventory, so a swap is two token transfers rather than a ledger operation, currently at zero fee in both directions
nodes.note: MCD_LITE_PSM_USDC_A 0xf6e72Db5454dd049d0788e411b06CfAF16853042 with its POCKET, JAR and LITE_PSM_MOM. tin and tout are not activated for either route but 'could change in the future' — a live fee of zero and a governable fee of zero are the same number and different instruments, and Ps carries neither. This is the sole par exit for the unit: Rd is correctly ABSENT for Sky, so law L7 (Cd -> Rd | Ps | liquidation capacity) is satisfied through Ps alone.

nodes.label: F18 the issuer maintains two of its own liabilities simultaneously, conver
nodes.text: the issuer maintains two of its own liabilities simultaneously, converts between them one-for-one and permissionlessly, and pays a different savings rate on each
nodes.note: RESIDUE. DAI at ~1.25% and USDS at ~3.52%, converted 1:1 at will through a permissionless converter over UsdsJoin/DaiJoin, with DAI_USDS 0x3225737a. Ps names a 1:1 swap backed by a RESERVE; here both sides are the issuer's own obligations and the rate spread is the migration incentive — the swap is a monetary-policy instrument, not a stability instrument. The same object appears at USDD as a Migrate contract off a deprecated liability (usdd.json F16).

nodes.label: F19 the savings claim and the stablecoin are issued on other domains as to
nodes.text: the savings claim and the stablecoin are issued on other domains as tokens minted and burned against the mainnet position
nodes.note: SUSDS_OFT and sky-oapp-oft; STARKNET_ESCROW_MOM sits in the ChainLog as a domain-specific defensive key. Lane 06 established that the remote savings claim carries no accrual state and is redeemable only against local peg-module inventory, so the two claims are not economically identical (spark-savings.json F16); Xf asserts a transfer and cannot record that the remote claim has a weaker settlement guarantee than the local one.

nodes.label: F20 a sub-entity receives its own collateral type backed by an oracle that
nodes.text: a sub-entity receives its own collateral type backed by an oracle that returns a constant price, purely so that a nominal collateral balance makes its debt ceiling reachable, and its operators then draw and repay the stablecoin into an off-protocol buffer with no vote and no delay, whitelisted per action and rate-limited
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and larger than the corpus records: eight allocator vault/buffer pairs are live in the ChainLog (SPARK, GROVE, BLOOM, INTERVAL, NOVA, OBEX, PATTERN, PRYSM), each with a sub-proxy and a StarGuard payload whitelist. Two gaps at once. (a) A credit line to a sub-entity that deploys the proceeds off-protocol has no symbol; Cd is wrong because there is no economic collateral. (b) AllocatorOracle is a deliberately uninformative oracle used as plumbing — Ex, Tp, Oa and At all presume the oracle carries information about the world, and this one is a constant 1:1 by design. The four actor tiers (Pause Proxy with the GSM delay, AllocatorDAO Proxy with its own delay, Operator with no spell and no delay inside rate limits, Keeper) are mandate slots 1 to 4 again, this time bounding a credit facility.

nodes.label: F21 the franchise is exercised by locking the governance token into an app
nodes.text: the franchise is exercised by locking the governance token into an approval-voting contract and approving a slate; the slate holding the most approvals is promoted, and only the promoted address may schedule an action
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and this is the control-plane gap the lane was told to write out. MCD_ADM 0x929d9A1435662357F54AdcF64DcEE4d6b867a6f9 is DSChief V3; lock/free against IOU tokens; vote(address[]) or vote(bytes32) over an etch'd slate; lift(whom) requires approvals[whom] > approvals[hat]. THE VOTING TOKEN IS SKY, NOT MKR, and MKR converts one way at 1 MKR -> 24,000 SKY through 0xA1Ea1bA18E88C381C724a75F23a130420C403f9a; converting back requires an external exchange. Nothing in 58 symbols names a voting rule, a franchise, a quorum or a threshold. There is no fixed quorum here at all — the threshold is whatever the incumbent slate currently holds, which is a materially different governance risk from a fixed quorum and is invisible to the vocabulary. Contested Ve is REJECTED: DSChief locks without time-weighting and without escrow duration, so it is not vote-escrow.

nodes.label: F22 every governance action executes only as a plan scheduled at least a f
nodes.text: every governance action executes only as a plan scheduled at least a fixed delay in the future, run by delegatecall from an isolated proxy after checking the target's code hash, and the delay itself can be changed only through a plan, so it cannot be shortened faster than the delay
nodes.note: MCD_PAUSE 0xbE28 is DSPause: plan = {usr, tag, fax, eta}, plot schedules with eta >= now + delay, exec checks the code hash against tag, drop cancels; execution runs in MCD_PAUSE_PROXY 0xBE8E3e whose isolated storage protects the pause. Up covers the UUPS/ERC-1967 proxies over sUSDS and stUSDS whose administrator is that proxy, so L15 (Up -> Tg) is satisfied. Live delay 172800s (48h) per the on-chain read recorded at C:\defiformal-work\06-yield-vaults\02-decomp\spark-savings.json F11; not re-read by this lane. Tg names the delay and not its holder: the vocabulary has no party sort, so 'a 48-hour delay held by a plurality-elected hat' and 'a 48-hour delay held by a 2-of-3 multisig' are the same symbol.

nodes.label: F23 ten dedicated contracts hold narrowly scoped defensive powers — stop a
nodes.text: ten dedicated contracts hold narrowly scoped defensive powers — stop an oracle, freeze liquidations, lower a debt ceiling, halt the rate setter, stop the splitter, disable a direct-deposit module — which execute immediately and bypass the delay, and a standing library of pre-deployed single-purpose emergency transactions exists to be executed rather than written
nodes.note: FORCED, and this is the sharpest control-plane residue in the lane. CLIPPER_MOM, OSM_MOM, LINE_MOM, LITE_PSM_MOM, DIRECT_MOM, SPLITTER_MOM, SPBEAM_MOM, STUSDS_MOM, STARKNET_ESCROW_MOM plus thirteen EMSP_* spells and factories. The structural fact is that the delay's LENGTH DEPENDS ON THE SIGN OF THE CHANGE: making the system safer is instant, making it riskier waits 48 hours. Tg names a delay and Gp names a pause; neither names a directionally asymmetric delay, and that asymmetry is the whole design of Sky's control plane rather than an accessory to it. Nor does any symbol name a standing library of pre-audited governance transactions. The liquidation circuit breaker alone has four escalating states — all enabled, no new liquidations, no resets, complete freeze — where Gp offers one bit.

nodes.label: F24 the governance token is itself locked as collateral to borrow the stab
nodes.text: the governance token is itself locked as collateral to borrow the stablecoin while its owner retains delegable voting power over the protocol that holds it, and a separate savings class documented as taking a greater share of system risk funds that borrowing at a higher rate
nodes.note: DEPARTURE: the corpus carries neither Cd-on-the-governance-token nor Tr for Sky. LOCKSTAKE_ENGINE 0xCe01C9 with LOCKSTAKE_SKY, LOCKSTAKE_CLIP and LOCKSTAKE_ORACLE; the borrow position is non-transferable and the receipt token is non-transferable, but the voting power stays delegable (https://developers.skyeco.com/protocol/rewards/staking-engine/, accessed 2026-08-04). Tr is FORCED: stUSDS 0x99CD4Ec3f88A45940936F469E4bB72A2A701EEB9 is documented as the 'first Expert token' taking 'a greater share of system risk' at ~6.31%/yr against sUSDS's ~3.52%, but there are no attachment points and the seniority is documented rather than settled by a waterfall contract. TWO PROHIBITIONS TO CHECK AT STAGE 3: X3 (protocol token as collateral AND oracle market AND backstop) is partially armed — SKY is collateral, LOCKSTAKE_ORACLE prices it, and the FLOP path makes it the recapitalisation asset; X6 (borrowable voting power + immediate execution) is armed on its first conjunct and disarmed by the 48-hour pause of F22.

nodes.label: USDD
F1 a user opens a vault under one of a small set of named collateral type
nodes.text: a user opens a vault under one of a small set of named collateral types and mints the stablecoin against it in a ledger whose operations are slip, frob, grab, fold and file
nodes.note: A near-verbatim Multi-Collateral Dai fork: Vat, Dog, Clip, Spot, Jug, Median, OSM, a user Proxy, PSM and Migrate, with DSS's own function signatures. Live collateral types on TRON are TRX-A, TRX-B, TRX-C, sTRX-A, USDT-A, PSM-USDT and SA001-A. UNKNOWN: SA001-A appears in the published collateral address list (TXdYNjXaHn3c1whomRpzCkaFbjfCffMFGf, https://docs.usdd.io/introduction/collateral-asset-contract-addresses.md, accessed 2026-08-04) with no explanation anywhere in the documentation, so the collateral set cannot be asserted complete.

nodes.label: F2 a vault must stay above a minimum collateralisation the documentation
nodes.text: a vault must stay above a minimum collateralisation the documentation says varies with the volatility of the asset
nodes.note: The test is DSS's art x rate <= ink x spot with spot written by Spot from the OSM. The per-asset ratios themselves are not published as a table at any page reached: UNKNOWN, which means a construction can assert the test exists and cannot assert its calibration.

nodes.label: F3 each collateral type is priced by a three-stage pipeline: a medianiser
nodes.text: each collateral type is priced by a three-stage pipeline: a medianiser computes a price from a list of supported feeds, a delay contract holds a current and a next price, and a third contract writes the safety-margined price into the ledger
nodes.note: Underlying feeds are Chainlink and WinkLink. This is a TIGHTER Ex fit than Sky's, because the medianiser is itself an on-chain contract and Ex explicitly admits 'push/pull/medianizer'. UNKNOWN: the OSM delay length is not stated in the documentation, so L13's freshness bound cannot be checked.

nodes.label: F4 debt accrues by a stability fee accumulated per collateral type and fo
nodes.text: debt accrues by a stability fee accumulated per collateral type and folded across the ledger by a permissionless call
nodes.note: Jug carries a per-ilk duty; the entry point is documented as rip(ilk) rather than DSS's drip(ilk), calling Vat.fold to update rate, debt and surplus. A renamed function on an otherwise identical accumulator is the kind of fact that makes source-level identity claims checkable and vocabulary-level identity claims useless.

nodes.label: F5 the level of the borrow rate is a written number set by an authority t
nodes.text: the level of the borrow rate is a written number set by an authority the documentation does not name
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and weaker than Sky's version of the same gap in an instructive way. Sky at least publishes who may write the number and inside what band (sky.json F6-F10). Here duty is settable and no page names the setter, the bounds, the cadence or the process. The vocabulary cannot express either object, so it cannot express the difference between them either — a bounded delegate and an unnamed writer decompose identically, which is the whole content of this lane's control-plane finding.

nodes.label: F6 the advertised savings rate is administered by a published reaction fu
nodes.text: the advertised savings rate is administered by a published reaction function whose inputs are a seven-day moving average of competitor stablecoin yields, the United States Federal Reserve policy rate, a competitive market premium, and the protocol's own underlying yield
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the second of the four rate instruments this lane was sent to separate. Three of four inputs come from OUTSIDE the protocol, including a central-bank policy rate. This is not Em (no token is emitted), not Ix (the index does not track realised returns), not As (quantity, not price) and not the Sky object (no on-chain agent, no bounds, no step). Nothing in 58 symbols names a rate whose level is a declared function of external market and central-bank rates — a policy rate with a published reaction function, which is the standard instrument of actual central banking. CORRECTION TO THE CORPUS: the corpus records a residue reading 'a foundation reserve subsidising an advertised savings rate out of band' and asserts 'the treasury tops up an interest rate in the stablecoin itself'. That is not supported at primary source. What the docs state is the four-input formula. Whether the gap between the administered rate and the earned yield is funded from a reserve is stated nowhere I could find: UNKNOWN. The residue should be restated as recorded here.

nodes.label: F7 a holder may deposit the stablecoin into a share token whose exchange
nodes.text: a holder may deposit the stablecoin into a share token whose exchange rate against it rises as returns accrue, redeemable at any time with no lockup
nodes.note: DEPARTURE: the corpus carries Ix for USDD but not Sh, while carrying Sh for sUSDe, which is the same ERC-4626 shape — share accounting and a rising exchange rate. Inconsistent treatment of one shape across two rows of the same category, corrected here.

nodes.label: F8 the yield paid on that share is produced by deploying idle capital int
nodes.text: the yield paid on that share is produced by deploying idle capital into third-party lending venues, where the venues, the caps and the phasing are chosen jointly by two named teams after review of market conditions and liquidity, and only the execution is on-chain
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A discretionary reserve manager standing behind a nominally permissionless CDP. CROSS-LANE: this is the yield lane's five-part delegated allocation mandate again — named agent, domain whitelist, magnitude cap, rate-of-change limit, revocation — except that only SLOT 1 IS VISIBLE HERE. The agent is named ('the USDD and JUST DAO teams'); no domain list, no cap, no step limit and no revocation path is published. That is a useful measurement in itself: the schema's slots are separable, and a protocol can ship the agent without the envelope. Compare Sky, which publishes all five (sky.json F6-F10), and Spark, which publishes all five in the allocation dress (spark-savings.json F17-F20).

nodes.label: F9 when a vault falls below its minimum ratio anyone may seize it, the se
nodes.text: when a vault falls below its minimum ratio anyone may seize it, the seizure starts an auction, keepers are paid a fixed incentive for starting one, the proceeds repay the debt and any excess collateral returns to the owner
nodes.note: Clip exposes kick(tab,lot,usr,kpr), take(id,amt,max,who,data), redo(id,kpr), yank(id) and file(what,data), with tip documented as a 'fixed incentive for starting an auction'. NOTE FOR THE NESTING CLAIM: USDD's Clip documents tip and cut but never a chip, so the proportional keeper fee that Sky and Lista both pay is not evidenced here. The corpus asserts Lista subset-of USDD subset-of Sky differing only by At, Xf and Fd; at parameter level the nesting is real for the skeleton and imperfect for the incentives.

nodes.label: F10 the auction clears by a price that decays at a fixed rate per second a
nodes.text: the auction clears by a price that decays at a fixed rate per second and can be reset by anyone who is paid for resetting it
nodes.note: RESIDUE. cut is documented as the 'price decay factor per second'. Reachable only through the contested symbol Da, which this lane declines to use, recording the behaviour here as the corpus did. CROSS-PROTOCOL: identical to sky.json F12 and lista-cdp.json F8 down to the kick/take/redo interface, verified against three independent documentation sites and two source trees.

nodes.label: F11 the architecture provides for auctions that sell governance tokens whe
nodes.text: the architecture provides for auctions that sell governance tokens when the protocol runs a deficit
nodes.note: RESIDUE, the same recapitalisation-by-dilution gap as sky.json F14: Sl assigns a loss to a class and Bs pre-stakes capital to be slashed, and neither says new equity is issued against the loss after the fact. Weaker evidence than Sky's: the module is described in the architecture page, and no deployed debt-auction address is published, so whether it is live is UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F12 a shortfall the auction did not cover is carried by the system rather
nodes.text: a shortfall the auction did not cover is carried by the system rather than by any named holder
nodes.note: FORCED, and thinly evidenced. The DSS skeleton implies a Vow, the architecture page describes the deficit path in outline, and no USDD page describes the surplus/deficit accounting in the detail Sky's Vow page gives. Carried because deleting it would leave the deficit path empty; flagged so stage 3 can weigh it as weaker than Sky's identically shaped obligation.

nodes.label: F13 the stablecoin swaps one-for-one against named reserve stablecoins wit
nodes.text: the stablecoin swaps one-for-one against named reserve stablecoins with no service fee, so the user pays only transaction cost, subject to a published availability cap
nodes.note: UsddPsm with AuthGemJoin adapters for USDT and USDC and a UsddJoin for minting and burning, discovered through a ChainLog registry under MCD_PSM_USDT_A and MCD_PSM_USDC_A, multi-decimal (6 against 18), Solidity ^0.6.12, deployed on TRON, Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain (https://github.com/decentralized-usd/psm, accessed 2026-08-05). The code carries separate tin and tout fees under governance control; the user-facing docs say the fee is currently zero. As at Sky, a live fee of zero and a governable fee of zero are the same number and different instruments, and Ps carries neither. This is the only par exit: Rd is correctly ABSENT, so L7 is discharged through Ps alone.

nodes.label: F14 either direction of the peg swap can be paused independently by an aut
nodes.text: either direction of the peg swap can be paused independently by an authorised party
nodes.note: The one control-plane fact in this application evidenced at source rather than asserted in prose. Which party holds the pause is not published: UNKNOWN. Gp names the facility and, as everywhere in this lane, not the holder.

nodes.label: F15 the issuer exists separately in three domains, with its own token cont
nodes.text: the issuer exists separately in three domains, with its own token contract and its own local collateral in each, and mints locally against local backing rather than bridging a single supply
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE: the corpus carries Xf for USDD and this construction drops it. USDD on TRON TXDk8mbtRbXeYuMNS83CfKPaYYT8XWv9Hz, on Ethereum 0x4f8e5de400de08b164e7421b3ee387f461becd1a, on BNB 0x45e51bc23d592eb2dba86da3985299f7895d66ba, with TRX and sTRX ilks on TRON, USDT/USDC on Ethereum and USDT on BNB. Xf names moving an asset across domains and L9 requires debit(source) = credit(destination); nothing here is moved, so L9 does not apply and asserting Xf would assert a conservation relation that does not hold. One brand, one peg, three domains, three collateral sets, and no symbol for it. If a canonical bridge exists it was not found at primary source: UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F16 a core contract exists whose only job is to convert holders of the iss
nodes.text: a core contract exists whose only job is to convert holders of the issuer's own predecessor liability into the current one
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Migrate is listed among the ten core contracts. The predecessor, USDDOLD, was minted by whitelisted TRON DAO Reserve institutions burning TRX against a basket of BTC, USDT, USDC and TRX (https://docs.usdd.io/introduction/what-is-usddold.md, accessed 2026-08-04) — a completely different issuance mechanism under the same brand. Two liabilities of one issuer, one deprecated, one successor, with a conversion path and no symbol. The same object appears at Sky as the DAI/USDS converter (sky.json F18), where it is additionally a rate instrument. RELATED CORRECTION: the corpus carries At for USDD on the grounds that 'the TRON DAO Reserve publishes a transparency dashboard'. USDD 2.0's own documentation places the TDR in the past as the issuer of USDDOLD, and the current governance and architecture pages do not mention it. At is dropped; whether the TDR still stands behind USDD 2.0 is UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F17 the protocol states that its framework is community-driven and that cr
nodes.text: the protocol states that its framework is community-driven and that critical changes are subject to community review and approval, and names no governable parameter, no timelock, no voting threshold and no administrative address
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a THREE-SYMBOL DEPARTURE. The corpus carries Tg, Up and Gp for USDD. (a) Tg: no timelock is named at any primary source; secondary reporting describes a transition of governance to JST under JUST DAO, and JustLend's own docs describe a GovernorBravo + WJST + 48-hour Timelock stack for JustLend, but I could not confirm at a USDD primary source that USDD's own parameters sit under that timelock. UNKNOWN, so Tg is dropped. (b) Up: the 'Proxy contract' listed among the core contracts is the DSS user proxy, not an upgrade proxy; no upgradeability claim is evidenced. Up is dropped. (c) Gp survives only in the narrow, source-evidenced form of F14. (d) Em is also dropped: the corpus carried it for a savings subsidy that F6 shows is not evidenced. The measurement to report is that five of the corpus's thirteen elements for USDD are unsupported at primary source, four of them control-plane symbols, and that the security page repeats the governance page's principles without implementation detail (https://docs.usdd.io/security/secure-framework.md, accessed 2026-08-04). The vocabulary reads an undocumented control plane and a documented one identically.

nodes.label: 04-liquid-staking
Babylon Protocol
F1 A Bitcoin holder locks BTC on Bitcoin, in a Taproot output it construc
nodes.text: A Bitcoin holder locks BTC on Bitcoin, in a Taproot output it constructs itself with the NUMS point as internal key so that key-path spending is disabled, and never surrenders custody and never bridges the coin; the protocol holds nothing.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the assumption break for the whole Security-reuse register. Every other protocol in this category custodies the stake and Bs presumes it. Here the securing relationship is a set of pre-signatures held by third parties, not a balance held by a contract. The sharper statement is that the stake never enters the system that slashes it.

nodes.label: F2 The output carries exactly three spending paths: a pure timelock retur
nodes.text: The output carries exactly three spending paths: a pure timelock returning the coin to the staker after at most 65,534 blocks, an unbonding path requiring the staker plus a threshold of lexicographically sorted covenant keys, and a slashing path requiring the staker plus the named finality provider plus that same covenant threshold.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A security relationship expressed as a disjunction of script conditions on a foreign chain has no representation in the carrier, which models positions as balances in ledgers.

nodes.label: F3 [Vl sub-mechanism 2 of 5: stake allocation and scheduling] The staker
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 2 of 5: stake allocation and scheduling] The staker names its finality provider inside its own Bitcoin output at the moment of locking; there is no scheduler, no allocation authority and no reassignment.
nodes.note: Not residue: allocation is closed by construction, because it is user-directed at output creation and immutable thereafter. Recording that is a different act from recording an unnamed mechanism, and the vocabulary cannot distinguish the two, which is the same defect the options lane recorded in FINDINGS-STAGE1. Babylon is the second of the five here to close one of Vl's sub-mechanisms by construction rather than by mechanism.

nodes.label: F4 The staking transaction is registered on Babylon Genesis by submitting
nodes.text: The staking transaction is registered on Babylon Genesis by submitting a Bitcoin inclusion proof, verified against a Bitcoin light client the chain runs itself; Bitcoin is entirely unaware that Babylon exists.
nodes.note: Xm is FORCED and retained. Law L18 asks Xm for explicit finality, chain binding and replay protection, and the confirmation-depth and light-client machinery supply them. What Xm cannot express is that the direction of trust is inverted: nothing is being sent, a foreign chain is being observed, and the observed chain has no counterparty role.

nodes.label: F5 A delegation becomes ACTIVE only once 6 of 9 covenant committee member
nodes.text: A delegation becomes ACTIVE only once 6 of 9 covenant committee members submit pre-signatures for the unbonding, slashing and unbonding-slashing transactions; the committee runs a daemon that watches for pending registrations and signs, and it is mutable by governance.
nodes.note: Aw is FORCED and retained, and the corpus is right that it drastically understates the object. This is covenant emulation: a threshold signer set standing in for an opcode Bitcoin does not have. The committee is a trusted party inside the security model, load-bearing for both exit and enforcement; its absence breaks on-demand unbonding and its collusion is a live risk. Two facts no gate symbol can carry: Babylon Labs holds 3 of the 9 seats against a quorum of 6, and Babylon's own docs warn the published key list may be outdated because the node parameters are the source of truth.

nodes.label: F6 The unbonding and slashing transactions exist fully signed before the
nodes.text: The unbonding and slashing transactions exist fully signed before the events that would justify them, and are merely waiting to be broadcast.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A conditional obligation that has already been executed and is waiting for someone to publish it is not a queue, not an escrow and not an option. This is the primitive that makes the rest of the protocol work and nothing in the 58 names it.

nodes.label: F7 [Vl sub-mechanism 1 of 5: registration] A finality provider registers
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 1 of 5: registration] A finality provider registers by BIP-340 public key with a description and a commission rate of at least 3%, and only a registered provider may be named in a staking output.
nodes.note: Fd is a CANDIDATE symbol, used with the required mark, and names the minimum commission. Vl is not used. The registered object is not a validator: it validates nothing on Bitcoin, it does not necessarily produce blocks on the chain it finalises, its key for the actual duty is a per-height one-time signature key rather than a persistent consensus key, and Babylon Genesis carries a second, separate validator-like population, the CometBFT validators staked in BABY. One symbol cannot distinguish two validator-like populations on one chain, which is why Vl is equivocal here for a third distinct reason.

nodes.label: F8 At most 60 finality providers are active, selected as the top provider
nodes.text: At most 60 finality providers are active, selected as the top providers by delegated value that have BTC-timestamped public randomness for the height in question.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and absent from the corpus. Aw names a gate on identity; this is a competitive ranking with a hard cap, which makes the provider population bounded and rivalrous rather than open. Nothing names a capped, value-ranked, per-height active set.

nodes.label: F9 A provider commits Merkle-tree public randomness for future heights, a
nodes.text: A provider commits Merkle-tree public randomness for future heights, and the commitment takes effect only after it has been timestamped into Bitcoin; a block is final once providers holding more than two thirds of voting power have cast one-time-signature votes, in a second round on top of the chain's ordinary consensus.
nodes.note: RESIDUE on both halves. A protocol whose votes are valid only if a foreign chain has already witnessed the commitment is unlike anything Ex or Xm names. And the duty the stake secures is a second finality round after consensus has concluded, which is not the duty of a validator and is what makes Vl equivocal here rather than merely compressed.

nodes.label: F10 [What the staked collateral secures] The locked BTC secures the finali
nodes.text: [What the staked collateral secures] The locked BTC secures the finality of Babylon Genesis, and by first-party framing of Bitcoin Supercharged Networks beyond it.
nodes.note: Rs is a CANDIDATE, used with the mark. UNKNOWN, and this is the single most important open question for this application: whether one BTC delegation can secure several networks simultaneously and how slashing is scoped across them. If the answer is yes with per-network slashing conditions, Babylon inherits exactly the problem EigenLayer solved with magnitudes, and that is the difference between Rs being adequate here and being empty. The BSN documentation section exists but the page returned 404 on direct fetch.

nodes.label: F11 [Who may write a slashing condition over the collateral] No third part
nodes.text: [Who may write a slashing condition over the collateral] No third party may. The only slashable fault is equivocation at a single height, defined by the chain's own finality module; there is no analogue of an external service authoring its own slashing predicate.
nodes.note: The answer is negative and the carrier cannot state a negative. This is the exact converse of EigenLayer F9, where any AVS may author the predicate, and the two protocols occupy opposite ends of an axis the vocabulary does not have: who is permitted to define the fault. Both ends read as an empty array.

nodes.label: F12 [Whether the same collateral can be committed twice] It cannot without
nodes.text: [Whether the same collateral can be committed twice] It cannot without a new Bitcoin transaction: a staking output names its finality provider at creation and the covenant pre-signs against that exact output, so the same satoshis cannot be re-committed while locked.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Exclusivity here is obtained from UTXO uniqueness on a foreign chain; EigenLayer obtains the same property from a conserved magnitude budget. Two protocols achieve the same guarantee by wholly unrelated means and the vocabulary names neither the guarantee nor either mechanism.

nodes.label: F13 [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5, trigger: penalty attribution] A provider tha
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5, trigger: penalty attribution] A provider that signs two conflicting blocks at one height mathematically reveals its own private key through the extractable one-time signature scheme; the module records the equivocation evidence such that anyone can extract the key, after which anyone may complete and broadcast the pre-signed slashing transaction.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and stage 1 found no analogue anywhere in the twelve categories. Sl names a loss being assigned; here nothing is assigned. A secret becomes public and an already-authorised transaction becomes broadcastable by the general public. The enforcement primitive is cryptographic disclosure, not allocation.

nodes.label: F14 [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5, effect] The slashing transaction destroys sl
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5, effect] The slashing transaction destroys slashing_rate = 0.001, one tenth of one percent, of the delegation, paying it to an OP_RETURN output tagged with the string 'babylon' so that the destruction is provable and self-identifying on the securing chain.
nodes.note: CORRECTION OF MAGNITUDE, and it changes what the construction claims. The corpus treats the BTC as first-order slashable first-loss capital. On mainnet a double-sign burns 0.1%. Any construction that models Babylon slashing as materially loss-bearing models the wrong magnitude. Bs is retained only because slashable capital demonstrably exists and Sl only because the loss lands on a named class, the delegators of the faulty provider; both carry near-zero economic content here, and the dominant consequence for the staker is F15, not this. The corpus also does not record that the burn is provable and tagged, which is arguably the most interesting fact about it. Live chain parameters are authoritative over the repository's parameter file.

nodes.label: F15 A provider that equivocates loses its voting power, and one whose miss
nodes.text: A provider that equivocates loses its voting power, and one whose missed blocks exceed the threshold over a 10,000-block window at a 0.2 minimum signed ratio is marked sluggish and jailed for 600 seconds.
nodes.note: RESIDUE recorded alongside a used symbol. Ep names the window and the jail duration. What has no symbol is that the dominant sanction in this protocol is the loss of future income rather than the loss of principal: the stake stops earning and the provider is removed from the active set. Nothing in the 58 expresses a sanction that is entirely opportunity cost. Permanence of the removal after equivocation (tombstoning) is UNCONFIRMED at first-party source: the module README confirms voting-power removal and evidence recording, and stage 1 could not confirm permanence.

nodes.label: F16 [Vl sub-mechanism 4 of 5: exit] Exit is a race between two paths: wait
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 4 of 5: exit] Exit is a race between two paths: wait out the 64,000-block staking timelock, or broadcast the covenant-pre-signed unbonding transaction and then wait a further 301 blocks, during which the coin is out of the staking output and still slashable because the slashing timelock equals the unbonding time.
nodes.note: CORRECTION: Wq is DROPPED from the corpus construction. There is no queue. No ordering exists, no shared exit liquidity exists, no finalisation step exists, and each delegation unbonds independently on its own Bitcoin timelock; the lifecycle is a per-delegation state machine, PENDING to VERIFIED to ACTIVE to UNBONDED or EXPIRED. RESIDUE: a post-exit window during which capital has left the securing position but remains liable is an object nothing names. Stage 1 also records a trap: networks/bbn-1/parameters/global-params.json states unbonding_time 1008, which is the Phase-1 regime; the live chain value is 301 and the live value governs.

nodes.label: F17 At each block the incentive module intercepts the fee collector and cr
nodes.text: At each block the incentive module intercepts the fee collector and creates a BTC-staking gauge; the finality module's end-blocker then splits it across delegations by voting power, net of each provider's commission, with the BTC-staking portion strictly less than one so the remainder goes to the chain's own CometBFT validators and their delegations.
nodes.note: Em is retained: BABY rewards are protocol-funded through the chain's minting and fee machinery, unlike the AVS-funded rewards of EigenLayer where Em is dropped. Fd is a CANDIDATE symbol, used with the required mark, and is ADDED for the commission and the portion split. UNKNOWN: the live mainnet value of the BTC-staking portion parameter.

nodes.label: F18 A per-stakeholder reward gauge accrues against a cumulative reward fig
nodes.text: A per-stakeholder reward gauge accrues against a cumulative reward figure recorded at the stakeholder's start period, and tracks what has already been withdrawn.
nodes.note: Ix is ADDED. This is the standard cumulative-index accrual pattern and it is the one place in this protocol where a core accounting symbol fits without qualification. Sh is deliberately not used: the claim is on a stream of emitted rewards, not on a pool balance.

nodes.label: F19 A user who holds both an active BTC delegation to an active finality p
nodes.text: A user who holds both an active BTC delegation to an active finality provider and a BABY delegation to a CometBFT validator earns an additional reward computed from a score over active satoshis and active BABY jointly.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and NEW: the costaking module did not exist when the corpus was written. A reward keyed on the holder occupying two different positions in two different consensus systems at once is neither an emission of a schedule nor a distribution of a fee; it prices a conjunction of holdings. It also links the BTC staking system to the chain's own proof-of-stake system in a way the corpus model does not contain.

nodes.label: F20 An allow-list restricts which staking transactions may register at all
nodes.text: An allow-list restricts which staking transactions may register at all, and it expires at block height 139,920, after which registration is open.
nodes.note: RESIDUE recorded alongside used symbols: Aw has no temporal dimension. A permission gate that switches itself off at a scheduled block is a gate with an expiry, and combining Aw with Ep expresses the two facts side by side without expressing that one governs the other.

nodes.label: F21 Babylon aggregates its own state into succinct checkpoints written int
nodes.text: Babylon aggregates its own state into succinct checkpoints written into Bitcoin, so that its proof-of-stake history is bounded by Bitcoin's, and separately runs epoched staking over its CometBFT validator set.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Xm is retained in the construction for F4, reading Bitcoin, and is deliberately not claimed here for writing to it: Xm names verifying a message delivered from another domain, and here nothing is delivered, nothing is addressed, and the destination chain has no notion of the sender. Borrowing another chain's finality as a clock has no symbol, and it is one of the two protocols Babylon is, the other being the staking protocol.

nodes.label: F22 [Vl sub-mechanism 3 of 5: deposit front-running defence] There is none
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 3 of 5: deposit front-running defence] There is none and none is needed: the staker constructs the output, holds its own key and never hands the coin to a third party, so there is no deposit for an operator to front-run.
nodes.note: Closed by construction, not residue. Three of Vl's five sub-mechanisms are present here in some form (F7 registration, F16 exit, F13 and F14 penalty); allocation (F3) and front-running defence (this entry) do not arise. WBETH and Babylon are the two members of this category that do not have the front-running problem, and they lack it for opposite reasons: WBETH because no validator action happens on chain at all, Babylon because the depositor never parts with the coin.

nodes.label: Binance staked ETH (WBETH)
F1 Anyone may send ETH to the token contract through a payable deposit(ad
nodes.text: Anyone may send ETH to the token contract through a payable deposit(address referral) and be minted msg.value * 1e18 / exchangeRate() WBETH, with no account, no KYC and no allowlist.
nodes.note: CORRECTION to the corpus, and the corpus is materially wrong here. The corpus marks Aw with the justification 'minting and redeeming require a Binance account... this gate is a login'. The verified implementation source of WrapTokenV3ETH shows deposit() carrying only require(msg.value > 0). Aw is DROPPED from the construction for this reason. The record was overturned from verified on-chain bytecode alone, there being no repo and no specification.

nodes.label: F2 A holder's WBETH balance is a fixed quantity that never changes withou
nodes.text: A holder's WBETH balance is a fixed quantity that never changes without a transfer; the ETH entitlement rises because a single stored scalar, exchangeRate(), rises.
nodes.note: Ix is FORCED and retained. The corpus marker is right in substance: Ix presumes an index derived from observable state, and here the state is not observable and the index is a claim. The gap is not index-versus-share; it is *asserted* versus *derived*, and the vocabulary has no way to mark which.

nodes.label: F3 The on-chain ledger is a plain fixed-quantity ERC-20 with no share led
nodes.text: The on-chain ledger is a plain fixed-quantity ERC-20 with no share ledger and no on-chain pool: a holder's entitlement is balance x storedRate, not a proportion of any quantity the contract holds.
nodes.note: CORRECTION: Sh is DROPPED from the corpus construction. Sh requires that the claim be proportional to a pool, i.e. value = shares/totalShares x poolValue. Here the rate is set exogenously and independently of totalSupply, so if the off-chain backing halved no on-chain quantity would change unless a whitelisted caller wrote a new number. Carrying both Sh and Ix would also double-count the same claim under its two dual descriptions.

nodes.label: F4 Only whitelisted callers may write the exchange rate, and each write i
nodes.text: Only whitelisted callers may write the exchange rate, and each write is bounded by a per-caller allowance that refills on a per-caller interval; a write that is zero, unchanged, or exceeds the remaining allowance reverts.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a CORRECTION that overturns the corpus record's central claim. The corpus says 'an ERC-20 whose exchange rate an admin key increments on a schedule'. The oracle role is held by a verified contract, ExchangeRateUpdater (MIT), whose guards read 'RateLimit: caller is not whitelisted' and 'ExchangeRateUpdater: exchange rate update exceeds allowance'. Nothing in the 58 names a governor on an oracle's discretion: it is not Tg (no delay, no queue, no proposal), not Gp (it cannot stop anything), not At (no attester, no assurance level). It is the only thing standing between a compromised oracle key and arbitrary repricing of the second-largest liquid-staking position in DeFi.

nodes.label: F5 Any holder may call requestWithdrawEth, which unconditionally burns th
nodes.text: Any holder may call requestWithdrawEth, which unconditionally burns the caller's WBETH at the prevailing rate and registers a withdrawal request in a separate unwrap contract recording recipient, wbethAmount, ethAmount, triggerTime, claimTime and an allocated flag.
nodes.note: Wq is ADDED to the corpus construction: the corpus records no queue at all. Rd is retained but its corpus justification is CORRECTED. The corpus says redemption 'is an exchange feature governed by exchange terms and KYC, not a right the contract enforces'. The contract enforces the burn and the queue entry unconditionally for any holder with no KYC; what it does not enforce is payment (F6). The overstatement the corpus warns about is real but located in a different place.

nodes.label: F6 A registered request becomes claimable only after an operator marks it
nodes.text: A registered request becomes claimable only after an operator marks it allocated and after a minimum lock of two days (MIN_LOCK_TIME, with a settable lockTime); the contract is under no obligation to be funded, and is topped up from an off-chain balance through rechargeFromRechargeAddress.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the sharpest single finding about this protocol. Wq names a queue the protocol is obliged to clear. This is an enforced request against a discretionary fulfilment, and the distinction is the whole risk: solvency of the queue is an off-chain fact. The corpus's 'no on-chain redemption guarantee' is half right; the precise statement is that the path exists and the obligation to fund it does not.

nodes.label: F7 A blacklister may permanently strand a named holder's redemption by bl
nodes.text: A blacklister may permanently strand a named holder's redemption by blacklisting the address on claimWithdraw, while leaving the token transferable to everyone else and leaving that holder's ability to mint untouched.
nodes.note: Fz is a CANDIDATE symbol, used here with the required mark, and is ADDED: the corpus records no freeze symbol at all. Law L28 requires a named authority, enumerated triggers, an appeal path and holder disclosure; none is published for WBETH, so the warrant is unmet and that is itself the finding. Fz is also approximate in scope: this is a selective freeze on *redemption only*, not on transfer, which Fz cannot distinguish.

nodes.label: F8 An operator may pause the token contract and the unwrap contract, halt
nodes.text: An operator may pause the token contract and the unwrap contract, halting mint and claim.
nodes.note: ADDED. The corpus canonical form omits any control-plane symbol beyond Up.

nodes.label: F9 Both the token and the unwrap contract are EIP-1967 proxies whose admi
nodes.text: Both the token and the unwrap contract are EIP-1967 proxies whose admin may replace the implementation immediately, with no timelock and no governance process.
nodes.note: Law L15 (Up requires Tg or a bounded emergency process) is UNMET: no timelock exists. Prohibition X9 (Up with immediate single-key control) is ARMED on the last published role map, which puts the proxy admin at a Binance EOA. UNKNOWN whether that assignment still holds: the map is from 2023-10-09 and describes WrappedTokenV1ETH, while the live implementation is WrapTokenV3ETH; stage 1 could not re-read live role values (Etherscan 403, Blockscout proxy-read 404, no eth_call available). Stage 3 should treat X9 as armed-pending-verification, not as proven.

nodes.label: F10 The backing of the token is an off-chain balance sheet: no attestation
nodes.text: The backing of the token is an off-chain balance sheet: no attestation object naming an attester, an assurance level, a frequency or a staleness bound is published for WBETH or BETH.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. At is deliberately not used. Law L27 requires a named attester, independence, a stated assurance level, a staleness bound and recourse. The proof-of-reserves page supplies a Merkle-tree and zk-SNARK methodology, names no auditor, states no frequency, and does not enumerate WBETH or BETH among covered assets. There is no symbol for 'backed by an off-chain balance sheet you cannot inspect'.

nodes.label: F11 [Vl, all five sub-mechanisms] The protocol performs no validator actio
nodes.text: [Vl, all five sub-mechanisms] The protocol performs no validator action on chain of any kind: there is no validator registry, no key registration or vetting, no withdrawal-credential proof, no allocation of stake across operators, no deposit front-running defence, no exit request or exit signalling, no slashing record and no operator set. The three writes that touch the staking side (moveToStakingAddress, supplyEth, setNewEthStaked) move value to a Binance-controlled address or assert a number, and the trail ends on chain.
nodes.note: This is NOT residue in the ordinary sense, and saying so precisely is the deliverable. Vl is INAPPLICABLE here, not approximate: the obligation cannot arise, because the protocol performs no validator action within the ledger the model describes. Zero of Vl's five sub-mechanisms are present, in a position that stage 1's ranking puts at $6.9B, second largest in the category. The vocabulary reads this absence identically to an unnamed mechanism, which is the same defect the options lane recorded in FINDINGS-STAGE1: the requirement language admits only discharge-by-naming and has no way to say that an obligation is closed by construction. Any claim that Vl covers liquid staking has to survive this entry.

nodes.label: F12 [What the collateral secures, who may write a slashing condition over
nodes.text: [What the collateral secures, who may write a slashing condition over it, whether it may be committed twice] Nothing on chain, no one, and unanswerable: there is no restaked collateral, no slashing condition, no party empowered to author one, and no on-chain record of the backing position against which a second commitment could be detected.
nodes.note: Stated because the category asks it of every member. All three answers are negative, and a negative answer is exactly what the carrier cannot record: an empty element array here means the same thing as an unnamed mechanism, which it is not.

nodes.label: F13 The same ERC-20 is simultaneously a permissionless on-chain claim mint
nodes.text: The same ERC-20 is simultaneously a permissionless on-chain claim mintable by anyone at a posted rate and an exchange product gated by an account and by terms of service, with different rights behind each door; through the exchange, wrapping and unwrapping BETH are at zero fee.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The vocabulary has one gate symbol and no way to say that one door is code and the other is a login, with materially different rights behind each. This also explains why the corpus's Aw marker felt true while being false about the contract: it described the exchange door and attributed it to the ledger.

nodes.label: F14 The conversion rate is updated once daily at 00:00 UTC, and staking an
nodes.text: The conversion rate is updated once daily at 00:00 UTC, and staking and redemption through the exchange are suspended each day from 23:45 to 00:15 UTC while it is applied.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Ep is deliberately not used: Ep names an epoch-gated transition enforced by the ledger, and this cadence and its suspension window are enforced by an exchange's operational schedule, not by code. The contract itself imposes no schedule on updateExchangeRate beyond the rate limiter's per-caller interval (F4).

nodes.label: F15 The rate was initialised at 1:1 with BETH at launch on 2023-04-27 08:0
nodes.text: The rate was initialised at 1:1 with BETH at launch on 2023-04-27 08:00 UTC, and the same token address serves Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Xf is deliberately not used: stage 1 found no evidence of an on-chain bridge, lock-mint or burn-mint path between the two deployments. Two independent deployments that happen to share a vanity address are not cross-domain asset transfer, and asserting Xf would be a forced fit on an address coincidence.

nodes.label: F16 Slashing exposure, reward computation and the reserve sit entirely ins
nodes.text: Slashing exposure, reward computation and the reserve sit entirely inside the custodian; a loss reaches the token only if a whitelisted caller writes a smaller number, and may not be written at all.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Sl is deliberately not used: Sl assigns a loss to a claim class through a rule the ledger executes. Here a loss is expressible only as a smaller asserted scalar, whose size per interval is capped by F4's allowance, so a large loss could not even be written promptly. Nothing in the 58 names a loss path that is discretionary in both its occurrence and its rate.

nodes.label: EigenCloud (EigenLayer)
F1 A depositor sends an ERC-20 (including a liquid staking token) into a
nodes.text: A depositor sends an ERC-20 (including a liquid staking token) into a whitelisted strategy and receives deposit shares: an internal, non-transferable pro-rata accounting claim, not a token. A Strategy Whitelister, currently the StrategyFactory, controls which strategies are eligible.

nodes.label: F2 [Vl sub-mechanism 1 of 5: validator key registration and vetting] A de
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 1 of 5: validator key registration and vetting] A depositor may instead deploy an EigenPod at a CREATE2 address salted on its own staker address, deposit 32 ETH with the pod as withdrawal credentials, and then prove on chain that a named validator's withdrawal credentials point at that pod; validator state is thereafter maintained by periodic checkpoints.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. This is a credential *proof*, not a registration and not a vetting: nobody approves the validator and nobody may reject it, and the proof binds a beacon-chain object to an execution-layer address. Vl is not used. Note the structural fact this makes visible: EigenPod contains a genuine validator lifecycle while core/ contains a thing that only rhymes with one, and one symbol cannot hold both.

nodes.label: F3 A pod's beacon-chain balance increase raises the owner's deposit share
nodes.text: A pod's beacon-chain balance increase raises the owner's deposit shares, while a balance decrease does not lower them and instead reduces a proportional beaconChainSlashingFactor that starts at 1 WAD, so the protocol never carries a share deficit.
nodes.note: Ix is deliberately not used. The scaling factors here (beaconChainSlashingFactor per pod, _depositScalingFactor per staker) are per-position and monotone decreasing by construction; Ix names a *global* index that changes claim value in both directions. Claiming Ix would flatten the asymmetry, which is the whole content of the design.

nodes.label: F4 A staker delegates its entire position to an operator; the delegation
nodes.text: A staker delegates its entire position to an operator; the delegation transfers no custody, no assets and no transaction authority, only the right to be counted as that operator's weight and the corresponding slashing liability.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Au is the nearest symbol and is deliberately not used: Au is delegated *execution* scope and law L17 asks it for bounded scope, revocation, expiry and nonce/domain separation. delegateTo moves no assets and grants no call rights; what is delegated is liability. The staker-to-operator-to-AVS graph is EigenLayer's core object and the vocabulary has no edge for it.

nodes.label: F5 An operator registers by naming a delegation approver, whose signature
nodes.text: An operator registers by naming a delegation approver, whose signature it may then require before any staker may delegate to it, and an allocation delay of its own choosing.
nodes.note: Aw names the approver gate. It does not name the fact that operator identity lives in one contract (DelegationManager) and per-set membership in another (AllocationManager), so that 'being an operator' is two separate registrations with different admission rules.

nodes.label: F6 [Vl sub-mechanism 2 of 5: stake allocation and scheduling] An operator
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 2 of 5: stake allocation and scheduling] An operator allocates a magnitude, a proportion of its delegated stake in a given strategy, to a named operator set; allocations are held per (operator, strategy, operator set) with a current magnitude, a pending diff and an effect block, and deallocations are processed through a per-(operator, strategy) queue in order.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and structurally different from Lido's scheduler (which allocates *principal* to operators). Here what is allocated is *slashability* over principal that does not move. The vocabulary has neither object. Bs names the capital; it does not name a budget over the capital's exposure.

nodes.label: F7 [Whether the same collateral can be committed twice] The sum of an ope
nodes.text: [Whether the same collateral can be committed twice] The sum of an operator's allocated magnitudes across all operator sets can never exceed INITIAL_TOTAL_MAGNITUDE (1e18, one WAD), which is reduced only by slashing, so the same *deposit* backs many operator sets but each unit of *slashability* is exclusively allocated and no two operator sets can slash the same stake.
nodes.note: CORRECTION, and the load-bearing one for this application. The corpus residue entry asserts that in EigenLayer 'the same collateral is simultaneously bonded to mutually-unaware slashing laws'. Unique Stake exists precisely to prevent that, and it is enforced by arithmetic rather than by convention: 'The sum of all magnitude allocations never being greater than the Total Magnitude ensures the property of Unique Stake... ensures that no two Operator Sets can slash the same stake.' Stage 2 does not carry the old framing. What remains RESIDUE is the object itself: nothing in the 58 names a conserved, partitionable slashability budget, monotone decreasing and reduced only by loss.

nodes.label: F8 [What the restaked collateral secures] The allocated stake secures an
nodes.text: [What the restaked collateral secures] The allocated stake secures an arbitrary external service, an AVS, whose duties, faults and correctness conditions the core protocol does not model and cannot read.
nodes.note: Rs is a CANDIDATE and is used with the mark. It is exact in name and thin in content: it asserts that restaking is present and stops. Law L22 asks Rs for an attributed slash condition, non-reflexive capital and a loss waterfall; the first is present (F9), the second holds for LST and native ETH strategies, and the third is F11 and F12.

nodes.label: F9 [Who may write a slashing condition] Any AVS may create an operator se
nodes.text: [Who may write a slashing condition] Any AVS may create an operator set, define its slashable strategies and its membership roster, and call slashOperator with a proportion in WAD; the core protocol validates the arithmetic and never the ground for the slash. ELIP-006 states the consequence plainly: an attacker who gains access to AVS keys can drain the entirety of operator and staker allocated stake.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Aw is retained in the construction for F1 and F5 but is not claimed here: Aw carries the gate and drops the law. The significant part is not that an AVS controls admission to its set, it is that an AVS authors the predicate under which other people's capital is destroyed, and the protocol that holds the capital cannot express what the predicate says.

nodes.label: F10 AVSDirectory is deprecated and AllocationManager is the sole registrat
nodes.text: AVSDirectory is deprecated and AllocationManager is the sole registration path from an AVS to an operator set.
nodes.note: Recorded because any decomposition anchored on AVSDirectory is stale. The published docs index still stamps itself EigenLayer v1.3.0 while the latest release is v1.13.0; the per-contract docs under docs/core/ are current and the index is not.

nodes.label: F11 [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5: penalty attribution] A slash reduces the ope
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5: penalty attribution] A slash reduces the operator's currentMagnitude, maxMagnitude and encumberedMagnitude proportionally and processes pending deallocations pro rata, so the loss falls on every staker delegated to that operator in that strategy and on no one else.
nodes.note: Sl is used and is a better fit here than in Lido: the loss is socialised across a *named* claim class, the delegators of one operator in one strategy, rather than across the whole supply. Bs is used because the allocated stake is genuinely slashable first-loss capital rented out, which is the closest fit any symbol achieves anywhere in this category. What Sl cannot express is that the size of the class is itself a variable the operator controls through F6.

nodes.label: F12 Slashed shares are first marked burnable-or-redistributable, and only
nodes.text: Slashed shares are first marked burnable-or-redistributable, and only after SLASH_RESOLUTION_DELAY_BLOCKS may anyone permissionlessly clear them, sending them either to the burn address 0x00000000000000000000000000000000000E16E4 or to the operator set's redistribution recipient.
nodes.note: RESIDUE on two counts, and NEW: the resolution delay shipped in release v1.13.0 on 2026-06-25, after the corpus record. First, a loss that has been *recorded* but not yet *effected*, awaiting a permissionless poke after a delay, is a state nothing in the vocabulary marks. Second, Sl assigns a loss to a claim class; ELIP-006 assigns it to a named counterparty as restitution, at an address fixed immutably at operator-set creation so stakers can price the risk at opt-in. That is a remedy, not an allocation, and the vocabulary cannot express the difference.

nodes.label: F13 Native ETH and EIGEN are excluded from redistribution: native ETH beca
nodes.text: Native ETH and EIGEN are excluded from redistribution: native ETH because paying a recipient would require beacon exits whose queue can range from hours to weeks, and EIGEN because it requires a delay on token protocol outflow for its intersubjective machinery.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The corpus records redistribution as prospective and records neither that it is live on mainnet nor the exclusions, and the exclusions are the interesting part: the protocol's own two native assets are the two that cannot be redistributed.
