Nothing names an asset-conditional loss remedy.

nodes.label: F14 [Vl sub-mechanism 4 of 5: exit] A staker undelegates or queues a withd
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 4 of 5: exit] A staker undelegates or queues a withdrawal, waits MIN_WITHDRAWAL_DELAY_BLOCKS (100,800 blocks on mainnet, about 14 days), and then completes the queued withdrawal either as shares or as tokens; for native ETH the beacon-chain exit queue sits underneath and is not modelled by these contracts.
nodes.note: Wq names the staker's queue and Ep the block-height gate. The validator-side exit that must complete underneath it for native restakers is outside the contract set entirely, which is the same gap Lido has, arrived at by a different route: Lido models the validator exit and does not name it, EigenLayer does not model it at all.

nodes.label: F15 Five further delays bind, each for a different party's benefit: ALLOCA
nodes.text: Five further delays bind, each for a different party's benefit: ALLOCATION_CONFIGURATION_DELAY of 126,000 blocks (17.5 days) before a new allocation binds, so stakers can leave before new risk attaches; an operator-chosen allocation delay; DEALLOCATION_DELAY of 100,800 blocks after which deregistration ends exposure, so an AVS keeps recourse; the withdrawal delay of F14; and the slash resolution delay of F12.
nodes.note: Ep names a gated transition and is retained. RESIDUE recorded here: Ep names an epoch and Wq a queue, and neither names a delay whose purpose is to give a *third party* time to react. Deregistering from an operator set does not end exposure, which is the clearest case: the delay exists solely so that the counterparty retains recourse against someone who has already left. The corpus lists this as one security parameter; it is now five.

nodes.label: F16 An AVS funds a rewards submission weighted across strategies, or an op
nodes.text: An AVS funds a rewards submission weighted across strategies, or an operator-directed submission scoped to an operator set for operators registered during the period; a singleton rewardsUpdater posts distribution roots that become claimable after an activation delay, and earners claim against Merkle proofs or nominate a claimer. The operator's default split is 1000 basis points, a flat 10%.
nodes.note: Fd is a CANDIDATE symbol, used with the required mark. CORRECTION: Em is DROPPED and Fd is ADDED. Em names protocol-funded emissions; these rewards are funded by the AVS that submits them, and reach earners as a distribution of received value. The corpus carries Em with no supporting marker. UNKNOWN and flagged: EmissionsController.sol exists in src/contracts/core/ with no coverage in docs/ at the commit stage 1 read, together with ProtocolRegistry.sol and ReleaseManager.sol; if EmissionsController is what its name suggests, Em may become load-bearing and should be re-tested rather than inherited. CALCULATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS and MAX_REWARDS_DURATION are named without values.

nodes.label: F17 An AVS registers an operator-table calculator and a global configurati
nodes.text: An AVS registers an operator-table calculator and a global configuration per operator set on the source chain; on a destination chain, an updater accepts a signed GlobalTableRoot and verifies individual operator tables against it by Merkle proof, with an EigenLabs-operated Generator calculating and signing the root and a permissionless Transporter distributing it.
nodes.note: ADDED. Xm names the verification and law L18 asks it for explicit finality, chain binding and replay protection. RESIDUE recorded here: what is being transported is not a message about an asset but *the security state itself*, exported to a domain where it will be relied upon, with a single named off-chain signer at the root of it. Nothing distinguishes exporting a stake table from delivering a message.

nodes.label: F18 For faults that are obvious to human observers but not provable in the
nodes.text: For faults that are obvious to human observers but not provable in the EVM, the designed fallback is forking the EIGEN token: a challenger creates a fork in which the malicious stakers are slashed, and AVSs and users choose which fork to respect.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Oa is the nearest symbol and is deliberately not used: Oa is an on-chain dispute game with a bonded challenger and a verifier, and a social fork of a token has neither, its outcome being which asset the market prices. UNCONFIRMED at primary source: docs.eigencloud.xyz blocked automated fetch (403) and blog.eigencloud.xyz presented a TLS certificate mismatch, so the design is sourced through search summaries. UNKNOWN whether intersubjective slashing is implemented on mainnet.

nodes.label: F19 A dedicated pause flag can halt the burn-and-redistribution flow indep
nodes.text: A dedicated pause flag can halt the burn-and-redistribution flow independently of the rest of the protocol.
nodes.note: Shipped with v1.13.0. A pause scoped to one flow rather than to a contract is finer than Gp expresses, but the symbol discharges the obligation.

nodes.label: F20 The core contracts are upgradeable and a permissions controller mediat
nodes.text: The core contracts are upgradeable and a permissions controller mediates who may act for whom.
nodes.note: CORRECTION: Tg is DROPPED. Stage 1 found no first-party citation of a governance timelock for EigenLayer, and invariant 5 of the run is cite-or-drop. Law L15 (Up requires Tg or a bounded emergency process) is therefore UNMET on the available evidence; F19's pause is the only bounded emergency process cited. UNKNOWN whether a timelock exists: this is an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence, and stage 3 should record it as such rather than as a defect. Stage 1 also did not verify deployed implementation addresses against the v1.13.0 tag, so deployed-to-repo correspondence is UNKNOWN. Licence note for the paper rather than the checker: the reference implementation is BUSL-1.1 (Layr Labs, Inc.) with change dates 2025-05-01 and 2027-02-06 to MIT and a production-use restriction.

nodes.label: F21 [Vl sub-mechanism 3 of 5: deposit front-running defence] There is none
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 3 of 5: deposit front-running defence] There is none, and none is needed: the pod is deployed at an address deterministic in the staker's own address, and the same party that supplies the 32 ETH also owns the withdrawal credentials it is deposited against, so the adversary Lido's DepositSecurityModule exists to defeat, an operator capturing a pool's ETH by pre-registering the pubkey against different credentials, has no counterpart here.
nodes.note: Not residue: the obligation is closed by construction because depositor and credential owner are the same party. The empty array records this identically to an unnamed mechanism, which it is not, and that conflation is the formalism finding this stage keeps reproducing across lanes. Three of Vl's five sub-mechanisms are present here (F2, F6, F14) plus penalty attribution (F11); this one does not arise, and stake allocation (F6) is present in a form that allocates exposure rather than principal.

nodes.label: ether.fi (eETH / weETH)
F1 A user deposits ETH into the LiquidityPool and receives eETH, recorded
nodes.text: A user deposits ETH into the LiquidityPool and receives eETH, recorded as a share of a ledger holding totalShares and shares[address] at a SHARE_UNIT of 1e18; the pool tracks value in two halves, totalValueInLp and totalValueOutOfLp.
nodes.note: The repository is untagged, so the commit hash is the only pin available; b4a0968 is dated 2026-07-15. Bytecode-level correspondence between the deployed upgradeable implementations and this commit is UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F2 An eETH holder's nominal balance changes when the pool's total value c
nodes.text: An eETH holder's nominal balance changes when the pool's total value changes, without a transfer.

nodes.label: F3 A single rebase may not raise the pool's total value by more than a ha
nodes.text: A single rebase may not raise the pool's total value by more than a hard cap expressed in basis points.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. This is an oracle-error containment device applied to the accounting itself rather than to the oracle: it bounds how far one report may move the ledger, whatever the report says. Gp names a pause and Ex's L13 warrant names freshness validation; neither names a ceiling on the rate of change of a claim's value.

nodes.label: F4 weETH is the non-rebasing wrapper over eETH shares and is the form eve
nodes.text: weETH is the non-rebasing wrapper over eETH shares and is the form every integration and every cross-chain deployment uses.
nodes.note: Ix is ADDED on this obligation. Same structure as Lido's wstETH: the wrapper is the adapter that discharges prohibition X4 (Rb into a balance-invariant ledger with no adapter).

nodes.label: F5 A committee of members submits reports keyed by a report hash; once th
nodes.text: A committee of members submits reports keyed by a report hash; once the committee's quorum size is reached the report is published, and an admin contract consumes it, with report periods and reference slots gating when a report is needed and when the previous one must have been handled.
nodes.note: Ex is FORCED and retained, for the same reason as Lido: this is a quorum-signed report of protocol state, not a price feed, and the failure mode is collusion on a balance. Three protocols in this category run this shape and none of them reports a price; that is the category-level finding on Ex.

nodes.label: F6 [Vl sub-mechanism 1 of 5: registration and vetting] A node operator mu
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 1 of 5: registration and vetting] A node operator must be registered and whitelisted in NodeOperatorManager, which holds its key data, and carries approval tags mapping it to the categories of pool funds (SourceOfFunds) it is permitted to serve.
nodes.note: Aw is ADDED to the corpus construction, which carries no permission symbol for ether.fi at all. Aw names the admission gate; it does not name the per-source-of-funds scoping, which partitions one operator set into sub-populations serving different pools of capital.

nodes.label: F7 Node operators do not self-select: they bid on chain for the right to
nodes.text: Node operators do not self-select: they bid on chain for the right to be assigned a validator, with bids bounded below and above by minBidAmount and maxBidAmount and a distinct whitelistBidAmount for whitelisted bidders, and the winning bid's revenue is forwarded to the treasury.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the clearest single gap in this protocol. A priced, cleared, on-chain primary market for the operator slot is not an emission, not a fee and not a permission gate; it is closest to a primary auction for a licence. Ba (batch-auction clearing) is deliberately not used: what clears is not a trade at a uniform price but an assignment of a right, and there is no batch.

nodes.label: F8 [Vl sub-mechanism 2 of 5: allocation and scheduling] Only addresses in
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 2 of 5: allocation and scheduling] Only addresses in the validatorSpawner mapping may create validators; creation binds an accepted bid to a newly deployed EtherFiNode beacon proxy and is tracked by a validator-creation status keyed on a hash.
nodes.note: RESIDUE recorded alongside a used symbol. Aw names the spawner allowlist. What has no symbol is that allocation of principal to operators here is determined by an auction outcome plus an allowlist rather than by a scheduling rule: there is no least-allocated-first policy and no per-operator cap analogous to Lido's stake share limit. Two protocols in this category solve the same allocation problem with structurally incompatible mechanisms and the vocabulary names neither.

nodes.label: F9 [Vl sub-mechanism 3 of 5: deposit front-running defence] A 1 ETH INITI
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 3 of 5: deposit front-running defence] A 1 ETH INITIAL_DEPOSIT_AMOUNT is deposited first, pinning the validator's withdrawal credentials to the EtherFiNode contract, before the remaining balance is committed; validators range from MIN_VALIDATOR_SIZE_WEI of 32 ETH to MAX_VALIDATOR_SIZE_WEI of 2048 ETH.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the third structurally different implementation of the same defence in this category: Lido answers it with a guardian signature quorum, Lido V3 with a predeposit plus an EIP-4788 credential proof and a forfeitable guarantee, ether.fi with a bare 1 ETH predeposit and no proof and no bond. The problem is category-universal and the three answers share no structure, which makes this the strongest candidate in the lane for a new element.

nodes.label: F10 [Vl sub-mechanism 4 of 5: exit signalling] Exit and consolidation requ
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 4 of 5: exit signalling] Exit and consolidation requests are issued from EtherFiNodesManager against a validator pubkey hash, with FULL_EXIT_GWEI of 2,048,000,000,000, and each of unrestaking, exit requests and consolidation requests is metered by its own named rate-limit identifier.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Wq names the user's queue (F13, F14, F15); nothing names the validator-side exit that must complete before those queues can be paid, and nothing names its metering. Any '32 ETH unit' framing of this protocol is stale: it is on Pectra-era 0x02 validators with consolidation, matching Lido's LIP-35 move.

nodes.label: F11 [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5: penalty attribution] A consensus-layer or re
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5: penalty attribution] A consensus-layer or restaking loss reaches eETH holders as a smaller rebase, with no operator-posted first-loss capital between the operator and the holder: permissioned operators are required to bid but are not required to post a bond as collateral, and solo stakers run without posting any collateral.
nodes.note: TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) Tr is DROPPED. The T-NFT/B-NFT two-tier structure the corpus describes as 'a bond, described in tranche language' is not part of the live system: TNFT.sol and BNFT.sol are in src/archive/, retained only for storage-layout continuity. Any decomposition carrying Tr for ether.fi decomposes a dead mechanism. (2) Bs is DROPPED. With B-NFT archived and the whitepaper stating operators post no bond, stage 1 could identify no operator-posted first-loss capital in the current design; UNKNOWN whether any exists. Sl therefore does the whole of the loss work here, and the absence of any junior layer beneath eETH holders is the finding.

nodes.label: F12 Staking rewards are split 90% to stakers, 5% to node operators and 5%
nodes.text: Staking rewards are split 90% to stakers, 5% to node operators and 5% to the protocol, and restaking rewards route separately through a rewards router and a cumulative-Merkle distributor.
nodes.note: Fd is a CANDIDATE symbol, used with the required mark, and is ADDED; Em is DROPPED. Em names protocol-funded emissions of an existing asset; what is distributed here is received reward value, not newly funded incentive. See F19 for what Em was standing in for.

nodes.label: F13 Standard exit: a holder burns eETH for an ERC-721 withdrawal request;
nodes.text: Standard exit: a holder burns eETH for an ERC-721 withdrawal request; an admin finalises a batch, and the claim rate is snapshotted at finalisation with ceiling rounding so that for any finalised token the claimable amount is invariant under subsequent rebases.
nodes.note: RESIDUE recorded alongside a used symbol, and the contract states this as its own invariant I3, property-tested, headed as 'the H-02 fix' from an audit. Rate freezing at finalisation is a deliberate severing of a claim from the accounting index at a named block: Rb and Wq together cannot say it, because it is the difference between a queue position and a fixed-price forward. Ft (fixed-term debt) is deliberately not used: there is no maturity date, only a frozen price.

nodes.label: F14 Instant exit: a holder redeems eETH or weETH for ETH or stETH immediat
nodes.text: Instant exit: a holder redeems eETH or weETH for ETH or stETH immediately in exchange for an exit fee, capped by a refilling token bucket over a time period and floored by a low-watermark expressed in basis points of pool TVL, with a stale-price window and a maximum price threshold on the stETH price feed.
nodes.note: Rd is ADDED: this door is a genuine direct redemption right, priced and capped. Ex is claimed here in its ordinary sense for once, because the stETH price feed is a real price oracle with a freshness bound, which satisfies law L13 and is a different object from the state-reporting committee of F5. The token bucket is RESIDUE; see F16.

nodes.label: F15 Priority exit: whitelisted addresses redeem through a separate queue w
nodes.text: Priority exit: whitelisted addresses redeem through a separate queue with an immutable minimum delay, for amounts between 0.01 and 1000 ETH, against a separately locked ETH balance.
nodes.note: Audited only in 2026-03, after the corpus record was written.

nodes.label: F16 The choice among three exit doors, differently priced and carrying dif
nodes.text: The choice among three exit doors, differently priced and carrying different rights, is itself a mechanism: instant is fee-bearing and bucket-limited, standard is free and rate-frozen at an admin's finalisation, priority is whitelisted and delay-bounded.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Wq names one queue. The corpus knows one withdrawal queue for ether.fi; the live protocol has three, and the routing between them determines the price a holder pays to leave. Nothing names a menu of exits with different terms over one claim.

nodes.label: F17 A refilling token-bucket budget meters unrestaking, exit requests, con
nodes.text: A refilling token-bucket budget meters unrestaking, exit requests, consolidation requests and instant redemptions.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and category-recurrent. This is not a pause and not a cap: it is a refilling budget on a state transition, and it appears four times in this one protocol and in three of the five protocols in this category (here, WBETH's exchange-rate allowance, Lido's per-module deposit rate limits and vault quarantine). Nothing in the 58 names it.

nodes.label: F18 [What the restaked collateral secures] The same principal that backs e
nodes.text: [What the restaked collateral secures] The same principal that backs eETH is natively restaked: the EtherFiNode holding the validators' withdrawal credentials is also an EigenPod, so one deposit serves Ethereum consensus and EigenLayer without a second user action and without a second lockup.
nodes.note: Rs is a CANDIDATE, used with the mark, and is exact in name and thin in content. It asserts restaking is a fact and stops.

nodes.label: F19 [Who may write a slashing condition over the restaked collateral] Neit
nodes.text: [Who may write a slashing condition over the restaked collateral] Neither ether.fi's contracts nor the eETH holder: AVS selection and registration live outside this repository, in etherfi-avs-operator, and the README states restaking and AVS management are strictly controlled by the Protocol.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the thinnest point in the carrier for this application. The party bearing the loss neither chooses nor can observe on chain who is empowered to author the slashing conditions over its principal; the control object is out-of-repo and permissioned. UNKNOWN which AVSs and which restaking venues are live as of 2026-08. Restaking rewards additionally route through KING, a separate protocol organisation, since 2026.

nodes.label: F20 [Whether the same collateral can be committed twice] Yes: the same pri
nodes.text: [Whether the same collateral can be committed twice] Yes: the same principal is committed to Ethereum consensus and to EigenLayer operator sets at once. Within EigenLayer the second commitment is bounded, because an operator's magnitude allocations cannot exceed its total magnitude; across venues nothing in ether.fi bounds or discloses the aggregate exposure.
nodes.note: CORRECTION. The corpus residue entry describes restaking 'into several heterogeneous security markets at once (EigenLayer, Symbiotic, Karak) with slashing conditions written by parties who do not know about each other'. Within EigenLayer that is refuted by Unique Stake. Across venues it is not refuted, but stage 1 found no first-party evidence that ether.fi currently restakes anywhere other than EigenLayer: EtherFiRestaker imports only EigenLayer's StrategyManager, DelegationManager and RewardsCoordinator. The multi-venue framing is therefore UNKNOWN rather than established, and stage 2 does not inherit it.

nodes.label: F21 A node contract may execute a bounded set of arbitrary calls into its
nodes.text: A node contract may execute a bounded set of arbitrary calls into its own EigenPod or into a named external target, gated per caller, per function selector and per target address.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the closest thing in this whole category to Au. Au is deliberately not used: law L17 asks delegated execution scope for bounded scope, revocation, expiry and nonce/domain separation, and only the first two are present. More decisively, the authority is delegated by the protocol to itself, mediated by a role registry, and its purpose is to let one protocol drive another protocol's state machine. Nothing names an adapter with a selector allowlist for driving a foreign protocol.

nodes.label: F22 A protocol-wide blacklister is wired into eETH, the LiquidityPool, the
nodes.text: A protocol-wide blacklister is wired into eETH, the LiquidityPool, the AuctionManager, both withdrawal queues and the redemption manager.
nodes.note: Fz is a CANDIDATE, used with the required mark, and is ADDED: the corpus element list for ether.fi contains no freeze or permission symbol at all. Law L28 asks Fz for a named authority, enumerated triggers, an appeal path and holder disclosure; stage 1 found the authority (RoleRegistry) but not the triggers, the appeal path or the disclosure, so the warrant is partly unmet.

nodes.label: F23 Authority for the whole protocol is centralised in one RoleRegistry co
nodes.text: Authority for the whole protocol is centralised in one RoleRegistry contract read by nearly every other contract through a shared mixin; two timelocks are deployed, an upgrade timelock and an operating timelock; every contract is UUPS- or beacon-upgradeable; and a mixin provides time-bounded rather than indefinite pauses.
nodes.note: Law L15 (Up requires Tg or a bounded emergency process) is satisfied twice over, by the upgrade timelock and by the time-bounded pause. RESIDUE recorded here: Tg, Up and Gp describe three separate control mechanisms and cannot express that one registry contract is the authority for all of them, which makes the registry a single point of governance failure that the triple conceals rather than reveals.

nodes.label: F24 Deposits were acquired through an off-chain loyalty-points programme w
nodes.text: Deposits were acquired through an off-chain loyalty-points programme whose balances were later converted into a token.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the reason Em is dropped rather than merely unused. Em names emissions of an existing asset on a published schedule; points are a discretionary, revocable, off-chain promissory ledger with no on-chain representation and no commitment. The on-chain residue of the early programme (EarlyAdopterPool, LoyaltyPointsMarketSafe, membership/) now sits in src/archive/, which is itself the evidence: the instrument lived and died off-ledger, and the vocabulary never saw it.

nodes.label: F25 Some validators are operated as distributed validators, one key split
nodes.text: Some validators are operated as distributed validators, one key split into keyshares across a cluster with a signing threshold, in the solo-staker programme.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The vocabulary has zero coverage of a threshold-signed distributed validator key. The scope claim is NARROWED from the corpus: stage 1 could place Obol/Charon only in the Operation Solo Staker programme, not demonstrably in the main permissioned operator set, and the primary page returned 404 on direct fetch so the 3/4 cluster threshold is UNCONFIRMED at first-party source. UNKNOWN what fraction of ether.fi's validator set is distributed. The category-level point that DVT is the largest unnamed mechanism by TVL stands on Lido's Simple DVT module plus SSV and Obol independently of this entry.

nodes.label: Lido
F1 A user who sends ETH to the core pool receives stETH minted 1:1 at dep
nodes.text: A user who sends ETH to the core pool receives stETH minted 1:1 at deposit, recorded not as a balance but as a share of a ledger whose balance function is shares x totalPooledEther / totalShares.
nodes.note: The accounting-oracle page is the stage-1-itemised first-party source that describes the pooled-ether recomputation and fee-share minting that the share ledger is defined against. The dedicated stETH contract page (docs.lido.fi/contracts/lido) is a sibling in the same verified docs tree but was not itemised in stage 1's evidence table; stage 3 may re-verify there.

nodes.label: F2 A holder's nominal stETH balance changes, up or down, when the oracle
nodes.text: A holder's nominal stETH balance changes, up or down, when the oracle report changes total pooled ether, with no transfer and no action by the holder.

nodes.label: F3 wstETH holds shares directly, so an integration that cannot tolerate a
nodes.text: wstETH holds shares directly, so an integration that cannot tolerate a moving balance holds a fixed-quantity token whose value per unit rises instead.
nodes.note: This is the Rb/Ix duality made explicit: the same claim is expressible as a moving balance or as a moving index over a fixed balance. It also discharges prohibition X4 (Rb into a balance-invariant ledger with no adapter) by being the adapter. Ix is added to the construction on this obligation alone; the core token is Rb.

nodes.label: F4 A quorum of a permissioned committee (documented 5 of 9) publishes onc
nodes.text: A quorum of a permissioned committee (documented 5 of 9) publishes once per 225-epoch consensus-layer frame a signed report of consensus-layer validator balances, pending balances, newly exited validators per module, withdrawal-vault and execution-layer reward balances, shares requested to burn, the withdrawal finalisation batches and a bunker-mode flag; the report is rejected unless it passes bounds in OracleReportSanityChecker.
nodes.note: Ex is FORCED and retained. Ex names a price feed (push/pull/medianizer); this is a quorum-signed report of protocol state and the failure mode is collusion on a balance, not manipulation of a market price. The sanity bounds satisfy law L13's freshness/validation warrant on Ex, so L13 is met. The category-level residue stands: nothing in the 58 distinguishes a state-reporting committee from a price feed.

nodes.label: F5 10% of rewards is retained as a protocol fee, minted as new shares, an
nodes.text: 10% of rewards is retained as a protocol fee, minted as new shares, and split between node operators and the DAO treasury at a rate that differs per staking module: Curated 5/5, the permissionless module 3.5/6.5, Simple DVT 8/2 for normal clusters and 6/4 for super clusters; 90% reaches stakers in every module.
nodes.note: Fd is a CANDIDATE symbol, used with the required mark. CORRECTION to the corpus. The corpus Fd marker states 'the 10% fee splits 5% to node operators and 5% to treasury'. First-party source states the split is per-module. A single global fee split is not a fact about Lido, and Fd carries a distribution rule without a way to scope it to a counterparty class.

nodes.label: F6 Only DAO-approved addresses may register as node operators in the Cura
nodes.text: Only DAO-approved addresses may register as node operators in the Curated module, and only clusters approved by a 5-of-7 SAFE multisig may operate in Simple DVT; Simple DVT onboarding is closed.
nodes.note: ADDED to the corpus construction. The corpus element list for Lido carries no permission symbol despite two of the three live modules being permissioned.

nodes.label: F7 Anyone may become a node operator in the Community Staking Module by p
nodes.text: Anyone may become a node operator in the Community Staking Module by posting a slashable stETH bond on a declining curve (portal states 2.4 down to 1.3 ETH), with the module capped at a 9% stake share.
nodes.note: Bs is exact for CSM and false for Curated, whose operators post nothing. The vocabulary has no way to scope a symbol to a subset of a protocol; see F8.

nodes.label: F8 [Vl sub-mechanism 1 of 5: validator key registration and vetting] Thre
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 1 of 5: validator key registration and vetting] Three mutually incompatible operator-admission and key-vetting regimes run side by side over one share ledger and one loss pool: permissioned and unbonded (Curated, NodeOperatorsRegistry), permissioned and cluster-managed by a 5-of-7 multisig over Obol and SSV clusters (Simple DVT), and permissionless and bonded (CSM). Separately, a guardian may invalidate specific already-submitted validator public keys with a single signature, bounded by maxOperatorsPerUnvetting, without removing the operator.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the first of the five mechanisms Vl compresses. Aw (F6) names one gate and Bs (F7) one bond; neither can be scoped to a subset of a protocol, and nothing names the coexistence of three trust models over one claim. Nothing at all names key-level vetting as distinct from operator-level admission: unvetSigningKeys invalidates a pubkey while leaving the operator registered, which is neither a permission change nor a removal. Vl is not used here: it names the aggregate category, not this mechanism, and using it would assert the sameness the code refutes.

nodes.label: F9 [Vl sub-mechanism 2 of 5: stake allocation and scheduling across opera
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 2 of 5: stake allocation and scheduling across operator modules] Buffered ETH is allocated across the module registry by MinFirstAllocationStrategy, which fills the least-allocated modules first in whole validator units until the amount is exhausted or capacity is reached, subject to a per-module stake share limit, a per-module priority exit share threshold, per-module deposit rate limits (maxDepositsPerBlock, minDepositBlockDistance) and a per-module withdrawal-credential type.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. This is a scheduler over heterogeneous counterparties with per-counterparty hard caps and rate limits, and nothing in the 58 names a scheduler. Any framing of it as 'who receives the next 32 ETH' is now stale: LIP-35 (shipped in lidofinance/core v4.0.0, 2026-07-24) makes module reward weight moduleActiveBalance / totalActiveBalance, i.e. balance-weighted rather than validator-count weighted.

nodes.label: F10 [Vl sub-mechanism 3 of 5, implementation A: deposit front-running defe
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 3 of 5, implementation A: deposit front-running defence] Buffered ETH may be deposited only after a 4-of-6 guardian committee signs, in EIP-2098 short form, over (blockNumber, blockHash, depositRoot, stakingModuleId, nonce); this defeats an operator who front-runs depositBufferedEther with a >=1 ETH direct deposit using the same pubkey and different withdrawal credentials in order to capture the pool's 32 ETH. Any single guardian may unilaterally pause deposits, with validity bounded by pauseIntentValidityPeriodBlocks.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Aw would call this a permission gate, which misreads it: the guardians do not decide who may deposit, they attest that a specific block's deposit root has not been poisoned. Gp names the unilateral pause but not the attestation, and the attestation is the mechanism. Quorum 4 of 6 is first-party; the corpus states no quorum.

nodes.label: F11 [Vl sub-mechanism 3 of 5, implementation B] In a stVault the node oper
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 3 of 5, implementation B] In a stVault the node operator locks a 1 ETH guarantee and submits a 1 ETH predeposit that pins the withdrawal credentials; PredepositGuarantee stages the remaining 31 ETH and releases it only once the validator's withdrawal credentials are proved against a beacon block root via EIP-4788 with BLS12-381 verification (EIP-2537). Wrong credentials cause the guarantee to be seized. Policies are STRICT, ALLOW_PROVE and ALLOW_DEPOSIT_AND_PROVE.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a CORRECTION to the corpus, which records only the committee-signature form. This is a structurally different answer to the same adversary: a cryptographic credential proof plus a forfeitable bond, with no committee and no signature quorum. One protocol now runs two incompatible anti-front-running mechanisms simultaneously, and the vocabulary has no symbol for either.

nodes.label: F12 [Vl sub-mechanism 4 of 5: exit signalling and the validator-side exit
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 4 of 5: exit signalling and the validator-side exit queue] A second oracle publishes packed exit requests naming (moduleId, nodeOperatorId, validatorIndex, pubkey), sorted ascending on that key, subject to a per-report cap and to an ETH-denominated per-frame budget that restores at 32 ETH per 0x01 validator and 2048 ETH per 0x02 validator; operator compliance with a published request is an off-chain social norm, and non-compliance is answered by submitting EIP-7002 triggerable-withdrawal requests through a gateway with msg.value covering the EIP-7002 fee.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The contract calls itself 'an on-chain message bus between the protocol's off-chain oracle and off-chain observers'. Wq covers the user's withdrawal request; nothing covers the validator-side exit that must complete before the user's queue can be paid, nor the fact that the primary enforcement is a social norm (SNOP 3.0) with a forced-exit fallback.

nodes.label: F13 [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5, regime A: penalty attribution] A consensus-l
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5, regime A: penalty attribution] A consensus-layer penalty or slashing appears as a lower reported validator balance and is absorbed as a negative rebase across the entire stETH supply, irrespective of which operator or module caused it.
nodes.note: Sl is retained and is FORCED in exactly the way the corpus states: it names the socialisation correctly and cannot express that the loss is not attributed to the party that caused it. This is the one of Vl's five sub-mechanisms the vocabulary can partly name, and the gap is recorded here rather than as an empty array because the symbol does discharge the allocation.

nodes.label: F14 [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5, regime B] A CSM operator's own posted bond a
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 5 of 5, regime B] A CSM operator's own posted bond absorbs penalties attributable to its own validators, and accumulated strikes trigger EIP-7002 ejection with a badPerformancePenalty, so a second, module-local, attributed loss regime runs simultaneously with the socialised one.
nodes.note: RESIDUE recorded alongside a used symbol: Bs names the bond and Sl names the socialisation, but nothing names a protocol running two loss regimes at once, nor the boundary that decides which loss goes to which.

nodes.label: F15 [Vl sub-mechanism 6, absent from the corpus: validator sizing, top-up
nodes.text: [Vl sub-mechanism 6, absent from the corpus: validator sizing, top-up and consolidation] Validators may be created with 0x01 credentials at 32 ETH or 0x02 credentials up to 2048 ETH; stake may be added to a live validator through TopUpGateway with a 2 ETH minimum and a 1.25 ETH margin; and stake may be migrated between operators through a three-contract consolidation pipeline (ConsolidationMigrator, ConsolidationBus, ConsolidationGateway).
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and NEW: absent from the corpus record, which predates lidofinance/core v4.0.0 (2026-07-24). Merging two existing validators and adding stake to a live one are neither registration nor exit; Vl has no place to put them. This is a sixth separable mechanism inside the one symbol, one more than the structural claim on trial asserts.

nodes.label: F16 A holder burns stETH into a withdrawal queue and receives an ERC-721 (
nodes.text: A holder burns stETH into a withdrawal queue and receives an ERC-721 (also ERC-4906) representing a queue position, between 100 wei and 1000 ETH; the accounting oracle path prefinalizes and finalizes batches at a maximum share rate of 1e27, locking ether and burning the shares, after which the NFT holder claims against a checkpoint hint.
nodes.note: The oracle report additionally carries an isBunkerMode flag that changes finalisation semantics under mass-slashing conditions. Nothing in the 58 names a protocol-wide mode switch that alters the settlement rule of a queue; that is residue carried in this note rather than as a separate obligation.

nodes.label: F17 The protocol asserts as a design invariant that all existing stETH can
nodes.text: The protocol asserts as a design invariant that all existing stETH can be converted into ETH at a 1:1 ratio.
nodes.note: ADDED. The right is asserted at 1:1 and mediated by F16's queue rather than being immediate, which satisfies law L14 (illiquid backing requires a queue or a bounded liquidity reserve) and keeps prohibition X5 (illiquid backing plus uncapped instant par redemption) disarmed.

nodes.label: F18 A vault owner may mint stETH as a liability against an isolated stakin
nodes.text: A vault owner may mint stETH as a liability against an isolated staking position whose collateral is a validator set, over-collateralised at a DAO-set reserve ratio, with locked value = liability + max(reserve implied by the ratio, max(1 ETH connect deposit, slashing reserve)); a vault below its force-rebalance threshold is unhealthy.
nodes.note: ADDED, both symbols. The corpus record predates Lido V3 entirely (mainnet 2026-01-30) and contains no trace of an over-collateralised minting path. Cd warrants Ct (law L1c) and Ct is present; law L1d's loss branch is satisfied by Sl and Bs, already in the construction.

nodes.label: F19 An unhealthy vault may be force-rebalanced by anyone, and while unheal
nodes.text: An unhealthy vault may be force-rebalanced by anyone, and while unhealthy is blocked from minting, from withdrawal, from beacon deposits and from full partial withdrawal; vault obligations are serviced in a fixed order, health first, then redemptions to service core withdrawals, then Lido fees.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Li is the nearest symbol and is deliberately not used: Li requires that third parties be paid to close positions, and stage 1 found no first-party statement of a payment to the force-rebalance caller. A permissionless close with no cited incentive is not incentivized liquidation, and asserting Li would be exactly the forced fit this stage exists to catch. Nothing names a fixed ordering over a position's competing obligations either.

nodes.label: F20 The same validator principal backs both the vault owner's own position
nodes.text: The same validator principal backs both the vault owner's own position and the stETH minted against it, and the DAO caps in basis points the fraction of total stETH supply that may be backed by external vault collateral rather than by the core pool (setMaxExternalRatioBP).
nodes.note: RESIDUE. This is the category's 'can the same collateral be committed twice' question in its Lido form: yes, once as an isolated staking position and once as backing for a fungible pool claim, with a single global cap as the only bound. Nothing in the 58 names a cap on how much of one claim class may be backed by a different collateral topology, and that cap is the seam between the two products. The protocol-levers page names the lever and carries no current numeric value.

nodes.label: F21 A vault's reported value is usable only if it matches the latest check
nodes.text: A vault's reported value is usable only if it matches the latest checkpoint and is under two days old, staleness blocking withdrawals, minting, rebalancing, beacon deposits and disconnection; and value increases above routine execution- and consensus-layer rewards are held in a timelocked quarantine buffer rather than credited immediately.
nodes.note: Ex is used for the Merkle-rooted state posting and its freshness gate, which is Ex's own L13 warrant. The quarantine is RESIDUE and is recorded here: a timelock applied to an anomalous reported *value* rather than to a transaction or a governance action has no symbol. Tg names delayed execution of a decision, not delayed recognition of a number.

nodes.label: F22 A DAO motion cannot execute for at least three days, and stETH, wstETH
nodes.text: A DAO motion cannot execute for at least three days, and stETH, wstETH or withdrawal-NFT holders who escrow their position (minimum five-hour lock) extend that delay dynamically between 5 and 45 days; at a first seal of 1% of stETH supply the timelock begins growing, and at a second seal of 10% the protocol enters rage quit, blocking all execution until the escrowed stETH has been fully withdrawn to ETH, with a 7-day rage-quit extension and a 60-to-180-day ETH withdrawal delay.
nodes.note: Tg names the delay and Ep the state-machine transitions. RESIDUE carried here: nothing names a second governance chamber whose ballot is a redemption. The corpus residue entry is correct but under-specified; LIP-28 gives a five-state machine, exact thresholds and three named committees (Reseal, Emergency 4/7 and 5/7, Tiebreaker 2/3).

nodes.label: F23 Every principal contract in the protocol is a proxy whose implementati
nodes.text: Every principal contract in the protocol is a proxy whose implementation the DAO can replace, and named committees can pause or reseal individual contracts outside the ordinary governance path.
nodes.note: Law L15 (Up requires Tg or a bounded emergency process) is satisfied by F22. Prohibition X9 (Up with immediate single-key control) is disarmed: upgrades pass through the dual-governance timelock. Stage 1 did not perform a byte-level source-vs-deployment diff, so the correspondence between the deployed implementations and any repo commit is UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F24 A stVault is grouped into an operator group and a tier carrying its ow
nodes.text: A stVault is grouped into an operator group and a tier carrying its own share limit, reserve ratio, force-rebalance threshold and fees; tier changes require dual confirmation from both the vault owner and the node operator, and the DAO may jail a specific vault, blocking minting while continuing to permit burns and administrative operations.
nodes.note: Aw names the tiering and the dual-confirmation gate. The jail is RESIDUE and is recorded here: it is neither a pause (the contract keeps operating) nor a permission gate (the owner's identity is unchanged) but a suspension of one specific capability of one specific position. Stage 1 also records the asserted invariant that slashing consequences are contained within the operator group, which is a per-group loss fence with no symbol.

nodes.label: 05-perpetuals
ApeX Protocol (ApeX Omni)
F1 orders rest in a price-time-priority central limit order book with mak
nodes.text: orders rest in a price-time-priority central limit order book with maker and taker fees tiered from 2/5 bps down to 0/2.5 bps, offering up to 100x leverage on majors
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Ob asserts an ON-CHAIN order book. ApeX's microstructure is a price-time-priority CLOB, but the venue never states where the book is kept (F2), so the 'on-chain' half of the symbol is unverified and probably false. Fee table at https://apex-pro.gitbook.io/apex-pro/apex-omni/trading-and-funding-fees.md (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F2 the venue does not state where its matching engine runs: the documente
nodes.text: the venue does not state where its matching engine runs: the documented architecture is an Access / Application / Blockchain layering whose execution layer 'leverages the zkLink engine' and whose settlement layer 'provides proof verification', reached through an operator-hosted REST and WebSocket API
nodes.note: RESIDUE — matching locus, and here the vocabulary is not merely blind to the answer: the protocol does not publish the answer. No symbol can express 'the locus is undisclosed'. Corroborating architecture claim at https://apex-pro.gitbook.io/apex-pro/what-is-apex-omni.md (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F3 every order, transfer and withdrawal carries a user-supplied ZkKeys si
nodes.text: every order, transfer and withdrawal carries a user-supplied ZkKeys signature — a zkLink L2 signature over the order parameters — in addition to HMAC-SHA256 API-key authentication of the session
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Au names a delegated execution scope. The API key is exactly that (a scoped session credential, with TradFi perps requiring a separately scoped key), but the scoping partitions ASSET CLASSES rather than permissions, and the second signature is self-custodial authorisation rather than delegation. The pair together — 'the operator may route but may not author an order' — has no expression.

nodes.label: F4 no constraint on the operator's ordering or matching discretion is pub
nodes.text: no constraint on the operator's ordering or matching discretion is published: there is no stated fairness rule, no sequencing commitment and no named sequencer, and zkLink X's own sequencing is described as delegable to third parties without ApeX stating whether it delegates
nodes.note: RESIDUE — operator discretion. Contrast Hyperliquid's in-block class ordering and Lighter's proven priority. The user-signed ZkKeys signature (F3) bounds what the operator may forge but not what it may reorder or withhold.

nodes.label: F5 state transitions are finalised by validity proofs on a zkLink X app-r
nodes.text: state transitions are finalised by validity proofs on a zkLink X app-rollup, batched at app-rollup and L2 levels before Ethereum settlement, with proofs first committed on a host chain that forwards sync hashes
nodes.note: RESIDUE — proof system. The 58 contain no element for a validity proof; `Zk` is contested-register and outside the vocabulary, and in any case names state validity, which is exactly what does NOT distinguish this venue from Lighter (whose proof covers the matching rule). Note also that the proof is a third party's: the stack is zkLink X, and no auditor is named for ApeX Omni itself (https://apex-pro.gitbook.io/apex-pro/faqs/apex-protocol-faqs/is-apex-omni-safe-are-your-smart-contracts-audited.md, 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F6 the data-availability layer under the venue is not stated: zkLink X of
nodes.text: the data-availability layer under the venue is not stated: zkLink X offers Ethereum, Celestia, EigenDA, Polygon Avail or a zkLink-organised committee, and ApeX's selection is documented nowhere
nodes.note: RESIDUE — data availability. The corpus residue asserts a data-availability committee for ApeX; stage 1 shows that is an inherited guess from the discontinued StarkEx product and is not established, so the DAC claim is DROPPED and replaced by this obligation.

nodes.label: F7 a censored trader exits in two steps — submit a forced exit on zkLink
nodes.text: a censored trader exits in two steps — submit a forced exit on zkLink L2, wait for on-chain confirmation, then claim on L1 by interacting directly with the ApeX zkLink contract on the chosen chain — with no deadline or exit-window duration stated anywhere
nodes.note: RESIDUE — exit. Two things are unnameable: the escape hatch itself, and the fact that its DEADLINE — the whole censorship-resistance argument — is absent. The absence of a parameter is not expressible. Per-chain contract addresses are published on the same page (BNB 0xb8d9f005654b7b127b34dae8f973ba729ca3a2d9, Ethereum 0x35D173cdfE4d484BC5985fDa55FABad5892c7B82, Arbitrum 0x3169844a120c0f517b4eb4a750c08d8518c8466a, Base 0xee7981c4642de8d19aed11da3bac59277dfd59d7, Mantle 0x3c7c0ebfcd5786ef48df5ed127cddeb806db976c).

nodes.label: F8 collateral is deposited on any of Ethereum, BNB Chain, Arbitrum, Base,
nodes.text: collateral is deposited on any of Ethereum, BNB Chain, Arbitrum, Base, Mantle or Solana into a per-chain contract, credited to an Omni funding account, and transferred internally into a Perps or Spot account
nodes.note: Xf names the asset movement. Xm is APPROXIMATE: the cross-chain state synchronisation is zkLink's (Nexus via zk-proof and Ethereum, Origin via zk-proof and a Light Oracle Network), the verification is not ApeX's own, and which scheme ApeX runs is undocumented (https://docs.zk.link/, 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F9 one account balance spans six chains: the chain of deposit is a coordi
nodes.text: one account balance spans six chains: the chain of deposit is a coordinate on a single account object rather than a separate account per domain
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Xf names the transfer and Xm the verification; neither says the ledger is unified. The contested `Ua` (unified-balance ledger) gestures at it and is outside the 58 — and unlike Hyperliquid, where the corpus declined `Ua` as merely scope, for ApeX this is the headline product claim.

nodes.label: F10 all positions share one unified margin pool backed by total account eq
nodes.text: all positions share one unified margin pool backed by total account equity in USDT, with no isolated mode available
nodes.note: Ct computes the test; it cannot say that the test is portfolio-wide by construction and that per-position ring-fencing is unavailable. Margin scope remains residue as it does for Hyperliquid.

nodes.label: F11 initial margin is position size times entry price times IMR, maintenan
nodes.text: initial margin is position size times entry price times IMR, maintenance margin is position size times mark price times MMR, and liquidation fires when the margin ratio (total maintenance margin over total equity) reaches 100%
nodes.note: A single trigger line, unlike Lighter's three-rung ladder — a distinction Ct cannot carry.

nodes.label: F12 eight non-USDT collaterals are valued as Amount x Index Price x Collat
nodes.text: eight non-USDT collaterals are valued as Amount x Index Price x Collateral Ratio under tiered haircuts and per-asset supply caps (USDC 99% on the first 5,000,000 then 97.5%, capped at 20,000,000; USDT 100% and uncapped), while a second balance — Perpetual Balance — is computed without the haircut
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Ct names the threshold test, not the map from token balance to margin value with per-asset ratios and supply caps — and certainly not the coexistence of TWO different valuations of the same collateral. This is absent from the corpus record entirely and it changes what Ct has to compute.

nodes.label: F13 positions are marked to Median(Price1, Price2, Last Price), where Pric
nodes.text: positions are marked to Median(Price1, Price2, Last Price), where Price1 is the index adjusted by the last funding rate over the fraction of the interval remaining and Price2 is the index plus a 5-minute moving average of the mid-index basis, and mark price — not last price — drives liquidations, unrealised PnL, bankruptcy price and margin requirements
nodes.note: Ex names the index feed. Its publisher is not named in ApeX's documentation, so this is an external oracle whose source is undisclosed — a weaker position than Ex implies. Tp is NOT claimed: the 5-minute moving average is computed inside an operator-run engine, not on chain, so 'on-chain time-weighted price' would be false.

nodes.label: F14 longs and shorts exchange funding every hour on the hour UTC at F = P
nodes.text: longs and shorts exchange funding every hour on the hour UTC at F = P + clamp(I - P, -0.05%, +0.05%), with the fee computed as position size times index price times F, the hourly rate capped at plus or minus 0.05%, and any excess beyond the cap absorbed by the platform rather than passed to the counterparty
nodes.note: Pf fits exactly — this is a genuine long/short transfer, so the category's 'perp tether' flag is refuted here. What Pf cannot carry is the truncation: above the cap the venue itself becomes the counterparty to the tether, which is an unpriced liability of the operator.

nodes.label: F15 on breach the liquidation engine closes positions in order of risk sev
nodes.text: on breach the liquidation engine closes positions in order of risk severity at available market prices, and charges a liquidation fee
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Li names third parties PAID to close positions. Here an operator-run engine closes them; the liquidation fee exists but is routed to the Insurance Vault's depositors (F18), not to a keeper. The 'incentivized third party' half of the symbol is absent.

nodes.label: F16 if a liquidated position cannot be closed at or above its bankruptcy p
nodes.text: if a liquidated position cannot be closed at or above its bankruptcy price, profitable opposite-side positions are closed at the bankruptcy price, ranked by leveraged return, with the ranking surfaced to users so they can manage their queue position
nodes.note: Ad fits. It is also, on this venue's own documentation, the FIRST and only loss-absorption layer — the ADL page names no fund that absorbs before it.

nodes.label: F17 no insurance fund exists: the string does not occur anywhere in the ve
nodes.text: no insurance fund exists: the string does not occur anywhere in the venue's 383 KB documentation corpus, and no capital is documented as absorbing a bankrupt position before auto-deleveraging
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the reason `Bs` is DROPPED from the corpus element set. The corpus justifies Bs with 'the insurance fund absorbs bankrupt-position losses but is protocol-owned and non-slashable'; BOTH halves fail — there is no fund, and what is called the Insurance Vault is user capital (F18). Removing Bs leaves Ad as the loss-absorption element, so the construction still discharges the requirement.

nodes.label: F18 users deposit USDT into a Protocol Vault branded the Insurance Vault,
nodes.text: users deposit USDT into a Protocol Vault branded the Insurance Vault, receive shares at NAV with no lock-up and redemption at any time, and earn 100% of the previous day's liquidation fees from all Omni perp trades, credited at 08:05 UTC
nodes.note: Sh names the pro-rata claim; Fd (CANDIDATE-REGISTER) names the routing of a fee stream to that claim class. What neither names — and what makes this venue's backstop different in kind from Hyperliquid's HLP and Lighter's LLP — is that the docs simultaneously call it 'a backstop for the protocol' and promise a 'stable, positive, and protocol-guaranteed' return: first-loss capital RECRUITED BY RENTING IT with a fee stream, with no stated loss-absorption duty.

nodes.label: F19 traders create and manage Omni Vaults (Community Vaults) that attract
nodes.text: traders create and manage Omni Vaults (Community Vaults) that attract external capital and pay the manager a performance fee, for example 10% of profits
nodes.note: Sh names the depositor claim only; the delegated trading mandate and its fee have no symbol. Unlike Hyperliquid, no minimum manager stake is documented.

nodes.label: F20 the venue renders a third party's order books — Polymarket's — inside
nodes.text: the venue renders a third party's order books — Polymarket's — inside its own interface, margined from the user's Omni account and settled in Polymarket USD
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Ag is route construction across venues for a swap; this is a HOSTED foreign book with a foreign settlement currency, margined from the host's account. Also absent from the corpus record: TradFi perpetuals, tokenised US stocks and Pre-IPO spot inside the same account.

nodes.label: F21 a trader's fee tier advances on the greater of 14-day volume or staked
nodes.text: a trader's fee tier advances on the greater of 14-day volume or staked APEX, and APEX / esAPEX staking carries revenue-sharing incentives
nodes.note: Fd (CANDIDATE-REGISTER) names the revenue share. `Em` is DROPPED relative to the corpus: stage 1 found esAPEX vesting and revenue sharing but no emissions schedule, so 'protocol-funded emissions' is unsupported and what is documented is fee distribution. Residual: a fee tier advanced by the MAXIMUM of two unrelated commitments (volume traded, capital staked) is a substitution rule with no expression.

nodes.label: F22 no upgrade authority, timelock, guardian or pause power over the contr
nodes.text: no upgrade authority, timelock, guardian or pause power over the contracts custodying user funds is documented, and the contracts in question are zkLink's rather than the venue's
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the reason `Tg` and `Up` are DROPPED from the corpus element set. The corpus asserts both with no visible support; stage 1 searched the documentation corpus and found no timelock, no governance execution delay and no upgrade authority. Recording 'the control plane is undocumented' is not the same as recording 'there is none', and the vocabulary can do neither. The predecessor product ApeX Pro (StarkEx) is discontinued and archived (https://l2beat.com/scaling/archived, 2026-08-04), so any StarkEx-derived control-plane claim in the corpus is inherited from a dead product.

nodes.label: Aster
F1 each perpetual market runs an independent price-time-priority order bo
nodes.text: each perpetual market runs an independent price-time-priority order book, and the Clearinghouse holds per-trader margin balances and open positions as the chain's core execution component
nodes.note: Ob names the book. Note this is an in-consensus book: the corpus marker calling Ob 'only approximately applies — matching is engine-side with on-chain settlement, not an on-chain book' is STALE and is dropped (see F2).

nodes.label: F2 all order matching and trading logic are processed and stored on-chain
nodes.text: all order matching and trading logic are processed and stored on-chain, inside Aster Chain — the venue's own Layer 1, launched 16 March 2026, running Proof-of-Staked-Authority consensus at 50 ms blocks with zero gas
nodes.note: RESIDUE — matching locus, and a DEPARTURE from the corpus, which groups Aster with the operator-run books. Its own documentation puts it on Hyperliquid's side of the split. This also refutes the corpus's three-model taxonomy: Aster is a FOURTH model — in-consensus, but with a closed validator set and closed-source node software (F3) — which has the failure modes of an operator behind the surface of a chain. Launch date corroborated at https://docs.asterdex.com/llms-full.txt (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F3 external validator participation is not supported in Phase 1, and core
nodes.text: external validator participation is not supported in Phase 1, and core chain contracts and RPC infrastructure are not open-sourced, as stated policy, in order to protect proprietary matching engine algorithms
nodes.note: RESIDUE — operator discretion. The set that matches, prices, signs the bridge and votes on listings is closed and its software is secret. Nothing in the vocabulary can record 'the execution rule is secret while the state commitment is public', which is precisely the trust argument the venue makes.

nodes.label: F4 no validity or fraud proof covers execution; safety rests on a permiss
nodes.text: no validity or fraud proof covers execution; safety rests on a permissioned PoSA validator set, while zero-knowledge verification is applied at the order layer — every hidden order requires ZK verification whether or not Account Privacy is enabled
nodes.note: RESIDUE — proof system. The 58 have no element for a proof at all, so they cannot record that this venue proves ORDER CONFIDENTIALITY rather than STATE VALIDITY — the inverse of every other venue in the lane. No audit of Aster Chain, the clearinghouse, the matching engine or the ZK privacy stack is published (https://docs.asterdex.com/overview/audit-reports.md, 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F5 data storage is hybrid: key trading and account events are recorded on
nodes.text: data storage is hybrid: key trading and account events are recorded on chain while certain operations remain off chain for privacy protection and system efficiency
nodes.note: RESIDUE — data availability. Which operations are withheld is not enumerated, so the reconstructibility of the venue's state from public data is unknown. Compare Lighter's sufficiency predicate ('enough to reconstruct every account'), which is the same design question answered precisely.

nodes.label: F6 there is no forced-inclusion path, censorship deadline or escape hatch
nodes.text: there is no forced-inclusion path, censorship deadline or escape hatch: withdrawals are batched and paid on 2-of-3 validator confirmation, typically in about 30 seconds, with a fee covering validator operating costs
nodes.note: RESIDUE — exit. Exit is entirely at the discretion of a closed 4-node set; the vocabulary can name neither the mechanism nor its absence.

nodes.label: F7 collateral is bridged in from BNB Chain, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Solana or
nodes.text: collateral is bridged in from BNB Chain, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Solana or SUI and credited once 3 of 4 validator nodes verify the deposit, at zero deposit fee, in 1 to 5 minutes
nodes.note: Xm is ADDED relative to the corpus, which lists Xf alone: the bridge is validator-signed and on-chain-verifiable on explicit 3-of-4 and 2-of-3 thresholds (https://docs.asterdex.com/aster-chain/overview.md, 2026-08-04). What neither symbol carries is that the bridge's signer set is the same committee that matches orders and publishes prices.

nodes.label: F8 initial margin is position size times mark price divided by leverage,
nodes.text: initial margin is position size times mark price divided by leverage, maintenance margin is tiered by position size, collateral is cross by default with per-position isolated margin and a multi-asset mode letting several tokens back one book
nodes.note: Ct computes the test; margin scope (cross / isolated / multi-asset) remains unnameable, as it does across the category.

nodes.label: F9 margin may be posted in yield-bearing instruments — asBNB, USDF, asUSD
nodes.text: margin may be posted in yield-bearing instruments — asBNB, USDF, asUSDF, asBTC and asCAKE — each of which is a claim on another protocol's strategy with its own minter contract, its own peg and its own auditor
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Nothing names 'collateral that is itself a position in another protocol', so the margin engine's exposure to an exogenous strategy is invisible. The corpus's candidate `Dp` describes the USDF issuer's hedge, not Aster's obligation. Audits cover these collateral products (Salus, PeckShield, HALBORN) and NOT the venue (https://docs.asterdex.com/overview/audit-reports.md, 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F10 positions are marked to the median of the index adjusted by funding ov
nodes.text: positions are marked to the median of the index adjusted by funding over the remaining interval, the index plus a 5-minute moving average of the mid-index basis, and the contract price, with exchanges deviating more than 5% from the median down-weighted, feeds staler than 3 seconds dropped, and a contract price more than 5% from mark replaced if not refreshed within 5 seconds
nodes.note: Tp discharges the 5-minute moving-average component; Ex the external legs. The staleness and deviation guards are the freshness validation that L13 demands of Ex, and are stated here as explicit numbers that the symbol cannot carry.

nodes.label: F11 each validator computes a weighted median spot price over 14 named exc
nodes.text: each validator computes a weighted median spot price over 14 named exchanges, and liquidation uses the median oracle price weighted by validator stake
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and a DEPARTURE: the corpus lists Ex as merely derived for Aster while raising endogenous-oracle residue for Hyperliquid, whose construction here is structurally identical. Ex names an EXTERNAL publisher; the publisher is the chain's own closed validator set, which is the opposite trust argument.

nodes.label: F12 the 1001x venue prices from Pyth as anchor, cross-verified against Cha
nodes.text: the 1001x venue prices from Pyth as anchor, cross-verified against Chainlink by the smart contract at trade time, with Binance Oracle as fallback where Pyth lacks a pair, and a circuit breaker on more than 1% divergence
nodes.note: Here Ex fits without qualification — genuinely external publishers, cross-verified on chain. One venue therefore runs an endogenous oracle and an exogenous one side by side, and the same symbol covers both.

nodes.label: F13 longs and shorts exchange funding on a default 8-hour interval at F =
nodes.text: longs and shorts exchange funding on a default 8-hour interval at F = [P + clamp(interest - P, -0.05%, +0.05%)] / (8/N), with interest 0.01% (0% for BNBUSDT) and the premium index recomputed every 5 seconds; on Shield Mode the same transfer is generated hourly from the long/short open-interest imbalance, clamped between a floor and a cap
nodes.note: Pf fits exactly on BOTH venues — the category's 'perp tether' flag is refuted here, including on the pool venue, which balances long/short interest by transfer rather than charging a utilisation borrow fee (https://docs.asterdex.com/trading/shield-mode/funding-fee-rate.md, 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F14 the venue reserves the right to change the funding floor, the cap and
nodes.text: the venue reserves the right to change the funding floor, the cap and the settlement interval under volatile market conditions
nodes.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER and APPROXIMATE. Sv is 'servicing & determination discretion', drawn from credit servicing; used here for a unilateral right to redetermine the parameters of the tether itself. It is the only element in the 58 that names discretion over a contract's cash flows, and it is warranted (Sh present). Recorded rather than dropped because this is the one place in the lane where an operator's discretion IS documented and therefore checkable.

nodes.label: F15 a position is liquidated when initial collateral plus realised plus un
nodes.text: a position is liquidated when initial collateral plus realised plus unrealised PnL falls below maintenance margin, evaluated against the stake-weighted median oracle price, with an IOC close attempted first and an Insurance Clearance Fee taken
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE for Li — the engine attempts the close and charges a fee to the insurance fund; no third-party keeper is paid. Li is retained because a genuine forced close against the book occurs.

nodes.label: F16 any residue that the IOC attempt cannot close is taken over at the ban
nodes.text: any residue that the IOC attempt cannot close is taken over at the bankruptcy price by the insurance fund, which covers the shortfall where it can
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Bs is 'slashable first-loss capital'. This fund IS first-loss and IS dedicated to the waterfall, which is why it is retained here and NOT for ApeX or edgeX, but it is fee-funded protocol reserve rather than a slashable bond, so the staking half is absent. This is the category residue the corpus already names ('insurance funds as a thing distinct from slashable backstops'), instantiated. Corroborated at https://docs.asterdex.com/llms-full.txt (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F17 when the insurance fund cannot cover the shortfall, profitable opposit
nodes.text: when the insurance fund cannot cover the shortfall, profitable opposite-side positions are reduced, ranked by PnL% times effective leverage for winners and PnL% divided by effective leverage for losers, with a four-bar LeveragePnLQuantile indicator exposing a trader's queue position
nodes.note: Ad is ADDED relative to the corpus, whose Aster element set contains no loss-absorption element at all and is therefore rejected by the requirement tables (satisfiesRequirementsAndWarrants: false). Aster documents TWO — the insurance fund (F16) and ADL — and the corpus records neither.

nodes.label: F18 on Shield Mode and 1001x the trader's counterparty is the ALP pool at
nodes.text: on Shield Mode and 1001x the trader's counterparty is the ALP pool at an oracle price, with no order book and no inventory-repricing curve; risk is managed by fees, caps and a liquidation loss rate rather than by a curve
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the reason `Pm` is DROPPED from the corpus element set. Pm is an oracle-priced INVENTORY CURVE; stage 1 establishes there is no curve at all, so the 'proactive market making' half is not approximate but absent. Zero-slippage oracle execution as an execution property has no symbol — the same gap the corpus records for Jupiter.

nodes.label: F19 ALP holders are the market-maker counterparty for pool-venue perp trad
nodes.text: ALP holders are the market-maker counterparty for pool-venue perp trades, and NAV accrues trading PnL on that flow, protocol trading fees, funding fees, liquidation profits and platform fees rather than distributing them
nodes.note: Sh names the pro-rata NAV claim. It does not name that the claim is structurally SHORT aggregate trader profit — the dominant risk of holding it. ALP is mintable on BNB Chain and Arbitrum, so the claim exists on domains other than the venue's own chain.

nodes.label: F20 Shield Mode liquidation triggers on last price against a liquidation p
nodes.text: Shield Mode liquidation triggers on last price against a liquidation price derived from margin, leverage, entry, funding and a liquidation loss rate that varies by pair and leverage band (BTC/ETH 75% at 1-200x, 70% at 201-500x, 65% at 501-1001x), and the 1001x venue charges no opening fee, permits no margin top-up, charges a dynamic PnL-based closing fee and caps net ROI at roughly 300%
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Two unnameable objects: a haircut applied AT liquidation that is distinct from both maintenance margin and the liquidation fee; and a payoff transformation as a venue parameter — a capped, fee-deformed perp is closer to Op than to Pf and no symbol composes 'perp with truncated upside'. Leverage terms at https://docs.asterdex.com/trading/1001x/leverage.md (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F21 with Account Privacy enabled a trader's balances and open positions ar
nodes.text: with Account Privacy enabled a trader's balances and open positions are hidden behind encrypted state, and internal transfers to other users are blocked while it is active
nodes.note: Sb (shielded-balance state) fits the balance half and is exercised here for the first time in the corpus — the vocabulary note records Sb as unused by all 72 corpus decompositions. It does not carry the fact that enabling privacy disables a different function (staking requires privacy off).

nodes.label: F22 a hidden order reveals neither size nor presence to the public book wh
nodes.text: a hidden order reveals neither size nor presence to the public book while sharing the book's liquidity, always carries ZK verification of order data whether or not Account Privacy is on, and produces hidden positions excluded from all public data and portfolio analytics; a fresh one-time stealth address is generated per trade so that activity cannot be correlated
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Sb is a shielded BALANCE, not a shielded resting ORDER, and nothing reaches per-trade stealth addressing. Sharper than the corpus records: privacy is MANDATORY at the order layer and OPTIONAL at the account layer — two privacy scopes with opposite defaults. The chain-level cryptography is documented at https://docs.asterdex.com/aster-chain/overview.md while the product page describes no cryptography at all, a seam recorded here rather than resolved.

nodes.label: F23 a trader may disclose their own trading history, or another trader's i
nodes.text: a trader may disclose their own trading history, or another trader's if supplied with that trader's viewer pass, without lifting privacy generally
nodes.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER and APPROXIMATE. Sd is a selective-disclosure proof about oneself; the viewer pass also releases ANOTHER party's history on presentation of a bearer capability, which is an auditability instrument rather than a proof. Like Sb, first use in the corpus.

nodes.label: F24 ASTER is staked to validators with a lock period and an early-exit pat
nodes.text: ASTER is staked to validators with a lock period and an early-exit path, rewards split into a Base APY pool allocated by each validator's share of processed transactions and Loyalty Rewards weighted by lock length through veASTER, and Account Privacy must be off to stake
nodes.note: Vl is ADDED relative to the corpus (CANDIDATE-REGISTER); Em covers the Base APY pool. Vl names a lifecycle, not the role bundle: this same set is matcher, oracle publisher, bridge signer and listing electorate.

nodes.label: F25 listing is decided by validator vote: any active validator holding at
nodes.text: listing is decided by validator vote: any active validator holding at least 20M staked ASTER may propose, and passage requires a double majority of more than 50% of stake and more than 50% of validators, formalised as AOS-1 for spot listing since 25 June 2026
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A listing franchise attached to consensus participation, decided by a double majority, is neither Vl (a lifecycle) nor Aw (an identity gate). Compare Hyperliquid, which prices the same right by Dutch auction: two venues answer the same design question with mechanisms the vocabulary cannot distinguish because it names neither.

nodes.label: F26 no timelock, guardian, pause authority or upgrade path for the chain o
nodes.text: no timelock, guardian, pause authority or upgrade path for the chain or its contracts is documented
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the reason `Gp` and `Up` are DROPPED from the corpus element set. Stage 1 searched the documentation corpus and found none; asserting a guardian or a mutable proxy on a closed-source chain with no published contracts would be a claim from memory, which the run's invariants forbid.

nodes.label: edgeX
F1 orders are matched in a central limit order book by a purpose-built Go
nodes.text: orders are matched in a central limit order book by a purpose-built Go microservice matching engine that operates independently of on-chain block times
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Ob asserts an ON-CHAIN order book, and the venue says in its own words that the engine runs off chain. The symbol is right about the microstructure and false about the qualifier, exactly as the corpus marker records.

nodes.label: F2 matching runs in an operator-run engine and only state roots are ancho
nodes.text: matching runs in an operator-run engine and only state roots are anchored to Ethereum, with the operator as sole block proposer
nodes.note: RESIDUE — matching locus. Same Ob as Hyperliquid's in-consensus book and Lighter's proven book; three trust models, one symbol. V2 architecture claim corroborated at https://edgex-1.gitbook.io/edgeX-documentation/edgex-v2.md (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F3 the venue has occupied two different loci while keeping the product, t
nodes.text: the venue has occupied two different loci while keeping the product, the account model and the API shape: V1 was 'powered by the StarkEx Layer 2 engine' as a validium, and V2 is a modular rollup that has 'temporarily adopted the Arbitrum technology stack as a transitional framework', with V3 announced as a sovereign AppChain
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE from the corpus, whose entire edgeX record describes the legacy StarkEx generation. A vocabulary blind to the locus cannot detect that a venue's failure mode changed underneath its users. Nothing in the framework has a notion of a venue persisting across an architecture change. EDGE Chain announced as 'an app-specific rollup powered by Arbitrum' at https://blog.arbitrum.io/edgex-announces-edge-chain-on-arbitrum/ (dated 2026-03-10, accessed 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F4 no constraint on the operator's ordering, matching or inclusion discre
nodes.text: no constraint on the operator's ordering, matching or inclusion discretion is published for either generation: there is no fairness rule, no sequencing commitment and no forced-ordering property, and the Cairo program that executed V1's state transitions is marked 'Code unknown'

nodes.label: F5 V1 batched trades through the StarkEx service to the SHARP shared prov
nodes.text: V1 batched trades through the StarkEx service to the SHARP shared prover, whose STARK proofs were verified on Ethereum before the StarkPerpetual contract would accept a state root; for V2 the documentation never states whether there are validity proofs, fault proofs, or neither
nodes.note: RESIDUE — proof system, and stage 1's judgement that this is the single most consequential unstated fact about the venue. The 58 have no element for a proof, so they can record neither the V1 regime nor V2's silence about it. StarkPerpetual 0xfAaE2946e846133af314d1Df13684c89fA7d83DD (https://l2beat.com/scaling/projects/edgex, 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F6 V1 is a validium: proof construction relies fully on data that is not
nodes.text: V1 is a validium: proof construction relies fully on data that is not published on chain, held by a data-availability committee with a threshold of 2 of 6 whose members are not publicly known and who have no on-chain assets at risk of being slashed in a data-withholding attack; V2's data-availability regime is not stated
nodes.note: RESIDUE — data availability. Nothing separates a validium from a rollup, which is the whole liveness and exit risk of the venue; and the quantitative version is what makes it live — the threshold is a number, it is 2 of 6, the members are anonymous and the stake at risk is zero. FinalizableCommittee 0x23bf3dcc14680162b7f5355aAbb56D31823c946e.

nodes.label: F7 on V1 a user may force the sequencer to include a trade or a withdrawa
nodes.text: on V1 a user may force the sequencer to include a trade or a withdrawal by submitting the request through L1, and if it is censored or down for 7 days anyone may freeze the system and withdraw by Merkle proof — but a forced TRADE requires the user to find a counterparty by out-of-system means; V2 asserts trustless permissionless withdrawals at any time even under operator sequence failure while specifying no mechanism, no deadline and no contract
nodes.note: RESIDUE — exit. Two unnameable things: an exit right whose exercise is conditioned on the user's own market access (find a counterparty out of band), and an exit CLAIM with no mechanism behind it. Compare Lighter, where order creation itself is forceable. Deadline and freeze mechanics from https://l2beat.com/scaling/projects/edgex (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F8 USDT is deposited from Ethereum mainnet after roughly 15 confirmations
nodes.text: USDT is deposited from Ethereum mainnet after roughly 15 confirmations (about 5 minutes) and credited to the trader's L2 account

nodes.label: F9 a deposit from a non-Ethereum chain is credited by transferring an equ
nodes.text: a deposit from a non-Ethereum chain is credited by transferring an equivalent amount from the venue's own asset pool on that chain, with rebalancing latency of up to 2 hours for single deposits over $300K
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the reason `Xm` is DROPPED from the corpus element set. This is not cross-domain message verification: it is a market-maker inventory standing in for a bridge, with its own solvency question and its own rebalancing risk. Xf covers the Ethereum path (F8) and nothing covers this one.

nodes.label: F10 a user may onboard by email, in which case an MPC wallet is created fo
