nodes.text: a user may onboard by email, in which case an MPC wallet is created for them and a fresh address is funded over Arbitrum
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Au (delegated execution scope) is the nearest symbol and is the wrong direction: the venue co-holds a share of the user's signing key rather than receiving a bounded authority from the user. A custody arrangement dressed as an account is not expressible.

nodes.label: F11 the account is cross-margined so that collateral is shared among all p
nodes.text: the account is cross-margined so that collateral is shared among all positions within one trading account, isolation is obtained by opening separate sub-accounts, and sub-account volume aggregates into the main account's fee tier
nodes.note: Ct computes the test; margin scope is unnameable here as everywhere in the category. The fee-tier aggregation across nominally isolated sub-accounts — a coupling between risk fences — has no symbol either.

nodes.label: F12 risk is parameterised per contract by a 22-step notional staircase pub
nodes.text: risk is parameterised per contract by a 22-step notional staircase published as API metadata rather than as protocol constants: for BTCUSDT tier 1 covers notional up to $50,000 at 100x with a maintenance-margin rate of 0.5%, rising to a top tier at 6x and 10.5%
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — the explicit initial-margin and maintenance-margin FORMULAS are not published anywhere, so Ct is discharged by a table of parameters with no stated computation over them. A risk parameter that is API data rather than a protocol constant is also a control-plane fact — the operator can restate it without an upgrade — that no element carries.

nodes.label: F13 the Index Price is a weighted average of prices collected from Binance
nodes.text: the Index Price is a weighted average of prices collected from Binance, OKX, Bybit and Coinbase with weights readjusted every four hours, and it drives funding
nodes.note: Ex fits: genuinely external publishers, unlike Hyperliquid's and Aster's validator-produced prices. V2 additionally claims a native Multi-CEX oracle aggregation pipeline (https://edgex-1.gitbook.io/edgeX-documentation/edgex-v2.md, 2026-08-04). Tp is NOT claimed — the weighting is across venues, not across time.

nodes.label: F14 a second and different price, the Oracle Price sourced from the indepe
nodes.text: a second and different price, the Oracle Price sourced from the independent provider Stork, drives margin requirements and liquidation prices
nodes.note: One symbol, two feeds, two jobs, two failure modes: nothing in the vocabulary says WHICH obligation a given price discharges, so a venue that funds off one publisher and liquidates off another decomposes identically to one that uses a single feed for both.

nodes.label: F15 longs and shorts exchange funding hourly at F = P + clamp(I - P, -0.05
nodes.text: longs and shorts exchange funding hourly at F = P + clamp(I - P, -0.05%, +0.05%) with P = [max(0, ImpactBid - Index) - max(0, Index - ImpactAsk)] / Index, longs paying shorts when the rate is positive
nodes.note: Pf fits exactly — a genuine long/short transfer, so the category's 'perp tether' flag is refuted here as it is for the other four.

nodes.label: F16 in cross mode a position is liquidated when the available balance reac
nodes.text: in cross mode a position is liquidated when the available balance reaches zero and the position margin drops to the maintenance-margin level
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — the page states the TRIGGER and nothing else. Whether a third party is paid to close the position, at what price, in what order, and with what fee is undocumented, so the 'incentivized' half of Li is unsupported rather than merely absent. Li is retained only because a forced close demonstrably occurs; it is the sole loss-handling element this venue's documentation supports, and stage 3 should treat that as fragile.

nodes.label: F17 what absorbs a bankrupt position is not documented: the strings 'insur
nodes.text: what absorbs a bankrupt position is not documented: the strings 'insurance fund', 'auto-deleveraging', 'bankruptcy price', 'socialised loss' and any liquidation-fee schedule are absent from the venue's entire 414 KB documentation corpus
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the reason `Bs` is DROPPED from the corpus element set — its justification ('insurance fund is non-slashable protocol capital') describes a fund that is nowhere asserted. `Sl` and `Ad` are likewise NOT claimed, for the same reason. The deeper finding: the vocabulary has a symbol for each candidate answer (Bs, Sl, Ad) and no way to record that NONE is asserted, so the honest decomposition of a venue running at scale with an unstated loss-absorption layer is indistinguishable from an incomplete one.

nodes.label: F18 critical contracts can be upgraded by an externally owned account, wit
nodes.text: critical contracts can be upgraded by an externally owned account, with no delay and no window for users to exit an unwanted upgrade, while the bridge contract itself is immutable and its committee security 'cannot be improved'
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and the strongest control-plane fact in the category. Up names a mutable implementation proxy and carries no delay parameter and no authority type, so it cannot say 'a single key, instantly, with no exit window' — which is L2BEAT's headline risk. `Tg` and `Gp` are deliberately NOT claimed (the corpus asserts Gp): the upgrading Safe 0x57814cC6e075f517781cB7c3B42897B3Bb2C54d8 'can upgrade with no delay', only the SHARP multisig 0x21F9eC47b19d95b5C2DDFB6Ae5D4F92fAdacAEc4 carries an 8-day delay, and no product-side guardian, pause or governance vote is documented. If the tables require a delayed or bounded emergency process alongside Up, this construction fails that requirement, and the failure is the finding. `Sh` and `Em` are DROPPED for the same evidentiary reason: no pro-rata pool, vault or LP claim is documented anywhere in the venue's corpus, and no emissions schedule is documented at a primary source — the EDGE token TGE and the Amber Group incubation appear only in third-party coverage and are recorded as UNKNOWN (https://edgex-1.gitbook.io/edgeX-documentation/llms-full.txt, 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: Hyperliquid
F1 a trader's limit and market orders are matched against a resting book
nodes.text: a trader's limit and market orders are matched against a resting book in price-time priority, with tick and lot quantisation and a margin check run both when the order is placed and again for the resting side at each match
nodes.note: Ob names the book and its priority rule; it says nothing about where the book is kept or who executes it, which is F2.

nodes.label: F2 the book, the margin state, the matching and the liquidations are the
nodes.text: the book, the margin state, the matching and the liquidations are the chain's own state machine — HyperCore is executed by the validator set under HyperBFT consensus, not by an off-chain operator
nodes.note: RESIDUE — matching locus. Ob is equally true of a book deployed as a contract on someone else's chain, of an operator-run engine with validity proofs, and of this. The single most important architectural fact about the category's largest venue is unnameable.

nodes.label: F3 within a block, actions are sorted into three classes — actions contai
nodes.text: within a block, actions are sorted into three classes — actions containing no GTC or IOC order, then cancels, then actions carrying at least one GTC or IOC — with proposed order preserved inside each class
nodes.note: RESIDUE — operator discretion. This is a fairness rule enforced at the ordering layer rather than the execution layer, i.e. a bound on the block proposer's discretion. No element in the 58 constrains who orders transactions or how; there is not even an execution-layer analogue of this rule to force it onto.

nodes.label: F4 the correctness of every fill, funding payment and liquidation rests o
nodes.text: the correctness of every fill, funding payment and liquidation rests on two-thirds of staking power being honest; there is no validity proof, no fraud proof, and the node that computes the state is distributed as a signed pre-compiled binary with no published source
nodes.note: RESIDUE — proof system. The vocabulary has no element for a validity proof (`Zk` is contested-register and outside the 58) and therefore also no way to record its absence. Cross-check: the only source-bearing artefact in the org is Bridge2.sol at https://github.com/hyperliquid-dex/contracts (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F5 the full order-book and account state is replicated to every validator
nodes.text: the full order-book and account state is replicated to every validator and served from public nodes and the public API; nothing is posted to, or reconstructible from, any other chain
nodes.note: RESIDUE — data availability. The DA regime here (replicated L1 state, no settlement layer beneath it) is a different object from blobs on Ethereum, a validium committee, or a DA menu, and the vocabulary cannot distinguish any of them.

nodes.label: F6 USDC enters and leaves HyperCore across a bridge contract on Arbitrum,
nodes.text: USDC enters and leaves HyperCore across a bridge contract on Arbitrum, with the L1 balance debited immediately on withdrawal and 1 USDC charged in place of Arbitrum gas

nodes.label: F7 a deposit is credited, and a withdrawal is paid, only against signatur
nodes.text: a deposit is credited, and a withdrawal is paid, only against signatures from validators holding more than two-thirds of staking power, with the validator set and its stake mirrored on the bridge contract

nodes.label: F8 a trader has no unilateral exit: there is no forced-inclusion transact
nodes.text: a trader has no unilateral exit: there is no forced-inclusion transaction, no censorship deadline and no escape hatch, so leaving the venue requires the validator set to sign
nodes.note: RESIDUE — exit. Compare Lighter's 14-day forced-transaction deadline and StarkEx's 7-day forced withdrawal: this venue's answer is 'none', and the vocabulary can record neither the mechanism nor its absence.

nodes.label: F9 during the post-withdrawal dispute period the bridge can be locked if
nodes.text: during the post-withdrawal dispute period the bridge can be locked if a withdrawal does not match L1 state, and unlocking requires cold-wallet signatures from two-thirds of the stake-weighted set
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Gp names an emergency guardian or pause; here the pause authority is the validator set itself acting through cold keys, not a named guardian, and its scope is the bridge rather than the venue.

nodes.label: F10 every validator publishes a spot price roughly every 3 seconds as a we
nodes.text: every validator publishes a spot price roughly every 3 seconds as a weighted median of eight named venues, and the clearinghouse takes the stake-weighted median of those submissions as the oracle price
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Ex names an EXTERNAL data oracle. Here the chain's own validator set is the publisher, so the trust argument is the opposite of Chainlink's: there is no external party to trust and no external party to blame. The venue-weight rule (assets whose primary liquidity is on Hyperliquid exclude external sources, and vice versa) is a further parameter with no expression.

nodes.label: F11 positions are marked to the median of three constructions — the oracle
nodes.text: positions are marked to the median of three constructions — the oracle price plus a 150-second EMA of (Hyperliquid mid minus oracle), the median of best bid, best ask and last trade, and a weighted median of five external perp mids — with a 30-second EMA substituted when only two components exist
nodes.note: Tp genuinely discharges the EMA components (an on-chain time-weighted price built from the venue's own mid). Ex covers the external legs. Neither names the median-of-medians composition itself.

nodes.label: F12 longs and shorts exchange funding hourly at one-eighth of an 8-hour ra
nodes.text: longs and shorts exchange funding hourly at one-eighth of an 8-hour rate F = P + clamp(interest_rate - P, -0.0005, +0.0005), capped at 4%/hour, with the payment notional computed at the spot oracle price rather than the mark price
nodes.note: Pf fits exactly: this is a long/short transfer tethering the perp to an index. Pf names the transfer but not which of the venue's several prices sets its notional, which here is a deliberate and unusual choice.

nodes.label: F13 a position must carry initial margin of position_size * mark_price / l
nodes.text: a position must carry initial margin of position_size * mark_price / leverage, and maintenance margin equal to notional * rate minus a maintenance deduction that keeps the requirement continuous across notional tiers; moving margin out must leave max(initial_margin_required, 0.1 * total_position_value)
nodes.note: Margining formulas cross-checked at https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/margining.md (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F14 collateral is pooled across every perp and spot market by default, and
nodes.text: collateral is pooled across every perp and spot market by default, and a trader may instead ring-fence a single position in isolated margin, or partition capital into sub-accounts and vaults
nodes.note: RESIDUE — margin scope. Ct computes the threshold test; nothing says which positions share a collateral pool. The contested `Ua` gestures at this and is outside the 58.

nodes.label: F15 when account equity falls below maintenance margin the engine sends ma
nodes.text: when account equity falls below maintenance margin the engine sends market orders to close enough of the position to restore the requirement, and any surplus collateral stays with the trader
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Li names INCENTIVIZED liquidation by third parties. Here the matching engine itself issues the closing orders; no keeper is paid a bounty and no liquidation auction exists. Only the 'position is force-closed against the book' half of the symbol applies.

nodes.label: F16 if equity falls below two-thirds of maintenance margin without the boo
nodes.text: if equity falls below two-thirds of maintenance margin without the book absorbing the position, the trader's entire cross position set and cross margin are transferred to the liquidator vault, and the resulting PnL stream accrues to HLP's depositors
nodes.note: Sl discharges the loss allocation: the liquidator vault is a component strategy of HLP, so gains and losses from backstop liquidation land on a named claim class. Li is again approximate for the same reason as F15. This is the obligation that replaces the corpus's Bs — see the construction note in F19.

nodes.label: F17 if account value goes negative anyway, traders on the opposite side ar
nodes.text: if account value goes negative anyway, traders on the opposite side are ranked by (mark_price / entry_price) * (notional_position / account_value) and closed against the distressed account at the previous mark price, and a user with no open positions never socialises platform losses
nodes.note: Ad fits exactly, including the rank ordering. The stated invariant (flat users are never touched) is a property of the mechanism that the symbol does not carry.

nodes.label: F18 a depositor into HLP holds a pro-rata claim on the vault's value, subj
nodes.text: a depositor into HLP holds a pro-rata claim on the vault's value, subject to a 4-day post-deposit lock-up, with no management fee and no profit share
nodes.note: Sh names the pro-rata claim. The 4-day lock-up is not Wq — it is a fixed dwell time on a share, not a queue on redemptions — and has no symbol.

nodes.label: F19 one pool, HLP, simultaneously makes markets through multiple strategie
nodes.text: one pool, HLP, simultaneously makes markets through multiple strategies, performs backstop liquidations, supplies USDC in Earn and accrues a share of trading fees, and it is community-owned rather than protocol-owned
nodes.note: RESIDUE — role multiplicity, and the reason `Bs` is DROPPED from the corpus element set. Bs is slashable first-loss capital posted as a bond; HLP is profit-seeking depositor capital that happens to sit in front of the waterfall, is not bonded and is not slashable. Stage 1 also corrects the corpus's count: five roles, not three. Nothing composes 'the loss absorber is also the price maker'.

nodes.label: F20 HYPE is delegated to validators under a 1-day delegation lockup with a
nodes.text: HYPE is delegated to validators under a 1-day delegation lockup with a 10k HYPE self-delegation floor locked for a year, commission may not be raised except to at most 1%, poor performers are jailed by peer vote and self-cure, and there is currently no automatic slashing for consensus faults
nodes.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER. Vl names the lifecycle but elides two different punishment regimes: consensus misbehaviour is socially punished (jailing, no automatic slashing) while HIP-3 deployer misbehaviour is mechanically slashed (F22). It also cannot say that this same set is the oracle publisher (F10) and the bridge's verifier set (F7).

nodes.label: F21 the validator set rotates on epochs of 100k consensus rounds (about 90
nodes.text: the validator set rotates on epochs of 100k consensus rounds (about 90 minutes), and unstaking from staking to spot passes through a 7-day queue that admits at most 5 pending withdrawals
nodes.note: Both fit: Ep for the epoch-gated set rotation, Wq for a genuine rate-limited redemption queue. Ep is ADDED relative to the corpus decomposition, which lists Wq but not Ep.

nodes.label: F22 the right to list a spot ticker is sold by a 31-hour Dutch auction dec
nodes.text: the right to list a spot ticker is sold by a 31-hour Dutch auction decaying to 500 HYPE, and the right to deploy a perp DEX requires 500k HYPE staked and maintained for at least 183 days, slashable by stake-weighted validator vote up to 100% for invalid state transitions and up to 50% or 20% for downtime and degradation
nodes.note: RESIDUE, twice over. (i) Permissionless listing priced by descending auction has no symbol, and the auction hyperparameters are SHARED across all deployed perp DEXs, coupling nominally independent venues. HIP-1 detail at https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hyperliquid-improvement-proposals-hips/hip-1-native-token-standard.md (2026-08-04). (ii) This is genuinely slashable bonded capital — the thing Bs names — but it secures listing quality, oracle honesty and uptime, NOT the loss waterfall, so Bs still cannot sit here. 'Slashable capital exists and does not back solvency' is a finding the vocabulary cannot state.

nodes.label: F23 a third-party front end can attach its own fee to order flow it origin
nodes.text: a third-party front end can attach its own fee to order flow it originates, up to 0.1% on perps and 1% on spot, charged inside the exchange's fee logic, requiring an ApproveBuilderFee action from the user's main wallet, at most 10 active approvals and at least 100 USDC in the builder's perps account
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Au (delegated execution scope) is the nearest symbol and does not fit: what the user approves is a fee ceiling for a named counterparty, not authority to act. Builder fills are published at https://stats-data.hyperliquid.xyz/Mainnet/builder_fills/{builder_address}/{YYYYMMDD}.csv.lz4 (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F24 a vault leader trades depositors' capital for a 10% profit share, must
nodes.text: a vault leader trades depositors' capital for a 10% profit share, must hold at least 5% of the vault at all times and cannot withdraw below it, pays a 10k USDC creation fee and imposes a 1-day depositor lockup
nodes.note: Sh names the depositor claim only. The mandatory non-withdrawable leader stake is a solvency-style constraint applied to a MANAGER rather than a borrower, and has no symbol; nor does the restriction that vaults may trade validator-operated perps only.

nodes.label: F25 orders must be placed within 1% of the oracle price, with HLP exempt s
nodes.text: orders must be placed within 1% of the oracle price, with HLP exempt so it can keep quoting, and open-interest caps scaled to liquidity block new positions when hit
nodes.note: RESIDUE. These are risk controls that act on the ORDER, not on the account; Ct is an account test. A per-participant exemption from a risk control has no expression at all.

nodes.label: Lighter
F1 orders submitted through API servers are ordered by a sequencer and ma
nodes.text: orders submitted through API servers are ordered by a sequencer and matched under price-time priority, with a health check applied to both sides of every trade
nodes.note: Ob names the book and its priority rule. Unlike ApeX and edgeX, the book here is genuine committed state — the Order Book Tree is Merkleised into the root the L1 verifier accepts — so 'on-chain' is defensible in a way it is not for the operator-run venues; the symbol cannot make that distinction.

nodes.label: F2 price-time priority is enforced by the address space rather than by a
nodes.text: price-time priority is enforced by the address space rather than by a rule: an ask at price p with nonce o occupies leaf index p*2^O + o and a bid occupies p*2^O + (2^O - 1 - o), so index order IS priority order, and every insertion proves non-crossing and every trade proves the supplied maker was the highest-priority crossing order by requiring crossingSize = 0 along the root-to-leaf path
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the single most valuable one in this lane: the vocabulary cannot express 'the matching RULE was proven'. `Zk` is contested-register, outside the 58, and names a verifiable STATE proof — which is what ApeX and edgeX also claim. Stage 1 supplies the exact statement the corpus could only gesture at, so a later stage can attempt to formalise it: crossing size zero on the highest-priority leaf, computed from internal-node subtree aggregates (AskSizeSum / BidSizeSum) under a Poseidon2 hash of (left, right, InternalData).

nodes.label: F3 the book is maintained by an off-chain sequencer whose only power is o
nodes.text: the book is maintained by an off-chain sequencer whose only power is ordering — since execution and matching are verified by the prover, every valid state transition is deterministically inferable from the transaction order and the oracle data
nodes.note: RESIDUE — matching locus AND operator discretion, which for this venue are one statement. The whitepaper names the alternative it rejects: designs 'where matching occurs directly at the Sequencer layer and proofs merely confirm that two orders intersect', in which 'the Sequencer could arbitrarily reorder or favor trades'. That is exactly ApeX's and edgeX's model, and all three emit the same Ob.

nodes.label: F4 batches are proven by Plonky2 circuits — TurboPlonk arithmetisation ov
nodes.text: batches are proven by Plonky2 circuits — TurboPlonk arithmetisation over Goldilocks with FRI — aggregated block to segment to batch, wrapped into a gnark PLONK proof over BN254 for on-chain verification against the Aztec Ignition setup, and the deployed ZkLighterVerifier can be regenerated from the published circuits
nodes.note: RESIDUE — proof system. No element names a validity proof, so nothing records that this is the one venue in the lane with source-to-deployment correspondence: L2BEAT's own upgrade note reads 'new lighter verifier and desert verifier deployed, succesfully regenerated from the sources', and running build_circuits.sh reproduces the verifier (https://github.com/elliottech/lighter-prover, 2026-08-04). Deployed: ZkLighterVerifier 0xac3Ce44B6ff4E402858C99D5699ff63131572BaA, DesertVerifier 0x866418061d4C1168e1c8E8f6facE79675395E008, ZKLighter 0x3B4D794a66304F130a4Db8F2551B0070dfCf5ca7.

nodes.label: F5 data availability is defined by a sufficiency predicate rather than by
nodes.text: data availability is defined by a sufficiency predicate rather than by a venue: an Account Delta Tree initialised empty each batch receives every update also applied to the Public Account Tree, is serialised, compressed and posted to Ethereum in a blob-carrying transaction with the market data, so replaying the blobs in order reconstructs the account state exactly — and two circuits bind the claim, a Blob Polynomial Equivalence Circuit evaluated at the point Ethereum's precompile uses and Account Delta Traversal Circuits at the same Fiat-Shamir point
nodes.note: RESIDUE — data availability. The design object is not a DA venue (Ethereum versus a committee) but a PREDICATE: post the minimum sufficient for the escape hatch, and prove that it is sufficient. L2BEAT classifies the result as a ZK Rollup with Ethereum blobs at Stage 0 (https://l2beat.com/scaling/projects/lighter, 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F6 a censored trader can force inclusion by queueing a priority transacti
nodes.text: a censored trader can force inclusion by queueing a priority transaction directly through the Ethereum contracts — deposits, withdrawals, order creation, order cancellation and burning of pool shares are all forceable — and if the sequencer misses the 14-day deadline, anyone may trigger desert mode, after which commitments stop, the state freezes, and users withdraw against the frozen root using blob data alone, with open positions settled at the latest mark price
nodes.note: RESIDUE — exit, and the reason `Wq` is DROPPED from the corpus element set. Wq names a redemption-rate limiter; this is a censorship-resistance device with an enforced deadline whose expiry FREEZES the chain, which is a different object. Sharper than the corpus's generic 'escape hatch' gap: because order creation and cancellation are forceable, a censored trader can not merely exit but TRADE. Whitepaper sections 2.2.2 and 6 at https://assets.lighter.xyz/whitepaper.pdf (2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F7 USDC is deposited into the Lighter rollup contract on Ethereum and cre
nodes.text: USDC is deposited into the Lighter rollup contract on Ethereum and credited to a Main Account, from which Sub-Accounts and Public Pools derive

nodes.label: F8 the L1 contracts accept a state root only against a verified proof, an
nodes.text: the L1 contracts accept a state root only against a verified proof, and bind L1-submitted priority transactions into L2 state through a queue the sequencer must consume
nodes.note: Xm names the domain-crossing verification. It cannot say that the verification is a validity proof rather than a signature quorum — the same message-passing symbol serves Hyperliquid's 2/3 validator signatures and this.

nodes.label: F9 an account walks a three-rung ladder C_i < M_i < I_i: below initial ma
nodes.text: an account walks a three-rung ladder C_i < M_i < I_i: below initial margin it is in pre-liquidation, below maintenance margin it is partially liquidated against the book, and below close-out it is fully liquidated
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Ct names ONE line. The third rung is what distinguishes partial from full liquidation, so collapsing the ladder loses the mechanism rather than a detail.

nodes.label: F10 beyond the base asset, ETH (and SPY and USO on the Robinhood deploymen
nodes.text: beyond the base asset, ETH (and SPY and USO on the Robinhood deployment) may be posted as margin under a three-parameter haircut — LTV 50% for margin contribution, LT 75% for the liquidation threshold, LF 95% as the minimum value received per unit at liquidation — with total account value computed as PortfolioBalance + sum over assets of LTV_j * MarginBalance_j * IndexPrice_j, and base collateral always valued at 100%
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Ct collapses three independent parameters into one threshold. LF in particular is a floor on VALUE REALISED at liquidation, which is not a threshold test at all. Missing from the corpus record entirely.

nodes.label: F11 positions are marked to the median of an impact price (the average exe
nodes.text: positions are marked to the median of an impact price (the average execution price of a $500 market buy and a $500 market sell), an index-plus-liquidity-premium smoothed by an 8-minute EMA and capped at plus or minus 0.5% of index, and the median mark across major CEXs
nodes.note: Tp discharges the 8-minute EMA, computed in-protocol and proven; Ex the index and CEX legs. The impact-price component — a price defined by executing a notional trade against one's own book — is neither, and has no symbol.

nodes.label: F12 the index price is taken from a combination of Chainlink, Stork and Py
nodes.text: the index price is taken from a combination of Chainlink, Stork and Pyth, but the external signatures are not verified, so the sequencer must be trusted to report the price truthfully
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and the most important safety property of the design. Ex imports PUBLISHER trust; here it imports SEQUENCER trust, because the publisher's signature is never checked. The engine is proven and the input is not — a seam with no expression at all, and invisible in the corpus decomposition, which lists Ex as merely derived.

nodes.label: F13 longs and shorts exchange funding hourly: a per-minute premium [max(0,
nodes.text: longs and shorts exchange funding hourly: a per-minute premium [max(0, ImpactBid - index) - max(0, index - ImpactAsk)] / index is sampled 60 times and time-weighted, then clamped at 0.05% around the 0.01% interest rate and again at 4% before dividing by 8, and the payment -1 * position * index * fundingRate is applied immediately to realised PnL through a Funding Prefix Sum accumulated in each block's pre-execution phase
nodes.note: Pf fits exactly. Tp is claimed for the 60-sample time-weighted premium, which is computed and proven in-protocol. What Pf cannot carry is that funding is applied as a prefix sum in a pre-execution phase, so it is charged before any transaction in the block executes.

nodes.label: F14 below maintenance margin the account is partially liquidated against t
nodes.text: below maintenance margin the account is partially liquidated against the order book, with a liquidation fee of up to 1% routed to the LLP when the fill beats the zero price, and below close-out it is fully liquidated — all of it executed by the protocol under circuit constraints rather than sold to keepers
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Li presumes an incentivized external liquidator, which is not the mechanism: liquidations are executed and PROVEN, so the fee is a charge to the liquidated account paid to a claim class rather than a bounty to a racer. 'Verifiable liquidation' is residue.

nodes.label: F15 the LLP — an insurance fund implemented as a specialised Public Pool t
nodes.text: the LLP — an insurance fund implemented as a specialised Public Pool that also makes markets — absorbs positions the book cannot take, and when absorbing one would push the LLP below its own initial-margin requirement the position is auto-deleveraged instead of assumed
nodes.note: Sl discharges the loss allocation: the absorbed loss lands on a named claim class (LLP depositors), not on protocol reserve. `Bs` is deliberately NOT used — the LLP is neither bonded nor slashable — and Sl plus Sh names it better than Bs would, which is why Bs is absent from this construction while Aster's fee-funded reserve still needs it. The solvency-conditioned handover from absorption to ADL is itself unnameable.

nodes.label: F16 auto-deleveraging matches bankrupt positions against opposite-side acc
nodes.text: auto-deleveraging matches bankrupt positions against opposite-side accounts whose zero prices align, ranked by leverage and unrealised PnL

nodes.label: F17 a Public Pool is a sub-account others buy into pro rata; it can trade
nodes.text: a Public Pool is a sub-account others buy into pro rata; it can trade but cannot transfer or withdraw its holdings, its operator is protocol-whitelisted, sets an operator fee and must satisfy a Minimum Operator Share (for example 10%, so 10,000 USDC of operator capital admits at most 90,000 of depositors), and there are no lockups
nodes.note: Sh names the claim, Aw the operator whitelist. Neither names the Minimum Operator Share — a mandatory skin-in-the-game ratio that bounds depositor capital by manager capital — nor the restriction that a pool may trade but never move its assets.

nodes.label: F18 access to the LLP is gated by staked LIT at a ratio of 10 USDC of depo
nodes.text: access to the LLP is gated by staked LIT at a ratio of 10 USDC of deposit per 1 LIT staked
nodes.note: Aw names the gate. It does not name that the gate is PRICED, and priced in a second token — the right to hold the backstop claim is bought with a different asset than the claim itself.

nodes.label: F19 standard accounts pay zero maker and taker fees at 300 ms taker and 20
nodes.text: standard accounts pay zero maker and taker fees at 300 ms taker and 200 ms maker latency, Premium accounts pay 0.4 to 2.8 bps scaling down with staked LIT in exchange for lower latency, and Plus accounts pay a flat 0.5 bps
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The fee schedule is a latency auction: the priced good is speed, not execution. Em, Fd and every fee-adjacent symbol miss it, and so does the corpus's 'zero-fee model' residue, which records the zero and not what is being sold.

nodes.label: F20 LIT carries a fixed 6% staking APR with a 3-day unstaking lockup, and
nodes.text: LIT carries a fixed 6% staking APR with a 3-day unstaking lockup, and the protocol buys LIT back daily on a 24-hour TWAP funded from trading-fee revenue
nodes.note: Em for the fixed APR (protocol-funded), Fd (CANDIDATE-REGISTER) for the fee-funded buyback. The 3-day lockup is not Wq — a dwell time is not a queue — which is the second reason Wq is dropped from this construction.

nodes.label: F21 a size-seeking trader can signal an RFQ through the order book, to whi
nodes.text: a size-seeking trader can signal an RFQ through the order book, to which market makers respond within 10 seconds, with a 2-minute execution window
nodes.note: Rf fits, and is ADDED relative to the corpus. What it does not carry is that the RFQ is signalled THROUGH the book rather than beside it, so the same venue runs two execution symbols over one liquidity pool.

nodes.label: F22 regular upgrades are initiated by a network governor and execute after
nodes.text: regular upgrades are initiated by a network governor and execute after a 21-day delay, and the governor also retains the ability to add or remove validators
nodes.note: Tg is ADDED relative to the corpus, which lists Up without it. This is the only venue in the lane where the control plane is documented precisely enough for the vocabulary to work as intended. Multisigs 0x92b12c9d85BF7bd2EF5d2F53F4cd4Ce0BE432045 and 0x97A90Ec950B6BCd9B190b566525B2Bb92A2C03a2; UpgradeGatekeeper 0x94da8A995D0D82Ef0fE7E509C6D76c22603B6f67.

nodes.label: F23 a security council may reduce the upgrade delay to zero in an emergenc
nodes.text: a security council may reduce the upgrade delay to zero in an emergency, and it does not currently satisfy the Stage 1 requirements
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE — Gp names an emergency guardian or PAUSE. The emergency power here is the opposite of a pause: it ACCELERATES a state change by deleting the delay users rely on. A symbol for 'the guardian can cancel the timelock' does not exist, and the composition Tg + Gp reads as strictly safer than it is.

nodes.label: F24 a second sovereign deployment of the same stack, Lighter on Robinhood,
nodes.text: a second sovereign deployment of the same stack, Lighter on Robinhood, runs with USDG as base collateral and SPY and USO as margin assets, under its own verifier contract
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Nothing in the vocabulary distinguishes an INSTANCE of a venue from the venue, so two deployments with different collateral, different users and different verifiers decompose identically. Missing from the corpus record.

nodes.label: 06-yield-vaults
CIAN Yield Layer
F1 a depositor brings the vault's accounting asset, or one of four relate
nodes.text: a depositor brings the vault's accounting asset, or one of four related staking tokens through a converter path, and receives a transferable pro-rata share of the vault
nodes.note: Live symbol() = ylstETH, name() = CIAN yield layer stETH, asset() = WETH. The audit records that the vault is NOT ERC-4626 compliant because withdraw and redeem revert (see F15).

nodes.label: F2 every share's redemption value moves by a single stored global index
nodes.text: every share's redemption value moves by a single stored global index
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call exchangePrice = 1.0735855763962243, totalAssets = exchangePrice * totalSupply / PRECISION on 0xB13aa2d0345b0439b064f26B82D8dCf3f508775d, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: Ix names the FORM only. See F3 for what writes it.

nodes.label: F3 that index is written by an off-chain operator at its own discretion,
nodes.text: that index is written by an off-chain operator at its own discretion, with no oracle input, no attester, no staleness recourse beyond a revert, and no derivation from realised profit and loss
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the single largest unmitigated risk in the protocol. The audit's warning W4 reads 'Protocol owner can set arbitrary exchange price to pools' and W6 'Protocol owner can artificially mint Vault shares'. Not Ex (no external data source), not At (L27 requires a named attester, independence, a stated assurance level, a staleness bound and recourse), not Ix (an index a party may set to any value is not an accrual). An ASSERTED NAV with no attester has no symbol. The corpus's Ex points at the wrong object for this reason.

nodes.label: F4 the vault refuses to report its own assets — and therefore refuses dep
nodes.text: the vault refuses to report its own assets — and therefore refuses deposits and redemptions — if the index has not been written within three days
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call maxPriceUpdatePeriod = 3 days, lastUpdatePriceTime = 1785722699 on 0xB13aa2d0345b0439b064f26B82D8dCf3f508775d, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. This is stronger than 'an off-chain agent should call rebalance': it is the contract DECLARING that it cannot function without one, and it is the FIRST failure — earlier than any liquidation. No symbol records that a mechanism requires an external caller to stay alive.

nodes.label: F5 total deposits into the vault are capped at a fixed quantity of the ac
nodes.text: total deposits into the vault are capped at a fixed quantity of the accounting asset
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A supply cap as a risk-fencing primitive has no symbol; the corpus records the same gap at Steakhouse.

nodes.label: F6 the vault's assets are deployed as a recursive leveraged loop in an ex
nodes.text: the vault's assets are deployed as a recursive leveraged loop in an external lending market: supply a staking token, enter its correlated-asset mode, borrow the accounting asset against it, re-stake, repeat
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Pl, Im and Cd all belong to the external lending market, not to CIAN, and emitting them would claim CIAN implements pooled lending. The vocabulary has no way to mark an element as CONSUMED from a dependency rather than implemented, which is the same defect the corpus hit with Spark/Ps and Steakhouse/Im. Also unnamed: composition depth — one live strategy deposits into a vault curated by a third party, so the depositor sees one share price over three stacked mandates each charging its own fee.

nodes.label: F7 each leverage or deleverage step borrows and repays within a single se
nodes.text: each leverage or deleverage step borrows and repays within a single settlement scope, from one of three flash-loan providers selected by the caller, with reentrancy blocked while a loan is open
nodes.note: CORRECTION to the corpus: the enumerated sources are AAVEV3, BALANCER and MAKER. The corpus's mention of Morpho as a source is not supported.

nodes.label: F8 any transaction that ends with the position's collateral ratio above a
nodes.text: any transaction that ends with the position's collateral ratio above a stored ceiling reverts
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, corpus marker retained and sharpened. The liquidation test that matters belongs to the external lending market; CIAN's own check is a one-sided post-condition strictly inside it. It can revert a transaction that ends too levered; it cannot compel one, cannot reject an under-levered or simply bad allocation, and cannot fire at all if the operator stays silent. The vocabulary has one symbol for 'a solvency test exists' and cannot distinguish being subject to one from operating deliberately against one.

nodes.label: F9 the ceiling the vault enforces is a self-imposed inner bound below an
nodes.text: the ceiling the vault enforces is a self-imposed inner bound below an immutable maximum, and the position is deliberately kept pressed against it
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Ct names the constraint; nothing names recursive leverage as an OBJECTIVE. Modelling hazard the corpus does not record: the documented implementation publishes MAX_PROTOCOL_RATIO = 0.85e18 while the live implementation 0x9191dc9e81bef6feea0dc4d6994d5392b898edf8 carries 0.93e18 — the real ceiling is eight points looser than the published one.

nodes.label: F10 the leverage and deleverage entry points are callable only by one stor
nodes.text: the leverage and deleverage entry points are callable only by one stored address, which resolves to a contract that forwards arbitrary batched calls from a set of cloud-hosted signing keys
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 1 (named agent), partial fit. DEPARTURE: the corpus carries no access element for CIAN. Aw names the caller enumeration (onlyRebalancer, then onlyOperator over a Manager whose docstring reads 'used to manage KMS addresses for batch operations'); it does not name that what is enumerated is an authority over other people's principal. The complete authority path is cloud key -> Manager.multiCall -> Strategy.leverage/deleverage and Vault.updateExchangePrice/stakeTo/transferToStrategy.

nodes.label: F11 that agent supplies the leverage amount, the swap route, the slippage
nodes.text: that agent supplies the leverage amount, the swap route, the slippage floor and the flash-loan source as call arguments; nothing in the contracts computes them, schedules a rebalance, defines when a target has been missed, or compels the agent to act at all
nodes.note: RESIDUE — the central finding of this lane. A public helper getLeverageAmount() computes exactly the amount needed to reach the target, but it is a helper, not a constraint: nothing forces the agent to call it or to use its output. Au fails L17 (no expiry, no nonce, and it operates over pooled third-party principal rather than the principal's own assets); Tg fails because the agent acts immediately; Sv fails because the agent determines nothing about a claim, he chooses where principal sits; Gp names only the kill switch. The vocabulary has no symbol because the object is not on the chain: the contract encodes an ENVELOPE and a human supplies the POINT inside it. Of the five-slot mandate shape, CIAN fills slots 1, 2, 3 and 5 and leaves slot 4 EMPTY — there is no cooldown, no step limit and no delay on anything the agent or the owner does. CIAN's own audit reply states the thesis outright: 'The adjustment of the allocation scheme cannot and should not be automated by the smart contract.'

nodes.label: F12 capital may be forwarded only to strategy contracts the owner has regi
nodes.text: capital may be forwarded only to strategy contracts the owner has registered with the vault
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 2 (domain whitelist). RESIDUE. The named strategy set for this vault is enumerated in the documentation (converter, leveraged-LST, a curated third-party vault, and three lending-market variants).

nodes.label: F13 no single strategy may hold more than a set fraction of the vault's to
nodes.text: no single strategy may hold more than a set fraction of the vault's total assets, checked at the moment of transfer
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 3 (magnitude cap). RESIDUE. The check is `if ((nowAssets_ + _amount) > (totalAssets() * positionLimit_ / 1e4)) revert InvalidLimit()` — the vault's ONLY structural constraint on a strategy.

nodes.label: F14 the owner may replace the agent at any time, and either the owner or t
nodes.text: the owner may replace the agent at any time, and either the owner or the agent itself may pause the vault, while only the owner may unpause it
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call paused() = false; owner() = 0x261090afe1e7305474f4e3eefcaca9964ebffff5, a 3-of-4 Safe, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: MANDATE SLOT 5 (revocation and halt). Gp names the pause but not the mandate it suspends, and it cannot express that the agent can halt itself — unusual, and worth carrying into stage 4 as the inverse of Sky's deliberate grantor/revoker split.

nodes.label: F15 the standard withdrawal path is disabled outright: a depositor files a
nodes.text: the standard withdrawal path is disabled outright: a depositor files a redemption request naming a payout token and waits for a designated operator to settle it in a batch, documented at about five days
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. withdraw() and redeem() both revert with NotSupportedYet. Wq names an ordering of exits; here there is a pending set, a batch and an operator, and CIAN describes it as 'batched execution with manual review'.

nodes.label: F16 the amount a request settles for is decided by the entity that confirm
nodes.text: the amount a request settles for is decided by the entity that confirms it
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Auditor testimony, verbatim: 'The users have to trust protocol owners to act honestly since, once they deposit funds into the Vault, they cannot withdraw without external confirmation. The withdrawn amount is also decided by the entity that confirms the withdrawal requests.' Wq names an ordering; it does not name a queue whose SETTLEMENT AMOUNT is discretionary.

nodes.label: F17 eight per cent of gains is taken by the operator as a performance fee,
nodes.text: eight per cent of gains is taken by the operator as a performance fee, under a hard ceiling of fifteen per cent, with the documented exit and management fees currently set to zero
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call revenueRate = 800, exitFeeRate = 0, managementFeeRate = 0, MAX_REVENUE_FEE_RATE = 1500, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Fd (candidate) was considered and rejected: Fd names distribution of realised surplus to a claimant class, and this is remuneration of the discretionary agent — slot 6 of the mandate shape, which the corpus already recorded as unnamed at Yearn ('no element for a performance fee taken by a manager out of a claim class'). Modelling hazard: a construction built from the docs (8% plus a 0.02% exit fee) reproduces a protocol whose live exit fee is zero.

nodes.label: F18 prices consumed by the position come from the external lending market'
nodes.text: prices consumed by the position come from the external lending market's own oracle, and an independent price feed is used as a sanity check before a deposit is accepted
nodes.note: CONSUMED, NOT OWNED. CIAN operates no oracle. Ex is retained because a live external feed genuinely gates deposits, but note that the vault's own NAV does not come from it (F3), so the corpus's Ex points at the wrong object.

nodes.label: F19 the vault implementation can be replaced instantly by a three-of-four
nodes.text: the vault implementation can be replaced instantly by a three-of-four multisig, with no delay anywhere in the path
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call ProxyAdmin 0xf24955e9d0a05222373d4555f8831f7a05e83f62 owner() = 0x261090afe1e7305474f4e3eefcaca9964ebffff5, getThreshold() = 3 of 4, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: CORRECTION to the corpus, which records armedProhibitions: []. L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is VIOLATED: no timelock protects the Yield Layer. The only timelock found on chain (0xb39e6f93cff9Af7011810f41a4ed9b14582019b7, delay 86400) belongs to the 2022-era flagship product and is itself administered by an EOA. The address the documentation labels MultiSig, 0x8FA9aa69a6e94c1cd49FbF214C833B2911D02553, returns empty code — it is an EOA. Stage 3 should expect this construction to fail L15, and that failure is the finding. Epistemic label for the whole spec: no source repository of these contracts exists in public — verified bytecode only, one audit whose scope explicitly EXCLUDES the strategies, so the leverage and LTV logic that is the entire product was never audited.

nodes.label: Convex Finance
F1 a depositor's liquidity-pool token is staked by the protocol into the
nodes.text: a depositor's liquidity-pool token is staked by the protocol into the corresponding external gauge and credited one-for-one into a per-pool reward contract, withdrawable at any time with no deposit or withdrawal fee
nodes.note: Sh is approximate: the receipt is one-for-one rather than a varying pro-rata ratio, the degenerate case of a proportional pool claim. Rd is a DEPARTURE from the corpus, which omits it: the unconditional par withdrawal right is the whole difference between this deposit path and the CRV path in F5. Live Booster.poolLength() = 580.

nodes.label: F2 the external gauge's emissions token, the protocol's own token and arb
nodes.text: the external gauge's emissions token, the protocol's own token and arbitrary third-party reward tokens accrue to the staker by a per-token reward-per-share index

nodes.label: F3 each harvest's rewards are paid out linearly over a rolling one-week p
nodes.text: each harvest's rewards are paid out linearly over a rolling one-week period rather than at once
nodes.note: DEPARTURE: the corpus omits Sr for Convex. The reward contracts stream a rate over a fixed duration, which is what Sr names.

nodes.label: F4 the reward rate on every pooled deposit is multiplied by a boost deriv
nodes.text: the reward rate on every pooled deposit is multiplied by a boost derived from the protocol's share of a different token's escrowed supply, held by the protocol rather than by the depositor, up to a hard multiple of two and a half
nodes.note: RESIDUE. working_balance = min(l, 0.4*l + 0.6*L*V/V_total). Neither Sh nor Ix can express a claim whose accrual rate depends on an external, transferable, pooled quantity held by a third party. This is the mechanism that makes aggregation rational — Convex's entire economic reason to exist — and it has no name.

nodes.label: F5 the governance token of the upstream protocol, when deposited, is adde
nodes.text: the governance token of the upstream protocol, when deposited, is added to a single permanent escrow position from which no party can ever withdraw it
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Rd explicitly does NOT apply: the structured ABSENCE of a redemption right is the design. Live 2026-08-04: veCRV.balanceOf(0x989AEb4d175e16225E39E87d0D97A3360524AD80) = 420,633,657.30 of a 783,593,117.83 total supply, 53.68%; locked__end = 2030-07-25.

nodes.label: F6 that escrow is re-extended toward its maximum term by any permissionle
nodes.text: that escrow is re-extended toward its maximum term by any permissionless deposit call whenever it would otherwise begin to decay
nodes.note: RESIDUE. MAXTIME = 4*364 days and _lockCurve() calls increaseTime whenever the week-rounded target exceeds the stored unlock, so the commitment renews itself forever without any governance act. No symbol names a self-renewing commitment.

nodes.label: F7 in exchange the depositor receives a transferable token whose only exi
nodes.text: in exchange the depositor receives a transferable token whose only exit is sale on a secondary market, since the position behind it has no redemption function
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A liquid wrapper of a permanently locked position, whose peg is a market rather than a redemption. This pattern — liquid staking, liquid restaking, liquid lockers — is one of the most replicated in DeFi and there is no symbol for it.

nodes.label: F8 holders of that wrapper receive the upstream protocol's admin fees and
nodes.text: holders of that wrapper receive the upstream protocol's admin fees and may elect any mix between receiving them in the fee asset and receiving the two governance tokens
nodes.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fd). CORRECTION to the corpus, which describes this as 3CRV revenue: admin fees now arrive as crvUSD. The depositor's election between a cash asset and a governance asset is not named by Fd and is a second instance of the elective-return pattern seen at Huma 2.0.

nodes.label: F9 voting weight over the escrowed position is non-transferable and is a
nodes.text: voting weight over the escrowed position is non-transferable and is a function of the time remaining on a lock
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the largest single residue finding in this lane by TVL. Ep names a period boundary; Tg names a delay before execution; neither names a weight that is a function of time remaining. The corpus emits Ve here on contested-register grounds, calling it the strongest such case in its lane. Ve is not among the 58, so this construction does not emit it — with the consequence the corpus itself anticipated: strip the vote layer and what remains (Sh + Ix + Sr + Em) is indistinguishable from any staking-rewards contract.

nodes.label: F10 the protocol's own token can be locked for a sixteen-week minimum to o
nodes.text: the protocol's own token can be locked for a sixteen-week minimum to obtain a governance weight measured at weekly epoch boundaries
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call lockDuration() = 9,676,800, epochCount() = 232, lockedSupply() = 46,056,535.73 on 0x72a19342e8F1838460eBFCCEf09F6585e32db86E, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, corpus marker retained: Ep means an epoch-GATED TRANSITION and here the epochs gate voting weight and reward eligibility rather than a state transition. CORRECTION to the corpus marker's text: vote-lock epochs are weekly (Thursday 00:00 UTC) but the upstream gauge-weight vote is BI-weekly (Thursday 00:00 to Tuesday 00:00).

nodes.label: F11 lock-holders vote in a proposal on this protocol whose weights are anc
nodes.text: lock-holders vote in a proposal on this protocol whose weights are anchored to a historical epoch balance, and a separate executor contract later casts the aggregated result into the foreign protocol's gauge controller through a registered surrogate
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Two votes at different addresses with different electorates, joined by a surrogate registry and a one-level delegation. NEW MECHANISM the corpus does not carry: convex-eth/voting was created 2026-04-15 and is live — Booster.voteDelegate() = 0x5349fFbA494Ac3C888ffA16Fd438f44b8C67fb07, exactly the VoteDelegateExtension in that repo's deployment/mainnet.json. Any decomposition reading only convex-eth/platform describes Convex as it was in 2025.

nodes.label: F12 the protocol acquires and exercises governance rights inside four fore
nodes.text: the protocol acquires and exercises governance rights inside four foreign protocols that it does not control
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Au covers an execution scope granted by a principal over its own assets; nothing covers acquiring voting rights in a system you are not part of and renting them out. Related boundary finding: no Convex contract implements a vote-incentive market — a code search over convex-eth/platform returns one body-less interface and one test script, and convex-eth/voting returns zero. The bribe market exists (Votium) but is a separate protocol with no shared addresses, so the corpus's residue item 'no element for a bribe market' should be re-scoped as a boundary finding rather than a missing element of Convex.

nodes.label: F13 seventeen per cent of all harvested emissions revenue is taken and spl
nodes.text: seventeen per cent of all harvested emissions revenue is taken and split ten to wrapper-stakers, four and a half to lock-holders and two to the treasury, each component bounded in code and the total capped at twenty per cent
nodes.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fd), promoted from a corpus marker. CORRECTION: the widely quoted 16% with a 10/5/1 split is outdated; live Booster values are lockIncentive 1000, stakerIncentive 450, earmarkIncentive 50, platformFee 200 against MaxFees 2000.

nodes.label: F14 half a per cent of that revenue is paid to whichever anonymous address
nodes.text: half a per cent of that revenue is paid to whichever anonymous address calls the harvest function
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Fd names distribution of surplus to claimants; this is a subsidy for liveness, paid to a stranger for performing work the protocol cannot perform for itself. The same object appears at CIAN and Huma as an unpaid keeper dependency, which makes the paid version the interesting control.

nodes.label: F15 the protocol's own token is minted to depositors in proportion to harv
nodes.text: the protocol's own token is minted to depositors in proportion to harvested revenue, on a schedule whose multiplier steps down with cumulative supply and reaches zero at a hard cap
nodes.note: CORRECTION the corpus does not carry and stage 1 asked to be checked: the mechanism is in code but numerically dead. Live totalSupply() = 99,983,304.90 of a 100,000,000 cap, i.e. cliff 999 of 1000 and a multiplier of 0.001, zero at the next cliff. Em is retained because this obligation exists and only Em discharges it, but it must NOT be treated as a source of return: the corpus's canonicalForm lists Em as load-bearing and a construction that explains Convex's economics through it reproduces a protocol that no longer exists.

nodes.label: F16 arbitrary third-party reward tokens attached to an upstream gauge are
nodes.text: arbitrary third-party reward tokens attached to an upstream gauge are forwarded through per-pool stash contracts and virtual-balance children whose balances mirror the parent pool without holding its assets
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A pass-through claim on an unknown future token set, accounted by mirroring another contract's balances. No symbol names a shadow-balance accounting adapter.

nodes.label: F17 the owner may shut the entire system, pulling every deposited position
nodes.text: the owner may shut the entire system, pulling every deposited position out of the external gauges and marking every pool closed, and may shut individual pools
nodes.note: Live Booster.owner() = 0x3cE6408F923326f81A7D7929952947748180f1E6 (BoosterOwner), feeManager a 3-of-5 Safe.

nodes.label: F18 no deployed contract's code can be replaced: the protocol commits to i
nodes.text: no deployed contract's code can be replaced: the protocol commits to immutability and offers shutdown-and-redeploy as its only migration path
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the second correction stage 1 asked to be checked. The corpus emits Up and Tg for Convex; both are REFUTED. Blockscout reports proxy = None on Booster, VoterProxy, CVX, cvxCRV, CrvDepositor and CvxLockerV2, and no timelock is documented or found anywhere in the system. Immutability plus a kill switch is a materially different risk object from an upgradeable proxy and must not decompose to the same symbols. The residue is structural: the vocabulary can name mutability (Up) and delay (Tg) but has no way to ASSERT their absence, so a protocol that has bound itself and one that simply has not been audited for it are indistinguishable.

nodes.label: Huma Finance V2
F1 a depositor brings a stablecoin, without identity checks or accreditat
nodes.text: a depositor brings a stablecoin, without identity checks or accreditation, and receives a transferable token representing the deposit
nodes.note: SCOPE DECISION, stated explicitly as stage 1 requires. Obligations F1-F11 decompose HUMA 2.0, the permissionless Solana product launched April 2025, which carries 100% of the $219,355,660.45 that ranks this application. Obligations F12-F24 decompose HUMA INSTITUTIONAL, the permissioned tranched product the corpus's element set actually describes; each is marked. The two must not be conflated: decomposing both under one name produces a construction that reproduces neither. CORRECTION to the corpus: Aw is REFUTED for the TVL-carrying entity — Huma 2.0 is open to all. EPISTEMIC LABEL for F1-F11: the Solana program HumaXepHnjaRCpjYTokxY4UtaJcmx41prQ8cxGmFC5fn is closed-source, absent from the 00labs org, and returns is_verified false from the Solana verified-builds registry, so every obligation here rests on documentation and audit scopes rather than on readable source.

nodes.label: F2 the default claim class pays an administered eight per cent annual rat
nodes.text: the default claim class pays an administered eight per cent annual rate, stated as subject to monthly adjustment at the issuer's discretion
nodes.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. The same administered-rate object as the Sky Savings Rate, appearing independently at a second protocol in this lane: no utilisation curve, no auction, no market. DEPARTURE: the corpus emits Ix for Huma and stage 1 records no evidence of index accrual on either product — the EVM path computes and PAYS OUT yield at epoch close (processYieldForLenders then payoutYield) rather than accruing it into a share price, and the Solana accrual form is unverifiable because the program is closed. Ix is therefore dropped rather than assumed.

nodes.label: F3 the holder may switch instantly, for gas only, to a second claim class
nodes.text: the holder may switch instantly, for gas only, to a second claim class that pays no cash yield at all
nodes.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. A claim class whose holder ELECTS between a cash yield and a non-cash reward stream, switchable at will, has no symbol. Convex's cvxCRV reward-ratio election is the same shape in a different setting.

nodes.label: F4 in exchange the zero-yield class maximises an off-chain point balance
nodes.text: in exchange the zero-yield class maximises an off-chain point balance which is the holder's entire return
nodes.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. Em requires protocol-funded emissions of a token; points are an off-chain ledger of a future discretionary claim. The same object appears at Pendle, which taxes third-party points at 5%.

nodes.label: F5 a depositor may optionally commit for three or six months to multiply
nodes.text: a depositor may optionally commit for three or six months to multiply that point rate; commitments can be lengthened but never shortened, and breaking one retroactively forfeits the bonus, including on transfer
nodes.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. The lockup does not change the yield, the claim's seniority or its redemption terms — its only consequence is a discretionary multiplier on a non-token reward. Nothing in the vocabulary names a commitment with no claim-side effect.

nodes.label: F6 redemption requests are batched and settled by a scheduled off-chain j
nodes.text: redemption requests are batched and settled by a scheduled off-chain job in an all-or-nothing manner
nodes.note: HUMA 2.0. APPROXIMATE: Wq names the deferred exit, not the all-or-nothing settlement rule.

nodes.label: F7 redemption is first-come-first-served against a global daily cap that
nodes.text: redemption is first-come-first-served against a global daily cap that resets at midnight UTC, and requests above the cap are rejected outright rather than queued, against a documented service level of one to seven days
nodes.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. Wq names a queue that preserves order across time; this is a RATIONING RULE that discards excess demand at a period boundary, plus a promise that appears in no contract.

nodes.label: F8 a holder may bypass the redemption path entirely by selling the claim
nodes.text: a holder may bypass the redemption path entirely by selling the claim token into third-party automated market makers
nodes.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. The real exit liquidity for the ranked entity is supplied by protocols outside it, and the vocabulary again has no way to mark an element as inherited from a dependency. Same defect as Spark/Ps and CIAN/Ct.

nodes.label: F9 the yield paid to depositors originates in transaction fees from busin
nodes.text: the yield paid to depositors originates in transaction fees from businesses using an accelerated cross-border payment rail, in practice short-duration advances originated by a single named counterparty
nodes.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. No element for the SOURCE of yield, and none for originator concentration: the borrower on the deployed EVM pools is named in the deployment itself (Arf). A protocol can be fully expressible in this vocabulary while its solvency argument is entirely invisible.

nodes.label: F10 the deposits fund advances that are not secured by on-chain collateral
nodes.text: the deposits fund advances that are not secured by on-chain collateral
nodes.note: HUMA 2.0. Documentary only: the program is closed-source and not a verified build, so this cannot be checked against code for the entity carrying the TVL. Stage 3 should note that emitting Uc here arms L3 (Uc implies Aw + At + (Bs|Tr) + obligor) against a product that has none of Aw, At or Tr — see F21.

nodes.label: F11 the redemption round and the price refresh happen only because schedul
nodes.text: the redemption round and the price refresh happen only because scheduled off-chain jobs run and call them
nodes.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. Ep names a period boundary; nothing names that the boundary exists only if someone calls it. Third instance of the keeper-liveness gap in this lane, after CIAN's three-day NAV revert and Convex's paid harvest bounty.

nodes.label: F12 a lender passes identity and accreditation checks and is approved by a
nodes.text: a lender passes identity and accreditation checks and is approved by a designated operator before being allowed to deposit
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. This is where the corpus's Aw belongs; it does not apply to the ranked entity.

nodes.label: F13 deposits go into a senior or a junior claim with declared seniority on
nodes.text: deposits go into a senior or a junior claim with declared seniority on loss and a fixed or risk-adjusted split of yield between them
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only.

nodes.label: F14 the senior claim may not exceed four times the junior claim, enforced
nodes.text: the senior claim may not exceed four times the junior claim, enforced on deposit and again in the ordering of redemptions
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. RESIDUE, upgraded from a corpus observation to a verified constant: lpConfig.maxSeniorJuniorRatio = 4. Tr names the waterfall, not the thickness constraint that makes it safe. It is also the magnitude cap (slot 3) on the mandate in F17-F20.

nodes.label: F15 a first-loss cover funded by borrowers, insurers and administrators ab
nodes.text: a first-loss cover funded by borrowers, insurers and administrators absorbs a default ahead of the junior claim, up to the lesser of a cap and a rate applied to the default amount, and its capital is deliberately left undeployed
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. APPROXIMATE, corpus marker retained: this is genuinely first-loss capital but it is not slashed by a protocol rule, it simply sits lower in the waterfall. Tr and Bs overlap here and the vocabulary gives no guidance on which to prefer.

nodes.label: F16 all administrative fees are automatically routed into that cover until
nodes.text: all administrative fees are automatically routed into that cover until it reaches its maximum
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fd), a DEPARTURE the corpus does not carry: realised fees are recycled into the backstop rather than paid out, which is a distribution with a named non-obvious recipient.

nodes.label: F17 one stored address is the only caller permitted to approve a borrower
nodes.text: one stored address is the only caller permitted to approve a borrower into the pool
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. MANDATE SLOT 1 (named agent), partial fit — Aw names the enumeration (_onlyEvaluationAgent), not the authority. The address is a single field, address public evaluationAgent, set by the pool owner or the protocol owner.

nodes.label: F18 that address alone declares a borrower in default, and the loss it dec
nodes.text: that address alone declares a borrower in default, and the loss it declares flows directly into the seniority waterfall
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Sv), promoted from a corpus marker into the construction and the single best fit for this candidate in the lane. triggerDefault(address) is _onlyEvaluationAgent and returns (principalLoss, yieldLoss, feesLoss) straight into the waterfall. This is servicing and determination discretion in its intended sense, and it satisfies L6.

nodes.label: F19 the same address alone sets the borrower's credit limit and the yield
nodes.text: the same address alone sets the borrower's credit limit and the yield in basis points, and may revise both afterwards by raising the limit, changing the yield, extending the term or waiving a late fee
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. RESIDUE, and the precise boundary of the lane's best-fitting candidate: Sv names the authority to DETERMINE AN OUTCOME on a claim; it does not name the authority to SET THE PRICE or SIZE THE EXPOSURE. Those are allocation acts and they are unnamed. Also unnamed: Aw is a static admission test, and approveBorrower opens a continuing relationship that is repriced and resized over time.

nodes.label: F20 that address is required to hold junior-tranche capital in the very po
nodes.text: that address is required to hold junior-tranche capital in the very pool whose credit it underwrites, checked as a liquidity requirement
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. RESIDUE, and unique in this lane: slot 7 of the mandate shape, skin in the game. _checkLiquidityRequirementForEA makes Huma the only protocol here whose discretionary agent is capitalised against its own decisions. Bs names slashable first-loss capital but not capital posted as a CONDITION OF HOLDING AN AUTHORITY.

nodes.label: F21 the financed obligation is minted as a non-fungible token recording an
nodes.text: the financed obligation is minted as a non-fungible token recording an amount, a currency code, a creation date, a maturity date, a paid amount and a creator, by whoever holds the minting role
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. RESIDUE, and sharper than the corpus's version. The struct stores NO PAYER, no document hash, no jurisdiction and no verification of any kind; the only link to the world is a hash of the originator's own internal reference and an opaque uri. So the receivable is an on-chain object but an ASSERTION, not evidence. DEPARTURE: the corpus emits At as the closest available symbol. At is REFUTED, not merely approximate — L27 requires a named attester, independence, a stated assurance level, a staleness bound and recourse, and none exists, so At cannot be discharged at all. Dropping At will make L3 fail in stage 3 for the Uc emitted at F10 and F22; that failure IS the finding, and X11b (Uc with all of them and weak underwriting, class H) should be considered for arming. No element for off-chain legal recourse either: nothing in the contracts references a jurisdiction, a governing agreement or a servicer of record, yet that is what makes the pool solvent.

nodes.label: F22 a borrower draws against a revolving line, a receivable-backed line at
nodes.text: a borrower draws against a revolving line, a receivable-backed line at an advance rate below one hundred per cent, or an outright purchase of the receivable, each with a due date and a period count
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. Ft is APPROXIMATE and its scope must be stated: it names the BORROWER-side dated obligation, not the investor claim, which is open-ended with epoch redemption. Stage 1 records that Ft is doubly wrong for Huma 2.0, where the investor holds a perpetual token whose optional lockup dates nothing.

nodes.label: F23 redemption requests are batched to a period aligned with the pool's pa
nodes.text: redemption requests are batched to a period aligned with the pool's payment cycle, senior filled first, shortfalls pro-rated, the unfilled portion rolled to the next period, and the proceeds claimed by a separate call
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. Senior is filled first specifically to avoid breaching the 4:1 ratio of F14, so the ordering is a solvency device rather than a fairness rule — which Wq does not name. The concrete epoch length is UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F24 designated pausers can stop all outbound movement of money, and only t
nodes.text: designated pausers can stop all outbound movement of money, and only the protocol owner can restart it
nodes.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. MANDATE SLOT 5 (halt). DEPARTURE: the corpus carries no control-plane element for Huma. Gp does not express that the right to stop and the right to restart are deliberately held by different parties — the same split Sky builds explicitly with grantors and revokers. Stage 1 also records a ninth role that exists only in code, a Sentinel service account (onlyPoolOwnerOrSentinelServiceAccount), which is the on-chain identity of the automation in F11.

nodes.label: Pendle
F1 a deposit of an external yield-bearing token (wstETH, sUSDe, aTokens,
nodes.text: a deposit of an external yield-bearing token (wstETH, sUSDe, aTokens, GLP) is wrapped into a uniform token whose redemption value tracks the source protocol's exchange rate
nodes.note: Ix names the accrual (SY.exchangeRate). It does not name the adapter role itself: an SY wrapper is bound at deployment to exactly one named external protocol and cannot be redirected. That binding is the reason Pendle has no allocation mandate, and it has no symbol.

nodes.label: F2 the wrapped token is split, in accounting-asset units, into a principa
nodes.text: the wrapped token is split, in accounting-asset units, into a principal claim and a yield claim that trade separately

nodes.label: F3 the principal claim is a zero-coupon claim on the accounting asset dat
nodes.text: the principal claim is a zero-coupon claim on the accounting asset dated to a fixed maturity and pays nothing before it
nodes.note: FORCED FIT, carried from the corpus marker and sharpened by stage 1. Ft is filed under Credit as fixed-term DEBT; a PT is not a debt, nobody owes anything, it is a stripped principal claim on a yield-bearing token. The maturity concept is right, the liability framing is wrong.

nodes.label: F4 at maturity the principal claim redeems one-for-one for the accounting
nodes.text: at maturity the principal claim redeems one-for-one for the accounting asset with no fee, and before maturity the principal and yield claims can be burned together back into the wrapper
nodes.note: Ep is used for the expiry boundary that switches PT from non-redeemable to redeemable. This satisfies L5 (Py to (Sh|Ix|Rb) + Ep + Rd).

nodes.label: F5 the yield claim accrues the wrapper's variable interest by a reciproca
nodes.text: the yield claim accrues the wrapper's variable interest by a reciprocal-difference formula over a stored and a current index, and separately accrues each of the wrapper's external reward tokens by its own per-token index
nodes.note: One symbol serves two structurally different accruals (an interest accumulator and a set of per-token reward accumulators). The vocabulary cannot distinguish them.

nodes.label: F6 the accrual index is a monotonic high-water mark: if the source exchan
nodes.text: the accrual index is a monotonic high-water mark: if the source exchange rate falls the yield claim stops accruing entirely, and the drawdown is borne by the principal claim at redemption
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Ix permits an index to move in both directions; PMath.max(SY.exchangeRate(), _pyIndexStored) is a ratchet. Sl (socialized-loss allocation) was considered and rejected per stage 1: there is no loss event, only an accounting asymmetry that assigns every drawdown to one claim class. A loss-allocation rule disguised as an accounting choice has no symbol.

nodes.label: F7 the yield claim's notional shrinks to zero by construction as the rema
nodes.text: the yield claim's notional shrinks to zero by construction as the remaining accrual window closes
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Every claim symbol in the vocabulary (Sh, Ix, Rb) describes a claim whose notional is preserved or grows. A decaying-notional claim has no symbol.

nodes.label: F8 after maturity the yield claim's index freezes at a snapshot, only alr
nodes.text: after maturity the yield claim's index freezes at a snapshot, only already-accrued interest remains claimable, and every reward token subsequently arriving on that expired claim is swept to the treasury
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Not a fee and not a redemption charge: an abandonment sweep of a live claimant's property to the protocol. Fd was considered and rejected — nothing is being distributed to a claimant class, the claimant is being escheated.

nodes.label: F9 the principal claim is priced against the wrapper by a pool whose inva
nodes.text: the principal claim is priced against the wrapper by a pool whose invariant is a logit curve in implied-rate space, whose stiffness parameter grows without bound and whose intercept decays as time-to-expiry shrinks, so identical pool state prices differently on a different day
nodes.note: RESIDUE, the single clearest missing element in this lane. Cp, Wg, St, Cl and Pm are all static invariants. The contested symbol Tw is time-weighted AMM EXECUTION, a different mechanism, and stage 1 confirms the corpus was right to reject it. Note also that the corpus's phrasing (scalar and anchor both decay) has the sign of the stiffness term backwards: rateScalar = scalarRoot * 365d / timeToExpiry DIVERGES. Also unnamed: that the pool quotes an interest rate rather than a price ratio and persists lastLnImpliedRate as its state. Stage 1 did not characterise contracts/limit/ (PendleLimitRouter), so the limit-order execution path is deliberately not decomposed here rather than guessed at between Ob and Rf.

nodes.label: F10 the curve's intercept is recomputed before every single trade so that
nodes.text: the curve's intercept is recomputed before every single trade so that the pre-trade implied rate equals the implied rate left by the previous trade
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Not slippage, not a fee, not an oracle: the invariant rewriting its own parameters from its trade history to preserve a derived quantity. No AMM symbol covers a curve parameterised by its own past.

nodes.label: F11 a liquidity provider deposits the wrapper and the principal claim and
nodes.text: a liquidity provider deposits the wrapper and the principal claim and holds a transferable pro-rata claim on the pool and its fee income, with a minimum quantity permanently locked at initialisation
nodes.note: DEPARTURE from the corpus, which omits Sh for Pendle. The market LP token is a pro-rata pool claim and one of the four sources of depositor return named in stage 1.

nodes.label: F12 the swap fee is quoted as an interest-rate spread whose multiplier is
nodes.text: the swap fee is quoted as an interest-rate spread whose multiplier is exponential in years-to-expiry, so the same trade pays less notional the nearer maturity is
nodes.note: RESIDUE. There is no global swap-fee rate at all; lnFeeRateRoot is chosen per market by its creator under a cap. A fee that is a rate spread rather than a price spread has no symbol.
