nodes.note: Gp is correct here, unlike for BTCB. It does not distinguish a pause that reaches every holder's transfers (this one) from a pause that only stops new issuance; those are different powers over different parties.

nodes.label: F13 No party can seize or freeze an individual holder's balance: the token
nodes.text: No party can seize or freeze an individual holder's balance: the token has no blacklist and no forced transfer -- blacklister() and isBlacklisted(address) both revert and the source inherits only StandardToken, DetailedERC20, MintableToken, BurnableToken, PausableToken and OwnableContract.
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call blacklister() and isBlacklisted(address) at 0x2260fac5e5542a773aa44fbcfedf7c193bc2c599, both revert (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WrappedBTC/bitcoin-token-smart-contracts/master/ethereum/contracts/token/WBTC.sol (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: the corpus's Fz marker ('the custodian can pause minting and blacklist addresses') is dropped. Pause is true, blacklist is false. This obligation is a guarantee discharged by construction -- the power cannot arise -- and the requirement language admits only discharge by naming a satisfying element, so an absent power reads identically to an unspecified one. That is the options lane's finding exhibited on a bridge.

nodes.label: F14 Authority is held by two independent quorums that execute immediately:
nodes.text: Authority is held by two independent quorums that execute immediately: the Controller is owned by a 6-of-10 multisig at 0x972eed35781f09987a5c40f761f6a24623c570de and Members by a 5-of-9 at 0x4dbbbfb0e68be9d8f5a377a4654604a62e851e80, both Consensys MultiSigWallet instances with no delay of any kind.
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call owner(), required(), MAX_OWNER_COUNT() on Controller/Members owners; secondsTimeLocked(), delay(), getMinDelay() absent on all three multisigs (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WrappedBTC/DAO/master/README.md (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the correction that inverts the category reading. CORPUS DEPARTURE: Tg is dropped. It is the single symbol distinguishing WBTC from the Coinbase entry, and there is no timelock anywhere in the WBTC control plane. What WBTC actually has that the other two custodial wrappers lack is quorum, not delay -- and the vocabulary has Tg for delayed execution and NOTHING for 'k-of-n, immediate'. Control elements name the facility; the risk lives in the holder.

nodes.label: F15 The governance body the project documents is not the one that holds th
nodes.text: The governance body the project documents is not the one that holds the keys: the repository names 0xB33f8879...8A37c5 (8-of-13) as 'the WBTC DAO' and instructs readers to verify that it owns the Controller and Members, and it owns neither.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Six of the 6-of-10's signers do not appear in the repository's DAO member table, and the repo lists 24 merchants against 47 on chain. No element carries the identity of a holder, so a documented-versus-actual authority mismatch is unstateable and therefore uncheckable.

nodes.label: F16 The 6-of-10 can replace the contract that authorises minting and the r
nodes.text: The 6-of-10 can replace the contract that authorises minting and the registry of merchants and custodians, via Controller.setFactory() and Controller.setMembers(), without changing a line of the token's code.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Mutable authority without a mutable implementation: not Up (no proxy, no implementation slot, non-upgradeable Solidity 0.4.24 token), not Tg (no delay), not Gp. The corpus records neither the power nor its absence from the vocabulary.

nodes.label: F17 The token contract itself cannot be replaced or abandoned: it is a non
nodes.text: The token contract itself cannot be replaced or abandoned: it is a non-upgradeable Solidity 0.4.24 contract whose renounceOwnership() is deliberately reverted.
nodes.note: RESIDUE of the same kind as F13. Up names code mutability; the vocabulary offers no way to assert immutability as a positive guarantee, only to omit Up, which is indistinguishable from not having looked.

nodes.label: F18 WBTC circulates on seven chains, and the cross-chain leg is supplied b
nodes.text: WBTC circulates on seven chains, and the cross-chain leg is supplied by a third-party messaging protocol that the issuer selects and can replace -- announced on the access date as a move from LayerZero to Chainlink CCIP for the whole ~$7.3-7.7b float.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, with weak provenance: the CCIP migration is PRESS-CONFIRMED ONLY -- no first-party BitGo or Chainlink page was reachable -- and must not enter the paper as an issuer claim. The structural point stands regardless: one protocol in this category contains another as a swappable component, and containment between protocols is inexpressible in the carrier (the same gap the intents and yield lanes found). Here it means entry #1's design depends on entry #2's, and that dependence was being severed on the access date.

nodes.label: F19 The merchant's fee to the user is set off-chain by bilateral agreement
nodes.text: The merchant's fee to the user is set off-chain by bilateral agreement, with no minimum size stated and no on-chain record.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Fd (candidate) names surplus and fee distribution as a protocol mechanism; a bilaterally negotiated off-chain price is not that, and pricing the only path to redemption is exactly where the peg's frictions live.

nodes.label: 08-intents
Binance Wallet
F1 a venue is chosen for the user across third-party liquidity providers
nodes.text: a venue is chosen for the user across third-party liquidity providers on CeFi and DeFi exchanges; the user names no venue and is shown only the result
nodes.note: Ag is asserted on the operator's own wording. The venue set, the algorithm, the provider identities and the route are all unpublished, so unlike KyberSwap this Ag is discharged on assertion rather than on an inspectable mechanism. There is no repository for the routing engine and none for the router contract.

nodes.label: F2 the user is shown a single recommended provider rather than a route, a
nodes.text: the user is shown a single recommended provider rather than a route, and the rule by which that provider was chosen is not stated
nodes.note: RESIDUE. This is discretion, not an auction and not a route. No symbol names administrative allocation of a fill without a stated rule. Ag names the construction of a route; it does not name the unexplained selection of a counterparty.

nodes.label: F3 whether any counterparty ever signs a firm quote that this system then
nodes.text: whether any counterparty ever signs a firm quote that this system then fills is not stated at any primary source; the published wording ('CeFi and DeFi exchanges') is equally consistent with routing into an exchange-operated on-chain pool
nodes.note: UNKNOWN, recorded as residue. DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS: the corpus decomposes Binance Wallet as {Ag, Rf} with a marker saying Rf is 'partly INFERRED'. Stage 1 searched and found no primary evidence for RFQ at all, and there is no repository and no developer documentation to check against. Rf is therefore DROPPED from the construction rather than carried with a marker, per the standing rule that a finding of failure beats a forced fit.

nodes.label: F4 the user sets a slippage tolerance beside a displayed Minimum Received
nodes.text: the user sets a slippage tolerance beside a displayed Minimum Received, and bears every adverse move between signature and inclusion; all swaps are final once confirmed
nodes.note: RESIDUE, the same gap as LiquidMesh F4. No element names a settlement-enforced output floor on a swap the user executes for themselves; In presumes a filler distinct from the signer, and there is none.

nodes.label: F5 the user pays network gas on every swap, including on swaps that fail,
nodes.text: the user pays network gas on every swap, including on swaps that fail, and no fee sponsorship is offered at any point
nodes.note: DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS. The corpus carries a CANDIDATE-REGISTER marker for Gs (sponsored-fee liability) on Binance Wallet and a residue line about gasless swap UX. The primary announcement says the opposite in terms: 'users will still need to pay for network gas fees'. Gs is unwarranted and is not carried. Recorded as an obligation so the negative is on the record rather than merely absent.

nodes.label: F6 the user's transactions are shielded from the public mempool by defaul
nodes.text: the user's transactions are shielded from the public mempool by default, by a private-RPC programme operated by the host chain and its partners rather than by this application
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Two gaps at once: no element names a transaction's path to inclusion, and no element can express that a protocol's stated property is inherited from its host chain's infrastructure rather than produced by the protocol. The wallet consumes an ecosystem service here; it does not operate one.

nodes.label: F7 settlement runs through a router the operator built and controls, depl
nodes.text: settlement runs through a router the operator built and controls, deployed at a single vanity address across seven EVM chains and as a matching-prefix program on Solana, implemented as an EIP-2535 Diamond whose facets a single owner address may replace selector by selector
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and a departure from the corpus {Ag, Rf}. Up names a mutable implementation proxy; it does not name per-selector facet replacement, in which parts of the contract can be swapped independently. Owner is an EOA (0xEe7b429Ea01F76102f053213463D4e95D5D24AE8) with no timelock published, so X9 (Up with immediate single-key control) is armed and L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is not discharged.

nodes.label: F8 the settlement contract's bytecode is verified against a source blob t
nodes.text: the settlement contract's bytecode is verified against a source blob the operator uploaded to a block explorer, while no public, versioned or reviewable codebase for it exists anywhere
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No element expresses the evidentiary status of the code that implements the mechanism. 'Verified' here means the bytecode matches an uploaded blob, not that it matches a public codebase, and a decomposition cannot tell the two apart.

nodes.label: F9 the wallet holds the user's signing key as three MPC shares rather tha
nodes.text: the wallet holds the user's signing key as three MPC shares rather than as a single secret, so the party that routes the trade is also a party to producing the signature
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The 58 contain no symbol for custody or key management of any kind. This gap recurs at Jupiter F14 (a custodial vault holding resting orders) and is worth escalating beyond this category.

nodes.label: F10 the swap sits inside an application that already holds the user's KYC-
nodes.text: the swap sits inside an application that already holds the user's KYC-verified exchange account and balances, so the party that owns the demand also chooses the venue, and no consideration for that choice is disclosed in either direction
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the central one. Order-flow ownership stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. This is the purest order-flow owner in the lane: it owns the exchange account, the wallet, the router, the chain on which 98.3 percent of its volume settles, and the token universe the user can see. There is no public evidence of payment for order flow and equally none of its absence; unlike OKX no conflict-of-interest policy is published. The vocabulary spends four symbols on how an order is matched and none on who was entitled to decide where it went.

nodes.label: F11 the right to fill is not auctioned, not tendered and not priced: there
nodes.text: the right to fill is not auctioned, not tendered and not priced: there is no solver set, no bidding, no eligibility rule and no published list of the providers that supply the other side
nodes.note: RESIDUE, recorded as a null. Solver eligibility stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. Whether the operator or an affiliate is ever the maker is UNKNOWN and no primary source addresses it.

nodes.label: F12 the application claims to find the most competitive price from thousan
nodes.text: the application claims to find the most competitive price from thousands of options on CeFi and DeFi exchanges, with no benchmark named, no measurement published and no disclosure of the alternatives that were rejected
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Price-improvement benchmarking stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. X14's second limb (a price-improvement claim with no named benchmark) holds squarely; its first limb (exclusive market structure) is UNKNOWN, because the provider set is unpublished and therefore cannot be shown either exclusive or open.

nodes.label: F13 trading fees on all swaps were waived for eight months, scoped to part
nodes.text: trading fees on all swaps were waived for eight months, scoped to particular products and to backed-up keyless addresses only, with imported wallets excluded
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Nothing names a temporary, conditional, product-scoped and wallet-type-scoped price of zero, which is a distribution instrument rather than a fee schedule. The CURRENT STANDING SWAP FEE IS UNKNOWN: no primary source states it, and the figures circulating on review sites are not carried, per invariant 5.

nodes.label: F14 limit orders placed in the Alpha product execute against on-chain mark
nodes.text: limit orders placed in the Alpha product execute against on-chain markets and their fee was cut from 0.15 percent to 0.01 percent on one chain
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Ob was considered and is NOT asserted: no primary source establishes whether a book exists on-chain, off-chain, or at all, so the mechanism is UNKNOWN and only the fee change is citable.

nodes.label: F15 an exchange Spot or Funding balance can be turned into an on-chain tra
nodes.text: an exchange Spot or Funding balance can be turned into an on-chain trade with no wallet in the loop, and the order is auto-cancelled if the minimum received falls below the amount displayed
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The custody boundary is crossed inside the mechanism: custodied exchange funds originate an on-chain swap. No element names origination of an on-chain trade from an off-chain custodial balance.

nodes.label: F16 a token bought this way cannot be withdrawn or transferred out of the
nodes.text: a token bought this way cannot be withdrawn or transferred out of the operator's environment until the operator lists it on its own exchange
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Fz (freeze / forced transfer, candidate) is the nearest and is rejected: the BEP-20 token itself is not frozen and carries no transfer restriction; the constraint is on the venue's withdrawal function, imposed by the same party that chose the venue. L28 would require a named authority, enumerated triggers, an appeal path and holder disclosure; none is present. Different actor, different object.

nodes.label: F17 the Alpha product is a region-gated and compliance-gated beta availabl
nodes.text: the Alpha product is a region-gated and compliance-gated beta available only to accounts the operator deems eligible
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and a departure from the corpus {Ag, Rf}. Aw is an on-chain permission gate; this one is off-chain, applied at the product surface by the operator, and unenforced by the router, which anyone may call. Used per the standing principle of this lane: Aw for gates on the party seeking service, never for gates on who may fill.

nodes.label: F18 the operator disclaims being the counterparty and disclaims responsibi
nodes.text: the operator disclaims being the counterparty and disclaims responsibility for the third-party applications into which it routes the user's trade
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A routing system that selects venues while assuming no responsibility for them. Ag names the selection and is silent about who bears the consequence of it, which is precisely the commercial fact.

nodes.label: F19 the same router is deployed independently on twelve chains; no value c
nodes.text: the same router is deployed independently on twelve chains; no value crosses a domain and no message is verified between domains
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a deliberate negative for stage 3: Xf and Xm are NOT discharged. 98.3 percent of volume settles on one chain, which the vocabulary also cannot express.

nodes.label: Jupiter
F1 a route is constructed across venues the user did not choose, and retu
nodes.text: a route is constructed across venues the user did not choose, and returned as a fully assembled transaction the user need only sign

nodes.label: F2 the order is split across paths to a granularity of 0.01 percent by nu
nodes.text: the order is split across paths to a granularity of 0.01 percent by numerical optimisation (golden-section search and Brent's method) rather than by enumeration
nodes.note: Ag covers route construction and therefore covers this, but it cannot distinguish a router that enumerates from one that optimises, nor record the 100x performance difference Jupiter attributes to the change. Recorded so the construction is not read as ignoring the engine.

nodes.label: F3 quotes are solicited from independent third-party routing protocols as
nodes.text: quotes are solicited from independent third-party routing protocols as well as from venues, and the winning quote may come from a rival aggregator rather than from a pool
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the nesting finding this lane was asked to surface. Four engines compete inside one product: Metis/Iris and JupiterZ (Jupiter's own) against DFlow, OKX and Hashflow (other protocols'). Two of those leaves, OKX and DFlow, are separately ranked rows in this same corpus category. Ag names multi-venue route construction and has no composition operator, so it cannot express an Ag whose leaves are Ag. A flat ranking of this category double-counts volume and mis-attributes execution: a system that routes to routers is doing something a system that routes to venues is not.

nodes.label: F4 candidate routes are simulated on-chain before one is chosen, and are
nodes.text: candidate routes are simulated on-chain before one is chosen, and are ranked on predicted executed price rather than on quoted price
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A distinct epistemic act: the mechanism does not trust its own quotes and buys evidence before committing. Nothing in the 58 names simulate-before-choose, and Ag presumes the quote is the input to selection.

nodes.label: F5 quote sources that perform badly are automatically sidelined by the ro
nodes.text: quote sources that perform badly are automatically sidelined by the router without any governance act
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The venue set is not a constant and is revised by the router's own measurement of its suppliers. No element names a self-adjusting supplier set; Aw would be a gate, and this is a performance ranking with no stated threshold (the rule is UNKNOWN).

nodes.label: F6 a market maker's price is accepted by a user-signed transaction that t
nodes.text: a market maker's price is accepted by a user-signed transaction that the maker then executes and pays the gas for, giving the taker zero slippage and no gas cost
nodes.note: In IS REASSIGNED, not dropped. The corpus attaches In to Jupiter's limit/trigger/DCA products with a marker that the solver half is largely absent; under Trigger V2 those are custodial (see F14) and In fails there outright. It fits here instead: signed outcome constraints, a settlement verifier, competing third-party fillers, and a quote expiry with a fallback to on-chain routing, which is all four parts of L12. Gs is CANDIDATE-REGISTER and matches the corpus's own use at 1inch Fusion; L21's metering and fee settlement are absent.

nodes.label: F7 the market maker retains the right to decline execution after the take
nodes.text: the market maker retains the right to decline execution after the taker has accepted its quote
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS: Rf is DROPPED from Jupiter's construction. Rf is defined as a signed maker quote and asserts firmness; a maker holding last look has sold an option, not a price. Jupiter's own API design concedes it, forbidding modification of an RFQ transaction and confining RFQ to the managed path for exactly this reason. Rf is therefore wrong in kind for JupiterZ rather than approximate, and the standing rule is that a finding of failure beats a forced fit. If stage 3 or the council prefers the forced fit, the alternative is Rf carried with a last-look marker; this lane's finding is failure.

nodes.label: F8 two mutually exclusive API paths exist with different guarantees: a ma
nodes.text: two mutually exclusive API paths exist with different guarantees: a managed path that assembles and lands the transaction, charges a platform fee and can use RFQ, and a raw-instruction path that is composable, carries no platform fee and can only use the in-house router
nodes.note: RESIDUE, the same dispatcher gap as OKX F9 in a different form. Here the caller chooses rather than the system, but the vocabulary equally cannot express that the fee, the composability and the set of available fill mechanisms all change with the choice.

nodes.label: F9 the signed transaction is submitted through infrastructure the protoco
nodes.text: the signed transaction is submitted through infrastructure the protocol owns, a validator and RPC of its own, with a minimum tip, rather than through a public endpoint or a third-party relay
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No symbol names the transaction's route to inclusion, and none names owning it. MEV protection here is not a service bought or a chain-level default inherited (contrast Binance Wallet F6) but a consequence of vertical integration into block production.

nodes.label: F10 the protocol publishes a measured average positive slippage of +0.63 b
nodes.text: the protocol publishes a measured average positive slippage of +0.63 basis points as a product property, that is, a claim that executed prices beat quoted prices
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Price-improvement benchmarking stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. The benchmark is the protocol's own quote and the measurement is the protocol's own, so it is unfalsifiable from outside; the corpus residue 'no element for route-quality guarantees / price-improvement sharing' is confirmed and sharpened into a published number.

nodes.label: F11 a platform fee is deducted inside the quote at a rate that depends on
nodes.text: a platform fee is deducted inside the quote at a rate that depends on the asset classes being traded and rises to 50 basis points for any token listed within the previous 24 hours
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Fd is the nearest and is rejected: Fd names the distribution of surplus and fees, not their levy, and nothing names a fee schedule conditioned on the age or class of the asset. Schedule is 0 bps for stable-to-stable, LST-to-LST and pairs into the protocol's own tokens, 2 bps SOL to stablecoin, 5 bps LST to stablecoin, 10 bps otherwise, 50 bps under 24 hours.

nodes.label: F12 the fee is collected in a priority-ordered choice among the pair's tok
nodes.text: the fee is collected in a priority-ordered choice among the pair's tokens rather than in a fixed leg
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The protocol chooses which side of the trade to tax by the liquidity of the token (SOL, then stablecoins, then LSTs, then large caps, then other). No element names a fee whose denomination is itself a decision rule.

nodes.label: F13 an integrator sets a referral fee between 50 and 255 basis points on i
nodes.text: an integrator sets a referral fee between 50 and 255 basis points on its users' trades and the protocol keeps 20 percent of it; if the integrator's fee account is uninitialised the trade still executes and the integrator simply gets nothing
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A stated revenue split on someone else's users: distribution is sold, order flow is bought, and the price is a percentage of a fee neither party's user sees. This is the fourth distinct form the same unnameable primitive takes in this category (see LiquidMesh F10, OKX F11, KyberSwap F15).

nodes.label: F14 resting limit, OCO and recurring orders are held in a custodial vault
nodes.text: resting limit, OCO and recurring orders are held in a custodial vault operated by a third-party key manager, stored off-chain and private by default, rather than in an account the user controls
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the largest single gap in this application. THE 58 CONTAIN NO SYMBOL FOR CUSTODY AT ALL, which is worth escalating beyond this category (Binance Wallet F9 is the same gap). In is rejected because In presumes a signed constraint any party can enforce at settlement, and here a custodian holds the funds. Ob is rejected because the order is not on-chain. Sb is rejected because the privacy is non-publication by a custodian, not shielded state with a nullifier set. Under V1 these orders were on-chain accounts; the change of custody is a change of category, not a detail, and the corpus predates it.

nodes.label: F15 a keeper operated by the protocol fires those orders when a US dollar
nodes.text: a keeper operated by the protocol fires those orders when a US dollar price condition is met rather than a pool rate, sets the slippage for each slice itself, and the output amount is explicitly not guaranteed
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Ex is rejected: the price is consumed off-chain by the protocol's own keeper and never verified on-chain, so there is no feed, no medianizer and no staleness bound to name. The corpus's rejection of the contested symbol Tw for scheduled execution is correct and is now stronger than the corpus knew, since the slices are keeper-fired from a custodial vault against a US dollar trigger, which is further from a TWAMM pool invariant than V1 was. No element names a scheduled or time-sliced execution, and none names an execution with no output guarantee.

nodes.label: F16 the protocol assigns tokens a quality score and a verification status
nodes.text: the protocol assigns tokens a quality score and a verification status of its own devising, which condition how a token is surfaced and what it costs to trade
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A protocol-assigned quality label on the asset, feeding both display and price. LiquidMesh F16 is the same gap through a third-party risk vendor rather than an in-house score.

nodes.label: F17 access to the router is rationed by request-rate tier and filtered by
nodes.text: access to the router is rationed by request-rate tier and filtered by country, IP range and request header, so who may ask the router for a price, and how often, is itself allocated
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and a departure from the corpus {Ag, In, Rf}. Aw carries the deny rules; it cannot carry the graded rationing (0.5 to 150 requests per second), which is an allocation of execution quality rather than a binary permission. Used per this lane's standing principle: Aw for gates on the party seeking the service only.

nodes.label: F18 the routing engine is distributed as a closed binary and no source for
nodes.text: the routing engine is distributed as a closed binary and no source for the deployed aggregator program is published; a published audit inventory stands in its place
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Two of this lane's five have converged on the same answer to how you distribute a router without publishing it (see OKX F16). Third-party claims that Jupiter is open source are not supported by the contents of the jup-ag organisation and are recorded here as resolved against the marketing claim. The compensating control is the audit set at https://developers.jup.ag/docs/resources/audits (accessed 2026-08-05), which no element expresses either.

nodes.label: F19 the router owns venues on the other side of its own routing: a perpetu
nodes.text: the router owns venues on the other side of its own routing: a perpetuals exchange, a lending market with flash loans, a liquid-staking token, a launchpad with bonding curves, a prediction market and a validator, so it can internalise the flow it receives
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The corpus residue 'no element for the router also owning the venues it routes to' is confirmed and has grown since the corpus was written. Vertical order-flow capture has no symbol; note also that a construction listing Fl for Jupiter Lend would be capturing a different product, so Fl is deliberately not carried here.

nodes.label: F20 the protocol occupies four positions in the order-flow market at once:
nodes.text: the protocol occupies four positions in the order-flow market at once: it owns the default trade surface on its chain, it buys routing from rival protocols, it sells the right to fill to market makers including the last-look privilege, and it sells distribution to integrators at a stated split
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the central one. Order-flow ownership stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. The party at category rank 6 whose explicit product is the sale of order flow (DFlow) sells into this system, so the buyer and the seller of order flow appear in the same corpus with no symbol distinguishing their positions.

nodes.label: KyberSwap
F1 a route is constructed for a user who named no venue, across four clas
nodes.text: a route is constructed for a user who named no venue, across four classes of liquidity at once: automated market makers, order-book venues, the operator's own limit orders, and off-chain market-maker quotes
nodes.note: Over 400 venues on 25 networks. Unlike every other application in this lane, the simulation half of the route computation is public and inspectable (see F19). One further property that Ag cannot carry: the router is deployed at the IDENTICAL address on every supported chain (MetaAggregationRouterV2 at 0x6131B5fae19EA4f9D964eAc0408E4408b66337b5, https://docs.kyberswap.com/developer-guide/aggregator-api/contracts.md, accessed 2026-08-05), which is the exact inverse of OKX F14, where the settlement address is deliberately not a constant. The vocabulary expresses neither policy and so cannot distinguish a settlement layer you can pin from one you must ask an API about.

nodes.label: F2 quotes are obtained off-chain from private market makers and settled o
nodes.text: quotes are obtained off-chain from private market makers and settled on-chain only in the cases where they beat the on-chain alternative; callers may exclude those sources by name
nodes.note: DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS, which decomposes KyberSwap as {Ag} alone. The API exposes excludeRFQSources and the documentation states the settle-only-if-better rule, so this is a documented quote class rather than an inference. The quote's firmness is not documented, but no last look is documented either, so unlike Jupiter F7 there is no positive evidence against Rf.

nodes.label: F3 one of the four routed liquidity classes is the operator's own limit-o
nodes.text: one of the four routed liquidity classes is the operator's own limit-order product, so the router is also a venue operator on its own routes
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Ob is considered and NOT asserted: whether the book is on-chain is not established by any source in stage 1, so its mechanism is UNKNOWN. What is unnameable in any case is the routing preference for related liquidity. The corpus's version of this residue names KyberSwap Classic and Elastic, which is factually stale: neither appears anywhere in current documentation.

nodes.label: F4 the user sets a slippage tolerance between 0 and 2000 basis points and
nodes.text: the user sets a slippage tolerance between 0 and 2000 basis points and a deadline, and settlement reverts unless the amount received clears the resulting minimum
nodes.note: RESIDUE, the recurring gap of this category (LiquidMesh F4, Binance Wallet F4). No element names a settlement-enforced output floor on a self-executed swap.

nodes.label: F5 the user grants spending authority either as a standing token allowanc
nodes.text: the user grants spending authority either as a standing token allowance to the router or as a signed permit carried in the build request
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, but the best instance of Au in this lane: a permit carries expiry and nonce and so satisfies more of L17 than the bare approval contracts at LiquidMesh F17 and OKX F13. The allowance alternative still arms X16.

nodes.label: F6 the venue is re-decided on-chain at execution time, per hop, by compar
nodes.text: the venue is re-decided on-chain at execution time, per hop, by comparing candidate pools against their state in that block and switching away from the one named in the calldata
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a direct contradiction of what Ag presumes. Ag presumes the route is the thing being executed; here the route in the signed calldata is a proposal and the settlement contract may overrule it. No element names a settlement-time re-selection of the venue.

nodes.label: F7 that re-selection is aimed at specific adversaries: pools that have be
nodes.text: that re-selection is aimed at specific adversaries: pools that have been sandwiched or front-run in the same block, market makers that have widened their spread, and liquidity withdrawn just in time
nodes.note: RESIDUE. MEV defence implemented as a settlement-time decision rather than as private broadcasting, which is a fifth distinct answer to the same problem in a lane of five (LiquidMesh private relays, Binance Wallet chain-level private RPC, OKX whitelisted broadcast, Jupiter's own validator). No element names any of them.

nodes.label: F8 the user pays no fee for the swap, and the operator's revenue is inste
nodes.text: the user pays no fee for the swap, and the operator's revenue is instead the surplus of tokens above the ESTIMATED output, together with unconsumed dust from partial fills, while the user is protected only to the confirmed MINIMUM
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and where the money is. Nothing in the vocabulary names the gap between estimated output and minimum output as an economic object, so a decomposition of a protocol that advertises a zero fee cannot say how it earns. Fd is rejected: this surplus is captured, not distributed, and it belongs to no claim class. Fee schedule confirming the zero user fee: https://docs.kyberswap.com/getting-started/fee-schedule.md (accessed 2026-08-05).

nodes.label: F9 the operator holds pools, deployed as hooks on third parties' automate
nodes.text: the operator holds pools, deployed as hooks on third parties' automated market makers, whose swaps are restricted in the pool's own code so that only the operator's aggregator may take from them
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the sharpest instance in this whole category of the axis the corpus says is missing. Exclusivity over a venue is not the same obligation as routing to one. Aw is rejected under this lane's standing principle: Aw gates the party seeking the service, whereas this gates the TAKER, and does so to create an economic monopsony rather than to satisfy a compliance rule. Note the aggravating fact: unlike every other gate in this lane, this one IS on-chain and code-enforced, in a Uniswap v4 or PancakeSwap Infinity hook with salt-mined before-swap, after-swap and after-swap-returns-delta flags, and the vocabulary still cannot name it.

nodes.label: F10 for each such trade the aggregator computes the best route with those
nodes.text: for each such trade the aggregator computes the best route with those pools and the best route without them, and treats the difference as the additional value the exclusivity created
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A counterfactual route, computed but never executed, used as the accounting basis for splitting a gain. No element names a counterfactual as an input to a settlement.

nodes.label: F11 an off-chain signer produces a signed fair market price for that singl
nodes.text: an off-chain signer produces a signed fair market price for that single trade, which is carried in the transaction and validated by the hook against the pool's actual output
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Three symbols were considered and all fail. Ex is a data feed with push, pull or medianizer semantics; this is a per-trade, per-route signature solicited by the aggregator for one transaction. At is a reserve or NAV attestation about a balance sheet. Rf is a maker quote offering to fill; this signature offers nothing and only prices the benchmark. Price-improvement benchmarking stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief, and note the consequence for X14: KyberSwap is the ONLY application in this lane whose exclusive market structure comes with a benchmark that is actually named and signed, so X14's second limb is not armed here even though its first limb is armed most strongly of all five.

nodes.label: F12 when the pool can do better than the signed price the taker is given t
nodes.text: when the pool can do better than the signed price the taker is given the signed price and the pool keeps the excess; when it does worse the taker gets the actual output and nothing is kept
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Surplus absorbed by the VENUE rather than won by a searcher, one-sided by construction. Fd names distribution of surplus and is wrong for the capture step; what is captured is foregone arbitrage, not fee revenue.

nodes.label: F13 the captured surplus accrues over seven-day cycles, passes a 48-hour v
nodes.text: the captured surplus accrues over seven-day cycles, passes a 48-hour validation window, and is then distributed weekly in the pair's own tokens, 70 percent to the pool's liquidity providers and 30 percent to the hook's owner, to enrolled pools only and with no staking required
nodes.note: Fd is CANDIDATE-REGISTER and approximate: the object distributed is captured arbitrage, not protocol fee revenue, and one of the two recipients is the operator in its capacity as owner of the exclusivity rather than as a claim holder. Ep is a clean fit for the seven-day cycle plus 48-hour validation window before a distribution becomes claimable; the on-chain accounting is public at https://github.com/KyberNetwork/kyber-exclusive-amm-sc (accessed 2026-08-05). This is the price at which liquidity providers sell a monopsony, and only the payment half of that transaction is expressible.

nodes.label: F14 takers of the operator's limit orders pay a fee keyed to a six-band vo
nodes.text: takers of the operator's limit orders pay a fee keyed to a six-band volatility classification of the token, from 0.01 percent for super-stable pairs to 1 percent for super-high-volatility pairs
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The mechanism prices its own service by the riskiness of the asset. Jupiter F11 prices by the age of the asset. Neither conditioning is expressible, and Fd names distribution rather than levy in both cases.

nodes.label: F15 several fee recipients may be paid on a single trade, each with its ow
nodes.text: several fee recipients may be paid on a single trade, each with its own amount, its own side of the trade and its own receiving address, supplied as parallel lists
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The rent on one user's order is divisible along a chain of intermediaries. Of the four forms this primitive takes in this category, this is the only one that admits more than one beneficiary per trade (compare LiquidMesh F10, OKX F11, Jupiter F13).

nodes.label: F16 the terms a caller is offered depend on the wallet address in the requ
nodes.text: the terms a caller is offered depend on the wallet address in the request, which the documentation states is used to reach exclusive pools and rates
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Different wallets get different prices from the same endpoint. Aw is rejected on the corpus's own reasoning: its DFlow marker says Aw is a binary permission gate while segmentation is a graded pricing input, and is 'clearly the wrong shape'. The corpus expected this gap only at rank 6; it is present at rank 5 as well.

nodes.label: F17 a signed-intent router is deployed for intent-based liquidity withdraw
nodes.text: a signed-intent router is deployed for intent-based liquidity withdrawal, with separate hashing, nonce, accounting and storage contracts and its own hooks
nodes.note: DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS {Ag}, and the weakest element assignment in this spec. In is asserted on a GPL-3.0 public repository whose contract set (router, hasher, nonces, accounting, storage) is the shape of a signed-order system, plus a product-list entry for Smart Exit described as intent-based liquidity withdrawal. THE SOLVER HALF IS UNKNOWN: no source establishes a solver set, an auction, a settlement guarantee or a timeout, so three of L12's four parts are unevidenced. If stage 3 requires L12 to be evidenced part by part, this should degrade to residue; it is carried because the corpus itself carries In at Jupiter on a weaker basis.

nodes.label: F18 a cross-chain swap behind the same brand moves assets between 23 chain
nodes.text: a cross-chain swap behind the same brand moves assets between 23 chains, including to and from non-EVM domains, at fees that vary by corridor
nodes.note: Xf IS DISCHARGED BY DELEGATION to the bridges routed across, exactly as at OKX F17, and KyberSwap supplies neither Xm nor a named custodian. Stage 3 will therefore see Xf without Xm; that verdict records the vocabulary's missing composition operator, not a defect in KyberSwap. Corridor pricing (0.05 to 0.25 percent EVM to EVM, 0.25 percent for Bitcoin) is itself unnameable.

nodes.label: F19 the pool simulators that the route search runs on are published for al
nodes.text: the pool simulators that the route search runs on are published for all 129 liquidity sources, and third-party venue teams add their own venues to the router by pull request
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The venue set is maintained as an open commons by the venues themselves, which is a governance and supply arrangement with no symbol, and which makes this the only application in the lane whose route-construction substance is inspectable. Two cautions for a later stage: this repository and the aggregation router carry NO licence file at all, and public visibility is not a grant; and the deployed router is V2 while the public router repository contains a V3, so the published source does NOT correspond to what is deployed.

nodes.label: F20 the operator's commercial asset is the venue rather than the user: it
nodes.text: the operator's commercial asset is the venue rather than the user: it charges its users nothing, buys exclusivity over pools it did not build, pays the liquidity providers 70 percent of the arbitrage that exclusivity captures, and takes its own revenue from surplus at settlement
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the central one. Order-flow ownership stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS: the corpus claims KyberSwap decomposes identically to LiquidMesh. It does not. LiquidMesh owns no venue and no user, publishes nothing, hands the fee lever to whoever owns the user, and earns by selling latency and backrunning its own flow; KyberSwap owns exclusive venues in which it is the sole permitted taker, publishes its simulators, and earns from positive slippage. Their economic positions are opposites and they collide on Ag only because Ag names route construction and stops. Note also that the corpus was right about the missing axis but aimed one short: the sharpest counterexample is about who owns the VENUE, not who owns the order.

nodes.label: LiquidMesh
F1 a route across several venues on one chain is constructed for a caller
nodes.text: a route across several venues on one chain is constructed for a caller who named no venue; the caller may only supply an include or exclude list of DEXs and receives back a routePlans array of paths and per-DEX allocations

nodes.label: F2 the route is computed off-chain on the operator's own servers and hand
nodes.text: the route is computed off-chain on the operator's own servers and handed to the caller as pre-built calldata; no route search, quote or comparison of alternatives occurs on-chain and none is recorded
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Ag reads as an on-chain route-construction mechanism. Here the mechanism is a private server and a latency figure: the router contract executes a decision it did not make and cannot check. Nothing in the 58 distinguishes 'the protocol computes a route' from 'a vendor computes a route and the chain executes it'. There is no repository and the BSC implementation is unverified, so the substance is unfalsifiable from outside.

nodes.label: F3 the party that authored the route neither settles the trade nor bears
nodes.text: the party that authored the route neither settles the trade nor bears price risk: the user signs and broadcasts an ordinary chain-native transaction and any adverse move between quote and inclusion is the user's
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a deliberate null. In, Rf and Ba each presume a counterparty distinct from the signer; none is present. This absence is a fact about LiquidMesh rather than a failure of the vocabulary, and it is recorded so stage 3 does not read the thin decomposition as a gap in the tables.

nodes.label: F4 settlement reverts unless the amount received meets a minimum return f
nodes.text: settlement reverts unless the amount received meets a minimum return fixed in the signed calldata
nodes.note: RESIDUE. In is the nearest and is rejected: L12 requires signed constraints plus a settlement verifier plus a solver or fallback plus a timeout, and here the signer is the executor, so two of the four parts are vacuous. No element names a settlement-enforced output floor on a self-executed swap. This obligation recurs in all five applications of this category and is the single most common residue in it.

nodes.label: F5 a quote is refused outright when the computed price impact exceeds the
nodes.text: a quote is refused outright when the computed price impact exceeds the operator's threshold, returning error 40106 rather than a worse price
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A pre-trade refusal to serve on an execution-quality ground. Aw gates identity, not the quality of the trade being requested.

nodes.label: F6 the signed transaction may be handed back to the operator for broadcas
nodes.text: the signed transaction may be handed back to the operator for broadcast through private channels rather than the public mempool, at one of two privacy grades on EVM (public, private) or three on Solana (off, reduced, secure)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No element in the 58 names a transaction's path to inclusion, and none names a graded privacy level over that path. This is one of the two things LiquidMesh actually sells.

nodes.label: F7 the builders and validators that receive the flow are forbidden by agr
nodes.text: the builders and validators that receive the flow are forbidden by agreement from auctioning the user's transaction, and the flow is not disclosed to third-party searchers
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Order-flow ownership expressed as a negative covenant rather than as a sale. The operator holds a right over the flow it constructs and exercises it by forbidding downstream resale. The vocabulary has four symbols for how an order is matched and none for who holds it or what they may do with it.

nodes.label: F8 the operator extracts MEV by backrunning the very transactions it buil
nodes.text: the operator extracts MEV by backrunning the very transactions it built, and returns the majority of the proceeds to the trader; on Solana it instead buys priority through staked-validator and Jito paths and returns a portion of the saved tips
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Simultaneously extraction and protection, by the same party, on the same order. No element names either half. No percentage or formula is published, so the size of the rebate is UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F9 the guarantee sold is inclusion rather than price: quote latency, quot
nodes.text: the guarantee sold is inclusion rather than price: quote latency, quote freshness for newly created tokens, landing rate and uptime are the published product properties
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Every symbol in the 58 presumes inclusion and therefore cannot express reliability of inclusion as the thing being bought.

nodes.label: F10 a commission in basis points, taken from either the input or the outpu
nodes.text: a commission in basis points, taken from either the input or the output token at the caller's election, is charged on the trade and paid to the integrating wallet; the protocol defines the lever and collects nothing itself
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Fd is the nearest and is rejected: Fd names distribution of a protocol's own surplus or fees, whereas this is a fee the protocol defines, does not collect and does not distribute, so that whoever owns the user may tax them. Selling the monetization right rather than exercising it has no symbol. The mechanism is a named API parameter, not an abstraction.

nodes.label: F11 the only benchmark offered against the returned route is the operator'
nodes.text: the only benchmark offered against the returned route is the operator's own midPrice and priceImpactPct in the same response; no external reference price, no price-improvement measurement and no record of the alternatives considered is published
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Price-improvement benchmarking, stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. The benchmark and the thing benchmarked are produced by the same party in the same response. X14 concerns an exclusive market structure plus a price-improvement claim with no named benchmark; the second limb holds here, the first does not, because LiquidMesh owns no venue.

nodes.label: F12 no party other than the user may fill a LiquidMesh order: there is no
nodes.text: no party other than the user may fill a LiquidMesh order: there is no solver set, no auction, no RFQ tier, no maker and no filler of any kind
nodes.note: RESIDUE, recorded as a null. Solver eligibility, stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. The vocabulary can no more say 'this system has no filler market' than it can say what a filler market's entry rule is; the absence is invisible to a decomposition, which is why LiquidMesh and KyberSwap collide on Ag.

nodes.label: F13 a request originating from a listed restricted territory, or detected
nodes.text: a request originating from a listed restricted territory, or detected as VPN or proxy masked, is refused a quote with error 42106
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. Aw is an on-chain permission gate over a protocol; this gate is off-chain, applied by the operator at the quote endpoint, and is not enforced by the router contract, which anyone may call directly. Standing principle used throughout this lane: Aw is used where a gate decides who may obtain the service, and is NOT used where a gate decides who may fill someone else's order (see F12, and KyberSwap F10).

nodes.label: F14 trades touching tokenized US equities (bStock) are refused to a second
nodes.text: trades touching tokenized US equities (bStock) are refused to a second and much longer list of 57 further jurisdictions under its own error code 42107
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. Aw carries the refusal but cannot condition it on the instrument class being traded. Securities-style per-instrument geo-gating inside a swap-routing API is residue in everything but the bare refusal.

nodes.label: F15 the end-user address supplied with the request is screened against hac
nodes.text: the end-user address supplied with the request is screened against hack-associated and high-risk address lists before a quote is issued; supplying it became mandatory after a security update
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. Aw gates a holder's permission; this screens a counterparty's transaction history against third-party vendor lists. Same direction, different object.

nodes.label: F16 the token being traded is itself screened for scam and honeypot charac
nodes.text: the token being traded is itself screened for scam and honeypot characteristics before a quote is issued
nodes.note: RESIDUE. An asset-quality gate. Aw gates parties, not assets, and no other symbol names a protocol-assigned risk classification of the traded token as a precondition of service. Jupiter F16 is the same gap in a different form.

nodes.label: F17 the user grants token allowance to a standing approval contract that i
nodes.text: the user grants token allowance to a standing approval contract that is separate from the router, so the allowance outlives the trade it was granted for
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. Au is a delegated execution scope and L17 requires bounded scope, revocation, expiry and nonce or domain separation; an ERC-20 allowance to a router-owned approval contract has revocation only. Arms X16 (unbounded delegated authority or unlimited token approvals).

nodes.label: F18 the router deployed on BSC is an upgradeable proxy whose implementatio
nodes.text: the router deployed on BSC is an upgradeable proxy whose implementation the admin may replace, and the implementation it currently points at is not verified
nodes.note: Verified as an OpenZeppelin TransparentUpgradeableProxy, solc 0.8.17, EIP-1967, implementation 0x16F8a2735160E6c4614343959f82a9E1512BD14B which is NOT verified. L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is not discharged: no timelock, guardian or admin identity is published. X9 (Up with immediate single-key control) cannot be cleared because the admin is UNKNOWN. Departure from the corpus, which decomposed LiquidMesh to {Ag} alone.

nodes.label: F19 a bonding-curve launchpad is a first-class venue class, with dedicated
nodes.text: a bonding-curve launchpad is a first-class venue class, with dedicated trade types in the quote API and its own token-manager contract on BSC
nodes.note: RESIDUE by construction of the vocabulary: Bc (bonding-curve issuance) sits in the contested register and is therefore outside the 58. The router transacts against a bonding curve as an ordinary venue and the decomposition cannot say so.

nodes.label: F20 the same service is offered across EVM chains, Solana, Sui and Tron as
nodes.text: the same service is offered across EVM chains, Solana, Sui and Tron as independent per-chain routers; no value crosses a domain and no message is verified between domains
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a deliberate negative for stage 3: Xf and Xm are NOT discharged. Multi-chain presence is not a cross-chain mechanism, and the vocabulary has no way to state chain breadth as a competitive property. 96.9 percent of volume is on one chain (BNB Chain).

nodes.label: OKX DEX
F1 an order is split across several venues by an off-chain algorithm that
nodes.text: an order is split across several venues by an off-chain algorithm that selects on price, slippage and cost, over both automated market makers and private market makers
nodes.note: The splitting algorithm itself is closed; only its inputs and its named venue examples are published.

nodes.label: F2 quotes from private market makers are solicited off-chain and evaluate
nodes.text: quotes from private market makers are solicited off-chain and evaluated against on-chain venue quotes in the same selection
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. Rf asserts a signed maker quote. OKX names PMMs as a quote class but publishes nothing about whether the quote is signed, whether it is firm, or whether the maker retains a last look. Carried, because the quote class is documented; marked, because its binding character is UNKNOWN. Contrast Jupiter F7, where last look is documented and Rf is therefore dropped.

nodes.label: F3 in intent mode the user signs a declaration to swap A for B under stat
nodes.text: in intent mode the user signs a declaration to swap A for B under stated conditions rather than a transaction, the declaration is never exposed to the public mempool, and a settlement contract pays out at least the minimum stated in it or reverts and returns the tokens
nodes.note: DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS, which decomposes OKX as {Ag, Rf}. All four parts of L12 are present: signed constraints, a settlement verifier, a solver set, and a bounded auction window with a fallback to the classic path. The corpus's category claim that the four intent symbols 'do not begin to differentiate anything until rank 6 and below' fails at rank 3.

nodes.label: F4 the signed intent is offered to competing solvers who bid for the righ
nodes.text: the signed intent is offered to competing solvers who bid for the right to fill it in an auction lasting about two seconds, and the best bid wins
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a considered departure from stage 1, which called this 'arguably Ba' on OKX's own phrase 'parallel batch auction'. Ba is batch-auction CLEARING: a uniform price computed over a batch of user orders. Here many solvers bid on ONE order, and no uniform price is computed across a batch of anything. The corpus's own CoW Swap row records the missing object precisely ('the auction being a price DISCOVERY device for a single order rather than a matching device across orders'), so rejecting Ba here is consistent with the corpus's own reading, not a novel one. The vocabulary has no symbol for a solver tournament over a single order.

nodes.label: F5 the bids in that auction are sealed, so no solver can see another's pr
nodes.text: the bids in that auction are sealed, so no solver can see another's price before committing
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Sb is shielded-balance state and does not name bid privacy in an auction; nothing else comes near. Whether bids are sealed determines the auction's equilibrium and the decomposition cannot record it.

nodes.label: F6 only solvers on an operator-maintained allowlist may fill an intent, s
nodes.text: only solvers on an operator-maintained allowlist may fill an intent, subject to onboarding requirements, performance standards and anti-manipulation controls set by the operator
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Solver eligibility stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. Aw was considered and is rejected under this lane's standing principle: Aw is used for gates on the party seeking the service and never for gates on who may fill someone else's order. The corpus already treats this as residue at 1inch ('no element for resolver whitelisting/staking as a barrier to solver entry'), so the reading is the corpus's own.

nodes.label: F7 solvers operated by or affiliated with the operator compete in the ope
nodes.text: solvers operated by or affiliated with the operator compete in the operator's own auction for the operator's own order flow, and the operator publishes a policy saying so
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No symbol can express 'the operator is also a bidder', and none names a self-declared conflict as part of the mechanism. Published 2026-04-30, modified 2026-05-29; it is the single most useful primary document in this category because it is the only place any operator here states in writing what it does with the flow it controls. The disclaimers it makes (no preferential routing to affiliates, to the operator's venture portfolio, to protocols on the chain it owns, or to counterparties with revenue-sharing agreements) are themselves evidence that those relationships exist.

nodes.label: F8 the winning solver pays the settlement gas, so the user's cost of exec
nodes.text: the winning solver pays the settlement gas, so the user's cost of execution in intent mode is zero gas
nodes.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Gs). The corpus already uses Gs for exactly this shape at 1inch Fusion ('gasless swaps where the resolver pays settlement gas'). L21 (Gs implies Au plus metering plus fee settlement) is NOT discharged: the solver absorbs the cost as a cost of winning, with no delegated scope and no metering.

nodes.label: F9 the system, not the user, decides which of two incompatible execution
nodes.text: the system, not the user, decides which of two incompatible execution regimes runs, on trade size, token classification and a user-chosen speed mode, and which party bears price risk between signature and fill changes with that decision
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the sharpest structural gap in this application. In and Ag name the two regimes; nothing names the dispatcher that chooses between them, and nothing can express that the location of price risk is a function of that choice. In classic mode the user bears it; in intent mode the winning solver bears it between its bid and its settlement.

nodes.label: F10 the operator's own route may be presented as the default selection or
nodes.text: the operator's own route may be presented as the default selection or visually emphasised in the interface, including where its quoted received amount is not the highest available
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the purest case in the category of a mechanism the 58 cannot see, because it is not on-chain at all and yet determines where the majority of trades go. Price-improvement benchmarking stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief: the displayed route and the best route are conceded to be different objects. X14's second limb holds in the strongest available form, since the operator itself concedes the displayed route may not be best.

nodes.label: F11 a referrer commission is read out of the last words of the settlement
nodes.text: a referrer commission is read out of the last words of the settlement calldata behind magic flags, capped by the router at 3 percent (10 percent on Solana), charged on one side of the trade only, deducted before execution, and paid to the integrator rather than to the operator
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Fd is the nearest and is rejected: Fd names distribution of a protocol's own surplus or fees, whereas this is a third party's cut of someone else's user, compiled into the settlement layer and capped by it (CommissionLib.sol: commissionRateLimit = 300, event CommissionRecord(uint256, address referrerAddress), FROM_TOKEN_COMMISSION / TO_TOKEN_COMMISSION flags). Order-flow monetization enforced on-chain for a beneficiary who is not the protocol has no symbol.

nodes.label: F12 the same routing engine is sold to other order-flow owners, powering s
nodes.text: the same routing engine is sold to other order-flow owners, powering swaps inside a rival wallet, and is supplied as one competing quote engine inside a rival aggregator
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the nesting finding. One Ag runs inside another Ag: OKX is simultaneously its own wallet's aggregator, MetaMask's aggregator (see https://web3.okx.com/learn/okx-dex-api-consensys, accessed 2026-08-05), and a quoting participant inside Jupiter's meta-aggregator. The vocabulary has no composition operator, so a flat corpus row cannot say that one row is a component of another; two members of this category's top eight are components of a third, and any construction treating them as independent will double-count.

nodes.label: F13 the user grants token allowance to a separate approval contract per ch
nodes.text: the user grants token allowance to a separate approval contract per chain, distinct from the router that spends it
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, same reading as LiquidMesh F17. L17's expiry and nonce or domain separation are absent; X16 is armed. Solana and TON require no approval, which the decomposition also cannot express.

nodes.label: F14 the identity of the settlement contract is not a constant: routers may
nodes.text: the identity of the settlement contract is not a constant: routers may be replaced on upgrade and integrators are instructed to use whatever address the API returns rather than hardcoding one
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Up (mutable implementation proxy) was considered and is rejected: the verified BSC deployment 0x6015126d7D23648C2e4466693b8DeaB005ffaba8 is a plain DexRouter and NOT a proxy, so mutability is achieved by deploying a new contract and changing what an off-chain API answers. No element names mutation of a mechanism by redeployment plus a redirect, which is strictly less accountable than Up because there is no on-chain upgrade event to observe.

nodes.label: F15 MEV-protected broadcasting is available only to customers the operator
nodes.text: MEV-protected broadcasting is available only to customers the operator has approved by email application, on four named chains
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and residue in its substance. Aw carries only the gate on who may obtain the service; the object being gated, protection of a transaction's path to inclusion, has no symbol at all. Protection here is a commercial tier, not a property of the mechanism.

nodes.label: F16 a self-hosted routing client is distributed as a closed binary behind
nodes.text: a self-hosted routing client is distributed as a closed binary behind an API key and a whitelist form, computes routes locally from streamed pool state, and will additionally search for the most profitable round-trip across a set of intermediate tokens
nodes.note: RESIDUE, twice. First, the canonical routing artifact is a Docker image with no source and no license (the repository contains a Dockerfile, a compose file and docs, and no code), which no element can express. Second, cyclic arbitrage routing means the router is also a searcher, sold as such; the vocabulary has no way to say that the thing routing your order is also hunting round-trips.

nodes.label: F17 a cross-chain swap behind the same interface moves the user's asset be
nodes.text: a cross-chain swap behind the same interface moves the user's asset between domains by routing across third-party bridges the operator selects
nodes.note: Xf IS DISCHARGED BY DELEGATION, not by OKX's own contracts: the routed-to bridge moves the value, and OKX supplies neither Xm nor a named custodian. Because the vocabulary has no composition operator, a construction cannot say 'Xf present by delegation', so stage 3 will see Xf without Xm and without L8's alternative. That verdict is the nesting finding restated by the checker, not a defect in OKX. The corpus residue 'no element for cross-chain swap routing as a distinct product' stands and is confirmed.

nodes.label: F18 the splitting algorithm, the private-market-maker set, the solver allo
nodes.text: the splitting algorithm, the private-market-maker set, the solver allowlist and the auction's conduct are all unverifiable from outside, and the canonical settlement repository the operator once published has been withdrawn
nodes.note: RESIDUE. github.com/okx/WEB3-DEX-OPENSOURCE now returns HTTP 404 from the GitHub API and does not appear in the okx organisation listing; the code survives only in forks, of which the cited one carries Apache-2.0 at the root and SPDX MIT on individual files. No element expresses the evidentiary status of a mechanism, and with no versioned source of record there is nothing to diff a rotating deployment against.

nodes.label: F19 the operator stands on both sides of the order-flow market at once: it
nodes.text: the operator stands on both sides of the order-flow market at once: it owns users through an exchange and a wallet, owns a chain, sells its engine to rivals who own users, sells the right to fill through an auction it also bids in, and hands the fee lever to integrators
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the central one. Order-flow ownership stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS: the corpus claims OKX DEX decomposes identically to Binance Wallet. It does not. Binance Wallet is a pure demand-side owner with no sell-side product, no solver set, no published policy and no API; OKX is a supply-side vendor that also owns demand. Their economic positions are different in kind, and the corpus's identity claim {Ag, Rf} = {Ag, Rf} is an artefact of a vocabulary that names route construction and stops.

nodes.label: 09-rwa
BlackRock BUIDL (via Securitize)
F1 a qualified purchaser subscribes and receives a share in a British Vir
nodes.text: a qualified purchaser subscribes and receives a share in a British Virgin Islands limited company, recorded on chain as a six-decimal token
nodes.note: Sworn on Form D/A filed 2026-07-27: BVI, incorporated 2023, exemptions 06c plus 3C plus 3C.7, is40Act false, placement agent Securitize Markets LLC (CRD 283256), cumulative totalAmountSold $5,135,523,412 across 28 recorded investors, first sale 2024-03-04. Live on Ethereum: Class A 0x7712c34205737192402172409a8f7ccef8aa2aec, name BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund, totalSupply 224,848,357.43, walletCount 59; Class I 0x6a9da2d710bb9b700acde7cb81f10f1ff8c89041, supply 964,123,531.86. THREE FIGURES, THREE MEANINGS: totalIssued on Class A is 2,254,889,229.88 (cumulative gross issuance), and no single number is BUIDL's AUM without naming which chain, which class, and whether the figure is outstanding or cumulative.

nodes.label: F2 the fund targets a constant one-dollar share value with no price feed
nodes.text: the fund targets a constant one-dollar share value with no price feed of any kind on chain, warns in the same sentence that it may fail, and disclaims any sponsor obligation to support it
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and it is worth stating positively rather than as an omission. Ex is CORRECTLY ABSENT: there is no oracle, no price contract, no latestRoundData, and BUIDL is the only member of the five with no price source of any kind, because the unit is assumed at par and yield arrives as supply. The disclaimer is verbatim: you could lose money by investing in the Fund; although the Fund seeks to preserve the value of your investment at $1.00 per share, it cannot guarantee it will do so; the Fund's sponsor has no legal obligation to provide financial support to the Fund. Nothing in the vocabulary names a targeted-but-unguaranteed par value, which is the entire economic proposition of a money-market fund.

nodes.label: F3 yield is declared off chain against a snapshot of who held the token a
nodes.text: yield is declared off chain against a snapshot of who held the token at three in the afternoon eastern time, and paid the following business day by minting new tokens to them
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Verbatim: dividends are accrued each calendar day to the holder of record at 3:00pm ET, and paid out the following business day in the form of new BUIDL tokens. CORRECTION to the corpus, which records this as monthly; it is DAILY accrual paid next business day. Four symbols were considered and each fails for a stated reason. Not Ix: there is no index and the unit stays at one dollar. Not Rb: balances change by a discrete issuance event, not by a global scaling factor. Not Sh alone: the pro-rata claim per token is constant and what varies is how many tokens you are given. Not Ep: the 3pm instant is a wall-clock snapshot taken by an off-chain administrator, not an on-chain period boundary that gates a transition. A discretionary dividend declared off-chain against a holder-of-record snapshot and settled in kind by minting has no symbol.

nodes.label: F4 the token may only move between investors an off-chain onboarding proc
nodes.text: the token may only move between investors an off-chain onboarding process has whitelisted, checked on every transfer by an on-chain compliance service
nodes.note: BUIDL adheres to high KYC/AML standards and only permits token transfers to whitelisted investors. Verified rather than asserted: the deployed contract responds to getDSService(uint256), totalIssued(), walletCount() and isPaused(), and the service IDs returned match the DS Protocol constants TRUST_SERVICE 1, REGISTRY_SERVICE 4, COMPLIANCE_SERVICE 8 read from the interface source. Live services: Trust 0x3a68756d0335e75c909ba1e8fefc1d4832c36c60, Registry 0x0dac900f26de70336f2320f7ccedee70ff6a1a5b, Compliance 0x07a1ebfb9a9a421249ddc71bddb8860cc077e3a9. Every transfer runs preTransferCheck(address,address,uint) against the compliance service, so L16 (transfer-time enforcement) is discharged.

nodes.label: F5 the on-chain ledger is keyed on a legal identity rather than on an add
nodes.text: the on-chain ledger is keyed on a legal identity rather than on an address: wallets are attached to an investor identifier, and the investor carries attributes that expire and that point at an off-chain document
nodes.note: RESIDUE. balanceOfInvestor(string _id), registerInvestor(string,string), addWallet(address,string), setCountry(string,string), and setAttribute(string _id, uint8 _attributeId, uint256 _value, uint256 _expiry, string _proofHash) with constants KYC_APPROVED 1, ACCREDITED 2, QUALIFIED 4, PROFESSIONAL 8. Aw is a bit; this is a subsystem with its own key space, its own time dimension and its own pointer into a legal file. An attribute that EXPIRES means eligibility decays with no actor doing anything. It also means the chain is not a bearer ledger even in form, which is the on-chain half of the register-of-record finding at F10.

nodes.label: F6 the gate tests two distinct legal predicates at once, accredited-inves
nodes.text: the gate tests two distinct legal predicates at once, accredited-investor status under the securities law and qualified-purchaser status under the investment-company law, and the tighter of the two is what caps the fund's investor base
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The Form D's federalExemptionsExclusions are exactly 06c, 3C and 3C.7, and the product page corroborates with Investor Eligibility: Qualified Purchaser. Aw names the gate and never what it is testing for. It cannot distinguish a gate that exists to satisfy a resale restriction from one that exists to preserve a fund's exemption from registration, and THEY FAIL DIFFERENTLY AND THE REMEDIES DIFFER. Regulation S is NOT evidenced and is marked UNKNOWN rather than refuted, because Reg S offerings are not reported on Form D.

nodes.label: F7 the issuer can take tokens from one holder and give them to another, r
nodes.text: the issuer can take tokens from one holder and give them to another, recording a reason string on chain, and can burn them
nodes.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fz), and the only member of the five with a real seize. seize(address _from, address _to, uint256 _value, string _reason), burn(address,uint256,string _reason), issueTokens(address,uint256) and issueTokensCustom with a lock and a _releaseTime, all onlyIssuerOrAbove. RESIDUE INSIDE THE SYMBOL: Fz reads as an emergency lever, and here forced transfer is ROUTINE TRANSFER-AGENT ADMINISTRATION, the on-chain expression of remedies a registrar already has for lost certificates, court orders and escheatment. L28 (named authority, enumerated triggers, appeal path, holder disclosure) is partially discharged only, because the reason string is free text and no trigger list is published. Provenance caveat: these are the PUBLISHED INTERFACES (Solidity 0.4.23) and the deployed implementation records solc 0.8.13, so conformance is established by calling the contract and provenance is not.

nodes.label: F8 an issuer-level role can halt the token entirely
nodes.text: an issuer-level role can halt the token entirely
nodes.note: Live isPaused() returns false on the Class A token (JSON-RPC eth.llamarpc.com and ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, accessed 2026-08-04). Gp names the facility; who holds it is F13.

nodes.label: F9 a holder may redeem for cash on the same business day if the request r
nodes.text: a holder may redeem for cash on the same business day if the request reaches the transfer agent in good order between eight in the morning and three in the afternoon eastern time on a redemption date
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and the corpus marker stands: this is a subscription-document right against a BVI company exercisable on a business-day calendar, not a redemption the contract can honour. There is no on-chain redemption function that pays anything; the on-chain leg is a transfer to the transfer agent's wallet and the cash leg is banking. Ep was considered for the cut-off and REJECTED under the rule applied across this lane, that an off-chain banking calendar is not an on-chain epoch. UNKNOWN: BUIDL's authoritative subscription calendar; the monthly-close table on the platform page carries a Luxembourg-time reference and reads as a shared Securitize template rather than as BUIDL's own terms. The Form D swears a minimum of $100,000 while the product page advertises $5M with $250k subsequent for the Ethereum class; both are primary and both are reported.

nodes.label: F10 the holder must know whether the chain is the register of ownership or
nodes.text: the holder must know whether the chain is the register of ownership or a mirror of a transfer agent's book, and here a redemption completed on chain before the deadline is not a redemption: if the transfer agent has not yet determined the transfer to be final and recorded it in the fund's books, the shares are not redeemed that day and roll to the next redemption date
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and it is the single most important structural fact about BUIDL and the strongest sentence found anywhere in this category. Verbatim: redemptions of Shares effected on the blockchain at or immediately prior to the redemption deadline on a Redemption Date may not be recorded on the Fund's books and records prior to such deadline, including if the Transfer Agent has not yet determined that the transfer of Shares to its wallet is final; in such event, the Shares will not be redeemed on such Redemption Date; rather they will be redeemed on the next Redemption Date. The fund's books and records are a DISTINCT ARTEFACT from the blockchain and are AUTHORITATIVE OVER IT: the chain is an instruction channel the transfer agent reads, and the register is a separate book the transfer agent writes. Sv was considered for the transfer agent's determination and REJECTED: Sv names discretion over how an obligation is serviced or valued, not discretion over WHETHER AN EXECUTED ON-CHAIN TRANSFER EXISTS. Nothing in the 58 can say that a settled state transition may be treated as not having happened.

nodes.label: F11 the registrar of that authoritative book is a distinct SEC-registered
nodes.text: the registrar of that authoritative book is a distinct SEC-registered entity from the broker-dealer that sells the fund, and it outsources its own recordkeeping to a legacy stock transfer agent
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a CORRECTION: the corpus names the wrong company. The SEC-registered transfer agent is Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC, CIK 0001782266, TA file 084-06638, FINS 003641, TA-1/A filed 2025-12-30 from Miami, named Securitize LLC until 2025-04-14, sole member Securitize Inc., CEO Carlos Domingo. Securitize Markets, LLC is the BROKER-DEALER and placement agent (CRD 283256) and appears on the Form D as receiving sales compensation. Two companies, two registrations. Its own TA-1 declares an engaged service company in both directions, Pacific Stock Transfer (084-01145, Las Vegas), so the chain of custody of the authoritative record runs token to Securitize to a legacy Nevada transfer agent. Nothing in the vocabulary reaches one link of that chain, let alone three. The corpus's SUBSTANTIVE claim, that the transfer agent's book is the legal register and the token is a mirror, is confirmed and strengthened; only the entity name was wrong.

nodes.label: F12 the implementation behind the token can be replaced in one call, on a
nodes.text: the implementation behind the token can be replaced in one call, on a hand-rolled proxy that exposes nothing but an owner and a target
