Forced transfer is ABSENT: no forceTransfer, seize or recover exists in any Ondo contract read. What exists instead is an admin burn whose BURNER_ROLE member count is 0 on USDY, 0 on OUSG and 0 on NVDAon on 2026-08-04, a latent unassigned destructive power. Freeze, confiscate-by-burn and forced transfer are three different powers and Fz names one, so L28 (named authority, enumerated triggers, appeal path, holder disclosure) cannot be evaluated against what is actually deployed.

nodes.label: F14 any one of nine signers on a threshold-one multisig can halt USDY tran
nodes.text: any one of nine signers on a threshold-one multisig can halt USDY transfers
nodes.note: Gp names the pause. It does not name the holder, which is the whole content here: PAUSER_ROLE on USDY has 2 members, the 4-of-7 admin Safe and 0x2e55b738f5969eea10fb67e326bee5e2fa15a2cc, which is a Gnosis Safe with threshold 1 of 9 owners. The same hot address holds PAUSER_ROLE on OUSG and EXECUTOR_ROLE plus CANCELLER_ROLE on the Ondo Stocks timelock. This is the cross-lane party-sort gap recorded for 07-bridges, exhibited again on $1.1B of live supply. Role censuses read by eth_call against ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com on 2026-08-04.

nodes.label: F15 the code behind every core token can be replaced, and for the tokens c
nodes.text: the code behind every core token can be replaced, and for the tokens carrying most of the value the replacement is immediate
nodes.note: SCOPE, and Tg is MISLEADING UNQUALIFIED. USDY, rUSDY, USDYc, OUSG and OndoIDRegistry are EIP-1967 proxies upgraded by bare Safes with ZERO delay (4-of-7, 4-of-7, 3-of-5). The only TimelockController 0x3715b2154d2ff4c5b027c7a1f734b53f27bc34f1 has getMinDelay() = 7200 seconds and governs only USDon's ProxyAdmin and the tokenised-equity beacon; its TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE is renounced and its EXECUTOR_ROLE includes the 1-of-9 Safe and a bare EOA. USDY plus OUSG are about 87 per cent of Ondo's yield-asset value, so Tg describes the minority of the system and two hours is a fat-finger guard, not a governance window. Also unnameable: one beacon upgrade replaces the implementation of all 444 Ethereum tokenised-equity tokens at once, and Up carries no notion of fan-out. L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is discharged for USDon and the beacon and is NOT discharged for USDY, OUSG or the registry.

nodes.label: F16 the same claim exists on ten or more chains, moved by burning on one a
nodes.text: the same claim exists on ten or more chains, moved by burning on one and minting on another under a three-attestor quorum in which the issuer is itself an attestor, subject to per-pathway daily caps
nodes.note: Xm OVERSTATED as recorded. The DVN set is Canary DVN, LayerZero Labs DVN and Ondo DVN, so verification is an attestation quorum containing the issuer, not cryptographic verification of source-chain state. The exposure is direct and measurable: the Ethereum OFT adapter 0xa6275720b3fB1Efe3E6EF2b5BF2293148852307D holds MINTER_ROLE on USDY, so bridging literally mints and a quorum failure mints unbacked USDY. Rate limits are 450,000 out and 500,000 in per pathway per day for USDY. STALENESS: any Xm or Xf reasoning that assumed an Ondo-operated settlement chain is void, because Ondo Chain was cancelled on 2026-07-27 and replaced by an off-chain-enclave design (https://ondo.finance/ondo-chain, accessed 2026-08-04).

nodes.label: F17 a named third party attests daily to the assets said to back the token
nodes.text: a named third party attests daily to the assets said to back the tokens, and a named administrator independently computes the fund's net asset value from read-only account access
nodes.note: At is discharged here better than anywhere else in this category, and still incompletely against L27. Named attester: Ankura Trust Company as Verification Agent performing daily attestations, and NAV Consulting as OUSG's fund administrator with read-only account access (https://docs.ondo.finance/qualified-access-products/ousg/trust-and-transparency.md, accessed 2026-08-04). Missing from L27: no stated assurance level, no staleness bound, and no recourse against the attester. Note that the daily attestation covers existence of assets, not composition, and the issuer expressly disclaims responsibility for errors in any determination.

nodes.label: F18 the holder must know who owes them the money and what they can do abou
nodes.text: the holder must know who owes them the money and what they can do about it, and here the issuer's own live documentation names two different obligors for the same token while capping recourse at whatever collateral is recovered
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No element of the 58 names an obligor or a recourse position. The facts: one live page says USDY tokens are issued by Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited; another describes Ondo USDY LLC (Delaware) in the present tense; the product page reports Issuer Domicile: United States (https://ondo.finance/usdy, accessed 2026-08-04). UNKNOWN whether outstanding USDY was novated or whether two vintages have two obligors; EDGAR has no registrant for either entity, so no novation disclosure exists. Recourse is contractually capped: all payments shall only be satisfied by recourse to the sums received or recovered, and purchasers shall have no further recourse to the Issuer, with recourse to directors, officers and employees also excluded. A limited-recourse note and a full-recourse note are different instruments and no symbol distinguishes them. For the tokenised equities, disputes go to arbitration in Zurich under the Swiss Rules and holders are entitled to damages only, expressly not to specific performance.

nodes.label: F19 the holder must know whether the chain is the register of ownership or
nodes.text: the holder must know whether the chain is the register of ownership or a mirror of somebody's book, and across Ondo's three products the answer is three different things
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the largest gap by capital in the project. In no Ondo document does any sentence say the blockchain is the register of record. USDY: the chain controls, proved by an asymmetry in Ondo's own loss language, that a lost token cannot be recovered because it is designed to be a bearer instrument like a stablecoin while a lost Temporary Global Certificate can always be re-downloaded from the account system, and USDYc is described as an onchain bookkeeping representation of that certificate. OUSG: UNKNOWN, and this is the sharpest single gap, because a Delaware LP must keep a partner register, no transfer agent is named for OUSG anywhere, no document says which of the register and the token ledger controls, and the 2026 Form D reports 84 investors against a token freely transferable among all KYC'd parties. Tokenised equities: the chain records who holds and Ondo's KYC book records who may be paid, and the holder will not see their name on the share register for the underlying assets, which are held in the name of the Issuer. That last split, a real transferable claim that is nonetheless unredeemable in the hands of someone who cannot pass diligence, is the single most interesting formal feature of the design and has no name at all.

nodes.label: F20 the holder must know whether their claim is secured, perfected, and ab
nodes.text: the holder must know whether their claim is secured, perfected, and able to survive the issuer's insolvency, and here a first-priority security interest is asserted while the steps that would make it good are either private or absent
nodes.note: RESIDUE. CONFIRMED: Ankura Trust Company is collateral and security agent for USDY and for the tokenised equities; perfection is by control agreements entered with Ankura and each of the banks and custodians, which is the correct route for deposit accounts and securities entitlements; a secondary buyer appoints Ankura as Security Agent by the act of acquiring the token. UNKNOWN: no UCC-1 or financing statement is mentioned in any page fetched or archived; and because Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited is a BVI company, UCC Article 9 would not govern perfection against it in the ordinary way, so the governing law of the security agreement is undetermined. UNDER-MODELLED: enforcement is gated on a tokenholder vote, Ankura acting subject to USDY Tokenholder approval upon acceleration of the loans by the vote of USDY holders, and NOTHING ON-CHAIN IMPLEMENTS THAT VOTE. Bankruptcy remoteness is built by four devices, entity separation with an independent director, a restricted purpose clause, a non-petition covenant of one year plus one day, and limited recourse extended to persons; the last two are the textbook securitisation pair and are completely invisible in the 58 symbols. Bankruptcy remoteness is NOT claimed for OUSG at all.

nodes.label: F21 the holder must know what the reserve holds and who holds it, and here
nodes.text: the holder must know what the reserve holds and who holds it, and here the disclosure is a self-published portfolio page with no independent composition attestation, whose fund product is itself two tokenisation layers away from any Treasury
nodes.note: RESIDUE. At names the attestation, never the assets. Measured from Ondo's own reports on 2026-08-04: USDY outstanding $2.14B against assets $2.16B, a collateralisation ratio of 104.20 per cent, 99.21 per cent US Treasuries with weighted average maturity 173.76 days, 0.11 per cent SVB deposits, and a line item of $14,631,268 of USDY issued under the tokenised-equity programme sitting inside the USDY collateral pool. OUSG on the same date holds $378,543,269 as SWEEP 39.75 per cent, BUIDL 26.75 per cent, BENJI 16.86 per cent, FYOXX 16.23 per cent (https://ondo.finance/ousg, accessed 2026-08-04): every one of the four fund positions is itself a tokenised money-market fund, so an OUSG holder sits two tokenisation layers from the Treasuries. That composition, a claim on a token that is a claim on a token that is a claim on a fund, is the containment relation the intents and yield lanes independently found the carrier cannot state. Custody: the assets sit with unnamed banks and custodians party to the control agreements, and no custodian is named in any Ondo document fetched.

nodes.label: F22 the holder must know who may change what the money is invested in, and
nodes.text: the holder must know who may change what the money is invested in, and here the manager states an unconstrained discretion to change it with no target allocation, no band and no concentration limit disclosed anywhere
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and it converges with the 06-yield and 03-CDP finding that the vocabulary has no delegated allocation mandate. The portfolio may, in the future, include other US Treasury funds and/or direct investments in US Treasuries; WisdomTree is named in the prose and holds zero. No element is sensitive to a party who can change the entire risk profile of the instrument without touching a contract. Sv, which this construction does emit at F3, names discretion over a DETERMINATION (what the price is); it does not reach discretion over an ALLOCATION (what the assets are). That boundary is applied identically across all five specs in this lane.

nodes.label: F23 over-collateralisation is provided as sponsor equity under a contractu
nodes.text: over-collateralisation is provided as sponsor equity under a contractual floor tested at quarter end, and there is no second class of token, no subordinated holder and no distribution waterfall
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a CORRECTION the corpus requires. Tr is REFUTED for Ondo. The 3 per cent is real and citable, a 3 per cent first-loss position such that $100 of USDY is always secured by at least $103, and live collateralisation was 104.20 per cent on 2026-08-03. But it is a contractual minimum of SPONSOR EQUITY, not a junior note class: there is no second class of tokens, no subordinated holder, no distribution waterfall in normal operation, and no on-chain loss-allocation logic. A priority ordering appears only on enforcement, in the phrase less any sums which the Issuer is or may be obligated to pay to any person in priority to such Purchaser. The compliance test is at quarter end, so intra-quarter breach is contemplated. What is actually present is credit support supplied from OUTSIDE the structure by the sponsor, plus an Ondo Foundation guarantee for the tokenised equities, and nothing in the 58 names external credit support.

nodes.label: 10-options
Aevo (Ribbon Finance lineage)
F1 A user buys or writes a European option on the Aevo index from a cross
nodes.text: A user buys or writes a European option on the Aevo index from a cross-margin account, with daily, weekly, monthly and quarterly expiries at 08:00 UTC out to about three months, a $0.01 tick and a per-instrument maximum notional of $10,000,000.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.aevo.xyz/aevo-products/aevo-exchange/trading-on-aevo/options-specifications/eth-options.md (accessed 2026-08-04); 686 live ETH option instruments with per-instrument greeks, price_band 0.7 and max_notional_value 10000000 from GET https://api.aevo.xyz/markets?asset=ETH&instrument_type=OPTION (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: `Op` for the instrument only; F2-F4, F5, F8-F10 and F20 carry the six axes it collapses. Note for stage 3 that this construction departs from the corpus on `Ad` (added, F14), `Rf` (added, F7), `Up`, `Em` and `Sh` (dropped, F18/F19/F6).

nodes.label: F2 Exercise is never elected: the option is European and pays automatical
nodes.text: Exercise is never elected: the option is European and pays automatically at the 08:00 UTC expiry.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (a). Same gap as Derive F2.

nodes.label: F3 The payoff is paid in USDC as a cash difference against the Aevo index
nodes.text: The payoff is paid in USDC as a cash difference against the Aevo index; no underlying is delivered.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (b). Same gap as Derive F3.

nodes.label: F4 The premium is paid in full at execution.
nodes.text: The premium is paid in full at execution.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (d). The one-poled axis again: `Sr` names the streamed alternative, nothing names the upfront case.

nodes.label: F5 Both sides of every option are user accounts; the peer-to-pool layer t
nodes.text: Both sides of every option are user accounts; the peer-to-pool layer that gave the protocol its name — the Ribbon DeFi Options Vaults, which sold weekly options into an auction — was exploited on 2025-12-12 for roughly $2.7M (about 32% of the affected vault) following an oracle upgrade, and has been halted and is being decommissioned with a compensation mechanism, leaving the exchange unaffected.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.aevo.xyz/llms.txt (accessed 2026-08-04 — no options-vault section; under Aevo Strategies the only entry is Aevo Basis Trade) and https://www.theblock.co/post/382461/aevos-legacy-ribbon-dov-vaults-exploited-for-2-7-million-following-oracle-upgrade (press, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE on two counts, axis (c) and beyond it. No element names the underwriting topology. And nothing names an orderly wind-down of a product line with compensation — an act of governance that reassigns already-realised losses between claim classes, which is neither `Sl` (a rule applied to a loss event) nor `Gp` (a pause). The corpus's Ribbon-auction residue about a periodic sealed-bid auction of a bespoke instrument remains a valid vocabulary finding but is no longer a fact about the ranked protocol.

nodes.label: F6 Collateral may be posted in several accepted assets under a cross-marg
nodes.text: Collateral may be posted in several accepted assets under a cross-margin collateral framework, including aeUSD with its own deposit, redemption and composition regime, plus a spot-convert feature.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.aevo.xyz/llms.txt (collateral framework, aeUSD and spot-convert pages, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No element names a collateral eligibility schedule — which assets are accepted, at what haircut, under what cap. `Sh` is dropped from the corpus element set: a cross-margin account balance is not a pro-rata claim on a pool, and stage 1 evidenced no pool-share accounting anywhere in the exchange.

nodes.label: F7 Beside the book, a maker may quote into an RFQ or block-trade rail, an
nodes.text: Beside the book, a maker may quote into an RFQ or block-trade rail, and a separate OTC desk creates bespoke bilateral instruments with a protocol-level unwind endpoint, all settled by the same margin system.
nodes.note: `Rf` added to the corpus element set. RESIDUE inside the obligation: nothing names a bespoke bilateral instrument that a shared margin system nonetheless settles, nor an unwind primitive that reverses one.

nodes.label: F8 Orders are matched by an off-chain order book and checked by an off-ch
nodes.text: Orders are matched by an off-chain order book and checked by an off-chain risk engine before entry, and only once a maker and taker order are matched are they posted to Aevo's smart contracts.
nodes.note: FLAGGED FORCED FIT, and it is worse here than at Derive. `Ob` says ON-CHAIN order book; Aevo's is off-chain, and unlike Derive, Aevo documents no forced withdrawal and no escape hatch, so the trust assumption the symbol erases is strictly stronger. Retained for the same reason as Derive F8 — a double auction is the price-formation mechanism and nothing else in the 58 names it — with the falsified clause carried here.

nodes.label: F9 Under Standard Margin the risk engine evaluates the margin for every p
nodes.text: Under Standard Margin the risk engine evaluates the margin for every position in a portfolio individually rather than holistically, and rejects an order that would breach it.
nodes.note: `Ct` fits, axis (e) first value. THE CORPUS DEMOTED `Ct` TO 'derived'. It is a first-class, order-gating computation performed by a named engine before a trade may enter the book; the demotion is a decomposition artefact and it is one of the two reasons the tables reject Aevo.

nodes.label: F10 Under Portfolio Margin the requirement is Scenario Margin plus Floor M
nodes.text: Under Portfolio Margin the requirement is Scenario Margin plus Floor Margin: fifteen scenarios formed from three spot-movement levels crossed with five IV-shift positions, at maximum spot movement +/-20% and IV shift +50% / -25% in the initial ETH phase, with initial margin 1.25 times maintenance.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (e) second value. `Ct` is a scalar comparison and this is a maximum over a shock grid. It also refutes the corpus's identicalClaimedByLane [[Derive, Aevo]] on its first clause: Aevo runs 15 scenarios of one geometry, Derive 23 of another plus three separate loss families.

nodes.label: F11 Floor Margin = Net Short Exposure(Option) x Unit Floor Margin, at 0.01
nodes.text: Floor Margin = Net Short Exposure(Option) x Unit Floor Margin, at 0.01 ETH per unit in the initial ETH phase, added to the scenario result.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the second clause refuting Derive-equals-Aevo: Aevo floors a max-over-scenarios with a per-unit charge on net short exposure, Derive instead adds contingency terms and an oracle contingency. The vocabulary has no operator for composing a scalar floor with a grid maximum, so it cannot represent either, let alone their difference.

nodes.label: F12 Options and perpetual futures held in the same account share one margi
nodes.text: Options and perpetual futures held in the same account share one margin computation and one collateral pool, and perpetuals pay a funding transfer tethering them to the index.
nodes.note: `Pf` and `Ct` name the pieces. RESIDUE inside the obligation: nothing names the *sharing* — that a loss on one instrument type consumes the margin of another. X8 names the failure mode of the opposite arrangement (shared collateral across nominally isolated markets); there is no way to record cross-margining as a deliberate and disclosed design.

nodes.label: F13 When an account fails AB - OO - MM > 0 the Liquidation Engine seizes i
nodes.text: When an account fails AB - OO - MM > 0 the Liquidation Engine seizes it, cancels its open orders to free collateral, and works the position out with limit orders posted every 2 seconds for a maximum of 30 seconds, charging a liquidation fee on the fills.
nodes.note: `Li` names paid third-party closure; here the closer is the exchange's own engine working the book, which is closer to an operator-run workout than to an open liquidation market, and the symbol cannot tell the two apart.

nodes.label: F14 If the book cannot absorb the seized position, the insurance fund take
nodes.text: If the book cannot absorb the seized position, the insurance fund takes it at a markup, and a liquidation fee is charged on insurance-fund fills as well.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and deliberately so. `Bs` is the nearest and fails on its distinguishing clause: no stake, no staker class and no slashing condition is documented for the fund, and its size is UNKNOWN. This is the same correction stage 1 applied to Derive's Security Module — an unfunded-by-stakers protocol reserve is not slashable first-loss capital — and applying it consistently is what leaves this obligation as residue rather than as a cheap admissibility fix.

nodes.label: F15 If the insurance fund is insufficient, auto-deleveraging closes the po
nodes.text: If the insurance fund is insufficient, auto-deleveraging closes the positions of the most profitable opposing traders at mark price, distributing the loss among them rather than concentrating it on one counterparty.
nodes.note: `Ad` IS ADDED TO THE CORPUS ELEMENT SET AND THIS IS THE SECOND REASON THE TABLES REJECT AEVO. The corpus carries [Ct, Em, Ex, Gp, Li, Ob, Op, Pf, Sh, Up, Xf, Xm] with no `Ad`, despite auto-deleveraging having its own documentation page; L4 (Pf -> Ex + Ct + Li + (Ad|Sl|Bs)) then has an open third term. With `Ad` restored the loss-absorption term closes and the rejection disappears — it was an artefact. What `Ad` does not name: the rank key. Ranking by counterparty profitability makes ADL a levy on being right, a materially different risk from a rank by leverage or by recency.

nodes.label: F16 The three loss-absorption venues escalate in a fixed order — book work
nodes.text: The three loss-absorption venues escalate in a fixed order — book workout, then insurance fund, then auto-deleveraging — and each transfers the position on a different price basis: limit orders, then a markup, then mark price.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. `Li`, `Bs` and `Ad` name pieces; nothing names the ordering, the escalation triggers, or that the price basis changes at each step. This is the loss-absorption topology gap: four protocols in this category close the writer-default channel in four incompatible ways and the vocabulary represents all four as an unordered set of symbols.

nodes.label: F17 The index is built by excluding exchanges that are disconnected, admin
nodes.text: The index is built by excluding exchanges that are disconnected, administratively turned off or emitting detected-invalid data, taking the median of the survivors, discarding any source deviating more than 0.5% from that median, and averaging the remainder unweighted across ten named venues.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. `Ex` says push/pull/medianizer and collapses three distinct decisions: the median is used only as an outlier filter and the output is a mean; venues can be administratively turned off; and the venue list is itself governed. This is the third clause refuting Derive-equals-Aevo — Derive consumes signed SVI/forward/rate feeds from Block Scholes with confidence scores, Aevo builds its own trimmed-mean index from ten CEXs.

nodes.label: F18 The settlement-price observation window at expiry is not documented an
nodes.text: The settlement-price observation window at expiry is not documented anywhere in the exchange's documentation.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.aevo.xyz/llms.txt (full page index, accessed 2026-08-04) and https://docs.aevo.xyz/aevo-products/aevo-exchange/technical-architecture/index-price.md (accessed 2026-08-04) — index construction is specified, terminal fixing is not
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the strongest form of the terminal-fixing gap in this category: at Derive and Rysk the fixing is specified and unnameable; here it is unspecified, and nothing in the vocabulary or its laws would have forced it to be stated. UNKNOWN is recorded rather than guessed.

nodes.label: F19 The exchange runs on its own EVM optimistic rollup whose sequencer is
nodes.text: The exchange runs on its own EVM optimistic rollup whose sequencer is operated with Conduit, posting batches to Ethereum mainnet every hour with a two-hour dispute period and a two-to-three-hour confirmation window; deposits arrive over the Optimism Standard Bridge in about ten minutes.
nodes.note: `Xf` and `Xm` name the bridge and the message verification. RESIDUE inside the obligation: nothing names who orders the transactions, at what cadence, and what an hourly batch with a two-hour dispute period implies for the timeliness of a liquidation on a derivatives ledger — a third-party sequencer is the finality of this exchange. `Up` is dropped from the corpus element set: there is no public repository for the deployed system, so upgradeability is UNKNOWN and the corpus asserts a mechanism it cannot cite. The corpus residue about migrating balances between a rollup and L1 as a primitive distinct from bridging is marked unsupported — current docs describe a standard Optimism-bridge deposit and a 2-3 hour withdrawal.

nodes.label: F20 Mark prices and per-instrument greeks including implied volatility are
nodes.text: Mark prices and per-instrument greeks including implied volatility are computed by the exchange and published through /markets; no pricing model, surface parameterisation or margin-model source is published.
nodes.evidence: GET https://api.aevo.xyz/markets?asset=ETH&instrument_type=OPTION (per-instrument iv and greeks, accessed 2026-08-04); gh api orgs/aevoxyz/repos returns only `audit` and `aevo-sdk` (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (f). Aevo is book-priced for execution and model-priced for margin and mark, and the model is closed. There is no element for a pricing model, and no way to record that the model exists but is unauditable — which for a venue whose risk engine gates order entry off-chain is the central trust fact.

nodes.label: F21 AEVO governs the protocol through AGP proposals and a governance porta
nodes.text: AEVO governs the protocol through AGP proposals and a governance portal, with a DAO treasury administered by a Treasury and Revenues Management Committee and a Growth & Marketing Committee, and a buyback-and-burn system for protocol revenue.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.aevo.xyz/llms.txt (governance, AGP, treasury committee and buyback-and-burn pages, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: `Fd` is candidate register, used for the surplus-allocation rule; the residual claimant is the token holder by burn rather than by distribution, which `Fd` does not distinguish. `Em` is dropped from the corpus element set: no emissions programme is evidenced in current documentation, and buyback-and-burn is its opposite.

nodes.label: Derive (formerly Lyra V2)
F1 A user buys or writes an option on any of ~57 supported currencies at
nodes.text: A user buys or writes an option on any of ~57 supported currencies at any listed strike and expiry up to 400 days, held as a position inside a self-custodial subaccount.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/supported-products-1.md (accessed 2026-08-04); 884 live ETH option instruments and 57 currencies returned by POST https://api.lyra.finance/public/get_instruments and public/get_all_currencies (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: `Op` is used for the instrument only. It names 'strike/expiry/collateralized settlement' and says nothing about exercise style, settlement medium, underwriting topology, premium timing, margin regime or pricing regime; F2, F3, F10, F11, F12/F13 and F7/F8 are the six axes it collapses.

nodes.label: F2 Exercise is never elected: the option is European, cannot be exercised
nodes.text: Exercise is never elected: the option is European, cannot be exercised early, and pays at expiry with no action by the holder.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (a). `Op` presumes an expiry but does not distinguish European from American, from a pre-expiry exercise window (Hegic), or from perpetual (Panoptic). Four protocols in this category occupy four different values of this axis and the vocabulary cannot tell them apart.

nodes.label: F3 The payoff is paid in USDC as a cash difference; no underlying is ever
nodes.text: The payoff is paid in USDC as a cash difference; no underlying is ever delivered.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (b). `Op`'s 'collateralized settlement' clause does not distinguish cash from physical delivery. Rysk delivers the collateral at strike and Derive pays a difference; the two are the same symbol.

nodes.label: F4 The payoff is fixed against a 30-minute, one-minute-sampled TWAP of th
nodes.text: The payoff is fixed against a 30-minute, one-minute-sampled TWAP of the index (SETTLEMENT_TWAP_PERIOD = 30), and over that final window the option's mark migrates linearly from the forward price into the running average.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. `Ex` names the feed that supplies the samples and `Tp` names an on-chain time-weighted price, but `Tp` is warranted only by an on-chain venue (Cp/Cl/St/Wg/Pm/Ob) and this average is taken over a signed external feed, not over a venue's own trades. Neither names a terminal, irrevocable determination procedure with its own convergence schedule. Not forced onto `Tp`.

nodes.label: F5 Five feeds per market — spot, forward, perp, implied volatility and ri
nodes.text: Five feeds per market — spot, forward, perp, implied volatility and risk-free rate — are signed off-chain and submitted on-chain by a named data submitter, and are the protocol's source of truth for margin and mark.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/oracles-1.md (accessed 2026-08-04); src/feeds/{BaseLyraFeed,LyraSpotFeed,LyraForwardFeed,LyraVolFeed,LyraRateFeed,LyraSpotDiffFeed,SFPSpotFeed}.sol at https://github.com/derivexyz/v2-core/tree/96796a61dcb1dc852e25518b00cc1a79fb3caeeb/src/feeds (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: `Ex` fits: a push oracle with signed off-chain data posted on-chain.

nodes.label: F6 Each feed carries a confidence score between 0 and 1, and low confiden
nodes.text: Each feed carries a confidence score between 0 and 1, and low confidence raises the account's initial margin through an Oracle Contingency term.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. `Ex` names a feed as present or absent. Nothing names a scalar quality measure attached to a feed that increases a capital requirement when the feed is doubted — a graded, not binary, trust in truth.

nodes.label: F7 Implied volatility is supplied as a five-parameter SVI curve per expir
nodes.text: Implied volatility is supplied as a five-parameter SVI curve per expiry, with log-moneyness bounded at four standard deviations, total implied volatility capped at 24.0 and total variance at 144.0, produced by Block Scholes and posted on-chain.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (f) first half. There is no element for a pricing model and none for a surface — a function of two arguments (strike, tenor) that is itself an oracle output. The vocabulary spends five symbols (Cp/Wg/St/Cl/Pm) on algebraic variants of a scalar function of a two-asset pool and none on this.

nodes.label: F8 Execution prices are formed by a continuous central limit order book w
nodes.text: Execution prices are formed by a continuous central limit order book with pro-rata allocation above a FIFO floor (pro_rata_fraction 0.8, fifo_min_allocation 10).
nodes.note: FLAGGED FORCED FIT, axis (f) second half. `Ob` says ON-CHAIN order book; Derive's book is 'a centralized limit order book' matched off-chain by the exchange operator, and only matched trades settle on-chain. One of the symbol's two clauses is false. Retained because price formation by a double auction is the mechanism and nothing else in the 58 names it; the falsified clause is carried as F9.

nodes.label: F9 Order entry, matching and ordering are performed by a centralized oper
nodes.text: Order entry, matching and ordering are performed by a centralized operator; only settlement, collateral and liquidation are on-chain, and a user may exit unilaterally through a block-explorer escape hatch if the matching engine or interface fails.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and it is two findings. Nothing names off-chain matching with on-chain settlement — `Ob` silently asserts the opposite — and nothing names a unilateral, operator-independent exit from a system whose ordering is operator-controlled. The escape hatch is what makes F8's misfit tolerable here and its absence is what makes Aevo's worse; the vocabulary cannot see either.

nodes.label: F10 Both sides of every option are user subaccounts matched against each o
nodes.text: Both sides of every option are user subaccounts matched against each other; the protocol is never the counterparty, and an RFQ rail lets a maker return a signed quote on a multi-leg structure with its own fee schedule (cheapest leg free, second and third half price).
nodes.note: `Rf` fits the quote rail and stage 1 confirms it is a first-class parallel rail (private/send_rfq, send_quote, execute_quote, rfq_get_best_quote), not a consequence of `Ob`; the corpus listed it in `elements` but not in `canonicalForm`. RESIDUE within this obligation, axis (c): no element names the underwriting topology itself — that the writer is a peer rather than a pool — nor a per-leg fee schedule used as market-making policy.

nodes.label: F11 The premium is paid in full at execution, as a single transfer, and ne
nodes.text: The premium is paid in full at execution, as a single transfer, and never streams.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (d). The vocabulary covers exactly one pole of this axis: `Sr` names the streamed alternative used at Panoptic, and nothing names the upfront case. An axis with one nameable value is not a distinction the formalism can draw.

nodes.label: F12 A writer may margin each position on its own under Standard Margin, a
nodes.text: A writer may margin each position on its own under Standard Margin, a per-position collateral requirement evaluated continuously against the subaccount's balance.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/portfolio-margin-1.md and https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/pm2.md (accessed 2026-08-04); StandardManager.sol at https://github.com/derivexyz/v2-core/tree/96796a61dcb1dc852e25518b00cc1a79fb3caeeb/src/risk-managers (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); srm 0x28c9ddF9A3B29c2E6a561c1BC520954e5A33de5D in deployments/957/core.json
nodes.note: This is the one genuinely `Ct`-shaped computation in the protocol, and it is what makes Derive the only member of this category the requirement tables accept.

nodes.label: F13 Under Portfolio Margin 2 an account's maintenance margin is portfolio
nodes.text: Under Portfolio Margin 2 an account's maintenance margin is portfolio mark-to-market plus a maxLoss taken as the minimum over four scenario families — 23 joint spot/volatility shocks over spot -18%..+18% in 4.5% steps, a damped tail family at roughly +/-20-25%, two skew scenarios and a forward-basis family at +/-4.5% — plus collateral-haircut, perp, option and oracle contingencies; and a PM account may hold derivatives on only one base asset, under per-asset open-interest caps.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/pm2.md and https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/portfolio-margin-1.md (accessed 2026-08-04); pmrm2 0xc755DAe3fd295A687adf3e192387163f813F0598 live per POST https://api.lyra.finance/public/get_all_currencies (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (e). `Ct` is a scalar comparison; this is a minimum over four families of maxima over shock grids with different geometries, plus a composition rule over the families. Two corpus corrections ride here: the record says '27+ joint spot-and-volatility shock scenarios' where both docs pages say 23 regular scenarios with tail, skew and forward as separate families; and the corpus describes PM1, while the production engine is PMRM_2/PMRM_2_1 with a different formula, a collateral haircut and risk-free discounting that PM1 does not have. Also unnamed: a per-account instrument-scope restriction and an open-interest cap as solvency controls.

nodes.label: F14 When an account falls below maintenance margin a two-stage Dutch aucti
nodes.text: When an account falls below maintenance margin a two-stage Dutch auction opens: solvent bidding at a discount rising linearly from 5% to 30% over 15 minutes, with a per-bidder cap; and if that reaches 100% without clearing, an insolvent auction whose offer rises from portfolio mark-to-market to maintenance margin over 60 minutes and permits 100% of the account.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/liquidations-1.md (accessed 2026-08-04); liquidation/DutchAuction.sol, auction 0x141919f1FA90F99A3fbafFb0b111e4f84AB5aB52 in deployments/957/core.json at https://github.com/derivexyz/v2-core/tree/96796a61dcb1dc852e25518b00cc1a79fb3caeeb (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: `Li` names paid third-party closure and that much is right. It does not name the descending-price schedule (`Da`, contested register, not used), the two-stage escalation, or the change of price basis between the stages.

nodes.label: F15 If the auction leaves the account short, the Security Module pays the
nodes.text: If the auction leaves the account short, the Security Module pays the deficit from an owner-funded subaccount that a whitelisted set of modules may draw on.
nodes.evidence: src/SecurityModule.sol and securityModule 0x8dC92fB0e1C1F1Def6e424E50aaA66dbB124eb54 in deployments/957/core.json at https://github.com/derivexyz/v2-core/tree/96796a61dcb1dc852e25518b00cc1a79fb3caeeb (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/liquidations-1.md and https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/staking-rewards-program.md (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a STAGE-1 CORRECTION to the corpus. The corpus discharges this with `Bs` and its acceptance of Derive rests on that symbol. `SecurityModule.sol` is an Ownable2Step contract holding a stable-asset subaccount with an owner-managed isWhitelisted set: there is no stake, no staker and no slashing condition anywhere in it, and the stDRV programme is documented purely as emissions with a 28-day unlock or a 20% instant-exit penalty. `Bs` ('slashable first-loss capital') does not merely overstate the size, it asserts a kind of capital that does not exist here, so this construction drops `Bs` and reports a discretionary owner-funded bailout treasury as unnameable.

nodes.label: F16 If the Security Module cannot cover the deficit, the shortfall is char
nodes.text: If the Security Module cannot cover the deficit, the shortfall is charged to all USDC depositors as a temporary withdrawal fee equal to unpaid insolvent debt / (unpaid insolvent debt + deposited USDC), levied until the deficit clears.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. `Sl` names loss assigned to a claim class and the class — USDC depositors — is right, so with `Li` it discharges the loss-absorption term that `Bs` was carrying. What `Sl` does not carry: the loss is collected as a flow on exits rather than as a haircut on balances, so the levy is escapable by staying and unavoidable by leaving, which inverts the usual incentive to run. Added to the construction; the corpus omitted it.

nodes.label: F17 USDC cash balances accrue interest through the cash asset's interest-r
nodes.text: USDC cash balances accrue interest through the cash asset's interest-rate model, and while the Security Module is short, 100% of interest payments (SM_FEE = 100%) are routed to it until it is whole.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/liquidations-1.md (accessed 2026-08-04); src/assets/CashAsset.sol and src/assets/InterestRateModel.sol, cash 0x57B03E14d409ADC7fAb6CFc44b5886CAD2D5f02b in deployments/957/core.json at https://github.com/derivexyz/v2-core/tree/96796a61dcb1dc852e25518b00cc1a79fb3caeeb (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: `Fd` is candidate register, used for the surplus-routing rule that names the Security Module as residual claimant. The underlying cash market is in substance a pooled lending market (`Pl`: negative cash balances borrow from depositors), but stage 1 did not read InterestRateModel.sol, so `Pl` is not carried — cite or drop.

nodes.label: F17a The same subaccount may hold perpetual futures beside its options, set
nodes.text: The same subaccount may hold perpetual futures beside its options, settled continuously against the index through a funding transfer, and both are margined by one risk manager under one collateral pool.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.derive.xyz/reference/overview and https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/settlements.md (accessed 2026-08-04); src/assets/PerpAsset.sol at https://github.com/derivexyz/v2-core/tree/96796a61dcb1dc852e25518b00cc1a79fb3caeeb/src/assets and the perp contingency factor (0.03 MM / 0.04 IM) in https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/pm2.md (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: `Pf` fits the funding transfer. RESIDUE inside the obligation, shared with Aevo F12: nothing names that one collateral pool secures two instrument types, so a loss on the perp consumes the option's margin. X8 names the failure mode of the opposite arrangement and there is no way to record cross-margining as disclosed design. Note that L4 (Pf -> Ex + Ct + Li + (Ad|Sl|Bs)) is discharged here by `Sl` (F16) rather than by `Bs`, which is what the stage-1 correction to the Security Module leaves standing.

nodes.label: F18 Collateral moves between Ethereum and Derive Chain, an OP-Stack optimi
nodes.text: Collateral moves between Ethereum and Derive Chain, an OP-Stack optimistic rollup, with the L2 side of the protocol deployed as its own contract set.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.derive.xyz/reference/overview (accessed 2026-08-04); src/l2/ and deployments/{901,957}/ at https://github.com/derivexyz/v2-core/tree/96796a61dcb1dc852e25518b00cc1a79fb3caeeb (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)

nodes.label: F19 The PM2 risk manager is deployed behind an upgradeable proxy with a na
nodes.text: The PM2 risk manager is deployed behind an upgradeable proxy with a named proxyAdmin, and the contract set is controlled by the Derive DAO multi-sig with an intention to move to on-chain governance.
nodes.evidence: deployments/957/ETH_2.json recording pmrm2, pmrm2Imp and proxyAdmin 0x6ecce6823743c5F40505dB287bB77190E83b0916, and src/risk-managers/BaseManagerUpgradeable.sol at https://github.com/derivexyz/v2-core/tree/96796a61dcb1dc852e25518b00cc1a79fb3caeeb (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://docs.derive.xyz/docs/how-do-i-know-my-funds-are-safe.md (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: L15 (Up -> Tg | bounded emergency process) is left open: no timelock is documented. X9 ('Up with immediate single-key control') is not asserted armed, because the controller is a multisig — but no delay is evidenced either, so the corpus's blanket armedProhibitions: [] is unsupported rather than confirmed. `Gp` is dropped from the corpus element set: stage 1 found no citation for a pause or guardian mechanism, and invariant 5 is cite-or-drop.

nodes.label: F20 DRV is staked 1:1 for stDRV, which receives roughly 250,000 stDRV per
nodes.text: DRV is staked 1:1 for stDRV, which receives roughly 250,000 stDRV per week of protocol-funded rewards and unlocks after 28 days or immediately at a 20% penalty.
nodes.note: `Em` covers the emission. RESIDUE inside the obligation: nothing names a fixed unbonding cooldown with a priced early-exit penalty — `Wq` names a queue that clears against liquidity, which this is not. `Sh` is dropped from the corpus element set: stDRV is 1:1 rather than pro-rata on a growing pool, and no obligation here is discharged by pro-rata share accounting.

nodes.label: F21 Instruments are listed on a rolling calendar — 2 daily, 3 weekly and 3
nodes.text: Instruments are listed on a rolling calendar — 2 daily, 3 weekly and 3 monthly expiries, auto-replaced on expiry — with strike increments that are a function of the option's delta and time to expiry (ETH 40-60 delta: $25 at under a day rising to $200 beyond 35 days).
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Nothing names a listing process, let alone a state-dependent one: the set of tradeable instruments is a function of the market's own state, so the instrument universe moves as the market moves.

nodes.label: Hegic
F1 A buyer picks one of a fixed catalogue of deployed strategy contracts
nodes.text: A buyer picks one of a fixed catalogue of deployed strategy contracts — an ETH or BTC call struck at 100/110/120/130% of spot, a put at 70/80/90/100%, or a spread, straddle, strangle, strap, strip, inverse butterfly or inverse condor — and a holding period, pays a USDC premium and receives an ERC-721 position.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/Strategies/HegicStrategy.sol and packages/herge/deployments/arbitrum/.addresses.json (about 200 HegicStrategy_* addresses) at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: All mechanism claims here are read from source, not from docs: the public gitbook still documents the 2020-era V1 design (ETH/DAI liquidity pools) two generations behind the deployed Herge system. Dormancy is a first-class fact about this row, not a parenthesis: core commits stopped 2022-12-26, and https://api.llama.fi/overview/options reported $14,842 of 30-day notional and $0 over 24 hours against $8.98M of TVL on 2026-08-04 — capital parked, flow near zero.

nodes.label: F2 The Hegic Operational Treasury is the writer of every position; there
nodes.text: The Hegic Operational Treasury is the writer of every position; there is no counterparty user anywhere in the system.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/OperationalTreasury.sol at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); org repo description 'on-chain peer-to-pool options trading protocol' (gh api orgs/hegic/repos, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (c), and the protocol's defining mechanism. `Pl` is lending. `Cv` is adjudicated claims on pooled premium and Hegic's payoff is automatic and unadjudicated, so `Cv` fails on its distinguishing clause. Confirmed exactly as the corpus states.

nodes.label: F3 At purchase the treasury locks negativePNL — the maximum possible payo
nodes.text: At purchase the treasury locks negativePNL — the maximum possible payoff of that position — out of its USDC and adds the premium to lockedPremium; the reservation is released by unlock at expiry.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/OperationalTreasury.sol (buy, _lockLiquidity, unlock) at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the premise of F4-F6. Pre-locked maximum loss is Hegic's solvency primitive and no element names it. Same shape as Rysk F7 from the opposite side: Rysk escrows the user's maximum loss, Hegic escrows the pool's.

nodes.label: F4 Every write is admitted only if totalLocked + lockedPremium <= totalBa
nodes.text: Every write is admitted only if totalLocked + lockedPremium <= totalBalance() + coverPool.availableForPayment(), checked on the write itself, and refused otherwise.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/OperationalTreasury.sol (the require in _lockLiquidity) at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: DISCHARGE BY CONSTRUCTION for the threshold term. `Ct` is a per-position ratio evaluated continuously over a position's life, and its purpose is to detect a breach after the fact. This is a balance-sheet inequality over the whole book enforced at admission: nothing can breach it later, because a position that would breach it is never written. The tables reject Hegic for want of `Ct`; the empty array is the honest answer and the rejection is a fact about the requirement language, which admits only 'name a satisfying element' and has no way to say 'the obligation cannot arise'.

nodes.label: F5 DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION: there is no margin engine, no health facto
nodes.text: DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION: there is no margin engine, no health factor, no liquidator and no liquidation path for any position on either side.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/{OperationalTreasury.sol,Strategies/HegicStrategy.sol,CoverPool.sol} at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents) — no liquidation, health or auction surface exists in the Herge contract set
nodes.note: DISCHARGE BY CONSTRUCTION. The buyer has no obligation at all once the premium is paid, and the writer's obligation is pre-locked by F3, so `Li` has nothing to do. `Li` is warranted by `Ct` in the tables, so the absence propagates from F4.

nodes.label: F6 The buyer realises the payoff by calling payOff before expiry, which p
nodes.text: The buyer realises the payoff by calling payOff before expiry, which pays the strategy's net P&L in USDC; exercise is permitted only inside exerciseWindowDuration before expiry, and an in-the-money position not claimed in that window pays nothing, its reservation returning to the treasury.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/OperationalTreasury.sol (payOff requires ll.expiration > block.timestamp) and packages/herge/contracts/Strategies/HegicStrategy.sol (isPayoffAvailable requires positionExpiration < block.timestamp + exerciseWindowDuration) at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: RESIDUE on two counts, axes (a) and (b). The exercise style is a window *before* expiry with forfeiture after — neither European nor American, and not one of the two values the corpus's axis offers; the earlier V8888 generation was documented as American and Herge narrowed it. And nothing names the transfer of value from inattentive holders to the pool, which is a real economic term of the instrument. Settlement is cash, a net P&L rather than a delivery, which `Op` also cannot record.

nodes.label: F7 The premium is computed on-chain at purchase by that instrument's own
nodes.text: The premium is computed on-chain at purchase by that instrument's own PriceCalculator: either a single admin-set impliedVolRate scalar, or five admin-set int256 polynomial coefficients over the holding period; strikes are scaled to spot at purchase by a priceCorrectionRate.
nodes.evidence: packages/v8888/contracts/PriceCalculators/IVLPriceCalculator.sol and .../PolynomialPriceCalculator.sol (setImpliedVolRate and setCoefficients, both DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (f), and a corpus correction. There is no element for a pricing model and none for a volatility surface; an administered implied volatility is the degenerate limit of a surface and the vocabulary has neither the general object nor the limit. Where Derive expresses a surface as five SVI parameters per expiry, Hegic expresses it as a directory of 60+ deployed calculator addresses each holding a scalar or a quartic in time. The corpus residue 'premium pricing is a utilization-scaled IV formula' is a V1-era claim: in Herge the pricer takes no utilisation argument (calculateNegativepnlAndPositivepnl, calculateTotalPremium) and utilisation is handled separately by F9.

nodes.label: F8 The reference price for strike setting and payoff is read from a Chain
nodes.text: The reference price for strike setting and payoff is read from a Chainlink aggregator held by each strategy contract.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/Strategies/HegicStrategy.sol (AggregatorV3Interface priceProvider) and packages/herge/deployments/arbitrum/.addresses.json (PriceProviderETH 0x639Fe6ab55C921f74e7fac1ee960C0B6293ba612, PriceProviderBTC 0x6ce185860a4963106506C203335A2910413708e9) at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: `Ex` fits: a pull medianizer feed. Nothing names the terminal fixing, which here is simply whatever the feed returns at the moment the holder calls payOff — a fixing determined by the claimant's own transaction timing, which is a third distinct fixing regime beside Derive's TWAP and Rysk's 08:00 print.

nodes.label: F9 The only control on how much risk the pool may write is a pair of admi
nodes.text: The only control on how much risk the pool may write is a pair of admin-set notional caps — lockedLimit per strategy contract and LimitController.limit() globally — and an admin can stop the pool writing new risk by setting them.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/Strategies/HegicStrategy.sol (lockedLimit, setLimit) and packages/herge/contracts/Strategies/LimitController.sol at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. `Gp` names an emergency guardian or pause and the halt is achievable, but here the emergency stop and the ordinary utilisation control are the same admin-set scalar, so the vocabulary cannot distinguish 'the protocol was paused' from 'the cap was reached'. RESIDUE inside the obligation: no element names a notional cap as a solvency control, and this is the only thing preventing the pool from selling itself insolvent.

nodes.label: F10 When treasury USDC is short of a payout, _replenish draws from the Sta
nodes.text: When treasury USDC is short of a payout, _replenish draws from the Stake & Cover pool, selling staked HEGIC to the treasury at epoch[currentEpoch].changingPrice, a rate the admin sets for the next epoch.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/OperationalTreasury.sol (replenish) and packages/herge/contracts/CoverPool.sol (payOut, setNextEpochChangingPrice, coverToken = HEGIC 0x431402e8b9de9aa016c743880e04e517074d8cec, profitToken = USDC) at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: `Bs` is used on its core clause and the use is deliberate: cover providers are stakers, their capital is first-loss, and it is consumed to pay claims. This is the one place in this category where `Bs` is defensible, and it is the contrast that convicts the corpus's use of `Bs` for Derive's owner-funded Security Module. What `Bs` does not carry, and should: the backstop is denominated in the protocol's own token, entry and exit are epoch-gated, and the price at which it is worth anything is set by the entity it backstops. That is most of X3 ('protocol token as collateral AND oracle market AND backstop') but not all of it — the token is not user collateral and its conversion price is an admin scalar rather than a manipulable market, which is arguably worse than what X3 names and is not what X3 says. The corpus's armedProhibitions: [] is unsupported here.

nodes.label: F11 Cover providers hold a Hegic Herge Stake & Cover ERC-721 representing
nodes.text: Cover providers hold a Hegic Herge Stake & Cover ERC-721 representing a pro-rata claim on the cover pool, may only provide or withdraw within a five-day window at the start of an epoch, epochs run at least seven days, and anyone may close a stale epoch after ninety days.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/CoverPool.sol (windowSize = 5 days, MINIMAL_EPOCH_DURATION = 7 days, fallbackEpochClose) at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: `Ep` is added to the corpus element set, which omitted it: the epoch is a first-class, contract-enforced gate on entry, exit and instrument connection, not a strategy cycle. `Sh` carries the corpus's marker — the claim is pro-rata on a pool whose value depends on unrealised short-option liabilities that are not marked, so the share is a claim on an unenumerable pool.

nodes.label: F12 fixProfit closes an epoch and distributes accumulated USDC to cover pr
nodes.text: fixProfit closes an epoch and distributes accumulated USDC to cover providers, with a settlementFeeShare of 20 taken on premium.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/CoverPool.sol (fixProfit), packages/herge/contracts/ProfitDistributor.sol and packages/v8888/contracts/PriceCalculators/IVLPriceCalculator.sol (settlementFeeShare = 20) at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: `Fd` is candidate register, used for the surplus-allocation rule naming cover providers as residual claimant. The distribution is an admin transaction (fixProfit is role-gated), which `Fd` does not record.

nodes.label: F13 A new instrument comes into existence by deploying a strategy contract
nodes.text: A new instrument comes into existence by deploying a strategy contract and connecting it through addStrategy / connectStrategy, delayed by one or two cover-pool epochs; there is no expiry calendar and no strike grid, only a directory of about 200 strategy addresses and 60+ calculator addresses.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/OperationalTreasury.sol (addStrategy, connectStrategy with epoch delay) and packages/herge/deployments/arbitrum/.addresses.json at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: `Ep` discharges only the delay. RESIDUE: nothing names a listing process, and 'listing is contract deployment' is the third of five mutually incompatible listing regimes in this category (rolling delta-dependent calendar at Derive, fixed calendar at Aevo, deployment here, continuous taker-specified at Rysk, permissionless factory at Panoptic).

nodes.label: F14 Composed payoffs — straddles, strangles, straps, strips, spreads, inve
nodes.text: Composed payoffs — straddles, strangles, straps, strips, spreads, inverse butterflies and inverse condors — are each their own deployed contract with its own pricer and its own limit, rather than compositions a user assembles from legs.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/Strategies/ (14 payoff contracts) and packages/herge/deployments/arbitrum/.addresses.json at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No element names a composed payoff as a first-class instrument. The formalism's only composition operator is the union of element sets between protocols, which cannot express composition *within* one symbol's instrument space.

nodes.label: F15 DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can withdraw an arbitrary amount from the Operation
nodes.text: DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can withdraw an arbitrary amount from the Operational Treasury to an arbitrary address, set the implied-volatility scalar and the polynomial coefficients, set period limits and the benchmark, set the next epoch's conversion price, set the payoff pool and close epochs — with no timelock in the code read, and against plain non-proxy contracts.
nodes.evidence: packages/herge/contracts/OperationalTreasury.sol (withdraw(address,uint256), setBenchmark, setPeriodLimits, replenish) and packages/herge/contracts/CoverPool.sol (setNextEpochChangingPrice, setWindowSize, setPayoffPool, fixProfit), all OpenZeppelin AccessControl, at https://github.com/hegic/contracts/tree/54833086acc17d2a2bf90229040c456f2fda2624 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a corpus correction. `Up` is dropped from the corpus element set: the Herge contracts are plain and immutable with immutable constructor arguments — no proxy, no initializer, no implementation slot — and mutability is achieved by role-gated setter and by deploying and connecting new strategy contracts, which no element names. `Tg` requires a delay and none appears. X9 ('Up with immediate single-key control') is the right shape for an untimelocked admin withdraw, but X9's own text presumes `Up`, so the prohibition cannot fire on a protocol that achieves the same mutability without a proxy — a gap in the prohibition, not in the protocol. Who holds DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on the live Arbitrum deployment is UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: Panoptic V2
F1 Anyone deposits token0 and/or token1 into the pool's two ERC-4626 Coll
nodes.text: Anyone deposits token0 and/or token1 into the pool's two ERC-4626 CollateralTracker vaults and becomes a Panoptic Liquidity Provider holding a pro-rata claim, whose capital is lent to option sellers.
nodes.evidence: https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core#readme (CollateralTracker, ERC-4626, five actor roles) at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api readme); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/contracts/smart-contracts-overview (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: `Pl` carries the corpus's marker: the pool lends *positions* into Uniswap rather than fungible assets to a borrower who wants leverage. Also relevant to L2's exit-liquidity clause, discharged here by `Sl` (F17).

nodes.label: F2 Each CollateralTracker maintains its own market state including a glob
nodes.text: Each CollateralTracker maintains its own market state including a global borrow index, so a lender's claim accrues compound interest without a transfer.
nodes.evidence: contracts/types/MarketState.sol and https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core#readme (CollateralTracker: 'its own market state including a global borrow index for compound interest calculations') at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api)
nodes.note: `Ix` is added to the corpus element set, which carried only `Sh`. Index-based accrual and pro-rata shares coexist here and the corpus recorded one of them.

nodes.label: F3 An option seller borrows pooled liquidity and deploys it into a concen
nodes.text: An option seller borrows pooled liquidity and deploys it into a concentrated Uniswap V3 or V4 range; an option buyer borrows that same chunk back out of Uniswap and holds the underlying tokens, and it is the removal of the liquidity that creates the option.
nodes.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ and https://panoptic.xyz/docs/product/streamia (accessed 2026-08-04); contracts/SemiFungiblePositionManagerV3.sol and contracts/SemiFungiblePositionManagerV4.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: RESIDUE inside the obligation. `Cl` names range positions and `Pl` names the shared credit pool, but nothing names lending an LP position as the underwriting primitive, nor the SFPM's ability to mint *negative* liquidity — burning Uniswap liquidity as a position is what manufactures a long option, and no element anticipates a composition of `Cl` and `Pl` in which the composition is the instrument.

nodes.label: F4 A position has no strike and no expiry: it is a tick range, up to four
nodes.text: A position has no strike and no expiry: it is a tick range, up to four legs, encoded in one ERC-1155 tokenId, and it never expires and is never exercised at a price.
nodes.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ (accessed 2026-08-04) — 'Panoptions are perpetual and never expire'; contracts/tokens/ERC1155Minimal.sol and contracts/types/LiquidityChunk.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (a). `Op` names 'strike/expiry/collateralized settlement' and two of the three clauses are false. Stronger than the corpus recorded: it is not that the strike takes an unusual value, it is that the strike parameter has a different *type* — an interval of ticks rather than a price — so any formalism that quantifies over strikes cannot quantify over these.

nodes.label: F4a A buyer's position pays like a long option and a seller's like a short
nodes.text: A buyer's position pays like a long option and a seller's like a short one — the removed liquidity's payoff is convex in the price of the underlying pair, which is why the protocol calls them options and why they are collateralised as such.
nodes.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ and https://panoptic.xyz/docs/product/streamia (accessed 2026-08-04); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/panoptic-protocol/liquidations (Buying Power Requirement = notionalSize x (100% - S/K), accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: FLAGGED FORCED FIT, carried for the same reason the corpus carried it: the instrument is unambiguously an option economically and the vocabulary offers no alternative, while F4 and F5 falsify two of the symbol's three definitional clauses. RESIDUE inside the obligation: no element records that the payoff is *synthesised* from an AMM invariant — the LP payoff is a short-straddle-shaped function of `Cp` — rather than declared as a contract term.

nodes.label: F5 The payoff is realised continuously as the underlying range position's
nodes.text: The payoff is realised continuously as the underlying range position's composition changes with price; closing a position burns it and returns tokens, and there is no terminal fixing to determine.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (b). Neither cash nor physical settlement as the axis means them — a third value the corpus's binary does not have, and the one case in this category where terminal settlement-price determination is not merely unnameable but inapplicable.

nodes.label: F6 The buyer pays no upfront premium and instead owes streamia, a per-blo
nodes.text: The buyer pays no upfront premium and instead owes streamia, a per-block stream to the seller that accrues only while spot is inside the position's range.
nodes.note: `Sr` names the accrual, axis (d) second value. It does not name that the stream IS the premium — that this accrual discharges the consideration for an option — which is why the corpus flagged it. Negative accumulated streamia is itself a liquidation trigger.

nodes.label: F7 The rate of streamia is the Uniswap swap fee the removed liquidity wou
nodes.text: The rate of streamia is the Uniswap swap fee the removed liquidity would have generated, multiplied by a spread multiplier that grows with how much of that specific chunk has been removed (VEGOID = 8, nu = 1/VEGOID).
nodes.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/product/streamia (accessed 2026-08-04); VEGOID = 8 in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (f), and a fourth value the corpus's axis does not enumerate. The premium is not modelled, quoted or matched — it is *generated* by realised trading activity in another protocol and then scaled by local utilisation. Beside model-priced, book-priced and quote-priced there is realised-AMM-fee-priced, and no element names any of the four.

nodes.label: F8 Sellers pay interest to PLPs on the liquidity they borrow, at a rate p
nodes.text: Sellers pay interest to PLPs on the liquidity they borrow, at a rate produced by a PID controller with a persistent rate-at-target bounded between 0.001 and 2.0 ether per 365 days and initialised at 0.04.
nodes.evidence: MIN_RATE_AT_TARGET, MAX_RATE_AT_TARGET and INITIAL_RATE_AT_TARGET in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/blog/panoptic-v2-is-coming (V1 deposit-fee model replaced by an interest-rate lending model, accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: `Pl` implies a rate exists. RESIDUE inside the obligation: nothing names a controller with memory — a rate that is a state variable moving between firings rather than a function of current utilisation. The corpus record predates this change entirely and does not mention interest at all.

nodes.label: F9 The counterparty to a buyer is whoever's liquidity chunk was removed,
nodes.text: The counterparty to a buyer is whoever's liquidity chunk was removed, the funding for both sides comes from a shared pool, and the payoff shape is the AMM's own.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (c), and the sharpest case of it: Panoptic is peer-to-peer in exposure, peer-to-pool in funding and AMM-derived in payoff — three of the corpus's axis-(c) values at once. An axis whose values are not mutually exclusive is not a partition, which is a fact about the proposed refinement of `Op` as much as about the current symbol.

nodes.label: F10 The RiskEngine computes a collateral requirement for a whole position
nodes.text: The RiskEngine computes a collateral requirement for a whole position set — spreads, strangles, iron condors and synthetics — and isAccountSolvent compares it to the account's balance, accounting for cross-collateralisation between token0 and token1 through CROSS_BUFFER_0 and CROSS_BUFFER_1.
nodes.evidence: contracts/RiskEngine.sol (2,401 lines; isAccountSolvent, CROSS_BUFFER_0/1) at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 and https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core#readme (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/panoptic-protocol/liquidations (accessed 2026-08-04); RiskEngine.sol in scope at https://code4rena.com/audits/2025-12-panoptic-next-core (19 Dec 2025 - 7 Jan 2026, $56,000 USDC; accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: THE CORPUS DEMOTED `Ct` TO 'derived' AND THIS IS HALF OF WHY THE TABLES REJECT PANOPTIC. The threshold test is a standalone, separately audited 2,401-line contract whose entire purpose is this computation; it is as first-class as a mechanism gets. Promoted to the construction. The documented example — selling an OTM put starts at 20% collateralisation and rises as it moves in the money, Buying Power Requirement = notionalSize x (100% - S/K) — is the requirement `Ct` names.

nodes.label: F11 Collateral requirements scale with pool utilisation up to SATURATED_PO
nodes.text: Collateral requirements scale with pool utilisation up to SATURATED_POOL_UTIL = 9,000,000, and leverage of up to 10x buying and 5x selling holds only under normal conditions and changes in response to pool utilisation.
nodes.evidence: SATURATED_POOL_UTIL and BP_DECREASE_BUFFER in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. `Ct` tests a position against a requirement; nothing names a requirement that is a function of *pool* state, so a seller's margin can deteriorate because other accounts traded. This is a solvency coupling between users that the vocabulary represents as no coupling at all.

nodes.label: F12 The price source is the traded pool itself: an eight-slot sorted ring
nodes.text: The price source is the traded pool itself: an eight-slot sorted ring buffer giving a median tick, four exponential moving averages at 60, 120, 240 and 960 seconds combined as twapEMA = (6*fastEMA + 3*slowEMA + eonsEMA)/10, a clamp on how far a median observation may move, and MAX_TWAP_DELTA_DISPATCH = 513 ticks as the largest permitted gap between the current tick and the TWAP tick at dispatch.
nodes.evidence: EMA_PERIODS = 60 + (120 << 24) + (240 << 48) + (960 << 72), MAX_CLAMP_DELTA, MAX_TWAP_DELTA_DISPATCH = 513 and the median ring buffer in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ ('Panoptic operates oracle-free by design', accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: THE OTHER HALF OF WHY THE TABLES REJECT PANOPTIC. The corpus carries no price-source element at all — no `Ex`, no `Tp` — so L1's first term is open, and 'oracle-free by design' means no *external* feed, not no price source. `Tp` is exactly right for an on-chain time-weighted price and is warranted here by `Cl`. Promoted to the construction; with `Tp` and `Ct` restored the rejection disappears and is shown to be a decomposition artefact. What `Tp` does not name: that the output is an *ensemble* of four values rather than one.

nodes.label: F13 Safe mode is the disjunction of an external-shock test (|currentTick -
nodes.text: Safe mode is the disjunction of an external-shock test (|currentTick - spotEMA| > MAX_TICKS_DELTA), an internal-disagreement test (|spotEMA - fastEMA| > MAX_TICKS_DELTA/2) and a divergence test (|medianTick - slowEMA| > MAX_TICKS_DELTA/2), OR-ed with a guardian-settable lockMode; when it is on, or when the Euclidean deviation of spot, latest and current from the median exceeds MAX_TICKS_DELTA, solvency is tested at all four ticks instead of one.
nodes.evidence: isSafeMode, lockMode and getSolvencyTicks in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); contracts/PanopticGuardian.sol at the same commit; https://panoptic.xyz/docs/contracts/smart-contracts-overview (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. `Gp` names the guardian's lock and nothing else. RESIDUE in two directions: nothing names an automatic, graduated tightening triggered by the price source distrusting its own internal state — this is a circuit breaker whose trigger is self-diagnosis, not an operator's judgement — and nothing names a solvency test that is a *conjunction over an ensemble whose cardinality is a function of the ensemble's own dispersion*. Neither `Ex` nor `Tp` can express a risk test at four prices at once. Numeric values of MAX_TICKS_DELTA, MAX_CLAMP_DELTA and TARGET_POOL_UTIL were not read and are UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F14 A liquidator closes an insolvent account's positions and takes Bonus =
nodes.text: A liquidator closes an insolvent account's positions and takes Bonus = min{Collateral Balance / 2, Collateral Requirement at TWAP - Collateral Balance at TWAP}.
nodes.evidence: https://panoptic.xyz/docs/panoptic-protocol/liquidations (accessed 2026-08-04); getLiquidationBonus in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: `Li` fits. Note that the bonus is computed at the TWAP tick rather than the current tick, so the liquidation incentive is denominated in the same ensemble F12 produces.

nodes.label: F15 A shortfall remaining after liquidation costs and bonus is absorbed fi
nodes.text: A shortfall remaining after liquidation costs and bonus is absorbed first by a haircut on the account's unsettled premia.
nodes.evidence: https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core/blob/d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749/contracts/RiskEngine.sol — liquidation-bonus return docstring, 'the LeftRight-packed collateral remaining after liquidation costs and bonus; negative slots represent protocol loss before premia haircut' (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. `Sl` allocates loss to a claim class and `Tr` declares seniority over a loss event; between them they cannot express 'haircut the unpaid stream first'. The first absorber here is an accrued receivable — income already earned and not yet settled — subordinated ahead of the pool, which is a seniority claim over a flow rather than over a balance.

nodes.label: F16 What remains after the premia haircut is protocol loss borne by the Co
nodes.text: What remains after the premia haircut is protocol loss borne by the CollateralTracker, that is by the PLPs pro rata.
nodes.evidence: contracts/RiskEngine.sol ('negative slots represent protocol loss before premia haircut') at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents), against https://panoptic.xyz/docs/panoptic-protocol/liquidations (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: `Sl` fits and is added to the corpus element set, discharging L1's loss-absorption term alongside `Li` and L2's exit-liquidity clause. It also settles a documentation conflict: the docs say the pool will never incur a loss, the code returns protocol loss as a modelled outcome. The code is the evidence.

nodes.label: F17 A seller may force-exercise a buyer's out-of-range long position to re
nodes.text: A seller may force-exercise a buyer's out-of-range long position to reclaim the liquidity, paying the exercised user a fee that decays exponentially with distance from strike (FORCE_EXERCISE_COST = 30,000 scaled units, floored at ONE_BPS = 1000).
nodes.evidence: exerciseCost, FORCE_EXERCISE_COST = 30_000 and ONE_BPS = 1000 in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Not liquidation — the target is solvent — and not exercise, since the holder does not elect it. Nothing names compulsion without distress: one user closing another's healthy position and compensating them for it.

nodes.label: F18 PanopticFactoryV3 and PanopticFactoryV4 will open an options market on
nodes.text: PanopticFactoryV3 and PanopticFactoryV4 will open an options market on any Uniswap V3 or V4 pool permissionlessly, on any ERC20 pair.
nodes.evidence: contracts/PanopticFactoryV3.sol and contracts/PanopticFactoryV4.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/faq/ (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Listing is factory deployment, so the instrument universe is unbounded and ungoverned — the opposite pole from the governed expiry calendars at Derive and Aevo and equally unnameable. The vocabulary has no symbol for a listing process at any point on that range.

nodes.label: F19 Every user action funnels through dispatch() / dispatchFrom(), which w
nodes.text: Every user action funnels through dispatch() / dispatchFrom(), which will revert when the current tick is further than MAX_TWAP_DELTA_DISPATCH from the TWAP tick.
nodes.evidence: dispatch/dispatchFrom in https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core#readme and MAX_TWAP_DELTA_DISPATCH = 513 in contracts/RiskEngine.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A single entry point that admits or refuses every interaction on a price-agreement condition is neither a pause (`Gp`) nor a threshold test on a position (`Ct`) — it is an admission gate on the whole protocol, conditioned on the price source's internal consistency.

nodes.label: F20 Commissions on positions are split between the protocol, the PLPs and,
nodes.text: Commissions on positions are split between the protocol, the PLPs and, where a builder code is present, the integrator whose interface constructed the call; long positions above a rehypothecation threshold receive credited shares.
nodes.evidence: contracts/Builder.sol at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749 and https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core#readme (commissions, builder codes, rehypothecation threshold) (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api)
nodes.note: `Fd` is candidate register and names the surplus split. It does not name attribution to whoever constructed the calldata, which is the novel part — a fee share that follows the interface rather than the capital or the flow.

nodes.label: F21 Administration is performed by Gnosis-Safe transactions against contra
