nodes.text: Administration is performed by Gnosis-Safe transactions against contracts that the factory deploys as fresh non-proxy instances, with a guardian able to override safe mode and lock or unlock pools.
nodes.evidence: safe-txns-RiskEngine/ and gen_safetx.py at commit d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749, contracts/PanopticGuardian.sol (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents); https://panoptic.xyz/docs/contracts/smart-contracts-overview (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: `Up` is dropped from the corpus element set: stage 1 read no proxy, no initializer and no implementation slot in the V2 contracts, and the corpus asserts `Up` without an evidenced mechanism. Whether any component sits behind a proxy is UNKNOWN. `Tg` requires a delay and none is evidenced, so L15 does not arise because `Up` does not. RESIDUE: multisig administration of immutable, factory-deployed instances is a distinct control regime that neither `Up`, `Tg` nor `Gp` names.

nodes.label: F22 The protocol lends against, and prices with, the same Uniswap pool its
nodes.text: The protocol lends against, and prices with, the same Uniswap pool its instruments are written on, and mitigates the resulting manipulation channel with a median ring buffer, a four-EMA ensemble, a clamp on median movement, the dispatch TWAP-delta bound and safe mode.
nodes.evidence: https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core/blob/d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749/contracts/RiskEngine.sol (median buffer, EMA_PERIODS, MAX_CLAMP_DELTA, MAX_TWAP_DELTA_DISPATCH, isSafeMode) and https://github.com/panoptic-labs/panoptic-v2-core/tree/d65310d6cfbaadb6910fa9446cc59c6541060749/audits (2025-10-panoptic-v2.pdf, NM0701-FINAL_PANOPTIC_V2.pdf, code4rena-panoptic-next-core.md) (accessed 2026-08-04 via gh api contents)
nodes.note: RESIDUE about the prohibition tables rather than the vocabulary. X2 ('Fl + manipulable Cp/Cl price + Pl/Cd') is NOT armed — there is no flash liquidity — yet the failure mode X2 guards against is this protocol's central design problem, and five named mechanisms exist for no other purpose than to mitigate it. A prohibition is armed or it is not; there is no way to record 'the failure mode is present and explicitly defended', so the table scores an unmitigated design and a purpose-built defence identically.

nodes.label: Rysk V12
F1 A user sells an option by choosing asset, target price (strike), expir
nodes.text: A user sells an option by choosing asset, target price (strike), expiry and size; the protocol opens a request for quote to integrated market makers over WebSocket, and the maker returns a signed quote that is executed on-chain on acceptance.
nodes.note: `Rf` is the protocol's defining symbol and the corpus omitted it — its residue entry 'no element for the counterparty side' is a decomposition omission, not a residue. Note also the inversion this obligation records: the *user* is the seller and the market maker is the buyer, which no element expresses. `Dp` is dropped from the corpus element set (see F18) and `Em` is dropped for want of a citation.

nodes.label: F1a The instrument sold is an option with a named strike and a named expir
nodes.text: The instrument sold is an option with a named strike and a named expiry whose settlement is secured by collateral posted at inception, held as an oToken by the buyer.
nodes.note: Rysk is the one member of this category for which all three of `Op`'s clauses — strike, expiry, collateralized settlement — are literally true; at Panoptic two of the three are false and at Hegic the exercise semantics are neither of the styles the symbol implies. It is therefore the cleanest possible instance of the symbol, and the tables still reject it (F8, F10), which localises the failure in the requirement language rather than in `Op`.

nodes.label: F2 Quotes are aggregated over a fixed two-second window with live competi
nodes.text: Quotes are aggregated over a fixed two-second window with live competitiveness feedback to makers, and exactly one winning quote is surfaced and filled.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. `Rf` names a signed maker quote — one quote, no clock, no competition. This is a timed sealed multi-quote round with nonces and validity timestamps resolved to a single winner, i.e. a repeated sealed-bid auction; `Ba` is uniform-price clearing over a batch of fungible flow and is the wrong shape too. Not forced onto either.

nodes.label: F3 Options are European, expire at 08:00 UTC, cannot be exercised early,
nodes.text: Options are European, expire at 08:00 UTC, cannot be exercised early, and cannot be closed, bought back or offset before expiry.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (a). Beyond the exercise-style gap shared with Derive: nothing names a prohibition on closing a position. Locking the seller in until expiry is a material term of the instrument — a secondary market is documented as 'in development' — and it is invisible.

nodes.label: F4 Settlement exchanges the collateral itself at the strike: a cash-secur
nodes.text: Settlement exchanges the collateral itself at the strike: a cash-secured put delivers stablecoins for the underlying at the lower strike; the covered-call side is documented both as cash-settled and as physically settled.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (b). `Op` does not distinguish physical delivery from a cash difference, so the vocabulary cannot even record that Rysk and Derive differ here — nor that the sources conflict. Call settlement is partially UNKNOWN and stage 1 recorded it as such rather than resolving it.

nodes.label: F5 The counterparty is a market maker taking the other side bilaterally;
nodes.text: The counterparty is a market maker taking the other side bilaterally; Rysk Premium adds a curated pool that takes the maker side over the same rail.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (c). No element names the underwriting topology. `Pl` is lending; `Cv` requires adjudicated claims. And Rysk is simultaneously peer-to-peer at the base layer and peer-to-pool one layer up, which the vocabulary must state as a union of element sets rather than as a layering.

nodes.label: F6 The premium is paid in full at execution, in USD, deducted from the ma
nodes.text: The premium is paid in full at execution, in USD, deducted from the maker's pre-deposited balance in the accounting contract and credited to the seller against oTokens.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, axis (d), the same one-poled axis as Derive F11: `Sr` names the streamed alternative and nothing names an upfront premium.

nodes.label: F7 The seller posts the entire maximum payoff at trade time — the underly
nodes.text: The seller posts the entire maximum payoff at trade time — the underlying for a covered call, stablecoins equal to strike x size for a cash-secured put — into a MarginPool where it is locked for the life of the trade, never rehypothecated and never shared with any other position.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.rysk.finance/getting-started/solution-rysk-v12 and https://docs.rysk.finance/getting-started/protocol-and-product/how-it-works.md (accessed 2026-08-04); MarginPool 0x684404F2AEBAD87a6803F13741B1d638Bfe2C671 verified as an exact match on https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x684404F2AEBAD87a6803F13741B1d638Bfe2C671?fields=compilation (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the premise of F8-F10. `Ct` names a threshold on a ratio evaluated over a position's life. This is a single admission condition — full escrow of the maximum payoff — after which the ratio is constant by construction and no test has anything to measure. The vocabulary has no symbol for 'the obligation is pre-funded in full', so a protocol that closes the loss channel looks identical to one that ignored it.

nodes.label: F8 DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION: no maintenance-margin or health test exist
nodes.text: DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION: no maintenance-margin or health test exists or can exist, because no position can ever become under-secured.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.rysk.finance/getting-started/protocol-and-product/how-it-works.md (accessed 2026-08-04) — 'locked in Rysk's settlement layer for the life of the trade and never leaves the contract, with no rehypothecation, no shared portfolio risk, and no unsecured bilateral counterparty credit risk'
nodes.note: DISCHARGE BY CONSTRUCTION, not omission. The requirement tables demand that `Op` be accompanied by `Ct`; here the obligation `Ct` discharges cannot arise, because F7 makes the collateral ratio a constant fixed at 100% of maximum loss. The empty array is the correct answer and the checker will read it as an open term. That reading is a fact about the requirement language — which admits exactly one way to discharge a term, namely naming a satisfying element — and not a fact about Rysk. The corpus's `satisfiesRequirementsAndWarrants: false` for this protocol is a mis-diagnosis of exactly this kind.

nodes.label: F9 DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION: there is no liquidation path, no liquidato
nodes.text: DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION: there is no liquidation path, no liquidator, no auction and no health-driven forced close anywhere in the protocol.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.rysk.finance/getting-started/protocol-and-product/how-it-works.md (accessed 2026-08-04); no liquidation surface appears anywhere in https://docs.rysk.finance/ (page index accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: DISCHARGE BY CONSTRUCTION. `Li` pays third parties to close positions that have become under-secured; by F7 none can. Note the ordering: `Li` is warranted by `Ct` in the tables, so the absence propagates — a vocabulary that cannot say 'closed' also cannot say why the dependent symbol is absent.

nodes.label: F10 DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION: there is no insurance fund, no backstop, n
nodes.text: DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION: there is no insurance fund, no backstop, no socialised loss and no auto-deleveraging, because the protocol has no loss channel for them to absorb.
nodes.note: DISCHARGE BY CONSTRUCTION, and this is the term on which the tables actually reject Rysk. L1 requires (Li|Ad|Sl|Bs) beside `Op`. Every one of those four is a mechanism for handling a shortfall that cannot occur. Carrying any of them to make the construction admissible would be the forced fit the project's standing rule forbids; the rejection is the evidence, and the residue is the explanation.

nodes.label: F11 A maker's quote is only executable if the maker's USDT0 balance alread
nodes.text: A maker's quote is only executable if the maker's USDT0 balance already deposited in the accounting contract covers the premium.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A capital gate on *participation* rather than on a position. `Aw` gates on identity or permission, not on funding; `Ct` gates a position, not an actor's right to quote. This is how Rysk replaces counterparty credit assessment on the buy side.

nodes.label: F12 Prices are taken from Stork and cross-checked against Pyth, and when t
nodes.text: Prices are taken from Stork and cross-checked against Pyth, and when the two disagree beyond a threshold the system halts every process that requires an accurate price, with Stork as the fallback on divergence; Pendle assets are priced from the Pendle API.
nodes.note: `Ex` fits the feed. `Gp` is APPROXIMATE: it names an emergency guardian or pause, and here the trigger is automatic — a two-feed disagreement — rather than a guardian's decision. The vocabulary has no symbol for a self-triggering circuit breaker, the same gap Panoptic's safe mode exposes at a much larger scale.

nodes.label: F13 At the 08:00 UTC fixing the Stork price settles the option, and for co
nodes.text: At the 08:00 UTC fixing the Stork price settles the option, and for collateral assets a named team manually checks the price during a five-minute, smart-contract-enforced dispute period before settlement proceeds; funds are distributed within roughly two hours.
nodes.note: `Sv` is candidate register and is a good fit for determination discretion — this is exactly the terminal-fixing discretion the corpus flagged as unnamed. What `Sv` does not carry: the discretion is bounded by a contract-enforced five-minute window, so the protocol has made the *scope* of the operator's judgement a consensus-enforced quantity, which is the interesting part.

nodes.label: F14 Rysk Premium LPs deposit USDC and hold a pro-rata claim on the pool, w
nodes.text: Rysk Premium LPs deposit USDC and hold a pro-rata claim on the pool, with a deposit price and a withdrawal price struck from NAV once per epoch.
nodes.note: SCOPE FLAG: DefiLlama lists Rysk Premium as a separate protocol ($1.15M TVL, Yield category) from Rysk V12 ($30.15M TVL, Options Vault), and stage 1 recorded that the corpus fuses the two. Premium's obligations are carried here because Premium has no execution rail of its own — it is a taker on the V12 RFQ — but F14-F17 belong to the layer, not to the base protocol. `Sh` also inherits the marker the corpus put on Hegic's: the claim is on a pool whose value depends on unmarked short-option liabilities.

nodes.label: F15 The pool's NAV per share is computed off-chain using aggregated pricin
nodes.text: The pool's NAV per share is computed off-chain using aggregated pricing from a committee of option desks.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and the approximation is the finding. `At` names a NAV attestation, and L27 requires a named attester, independence, a stated assurance level, a staleness bound and recourse. None of the five is published, and the attesters are drawn from the same population of desks that quote into the pool — so the entity marking the LPs' claim is an interested party. The symbol is carried so that the law can fail against it rather than being silently unstated.

nodes.label: F16 Withdrawals are two-step and queue: if the pool's free balance is insu
nodes.text: Withdrawals are two-step and queue: if the pool's free balance is insufficient because collateral is locked in open positions the epoch advances without processing them, and the price the LP receives is the price of the first epoch in which withdrawals do clear.
nodes.note: `Wq` names the queue and `Ep` the epoch gate. Neither names that the *price* is struck at an unknown future epoch: the LP has written a short option on their own exit with no premium and no notice, which is a risk transfer created by a queueing rule.

nodes.label: F17 A named curator selects which instruments the pool writes and receives
nodes.text: A named curator selects which instruments the pool writes and receives a share of the option-sale fee, and governance sets the epoch prices and may withdraw fees independently.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. `Sv` is servicing and determination discretion, not instrument selection, and this is the same five-part shape the yield lane found — named agent, domain, magnitude, rate limit, revocation — one level down. The strike-and-tenor selection policy the corpus called Rysk's 'entire economic content' lives here, in Premium, not in V12, where the taker chooses.

nodes.label: F18 DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION: the protocol runs no hedging loop, no reba
nodes.text: DISCHARGED BY CONSTRUCTION: the protocol runs no hedging loop, no rebalancing and no directional book of its own — every position is fully collateralised at inception and left untouched until expiry.
nodes.evidence: https://docs.rysk.finance/getting-started/solution-rysk-v12 (accessed 2026-08-04); the Dynamic Hedging Vault core repository rysk-finance/dynamic-hedging returns HTTP 404 (gh api repos/rysk-finance/dynamic-hedging, accessed 2026-08-04); Rysk V1 TVL $193k vs Rysk V12 $30.15M on https://api.llama.fi/protocols (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: DISCHARGE BY CONSTRUCTION, and the largest corpus correction in this category. The corpus decomposes the Dynamic Hedging Vault of Rysk V1 / Rysk Beyond on Arbitrum — sunset, no options tradeable after 2024-05-10, core repo removed — and carries `Dp` for delta-hedge maintenance. V12 has no hedge, no vault in the core protocol, and runs on HyperEVM and Ethereum, not Arbitrum. `Dp` is dropped.

nodes.label: F19 The Ethereum settlement layer is an OwnedUpgradeabilityProxy compiled
nodes.text: The Ethereum settlement layer is an OwnedUpgradeabilityProxy compiled from Opyn GammaProtocol sources (solc 0.6.10), audited under the name Lean Gamma, with a separate upgrade-procedure audit.
nodes.evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x684404F2AEBAD87a6803F13741B1d638Bfe2C671?fields=compilation (exact creation and runtime match, verified 2026-06-10; accessed 2026-08-04); https://docs.rysk.finance/resources/security.md and https://docs.rysk.finance/resources/important-contracts.md (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: `Up` fits. RESIDUE inside the obligation: nothing in the vocabulary can express 'this mechanism is a vendored third-party protocol carrying its own upgrade authority', which is the actual trust statement. Whether the proxy owner is a timelock or a multisig is UNKNOWN, so X9 ('Up with immediate single-key control') is not asserted armed — but the corpus's blanket armedProhibitions: [] is unsupported, since the shape is present and the mitigation is unevidenced.

nodes.label: 11-fiat-stablecoins
Circle USDC
F1 USDC is a transferable receipt for a claim the issuer asserts is a pro
nodes.text: USDC is a transferable receipt for a claim the issuer asserts is a property claim rather than a contractual one: Circle states it holds only bare legal title to the reserve and no beneficial interest or property rights, so the reserve should not be considered property of its bankruptcy estate -- while conceding in the same filing that no court has tested this, that holders could face automatic-stay delays even if it holds, and that a US or French court could decide otherwise.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the sharpest epistemic gap in the category. The single most important fact about what a USDC is worth in the bad state is a LEGAL CONJECTURE with two jurisdictions and possibly different answers for EEA and non-EEA holders. The project's own epistemic labels -- theorem, measurement, conjecture -- are precisely the vocabulary the model lacks here: a construction can record that At is present and cannot record that the holder's creditor position is untested. Compare USD1, whose issuer states the opposite (contractual, no property interest), and USDG, whose issuer states a third thing (proportionate share of segregated assets, priority over unsecured creditors). Three different answers to 'what happens if the issuer cannot pay', and all three are At.

nodes.label: F2 The issuers of record are Circle Internet Financial, LLC for US holder
nodes.text: The issuers of record are Circle Internet Financial, LLC for US holders and Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS for EEA holders, so which entity owes the holder is decided by the holder's residence.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No symbol for an obligor, and none for an obligor that varies by who is asking. USDG has the same structure (Paxos Issuance Europe Oy for the EEA, Paxos Digital Singapore for everyone else), so the pattern is not incidental: two of the five largest fiat stablecoins are two instruments wearing one ticker.

nodes.label: F3 The holder base is formally two-tier: redemption is available only to
nodes.text: The holder base is formally two-tier: redemption is available only to Circle Mint account holders, and the USDC Terms state that Users Type B are not customers of Circle and hold only a contingent right conditional on opening an account.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. This is the assignment the corpus made -- and correctly -- but its own reasoning ('the gate is on Circle Mint access, not on token transfer') applies verbatim to the other four issuers, which the corpus did not code. Aw is retained here and ADDED to the other four by this lane. Law L16 (Aw -> transfer-time enforcement where eligibility follows the holder) is NOT satisfied: USDC transfers are permissionless and the gate is an onboarding application, a suitability check on business type and anticipated minting volume, and a wire relationship.

nodes.label: F4 For account holders minting is free, basic redemption is initiated wit
nodes.text: For account holders minting is free, basic redemption is initiated within two business days and is free, and standard redemption is initiated nearly instantly for a nominal fee; there is no stated minimum.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and the least approximate Rd of the five on latency and fee: this is the only member with a stated business-day commitment and a free path. Rd still asserts a right the system grants to account holders only. Note what the model cannot record: a two-business-day free tier and a near-instant paid tier are a priced liquidity ladder, and Rd is one bit.

nodes.label: F5 The issuer may decline to process any issuance or redemption without p
nodes.text: The issuer may decline to process any issuance or redemption without prior notice, may block addresses and freeze the USDC temporarily or permanently, and warns that a blocked holder may forfeit any rights associated with the USDC including the ability to redeem.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, same shape as Tether's suspension grounds: obligor discretion to refuse its own performance, exercised off-chain. Sv (candidate) considered and rejected on the same reasoning given in the USDT record F5.

nodes.label: F6 The reserve at 2026-06-30 is US$73,344,909,176 against US$73,268,560,0
nodes.text: The reserve at 2026-06-30 is US$73,344,909,176 against US$73,268,560,097 of USDC in circulation, of which US$61,917,347,895 sits in the Circle Reserve Fund -- a Rule 2a-7 government money market fund managed by BlackRock Advisors, LLC, custodied at BNY, available only to Circle, whose equity Circle Internet Financial, LLC holds 100% of 'on behalf of USDC holders' -- holding nine CUSIPs of Treasuries maturing 2026-07-02 to 2026-08-20, US$52.53bn of overnight Treasury repo and US$1.00bn of cash.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. 'A 2a-7 government money market fund managed by BlackRock and custodied at BNY, of which the issuer owns 100% of the equity on behalf of holders' is a four-party legal structure -- issuer, manager, custodian, beneficiary -- and At names the PDF that describes it. Not one of the four parties, nor the relation between them, is expressible.

nodes.label: F7 The remaining US$11,382,256,398 is cash held at regulated financial in
nodes.text: The remaining US$11,382,256,398 is cash held at regulated financial institutions in for-benefit-of accounts, primarily with banks designated by the Financial Stability Board as global systemically important banks; no individual bank is named in the reserve report.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the one with a realised failure behind it. The only time USDC has broken par, the cause was a bank failure, and the 10-K still lists credit risk to counterparties including banks as a live risk factor with no on-chain correlate. There is no element in a 58-symbol DeFi vocabulary for 'the reserve is a deposit and the deposit-taker failed'. Individual bank names: UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F8 Assurance is a monthly examination under AICPA attestation standards o
nodes.text: Assurance is a monthly examination under AICPA attestation standards on management's assertion that the fair value of the assets in the USDC Reserve is at least equal to USDC in circulation, at two report dates per month; the June 2026 report covers 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-30 and is signed 2026-07-29 by the Chief Accounting Officer.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and it fails L27's FIRST term, which is the surprise. The engaging accountant's signature block on page 1 is a rendered image and the firm name is not in the PDF text layer, so the identity of the monthly examiner is UNKNOWN FROM THE REPORT ITSELF; Circle's transparency page says only 'a Big Four accounting firm'. CORPUS CORRECTION: the corpus residue text says 'At names the monthly Deloitte report'. Deloitte & Touche LLP is confirmed as Circle's FINANCIAL-STATEMENT auditor since 2023 and as auditor of the Circle Reserve Fund, not as the monthly examiner. 'Deloitte performs the monthly USDC attestation' is plausible and unconfirmed and is not carried. The 2022 Circle blog post naming Grant Thornton is stale and must not be cited.

nodes.label: F9 Circulation is not supply: it is total supply across 36 named USDC App
nodes.text: Circulation is not supply: it is total supply across 36 named USDC Approved Blockchains less Tokens Allowed But Not Issued (1,380,790,392 at 2026-06-30, an artefact of how USDC is implemented on Algorand, Hedera, Polkadot Asset Hub and Solana), less Access Denied Tokens (123,219,920), less Circle Gateway pending burns (94,358), with a further 993,225 permanently frozen on the deprecated FLOW deployment.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No symbol distinguishes supply from issued supply from circulating supply, and the difference here is 1.9% of a US$73bn instrument. Note also that this is the only member of the five whose own attestation admits that its token standard on four chains produces units that exist and are not issued -- a chain-implementation artefact that becomes a line item in a reserve report.

nodes.label: F10 An access denial does not extinguish the liability: the tokens remain
nodes.text: An access denial does not extinguish the liability: the tokens remain owed until the segregated reserve funds are transferred to the relevant law enforcement agency, or until the denial is reversed and a redemption is made.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. This is a THREE-STATE object -- live, denied-but-still-owed, extinguished-into-forfeiture -- and Fz is a boolean. The third state is a transfer of reserve assets to a government, which is the reserve moving in response to an on-chain action, i.e. the one place in this whole category where an on-chain event reaches the reserve, and the model cannot see either end of it.

nodes.label: F11 A named blacklister may block any address: blacklister() is 0x0a06be16
nodes.text: A named blacklister may block any address: blacklister() is 0x0a06be16275b95a7d2567FbdaE118b36c7Da78f9, an externally owned account, and blacklist is present in the verified implementation's ABI.
nodes.note: CANDIDATE REGISTER, used with a note. Fz here is freeze-only with the three-state liability of F10 behind it; it is a different power from USDT's freeze-and-destroy, from PYUSD's freeze-and-wipe and from USD1's freeze-drain-reallocate, and Fz names all four identically.

nodes.label: F12 A named pauser may halt all transfers: pauser() is 0x4914F61D25e5c5671
nodes.text: A named pauser may halt all transfers: pauser() is 0x4914F61D25e5c567143774B76eDbF4d5109A8566, an externally owned account, and paused() reads false at 2026-08-04.
nodes.note: Gp is retained; USDC is the one member the corpus coded it for. This lane's finding is that the assignment was right and its exclusivity was wrong -- the same live pause exists in all five verified ABIs.

nodes.label: F13 Mint authority is a delegated QUANTITY rather than a role: masterMinte
nodes.text: Mint authority is a delegated QUANTITY rather than a role: masterMinter() is 0xE982615d461DD5cD06575BbeA87624fda4e3de17, a 7,667-byte contract named MinterAdmin, and the implementation exposes configureMinter, removeMinter and minterAllowance, so each minter holds an allowance that minting consumes.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Aw names an identity gate; nothing names a rate-or-quantity-limited delegated authority. Au was considered and REJECTED here on a precise test: law L17 requires of Au bounded scope, revocation, expiry and nonce/domain separation. A minter allowance has bounded scope (a quantity) and revocation (removeMinter) but NO expiry and NO domain separation, so it fails two of four -- unlike the EIP-3009 authorisations of F19, which satisfy all four. This is the same bounded-delegate shape the yield and CDP lanes converged on (named agent, domain, magnitude cap, rate-of-change limit, revocation), here missing the rate-of-change term that USDG's SupplyControl supplies.

nodes.label: F14 The implementation behind the proxy is FiatTokenV2_2 at 0x43506849D7C0
nodes.text: The implementation behind the proxy is FiatTokenV2_2 at 0x43506849D7C04F9138D1A2050bbF3A0c054402dd, compiled with solc 0.6.12, reached through a ZeppelinOS-style transparent proxy at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2E9Eb0cE3606eB48 whose implementation and admin live in the keccak256('org.zeppelinos.proxy.*') slots rather than EIP-1967 slots.
nodes.note: Firm fit. STAGE-1 GAP CLOSED: stage 1 could resolve the implementation only as 'consistent with the FiatTokenV2_2 family' from version() == '2'; the Blockscout record for the implementation address names the contract FiatTokenV2_2 directly, read 2026-08-04. Byte-for-byte correspondence between the Apache-2.0 repository build and the deployed bytecode remains UNVERIFIED and is not asserted.

nodes.label: F15 The proxy admin is 0x807a96288A1a408dBC13DE2b1d087d10356395d2, an exte
nodes.text: The proxy admin is 0x807a96288A1a408dBC13DE2b1d087d10356395d2, an externally owned account with no code, and there is no timelock anywhere in the control plane.
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call of the ZeppelinOS admin slot at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2E9Eb0cE3606eB48 and eth_getCode at 0x807a96288A1a408dBC13DE2b1d087d10356395d2 (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a live tables question stage 3 must answer rather than inherit. Tg is correctly ABSENT, so law L15 (Up -> Tg | bounded emergency process) is NOT satisfied, and prohibition X9 ('Up with immediate single-key control') arguably FIRES -- a single EOA can replace the implementation of a US$73bn instrument in one transaction with no delay. The corpus records armedProhibitions: [] for USDC. This construction does not assert that X9 fires (that is the checker's call, and 'single-key' may be read as excluding an operationally multi-party EOA), but it records that the corpus's empty list was never computed against this fact. Compare USDG, the only member of the five where L15 IS satisfied.

nodes.label: F16 Authority is genuinely divided across five distinct roles -- owner 0xF
nodes.text: Authority is genuinely divided across five distinct roles -- owner 0xFcb19e6a322b27c06842A71e8c725399f049AE3a, masterMinter, blacklister, pauser and a rescuer -- which is the only real role separation among the five; every one of them resolves to a single externally owned account or, for masterMinter, to a contract.
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call owner(), masterMinter(), blacklister(), pauser() at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2E9Eb0cE3606eB48 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0x43506849D7C04F9138D1A2050bbF3A0c054402dd (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, the bridges lane's finding again. Role separation is a real and material design property -- USDT's seven powers are one key, USDC's are five keys, USD1's are nine roles over two Safes -- and the vocabulary cannot state it, because control elements are unary predicates on a protocol and the risk is a property of the holder. rescuer() was not resolved to a non-zero address in stage 1's read and is not asserted.

nodes.label: F17 USDC moves between chains by burning on the source domain and minting
nodes.text: USDC moves between chains by burning on the source domain and minting on the destination domain against an attestation over the burn event, under the Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol.
nodes.note: FIRM, and the correction that refutes the category's headline claim. CCTP is genuine MECHANISM, not control-plane and not attestation: a burn is observed, a message is verified, a mint follows, and the invariant of law L9 (debit(source) = credit(destination)) is actually enforced by the protocol rather than asserted by an operator. The claim that 'every symbol these five use is control-plane or attestation' is FALSE AS STATED for USDC, and the evidence is a US Securities and Exchange Commission filing rather than a marketing page.

nodes.label: F18 CCTP V2, launched March 2025, adds a fee-generating fast-transfer path
nodes.text: CCTP V2, launched March 2025, adds a fee-generating fast-transfer path alongside the standard path.
nodes.note: The elements carry the transfer; the FEE TIER is residue. Fd (surplus & fee distribution) was considered and rejected -- this is a price charged for a faster finality assumption, not a distribution of surplus -- and no element expresses that one cross-domain path may be bought faster than another. Xf and Xm cannot distinguish a slow verified path from a fast paid one, and the difference is exactly the security assumption a user is paying to relax.

nodes.label: F19 A holder may authorise a transfer by signature and have any third part
nodes.text: A holder may authorise a transfer by signature and have any third party execute it: the deployed implementation exposes transferWithAuthorization, receiveWithAuthorization and cancelAuthorization under EIP-3009 and permit under EIP-2612, with authorizationState and a DOMAIN_SEPARATOR.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and a NEW ASSIGNMENT no lane has made -- the corpus codes Au for none of the five. Tested against law L17 (Au -> bounded scope + revocation + expiry + nonce/domain separation) an EIP-3009 authorisation satisfies all four terms exactly: scope is one amount to one payee, revocation is cancelAuthorization, expiry is validAfter/validBefore, and separation is a random nonce under an EIP-712 domain. It is approximate only in that Au's gloss says 'session policy, account abstraction' and this is a single-shot delegation rather than a session. Verified directly from the implementation ABI on 2026-08-04 rather than inherited. Present in four of five (absent only from USDT, whose 2018 Solidity 0.4.18 code predates both EIPs), so it is a real design axis and its omission from the corpus is the fourth coding artefact this lane found.

nodes.label: F20 Circle Gateway, launched July 2025, provides a unified USDC balance in
nodes.text: Circle Gateway, launched July 2025, provides a unified USDC balance instantly accessible across supported blockchains, holding balances in Circle smart contracts and producing the pending-burns deduction in the reserve report.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and an uncomfortable one. Gateway is not Xf (no asset moves) and not Xm (the message is not the point). It is closest to Ua, unified-balance ledger -- which sits in the CONTESTED REGISTER and is therefore unusable. So a live, shipped mechanism in the largest regulated stablecoin has exactly one word in the vocabulary and the vocabulary has disallowed it. Gateway postdates the corpus and appears in no corpus record.

nodes.label: F21 The issuer is licensed by many authorities and supervised as a payment
nodes.text: The issuer is licensed by many authorities and supervised as a payments and virtual-asset business rather than as a bank: a NYDFS BitLicense, state money-transmitter licences and FinCEN MSB registration in the United States; an AMF DASP registration and an ACPR electronic-money-institution licence in France; an ADGM FSRA licence; and a Bermuda Monetary Authority DABA licence.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No symbol for a supervising authority or for what it may order. Note also what falls with it: reserve-composition mandates under the GENIUS Act and MiCA are rules that FORBID the issuer from holding certain assets, i.e. constraints on the reserve, and the reserve has no representation for a constraint to bind.

nodes.label: F22 In December 2025 the issuer received OCC conditional approval to estab
nodes.text: In December 2025 the issuer received OCC conditional approval to establish Circle National Trust, which is to manage the USDC reserve and hold a first-priority perfected security interest in it as collateral trustee for the benefit of USDC holders.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a category no model in this project anticipates: a stablecoin's holder claim can be UPGRADED FROM AN UNTESTED PROPERTY THEORY TO A PERFECTED SECURITY INTEREST BY A BANK CHARTER, with no change to the token, the contracts, the reserve or the element set. The construction is invariant under the single largest improvement available to the instrument. That is the cleanest available demonstration that the model is not measuring what makes the token worth a dollar. This protection is FUTURE and NOT IN FORCE at 2026-08-04.

nodes.label: F23 The float accrues entirely to the issuer and its distributors: FY2025
nodes.text: The float accrues entirely to the issuer and its distributors: FY2025 reserve income was US$2,636,822 thousand and distribution and transaction costs were US$1,661,549 thousand, so 63% of the reserve yield was paid to distribution partners, principally Coinbase under a Collaboration Agreement with an initial three-year auto-renewing term; holders receive nothing.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, now quantified. Fd (surplus & fee distribution) and Em (protocol-funded emissions) both considered and REJECTED: neither can express 'the issuer keeps the interest and buys distribution with 63% of it', because the payment is a wire under a bilateral contract and touches no on-chain state. This is the exact contrast that makes USDG's record decisive: USDG pays an economically similar distribution and pays part of it through an on-chain accrual-and-claim ledger, so Fd fits there and not here. Same economics, different observability, and the vocabulary sees one and not the other.

nodes.label: F24 On-chain the token is plain balance accounting: 6 decimals, version()
nodes.text: On-chain the token is plain balance accounting: 6 decimals, version() returns '2', currency() returns 'USD', and Ethereum supply is 49,536,777,415.220915 at 2026-08-04 against attested all-chain circulation of 73,268,560,097.
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call totalSupply(), version(), currency(), decimals() at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2E9Eb0cE3606eB48 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://6778953.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/6778953/USDCAttestationReports/2026/2026%20USDC_Examination%20Report%20June%2026.pdf (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, as at USDT F12: Sh, Ix and Rb name three ways a claim's value can move and there is no name for a fixed-unit claim whose value does not move. RANKING BASIS NOTE: the attested circulation of 73,268,560,097 at 2026-06-30 is the citable figure and supersedes the corpus's DefiLlama US$72.20B for ranking purposes; the Ethereum leg is 68% of it, so any lane reading a single chain understates.

nodes.label: Global Dollar USDG (Paxos)
F1 USDG is an electronic-money claim with two obligors selected by the ho
nodes.text: USDG is an electronic-money claim with two obligors selected by the holder's residence: for EEA holders the issuer is Paxos Issuance Europe Oy, a Finnish electronic money institution supervised by the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority under LEI 743700KYSSTKZYGEUF50 and Business ID 3236886-2; for everyone else the issuer is Paxos Digital Singapore Pte. Ltd., a Major Payments Institution supervised by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a CORPUS CORRECTION. The corpus says USDG's distinguishing legal fact is 'the NYDFS trust charter'. USDG is not issued under a NYDFS trust charter at all; it is issued by a Singapore MPI and a Finnish EMI under MiCA. The residue item is right that a charter distinction exists and wrong about which charter. Beyond that: no symbol can express an obligor that varies by who is asking. The same structure appears at USDC (US LLC / French SAS), so two of the five are two instruments under one ticker.

nodes.label: F2 Holders have a right of redemption at any time and at par value, state
nodes.text: Holders have a right of redemption at any time and at par value, stated in the regulator's prescribed language -- 1 USDG = 1 USD, without incurring fees, on a one-for-one basis notwithstanding any change in the market value of stablecoins or reserve assets -- with tokens burned on redemption.
nodes.note: The STRONGEST Rd of the five and the only one that is a regulatory entitlement rather than a contractual facility: at any time, at par, no fee, no minimum, and unconditional on the market value of the reserve. It remains APPROXIMATE for the same structural reason as the other four -- all redemptions are subject to compliance review and may be delayed, and no on-chain path exists -- but the difference between this and USDT's 819 customers at a US$100,000 minimum with a greater-of-US$1,000-or-0.1% fee is the widest spread in the category, and Rd is the same symbol at both ends of it.

nodes.label: F3 Minting is available exclusively on the Paxos Platform to institutions
nodes.text: Minting is available exclusively on the Paxos Platform to institutions that have successfully completed the requisite onboarding procedures, so issuance and redemption are asymmetric: anyone may redeem, only onboarded institutions may mint.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE -- an off-chain onboarding gate, coded on the corpus's own USDC reasoning. CORPUS DEPARTURE: Aw is ADDED. Note the asymmetry itself is residue: no element can express that entry to a system is gated while exit is not, which is the opposite of the USDT and USD1 pattern where exit is gated and entry to the secondary market is not.

nodes.label: F4 Issuance destinations are whitelisted on-chain: the SupplyControl cont
nodes.text: Issuance destinations are whitelisted on-chain: the SupplyControl contract at 0x9a7164112029b81c07636ab7b59fa813e0883bbf exposes addMintAddressToWhitelist, removeMintAddressFromWhitelist, updateAllowAnyMintAndBurnAddress and the predicates canMintToAddress and canBurnFromAddress, so where new supply may be sent is enforced by contract rather than by policy.
nodes.note: FIRM -- the only genuinely ON-CHAIN Aw in the category. Every other permission gate among the five is a business relationship; this one is a predicate the contract evaluates. It is issuer-side rather than user-side (holders face no gate) which is the same qualification the bridges lane attached to Aw for WBTC's merchant registry.

nodes.label: F5 Each supply controller's minting is rate-limited on-chain: SupplyContr
nodes.text: Each supply controller's minting is rate-limited on-chain: SupplyControl carries per-controller limit configuration through contracts/lib/RateLimit.sol, with updateLimitConfig and getRemainingMintAmount, under SUPPLY_CONTROLLER_MANAGER_ROLE, SUPPLY_CONTROLLER_ROLE and TOKEN_CONTRACT_ROLE.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the run's THIRD independent arrival at one schema. The yield lane and the CDP lane both found a five-part primitive -- named agent, domain whitelist, magnitude cap, rate-of-change limit or delay, revocation -- bounding an allocation and a rate respectively. SupplyControl instantiates the identical schema bounding ISSUANCE: a named supply controller, a mint-address whitelist (F4), a per-period cap, a remaining-amount limiter, and role revocation. Three lanes, three categories, three different bounded quantities, one shape. It is also the mitigation an X9-style single-key-mint concern would demand, and the vocabulary cannot record that the mitigation exists. Ct was considered and rejected: Ct is a collateral or margin test on a position, not a rate limit on an authority.

nodes.label: F6 The reserve is at least 100% of outstanding EU-attributed USDG in high
nodes.text: The reserve is at least 100% of outstanding EU-attributed USDG in high-quality, low-risk assets such as cash and short-term government debt, legally segregated from the issuer's own funds and from the custodian's funds, held with qualified custodians, authorised by the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority and structured for bankruptcy remoteness, with MiCA additionally requiring a portion to sit with European banking partners.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Named custodians and named banking partners: UNKNOWN from primary sources. Note what is different here and equally unnameable: the reserve is not merely disclosed, it is CONSTRAINED BY A REGULATOR and held in trust accounts the regulator authorised. A supervised, segregated, bankruptcy-remote reserve and Tether's discretionary portfolio of gold, bitcoin and secured loans are the same symbol.

nodes.label: F7 In insolvency holders are entitled to a proportionate share of the seg
nodes.text: In insolvency holders are entitled to a proportionate share of the segregated reserve assets, with their claims taking precedence over unsecured creditors, distributed under Finnish insolvency law and overseen by the insolvency administrator and the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. This is the strongest creditor position of the five and it decomposes identically to the weakest. Tr (tranche waterfall) was considered and REJECTED for the same reason as at USDT F2, but note how close it comes: law L6's terms for Tr are declared seniority (yes -- priority over unsecured creditors), dispute forum (yes -- the District Court of Helsinki, F9), and a recovery-timing assumption (partly -- Finnish insolvency procedure). Three of L6's terms are satisfied entirely off-chain. Tr is withheld because no mechanism executes the waterfall. Stage 4 should note that a law whose terms are satisfiable outside the algebra cannot discriminate constructions inside it.

nodes.label: F8 USDG is not covered by any investor compensation or deposit guarantee
nodes.text: USDG is not covered by any investor compensation or deposit guarantee scheme: white paper field D.11 is false for both Directive 97/9/EC and Directive 2014/49/EU, though the underlying segregated accounts are.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The distinction between an instrument covered by a guarantee scheme and one whose reserve accounts are covered while the instrument is not is a two-level protection structure with no representation, and it is the same trap as USD1's FDIC-limit caveat: the retail mental model of 'it is in a bank' is exactly what these two disclosures deny.

nodes.label: F9 The governing law is the law of Finland and the competent court is the
nodes.text: The governing law is the law of Finland and the competent court is the District Court of Helsinki.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. There is no symbol for a FORUM. 'Who do you sue, and where' is answerable from primary documents for three of the five -- a Helsinki court here, confidential BVI-law arbitration seated in London for USDT, US courts under the BitGo terms for USD1 -- and unrepresentable for all five. Law L6 lists a dispute forum among Tr's terms, so the carrier's own constraint language references an object its element set cannot name.

nodes.label: F10 Assurance is monthly under Singapore standards: reports posted on or a
nodes.text: Assurance is monthly under Singapore standards: reports posted on or after 2026-02-27 are issued by KPMG LLP under standards established by the Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants, and earlier reports by Enrome LLP under the same standards, indexed monthly for 2024, 2025 and January to June 2026.
nodes.evidence: https://www.paxos.com/usdg-transparency (accessed 2026-08-04, content read via a rendered browser fetch) | https://globaldollar.com/about-usdg (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and the most degraded At of the five in practice. USDG is the only member attested under a non-US, non-ISAE standard -- ISCA rather than AICPA or ISAE 3000R -- which the corpus does not record and which matters for what At means. Worse: the per-month report PDFs are served through a JavaScript viewer that stage 1 could not resolve to direct URLs even under a rendered browser fetch, so THE ATTESTED RESERVE FIGURES AND COMPOSITION FOR USDG ARE UNKNOWN IN THIS RECORD. At marks the presence of an attestation and cannot record that the attestation is not retrievable. That is L27's staleness-and-recourse gap in its most acute form: an attestation nobody can read is indistinguishable, in the model, from one everybody can.

nodes.label: F11 Reserve revenue is passed back to Global Dollar Network partners rathe
nodes.text: Reserve revenue is passed back to Global Dollar Network partners rather than kept by the issuer, and the distribution is implemented on-chain: the deployed implementation contains ClaimableRewardsBase and ClaimableRewardsStorageV3 with payout groups, per-wallet shares, period accounting, _claimIndividualRewardsWithData and an individual claim path, audited by Zellic as 'USDG Rewards'.
nodes.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE, and the most consequential correction in this category. The corpus marks Fd as FORCED with the reason 'the surplus distribution is a legal agreement executed by wire, not an on-chain fee flow', and uses that as evidence for the category's central thesis. The premise is factually wrong: the deployed, verified implementation carries a rewards ledger with accrual, share accounting and a claim function, and it has been independently audited under that name. Fd IS NOT A FORCED FIT. Sh is APPROXIMATE -- shares are pro-rata within a payout group, but the pool they claim against is a stream of off-chain-funded reward rather than a pool of held assets. Ep is APPROXIMATE -- accrual is period-based (getCurrentPeriodNum, calculatePeriodsCrossed) which is an epoch-gated transition on the reward, not on the token. Ix was considered and REJECTED: no single global index was evidenced; the accounting is per-payout-group with a projected multiplier (projectMultiplier, MultiplierGrowthLib), which is index-LIKE and not shown to be an index.

nodes.label: F12 Reward entitlement survives a transfer of the token: updateSharesWithR
nodes.text: Reward entitlement survives a transfer of the token: updateSharesWithRewardPreservation, _transferWithDifferentPayouts and _updateWalletWithPayoutGroup re-attribute reward shares between payout groups when balances move.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. This is a real accounting mechanism attached to an ERC-20 transfer and it is neither Rb (nominal balances do not change) nor plain Sh (the share moves between claimants, not the claim between holders). A transfer simultaneously moves a balance and re-prices two third parties' entitlements. Nothing in the claims-and-accounting group can state that.

nodes.label: F13 The money funding the on-chain rewards ledger is off-chain reserve inc
nodes.text: The money funding the on-chain rewards ledger is off-chain reserve income paid under partner agreements on three distinct bases -- average USDG balance held, net USDG minted, and USDG transaction volume -- with an explicit disclaimer that nothing displayed constitutes a commitment or obligation to pay any particular amount.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the precise boundary of F11. The DISTRIBUTION is on-chain; the SOURCE and the OBLIGATION are not, and the issuer states in terms that there is no obligation. So the construction can name the payout rail and cannot name whether anything is paid into it. The specific revenue-share percentage is UNKNOWN from primary sources; figures of '97%' and 'over 90%' circulate in secondary coverage and were not confirmed at the issuer, and are not carried.

nodes.label: F14 An asset-protection authority may freeze an address and wipe a frozen
nodes.text: An asset-protection authority may freeze an address and wipe a frozen balance: the enforcement predicates _isAddrFrozen and whenNotPaused sit in the token's own transfer path in contracts/lib/PaxosBaseAbstract.sol under ASSET_PROTECTION_ROLE.
nodes.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xfacd5ff359adf87822374275699dd518aaf9a65f (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getFacet(0x8d1fdf2f) and getFacet(0xe2f72f03) at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D, both returning 0xe90c0e2fecd06c5875b50f6b13f3b8dbdb4ce946 (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: CANDIDATE REGISTER, used with a note, and carried on a verification stage 1 did not perform. freeze(address) and wipeFrozenAddress(address) are NOT in the implementation's ABI: they are reached through the facet router and currently route to the admin facet at 0xe90c0e2f..., confirmed by reading the live facet table on 2026-08-04. The enforcement lives in the token; the entry points live in a mutable dispatch table. See F18.

nodes.label: F15 A pause authority may halt transfers: PAUSE_ROLE gates pause() and unp
nodes.text: A pause authority may halt transfers: PAUSE_ROLE gates pause() and unpause(), which route through the facet table to 0xe90c0e2fecd06c5875b50f6b13f3b8dbdb4ce946, and the whenNotPaused modifier is enforced in the token's transfer path.
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getFacet(0x8456cb59) and getFacet(0x3f4ba83a) at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D, both returning 0xe90c0e2fecd06c5875b50f6b13f3b8dbdb4ce946 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xfacd5ff359adf87822374275699dd518aaf9a65f (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Gp is ADDED, and this is the member where the correction needed real work. A naive ABI read of USDG's implementation shows NO pause function, which would wrongly suggest USDG lacks Gp; the capability exists because the facet table maps the pause selectors. Verified by direct eth_call on the live table on 2026-08-04. With this, Gp is established as present and live in all five deployed tokens -- the corpus coded it in one.

nodes.label: F16 A holder may authorise transfers by signature: permit, transferWithAut
nodes.text: A holder may authorise transfers by signature: permit, transferWithAuthorization and cancelAuthorization route through the facet table to an authorisation facet at 0x7569ae2be6ac51ed7f92f8167090b52615f86497, and the implementation reserves the EIP-712, EIP-2612 and EIP-3009 storage slots in contracts/BaseStorageV3.sol.
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getFacet(0xd505accf), getFacet(0xe3ee160e), getFacet(0x5a049a70) at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D, all returning 0x7569ae2be6ac51ed7f92f8167090b52615f86497 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xfacd5ff359adf87822374275699dd518aaf9a65f (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and a NEW ASSIGNMENT the corpus codes for none of the five. Law L17's four terms are satisfied exactly by an EIP-3009 authorisation (bounded scope, cancelAuthorization, validAfter/validBefore, nonce under an EIP-712 domain). Approximate only against Au's 'session policy' gloss. As with F14 and F15 the capability is facet-routed and was established by reading the live table, not by inheriting a claim.

nodes.label: F17 The implementation is reached through an EIP-1967 proxy at 0xe34316763
nodes.text: The implementation is reached through an EIP-1967 proxy at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D and upgrades under UUPS -- upgradeTo, upgradeToAndCall and proxiableUUID live in the implementation USDG at 0xfaCd5Ff359aDF87822374275699DD518aaf9A65f, solc 0.8.28, fully verified 2026-02-27.
nodes.note: Firm fit, and the only member of the five whose upgrade logic lives in the implementation rather than the proxy -- a different failure mode (an implementation without upgradeTo bricks the proxy) that Up cannot distinguish from a transparent proxy, an EIP-1967 proxy, or USDT's five-function forwarding deprecation. Source is MIT at github.com/paxosglobal/usdg-contract and github.com/paxosglobal/paxos-token-contracts; byte-for-byte repo-to-deployment comparison was NOT performed and is not asserted. Note that the deployed verified sources include hardhat/console.sol among the compiled units.

nodes.label: F18 Beneath the proxy the token carries a second, finer mutability surface
nodes.text: Beneath the proxy the token carries a second, finer mutability surface: a facet router with setFacet(bytes4,address) and batchSetFacet(FacetCut[]) under DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, a facets mapping, and a fallback() that delegatecalls facets[msg.sig] and reverts with FacetNotFound when the selector is unmapped.
nodes.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xfacd5ff359adf87822374275699dd518aaf9a65f (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getFacet(bytes4) at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D across the pause, freeze, wipe, permit and EIP-3009 selectors (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the sharpest new finding in this record. Up is one bit; USDG has THREE NESTED MUTABILITY SURFACES -- proxy, implementation, per-selector facet table -- and the consequence is not merely that upgrades are finer-grained. It is that FOUR OF USDG'S OWN ELEMENTS EXIST ONLY BECAUSE A MUTABLE TABLE MAPS THEIR SELECTORS: Gp (F15), Fz (F14), Au (F16) and part of Fd (F11) are all facet-routed, and a single setFacet(selector, address(0)) removes any of them, after which the call reverts FacetNotFound. So an element set for USDG is a statement about the contents of an admin-controlled dispatch table at a block height, not about the code. The vocabulary has no way to say 'present, and revocable by table edit', and this is the third and strongest instance of the category-level gap first seen at USDT's dormant fee dial and USD1's null-but-installable checker: THE VOCABULARY DESCRIBES WHAT IS, NOT WHAT IS ARMED OR WHAT IS REVOCABLE.

nodes.label: F19 Every one of those mutability surfaces sits behind a 24-hour delay: ow
nodes.text: Every one of those mutability surfaces sits behind a 24-hour delay: owner() and defaultAdmin() are both 0x9036566EAa5f83e0b9E1161C6C602B0aDF997654, a verified TimelockController whose getMinDelay() returns 86400, and hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, that timelock) returns true, so setFacet, batchSetFacet and the UUPS upgrade are all delayed.
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call defaultAdmin() at 0xe343167631d89b6FFc58B88d6b7fB0228795491D returning 0x9036566eaa5f83e0b9e1161c6c602b0adf997654, getMinDelay() at that address returning 0x15180 (86400), and hasRole(0x00..00, 0x9036566e...) returning 1 (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Tg is ADDED, and it is the single sharpest GOVERNANCE difference in the category -- present in exactly one of the five and coded in none. USDG is the ONLY member that satisfies law L15 (Up -> Tg | bounded emergency process). USDT is a 3-of-6 multisig with no delay, USDC's proxy admin is a bare EOA, USD1's is a 3-of-5 Safe with no delay, PYUSD's is a bare EOA. The corpus lists armedProhibitions: [] for all five, which is the same answer for the one system that has a delay and the four that do not. This obligation is why the corpus's control-plane coding cannot be trusted as a discriminator: it recorded no difference where the only real one lives.

nodes.label: F20 A separate and much shorter delay governs handover of the admin role i
nodes.text: A separate and much shorter delay governs handover of the admin role itself: defaultAdminDelay() returns 10800, three hours, on transferring DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, alongside beginDefaultAdminTransfer, acceptDefaultAdminTransfer, cancelDefaultAdminTransfer, changeDefaultAdminDelay and rollbackDefaultAdminDelay.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Two delays of different lengths govern different things -- 86400 seconds on what the admin DOES, 10800 seconds on WHO THE ADMIN IS -- and Tg is one symbol. At PYUSD only the second delay exists, with no delay at all on the admin's actions, and Tg would be wrong there for exactly that reason (see the PYUSD record). Tg cannot distinguish 'the key acts slowly' from 'the key acts instantly but changes hands slowly', and those are opposite guarantees.

nodes.label: F21 USDG is deployed on Ethereum as an ERC-20, Solana as an SPL Token-2022
nodes.text: USDG is deployed on Ethereum as an ERC-20, Solana as an SPL Token-2022, and Ink, X Layer and Robinhood Chain as ERC-20s, on distributed ledgers the white paper confirms the issuer does not operate.
nodes.note: Xf and Xm are NOT CARRIED, deliberately. No primary statement of how USDG supply moves between these deployments could be found; the white paper describes per-chain issuance and describes no bridge. The mechanism is UNKNOWN and must not be assumed to be USD1's CCIP or anything else. This is a case where the honest record is an absence of evidence rather than evidence of absence, and the construction reflects that by carrying nothing.

nodes.label: F22 Ethereum supply is 500,509,895.398634 USDG at 6 decimals on 2026-08-04
nodes.text: Ethereum supply is 500,509,895.398634 USDG at 6 decimals on 2026-08-04, a fraction of all-chain supply.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, as at USDT F12: no element names a fixed-unit balance. RANKING BASIS WARNING: Ethereum-only is US$500.5M against the corpus's US$3.42B all-chain DefiLlama figure at the same date -- a factor of roughly seven. Any later lane reading a single chain for this member will be badly wrong, and nothing in the model records which chain a supply figure came from.

nodes.label: F23 The contracts are published under MIT licence and audited: github.com/
nodes.text: The contracts are published under MIT licence and audited: github.com/paxosglobal/usdg-contract and github.com/paxosglobal/paxos-token-contracts carry an audits directory holding Halborn on PaxosTokenV2 and Zellic on USDG Rewards and PAXG V2, with the USDG README naming Zellic and Trail of Bits.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. At is 'reserve / NAV / financial attestation'; a security audit is an attestation ABOUT CODE by a named firm with a stated scope, and it has no symbol. The category therefore has two independent assurance regimes -- one over the reserve, one over the contracts -- and the vocabulary names only the one that does not cover the code it is decomposing. Neither repository surfaced a release tag, so the citable artefact is the deployed verified source rather than a commit.

nodes.label: PayPal USD (PYUSD)
F1 PayPal is not the issuer: PYUSD is issued by Paxos Trust Company, N.A.
nodes.text: PayPal is not the issuer: PYUSD is issued by Paxos Trust Company, N.A., and PayPal's own 10-Q calls Paxos 'a third-party issuer (the PYUSD Issuer)' and states the claim precisely -- each token of PYUSD held by PayPal represents a contractual right to redeem with the third-party issuer of PYUSD for one U.S. dollar.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No symbol for an obligor. The brand-versus-obligor split is the same fact pattern as USD1 (World Liberty Financial owns the brand, BitGo Bank & Trust owes the money) and is unrepresentable in both.

nodes.label: F2 The obligor is not the counterparty: a PayPal or Venmo consumer's coun
nodes.text: The obligor is not the counterparty: a PayPal or Venmo consumer's counterparty is PayPal under PayPal's user agreement, while the obligor of last resort is Paxos under Paxos's stablecoin terms -- two hops, two contracts, one token.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, new -- not in the corpus. There is no symbol for an INTERMEDIATED CLAIM: a holder whose legal counterparty is a distributor standing between them and the issuer. This is a different structure from USDT's 819 direct customers and from USDC's two-tier terms, because here the intermediary is itself the dominant venue for the instrument.

nodes.label: F3 For a US consumer PYUSD lives inside PayPal's or Venmo's custodial led
nodes.text: For a US consumer PYUSD lives inside PayPal's or Venmo's custodial ledger and converts one-for-one to a PayPal balance; moving it on-chain at all requires being 'provisioned for external transfers' and passing PayPal's sanctions and anti-money-laundering controls.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and an unusual gate: every other Aw in this category gates ENTRY to issuance or redemption; this one gates EXIT FROM THE CUSTODIAL LEDGER ONTO THE CHAIN. Aw names an on-chain permission; this is a provisioning flag in a company database that decides whether the token behaves like a token. CORPUS DEPARTURE: Aw is ADDED, on the corpus's own USDC reasoning, and here there are two such gates -- PayPal provisioning for external transfer, and Paxos Platform onboarding for institutional mint and redeem (F5).

nodes.label: F4 The dominant use path never touches a blockchain: most PYUSD activity
nodes.text: The dominant use path never touches a blockchain: most PYUSD activity is a row change in PayPal's or Venmo's custodial database, and the token contract is a settlement layer for a payment network whose real ledger is invisible to it.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the sharpest instance in the whole category. There is no symbol for AN OFF-CHAIN LEDGER THAT SHADOWS THE TOKEN. Corroborated at a primary source rather than inferred: PayPal's 10-Q says on-chain sending requires provisioning, which is a statement that the on-chain representation is an opt-in feature of an off-chain product. Every element in a construction of PYUSD describes the minority of its behaviour.

nodes.label: F5 Direct redemption with the issuer is for institutional users who compl
nodes.text: Direct redemption with the issuer is for institutional users who complete Paxos Platform onboarding -- the issuer 'may also allow institutional users to directly purchase PYUSD from the PYUSD Issuer' -- with the minimum, fee and settlement time not stated in any source reachable at the access date.
nodes.note: BOTH APPROXIMATE. Minimums, fees and settlement times for direct Paxos redemption are UNKNOWN and are not repaired from secondary sources. Rd is doubly strained here: the consumer's practical redemption is a 1:1 conversion inside PayPal's ledger against PayPal, while the contractual redemption right runs against Paxos and is reachable only by institutions. Two different redemptions with two different counterparties, one symbol, and the one the vocabulary is describing is the one almost no holder uses.

nodes.label: F6 Reserves are US dollar deposits, US treasuries and cash equivalents he
nodes.text: Reserves are US dollar deposits, US treasuries and cash equivalents held in segregated, bankruptcy-remote accounts at a national trust bank.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The composition is stated only at this level of generality, and the attested per-month figures are UNKNOWN in this record: the report PDFs are served through a JavaScript viewer that stage 1 could not resolve to direct URLs even under a rendered browser fetch. So for two of the five members -- PYUSD and USDG, both Paxos-issued -- the model carries At while the numbers it points at are not retrievable. No bank is named.

nodes.label: F7 Assurance is a two-document regime: monthly attestations by KPMG LLP u
nodes.text: Assurance is a two-document regime: monthly attestations by KPMG LLP under AICPA attestation standards for reports posted on or after 2025-02-28 and by WithumSmith+Brown, PC before that date, PLUS a separate self-reported portfolio composition published five business days after month-end that is expressly not subjected to independent review.
nodes.evidence: https://www.paxos.com/pyusd-transparency (accessed 2026-08-04, content read via a rendered browser fetch)
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and a regime the corpus does not record. The MORE DETAILED document is the UN-REVIEWED one. At is a single predicate and cannot express that an issuer publishes two documents about the same reserve at different assurance levels, nor that a reader comparing issuers on 'detail of disclosure' is rewarded for reading the one nobody signed. Against law L27: named attester yes, independence yes, stated assurance yes for one document and NONE for the other, no staleness bound, no recourse.

nodes.label: F8 The issuer's own publications do not agree on who supervises it: paxos
nodes.text: The issuer's own publications do not agree on who supervises it: paxos.com/pyusd states the issuer is Paxos Trust Company, N.A. subject to strict regulatory oversight by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, while the PYUSD transparency page still describes 'Paxos' prudential regulator, the New York State Department of Financial Services' and its Dollar-Backed Stablecoins guidance as the body approving the examiner's appointment.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. CORPUS CORRECTION: the corpus says 'issued by Paxos Trust under NYDFS'. The consistent reading of the primary sources is that the issuer converted from a New York trust company to a national trust bank under OCC supervision during 2026 and one Paxos page is stale, but WHICH ONE, AND THE EFFECTIVE DATE, ARE UNKNOWN. Both are recorded. A stablecoin whose supervising authority cannot be read consistently off two pages of the issuer's own website is a fact about At's ENVIRONMENT that At cannot hold, and no symbol names a regulator or what it may order.

nodes.label: F9 A second regulator sits over the distributor rather than the issuer: P
nodes.text: A second regulator sits over the distributor rather than the issuer: PayPal is regulated by NYDFS as a virtual currency business and is a digital asset service provider under the GENIUS Act.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Two supervised entities on one instrument, supervised for different things by different authorities, and the model has no place for either.

nodes.label: F10 An asset-protection authority may freeze and destroy any balance: ASSE
nodes.text: An asset-protection authority may freeze and destroy any balance: ASSET_PROTECTION_ROLE holds freeze(address), freezeBatch(address[]), unfreeze, unfreezeBatch and wipeFrozenAddress(address), all present in the verified implementation ABI, with isFrozen(address) a public view.
nodes.note: CANDIDATE REGISTER, used with a note. PYUSD can freeze and destroy and CANNOT forcibly re-assign; USD1 can do all three; USDT can freeze and destroy; USDC can only freeze. Fz names all four. Note the batch forms: freezeBatch and unfreezeBatch make mass action a single transaction, which is an operational property of the power that no element records.

nodes.label: F11 A pause authority may halt all transfers: PAUSE_ROLE holds pause() and
nodes.text: A pause authority may halt all transfers: PAUSE_ROLE holds pause() and unpause(), both present in the verified implementation ABI; paused() reads false at 2026-08-04.
nodes.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Gp is ADDED. Verified in the implementation ABI on 2026-08-04. With this the corpus's PYUSD-subset-of-USDC claim loses one of the two symbols that made it a strict subset.

nodes.label: F12 Issuance destinations are whitelisted and issuance is rate-limited on-
nodes.text: Issuance destinations are whitelisted and issuance is rate-limited on-chain: increaseSupply, increaseSupplyToAddress, decreaseSupply, decreaseSupplyFromAddress, mint and burn are all mediated by a separate SupplyControl contract at 0x31d9BDeA6f104606c954f8FE6bA614F1bd347Ec3, reached through supplyControl(), carrying the same per-controller RateLimit and mint-address whitelist design as USDG.
nodes.note: Aw is FIRM for the whitelist half (an on-chain predicate on issuance destination). The RATE LIMIT half is RESIDUE: no element names a quantity-and-rate-bounded issuance authority. See the USDG record F5 -- this is the third independent lane arrival at the bounded-delegate-mandate schema (named agent, domain whitelist, magnitude cap, rate-of-change limit, revocation), here on issuance, and the corpus records it for neither Paxos token.

nodes.label: F13 The token is a ZeppelinOS-style proxy at 0x6c3ea9036406852006290770BEd
nodes.text: The token is a ZeppelinOS-style proxy at 0x6c3ea9036406852006290770BEdFcAbA0e23A0e8 with implementation PYUSD at 0x8C35caA5FD5bDc64b6b11344ad57594A3676256a, solc 0.8.28, fully verified 2026-02-09, whose proxy admin 0xc94BcF6E1d8b3558e3b62E743630D50497e3851C is an externally owned account with no code.
nodes.note: Firm fit, with the same X9 question as USDC: Tg is ABSENT, law L15 (Up -> Tg | bounded emergency process) is NOT satisfied, and a single EOA can replace the implementation with no delay. The corpus records armedProhibitions: [] and never computed it against this. Source is MIT at github.com/paxosglobal/pyusd-contract with audits by Trail of Bits (v1) and Zellic and Trail of Bits (PaxosTokenV2); no byte-for-byte repo-to-deployment comparison performed, and no release tag surfaced.

nodes.label: F14 The token's default admin -- which holds reclaimToken(), setSupplyCont
nodes.text: The token's default admin -- which holds reclaimToken(), setSupplyControl() and role administration -- is a bare externally owned account, owner() equal to defaultAdmin() equal to 0x3aF3E85f4f97DE7Ad0F000B724fB77Fe5FFc024b, and the only delay in the system, defaultAdminDelay() of 10800 seconds, applies to TRANSFERRING that role and not to using it.
nodes.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call owner(), defaultAdmin(), defaultAdminDelay() at 0x6c3ea9036406852006290770BEdFcAbA0e23A0e8 and eth_getCode at 0x3aF3E85f4f97DE7Ad0F000B724fB77Fe5FFc024b (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0x8c35caa5fd5bdc64b6b11344ad57594a3676256a (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and Tg is deliberately NOT ASSIGNED. defaultAdminDelay is NOT a timelock: it delays who the admin is, not what the admin does. USDG has both delays (86400 on actions, 10800 on handover); PYUSD has only the second. Assigning Tg here would make the two Paxos tokens look alike on precisely the axis where they differ most -- and that axis is the single sharpest governance difference in the category. Up cannot distinguish 'the key acts slowly' from 'the key acts instantly but changes hands slowly', and this is the instance that proves it matters.

nodes.label: F15 PYUSD shares the Paxos implementation base with USDG -- PaxosTokenV2 o
nodes.text: PYUSD shares the Paxos implementation base with USDG -- PaxosTokenV2 over BaseStorage, EIP2612, EIP3009 and AccessControlDefaultAdminRulesUpgradeable, with the same SupplyControl and RateLimit machinery -- but has NO rewards module and NO facet router.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Two tokens from one issuer on one code base differ by a rewards ledger, a facet router and a timelock, and the model's only way to state the relation between them is to compare element sets after the fact. The intents and yield lanes found the same gap between protocols (containment is inexpressible); here it appears between two instruments sharing a repository, which is the strongest form of it -- the shared base is a fact about the artefacts, and constructions are stated over behaviours.

nodes.label: F16 A holder may authorise transfers by signature: the implementation expo
nodes.text: A holder may authorise transfers by signature: the implementation exposes EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization, receiveWithAuthorization and cancelAuthorization, EIP-2612 permit, and transferFromBatch.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and a NEW ASSIGNMENT the corpus codes for none of the five. Law L17's four terms are satisfied exactly (bounded scope, cancelAuthorization, validAfter/validBefore, nonce under an EIP-712 domain); approximate only against Au's 'session policy' gloss, this being single-shot delegation. Verified from the implementation ABI on 2026-08-04. NOTE ITS LOAD: Au is the ONLY element separating PYUSD's construction from USDT's. Without it the two are set-identical, and the difference it names is that PYUSD's 2024 code post-dates two EIPs that USDT's 2018 Solidity 0.4.18 code pre-dates -- a fact about compiler eras, not about what makes either token worth a dollar.

nodes.label: F17 PYUSD is deployed on five documented mainnets -- Ethereum, Solana, Arb
nodes.text: PYUSD is deployed on five documented mainnets -- Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum, Polygon PoS and X Layer -- each with its own token contract AND its own Supply Control contract address, which is the signature of independent native issuance rather than a bridged representation.
nodes.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE, and the one this lane was asked to make with care: Xf and Xm are REMOVED. The corpus's Xm marker asserts that 'the LayerZero OFT deployment to Solana/Arbitrum is genuine cross-domain messaging'. NO PRIMARY PAXOS STATEMENT OF A LAYERZERO PATH FOR PYUSD WAS FOUND, and the documented picture -- five chains, each with its own token and its own supply controller -- is the signature of native per-chain issuance. Either the corpus is citing a distinct product (PYUSD0) or the claim is stale. Marked UNCONFIRMED in stage 1 and NOT CARRIED here, because carrying a cross-domain mechanism on an unverified premise is exactly the forced fit the contract forbids. The consequence is stated plainly in F18.

nodes.label: F18 With the cross-domain elements withdrawn, PYUSD's on-chain behaviour r
nodes.text: With the cross-domain elements withdrawn, PYUSD's on-chain behaviour reduces to transfer accounting, a permission gate on issuance, a freeze-and-wipe power, a pause, a signed-authorisation family and an upgradeable implementation behind a single key.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, recorded as an obligation because the collapse is itself the finding stage 1 predicted. PYUSD's construction {At, Au, Aw, Fz, Gp, Rd, Up} is a strict superset of USDT's {At, Aw, Fz, Gp, Rd, Up} by exactly one element, Au (F16). Two systems with different obligors, different charters, different reserves, different creditor positions and different seizure powers are separated by whether their compiler era supported EIP-3009. If a stage-3 auditor rejects Au as a forced fit, PYUSD and USDT become SET-IDENTICAL and the category carries three identical pairs rather than one. Either way the finding stands: the vocabulary's resolution in this category is not merely coarse, it discriminates on the wrong axis.

nodes.label: F19 PayPal pays a variable-rate PYUSD reward to eligible US users who hold
nodes.text: PayPal pays a variable-rate PYUSD reward to eligible US users who hold a PYUSD balance in the PayPal app, funded by PayPal as distributor rather than by Paxos as issuer or by any on-chain protocol.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Em rejected (not protocol emissions), Fd rejected (not a surplus distribution by the issuer -- it is marketing spend by the distributor), Ix and Sr rejected (the accrual is a field in PayPal's ledger). The contrast with USDG is the sharpest available test of the vocabulary's boundary: an economically similar payment IS partly on-chain there and earns Fd, Sh and Ep; here the same economics earn nothing. SAME ECONOMICS, DIFFERENT OBSERVABILITY, AND THE VOCABULARY SEES ONE AND NOT THE OTHER. The rate at 2026-08-04 is UNKNOWN from a dated primary quotation and is not carried.

nodes.label: F20 The same instrument is reversible on one side of the custodial boundar
nodes.text: The same instrument is reversible on one side of the custodial boundary and final on the other: dispute reversal and chargeback exist as primitives in PayPal's ledger and cannot exist in the token.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Nothing in the model can express an instrument whose FINALITY DEPENDS ON WHICH LEDGER YOU ARE LOOKING AT. The corpus names chargeback semantics as residue; the sharper statement is that the wrapper must support a forced reversal the token cannot, so the consumer product and the on-chain product are different instruments that share a unit of account.

nodes.label: F21 PayPal itself holds PYUSD on its own balance sheet, carried at amortis
nodes.text: PayPal itself holds PYUSD on its own balance sheet, carried at amortised cost and classified alongside cash and cash equivalents.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. The distributor is also a holder, and a large one, and its accounting treatment of the instrument is a public statement about what it believes the instrument is. No element names a party's position in the token it distributes, nor the reflexivity that follows.

nodes.label: F22 On-chain the token is plain balance accounting: 6 decimals and Ethereu
