nodes.text: On-chain the token is plain balance accounting: 6 decimals and Ethereum supply 1,832,790,045.376448 at 2026-08-04, against the corpus's US$2.68B all-chain figure.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, as at USDT F12: Sh, Ix and Rb name three ways a claim's value can move and none names a claim whose value does not move. The attested outstanding could not be retrieved (F6), so the on-chain Ethereum leg is the only figure this record can assert, and it is 68% of the corpus's all-chain number.

nodes.label: Tether USDT
F1 USDT is a transferable receipt for an unsecured, on-demand claim again
nodes.text: USDT is a transferable receipt for an unsecured, on-demand claim against a single private company, Tether International, S.A. de C.V., incorporated in El Salvador and authorised by the Comision Nacional de Activos Digitales under DASP registration PSAD-0028; the attested accounts classify the outstanding tokens as a refund liability under IFRS 9.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the category headline. There is no symbol for 'an El Salvadoran S.A. de C.V. owes you', none for the obligor at all, and none for creditor priority against it. The single most decision-relevant fact about USDT -- that the instrument is an unsecured refund liability of a private company -- is stated in the auditor's own classification and has no name in the 58. CORPUS CORRECTION: the corpus records the obligor as 'Tether Limited'; the customer-facing issuer at the 2026-02-20 RID is Tether International, S.A. de C.V., and the BDO opinion is addressed to that entity and no other.

nodes.label: F2 The claim is to face value only: holders are not entitled to any incre
nodes.text: The claim is to face value only: holders are not entitled to any increase in the value of the reserves in excess of the face value of the tokens, so the reserve surplus of US$4,109,529,196 at 2026-06-30 belongs to the shareholder and the holder is senior at par with no upside.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Tr (tranche waterfall) was considered and REJECTED, and the reason is worth stage 4's attention: this is a declared seniority over a loss event -- a one-line waterfall with holders at par and the shareholder taking the residual -- and law L6's own terms for Tr (declared seniority, dispute forum, recovery-timing assumption) are all satisfiable off-chain. USDT supplies two of the three (seniority; BVI-law arbitration seated in London). Tr is withheld only because no mechanism executes the waterfall: it is a sentence in a PDF and an insolvency outcome. The vocabulary offers no way to distinguish a declared seniority from an enforced one.

nodes.label: F3 The right to present the claim is not a property of holding the token:
nodes.text: The right to present the claim is not a property of holding the token: only 819 KYC Verified Customers may redeem, as of 2026-02-16, against a holder base of hundreds of millions; everyone else holds a bearer instrument whose only exit is the secondary market.
nodes.note: BOTH APPROXIMATE. Rd asserts a 'direct redemption right' and is silent on who holds it; here it is held by 819 named counterparties and by nobody else, so the symbol is true of the system and false of essentially every holder -- the same defect the bridges lane recorded for WBTC's 47 merchants. Aw is a CORPUS DEPARTURE: the corpus assigns Aw to USDC alone, on the reasoning that 'the gate is on Circle Mint access'. Tether's gate is identical in kind (KYC Verified Customer status, sole issuer discretion to reject) and was not coded. Either all five carry Aw or none does; this lane carries it in all five and marks it approximate wherever the gate is an off-chain business relationship rather than an on-chain check. Law L16 (Aw -> transfer-time enforcement where eligibility follows the holder) is NOT satisfied: USDT transfers are permissionless.

nodes.label: F4 Redemption carries a minimum of US$100,000 and a fee of the greater of
nodes.text: Redemption carries a minimum of US$100,000 and a fee of the greater of US$1,000 or 0.1%, settles by fiat wire to the customer's bank account, and has no published settlement-time commitment -- the lifecycle is six steps with no service level.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. Rd carries no minimum, no fee and no latency, and those three parameters are what actually decide whether the peg holds under stress. Redemption latency is UNKNOWN as a contractual matter -- the issuer commits to no bound. Wq (withdrawal queue) was considered and rejected: there is no queue, on-chain or stated; there is an unbounded discretionary process.

nodes.label: F5 The issuer may delay or suspend redemption where it determines a Prohi
nodes.text: The issuer may delay or suspend redemption where it determines a Prohibited Use, where directed by any government, where the account is under investigation, or on suspicion of fraud, and maintains sole discretion to approve or reject applications to become a customer at all.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Sv (servicing & determination discretion, candidate) was considered and REJECTED: Sv names a servicer's discretion over the performance status of an instrument whose determination feeds a state transition the model can see. Here the discretion is the obligor's own, over its own performance, exercised off-chain, unobservable and unfalsifiable. Flagged for stage 4 as the nearest existing candidate if 'obligor discretion to refuse performance' is to be given a home -- it would require broadening Sv from servicer to obligor.

nodes.label: F6 The reserve at 2026-06-30 is US$187,751,426,411 of total assets agains
nodes.text: The reserve at 2026-06-30 is US$187,751,426,411 of total assets against US$183,641,897,215 of liabilities, of which US$183,622,105,630 is digital tokens issued: US$114.96bn of Treasury bills under 90 days, US$25.62bn of repo, US$18.84bn of LBMA gold bars, US$5.80bn of bitcoin, US$3.76bn of public equities, US$5.24bn of other investments and US$13.45bn of secured loans.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, confirmed against the corpus's own residue list and sharper than it. Nothing in the 58 distinguishes US$114.96bn of sub-90-day T-bills from US$18.84bn of gold bars from US$13.45bn of over-collateralised secured loans, and that difference is the entire instrument. At names the PDF that describes the reserve; there is no symbol for the reserve. This is the strongest single instance in the project of the claim that everything determining whether the token is worth a dollar sits outside the model.

nodes.label: F7 Cash and bank deposits are US$40,307,440, which is 0.02% of the reserv
nodes.text: Cash and bank deposits are US$40,307,440, which is 0.02% of the reserve, and roughly US$23.6bn (12.6%) is gold, bitcoin, equities, other investments and secured loans -- assets whose realisable value in a redemption run is a judgement.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Prohibition X5 ('illiquid backing + uncapped instant par redemption') and law L14 ('illiquid backing -> Wq | bounded liquidity reserve') both quantify over a predicate -- 'illiquid backing' -- that no element of the vocabulary can evaluate, because the backing is not in the model. The corpus records armedProhibitions: [] for USDT; the honest statement is not that X5 is unarmed but that it is UNDECIDABLE in this carrier. That is a finding about the tables, not about Tether.

nodes.label: F8 No bank, depositary or custodian is named anywhere in the primary reco
nodes.text: No bank, depositary or custodian is named anywhere in the primary record: the offering document says only that the issuer 'primarily holds the Reserves with various third parties including banks and licensed financial institutions', and the assurance report names none.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and now unobservable as well as unnameable. The corpus lists banking and correspondent relationships as residue because the historical failure mode was a banking failure; at 2026-08-04 the primary documents do not name a single counterparty, so the fact is not merely unrepresentable in the model, it is unavailable to any modeller. Named banking and custody relationships: UNKNOWN from primary sources.

nodes.label: F9 Assurance is quarterly and is an ISAE 3000 (Revised) reasonable-assura
nodes.text: Assurance is quarterly and is an ISAE 3000 (Revised) reasonable-assurance engagement by BDO Advisory Services S.r.l., Milan, partner Lelio Bigogno, dated 2026-07-31, on the Financial Figures and Reserves Report as of 2026-06-30 23:59 UTC, with procedures including bank and depositary confirmation letters, third-party inventory and assay testing of precious metals on a sample basis, blockchain-to-ledger reconciliation and collateral verification on a sample of secured loans.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. Against law L27 (At -> named attester + independence + stated assurance + staleness bound + recourse) this satisfies three of five: named attester yes, independence yes, stated assurance level yes and at the highest available (reasonable assurance is the assurance level of an audit opinion). Staleness bound: no -- the cadence is quarterly by practice, not by covenant, and the report is point-in-time. Recourse: none. CORPUS CORRECTION: the corpus flags 'attestation vs audit' as the interesting distinction; it is not. The engagement is reasonable assurance. The interesting gap is F10.

nodes.label: F10 The attester expressly declines the solvency judgement: no assurance i
nodes.text: The attester expressly declines the solvency judgement: no assurance is given on the going-concern assessment, the Notes are outside the engagement, and the valuations 'do not reflect unexpected and extraordinary market conditions, or the case of key custodians or counterparties experiencing substantial illiquidity'.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a first-class one. At has no place to record what the attester REFUSED to say. Reasonable assurance on a schedule of assets says nothing about whether the entity can pay, and the auditor says so in terms. A model that carries At and not its carve-outs records the strongest possible signal about the reserve while discarding the explicit statement that the signal does not cover the question the reader is asking.

nodes.label: F11 The regulator is El Salvador's CNAD; disputes are routed to confidenti
nodes.text: The regulator is El Salvador's CNAD; disputes are routed to confidential BVI-law arbitration seated in London before a sole arbitrator; there is no deposit insurance, no trust, no stated security interest and no segregation covenant.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No symbol for a supervising authority, for what it may order, or for a dispute forum. Compare USDG, whose white paper names the District Court of Helsinki: 'who do you sue' is answerable for three of the five and unrepresentable for all five.

nodes.label: F12 On-chain the token is plain balance accounting: TetherToken at 0xdAC17
nodes.text: On-chain the token is plain balance accounting: TetherToken at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, Solidity 0.4.18, 6 decimals, Ethereum supply 92,056,579,574.486405 at 2026-08-04, inheriting Pausable, StandardToken and BlackList from a single Ownable with no role separation whatsoever.
nodes.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call totalSupply(), paused(), owner() at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE of a kind the corpus does not record at all. The claims-and-accounting group offers Sh (pro-rata pool share), Ix (index accrual) and Rb (rebasing); a fixed-unit transferable balance is none of the three, and it is what every member of this category actually is. The vocabulary can name three ways a claim's value can move and has no name for a claim whose value does not move.

nodes.label: F13 Issuance and destruction are treasury operations, not user-facing: iss
nodes.text: Issuance and destruction are treasury operations, not user-facing: issue(uint) and redeem(uint) are onlyOwner and mint to and burn from the owner's own balance; no contract function observes, values or is constrained by the reserve, and the contract contains no reference to a reserve.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a CORPUS DEPARTURE. Ps (peg-swap module, 1:1 reserve-backed) is DROPPED from this construction. The corpus carried Ps and marked it forced; carrying it imputes an on-chain 1:1 reserve mechanism that does not exist -- there is no module, no reserve object, no swap and no counter-asset. The bridges lane rejected Ps on identical reasoning for WBTC ('no on-chain module holding a reserve to swap 1:1 against'); this lane applies the same test and drops Ps from ALL FIVE members of the category. Under the project's standing rule that a finding of failure beats a forced fit, the honest record is that the category's defining behaviour -- one token, one dollar -- is discharged by no element.

nodes.label: F14 The issuer can freeze and irreversibly destroy any balance: addBlackLi
nodes.text: The issuer can freeze and irreversibly destroy any balance: addBlackList(address), removeBlackList(address) and destroyBlackFunds(address) are onlyOwner, the last emitting DestroyedBlackFunds; there is no forced transfer, only destruction.
nodes.note: CANDIDATE REGISTER, used with a note as the contract requires. Fz is 'freeze / forced transfer' and collapses three distinct powers with three distinct consequences for a holder: freeze (your balance is immobilised and still yours), seize-and-destroy (your balance ceases to exist), and forced transfer (your balance moves to an address chosen by someone else). USDT has freeze and destroy and NOT forced transfer; USD1 has all three; PYUSD has freeze and destroy; USDC has freeze with a three-state liability. Fz is true of all four and separates none of them.

nodes.label: F15 The trigger for freezing is a law-enforcement, regulatory or governmen
nodes.text: The trigger for freezing is a law-enforcement, regulatory or government request, and the issuer reserves the right to freeze tokens in external wallets for which it does not hold private keys; the issuer claims cooperation with more than 340 agencies in 65 countries and more than US$4.4bn frozen since launch, including more than US$344M across two addresses in coordination with OFAC on 2026-04-23.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Law L28 requires of Fz a named authority, enumerated triggers, an appeal path and holder disclosure. USDT satisfies NONE of the four in a machine-checkable way: the authority is 'any government', the triggers are open-ended, there is no appeal path and no disclosure obligation. These are issuer claims and are not independently attested; a machine-counted total of blacklisted addresses is UNKNOWN (a full eth_getLogs sweep of AddedBlackList was rate-limited off public RPC in stage 1). The corpus's own marker cites '2,000+ blacklisted addresses'; that figure is not reproducible from a primary source and this construction does not carry it.

nodes.label: F16 The issuer can halt every transfer globally: pause() and unpause() are
nodes.text: The issuer can halt every transfer globally: pause() and unpause() are onlyOwner; paused() reads false at 2026-08-04.
nodes.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Gp is ADDED. The corpus assigns Gp to USDC alone. pause() and unpause() are present in the verified ABI of all five deployed tokens and live under a named authority in every one; verified for this contract by reading the Blockscout ABI on 2026-08-04, which lists pause and unpause. This single correction breaks the corpus's claimed identity USDT = USD1 with USDC's set and changes four of the five decompositions. It is a coding artefact, not a design difference.

nodes.label: F17 The owner can impose a fee on every transfer of the instrument: setPar
nodes.text: The owner can impose a fee on every transfer of the instrument: setParams(uint newBasisPoints, uint newMaxFee) sets a per-transfer basis-point rate capped by maximumFee; both read zero at 2026-08-04.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, new -- not in the corpus. Fd (surplus & fee distribution) was considered and REJECTED: this is a levy on holders with no distribution rule attached, not a distribution of surplus. The deeper gap is that no symbol names a LATENT mechanism. The vocabulary is a vocabulary of what is, not of what is armed, and the distinction between 'absent' and 'set to zero by a 3-of-6 key that can change it in one transaction' is the whole risk on a US$92bn Ethereum-side float. The same gap recurs at USD1 (a null but installable compliance checker) and at USDG (capabilities that exist only while a facet table maps their selectors).

nodes.label: F18 The upgrade path is a forwarding deprecation rather than a proxy: depr
nodes.text: The upgrade path is a forwarding deprecation rather than a proxy: deprecate(address _upgradedAddress) sets deprecated = true and forwards transfer, transferFrom, balanceOf, approve and allowance to a new contract implementing UpgradedStandardToken, leaving storage behind; deprecated() reads false at 2026-08-04.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. Up is 'mutable implementation proxy'; this is not a proxy. Only five entry points forward, storage stays in the old contract, and the failure surface is different in kind -- partial forwarding and stale views rather than wholesale replacement. Up cannot distinguish a transparent proxy (USDC, PYUSD), an EIP-1967 proxy with a separate ProxyAdmin (USD1), a UUPS proxy with a facet router under it (USDG) and a five-function forwarding deprecation (USDT), and those are four different things to hold.

nodes.label: F19 Mint, burn, freeze, destroy, pause, the transfer-fee dial and the upgr
nodes.text: Mint, burn, freeze, destroy, pause, the transfer-fee dial and the upgrade are all onlyOwner and owner() is one address, 0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828, a MultiSigWallet with 6 owners and required() == 3, with no timelock of any kind.
nodes.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call owner() at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, getOwners() and required() at 0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828 (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the bridges lane's finding exhibited again on a larger instrument. Every control element in the vocabulary names a FACILITY -- Tg a delay, Up a proxy, Gp a pause -- and none names WHO HOLDS IT OR HOW MANY OF THEM THERE ARE. Here seven distinct powers are one 3-of-6 key. Tg is correctly absent (there is no delay) and its absence is indistinguishable from not having looked. Prohibition X9 ('Up with immediate single-key control') does NOT fire on a 3-of-6, which means the tables treat a three-signature immediate upgrade of a US$92bn instrument as unremarkable; the axis that matters is quorum against single key, and the carrier has no party sort in which to state it.

nodes.label: F20 Supply moves between Ethereum, Tron, Solana, Avalanche, TON and other
nodes.text: Supply moves between Ethereum, Tron, Solana, Avalanche, TON and other chains by the issuer burning on one and issuing on another under off-chain authorisation, over a chain set determined by the issuer alone; there is no bridge contract, no message and no verifier in this path.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Xf and Xm are explicitly NOT assigned and must not be: there is no lock, no proof, no verifier set, no threshold and no message -- an employee burns here and issues there. This is the same negative finding the bridges lane recorded for the custodial wrappers, and it is the correct reading of the corpus's own residue line. It also isolates the real cross-domain difference in this category: USDC (CCTP) and USD1 (Chainlink CCIP) run verified burn-and-mint; USDT runs operator fiat; USDG and PYUSD are UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F21 The issuer's answer to United States regulation was to create a differ
nodes.text: The issuer's answer to United States regulation was to create a different token with a different obligor: USAT, launched 2026-01-27, issued by Anchorage Digital Bank under OCC supervision with Cantor Fitzgerald as reserve custodian under the GENIUS Act, with separate reserves, separate issuance and separate redemption rails from USDT.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No relation between two issuances by one corporate group is expressible in the carrier -- the same containment gap the intents and yield lanes found between protocols, here between instruments of a single issuer. It matters because the regulatory regime a token may legally exist under is chosen by picking which token to hold, and the model cannot state that two tokens are siblings, let alone that one is the compliant sibling of the other.

nodes.label: F22 There is no canonical public source repository: the authority for USDT
nodes.text: There is no canonical public source repository: the authority for USDT-on-Ethereum is the verified bytecode, verified on Blockscout on 2019-04-18 as a partial (metadata-hash) match with no license declared, and the only GitHub artefact is an unofficial three-commit mirror that itself points back to a block explorer.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. No element names the correspondence, or its absence, between published source and deployed bytecode. The spot-exchange lane found the converse failure -- two artefacts sharing a version string and implementing different mathematics -- and the two together say the same thing: the model identifies a protocol by its element set and has no way to identify the artefact the element set was read from.

nodes.label: World Liberty Financial USD1
F1 The obligor is not the brand: the June 2026 examination states that US
nodes.text: The obligor is not the brand: the June 2026 examination states that USD1 is issued and redeemed by BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A., a national trust bank chartered and supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, while the USD1 brand and certain associated trademarks are owned and controlled by World Liberty Financial, Inc. and SC Financial Technologies, LLC.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a CORPUS CORRECTION that changes the instrument's category. The corpus treats World Liberty Financial as the issuer with 'reserves custodied at BitGo'. The attested position is that an OCC-supervised national trust bank issues and redeems, and WLF owns the brand. Every residue item beginning 'the issuer as obligor' must be re-pointed. Separately, the separation of brand-owner from obligor is itself a fact with no symbol: no element can say that the party whose name is on the token is not the party that owes you.

nodes.label: F2 The claim is contractual and confers no interest in any asset: 'USD1 h
nodes.text: The claim is contractual and confers no interest in any asset: 'USD1 holders' redemption rights are contractual and do not constitute a security interest in, or direct property interest in, any specific reserve asset.'
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and the single most important sentence in the USD1 record. It is the answer to 'what happens if the issuer cannot pay', it is the OPPOSITE of Circle's bare-legal-title property assertion and the OPPOSITE of Paxos's segregated-trust priority claim, and all three are At in the model. Against that, the assets sit in segregated FBO accounts at an OCC-supervised trust bank, which makes the holder's position materially better than USDT's and materially worse than the property claim USDC asserts. Three positions on one axis, one symbol.

nodes.label: F3 Only registered customers of the issuer in Good Standing may mint or r
nodes.text: Only registered customers of the issuer in Good Standing may mint or redeem; persons who hold USD1 without an account are 'Users' who may transfer USD1 on supported networks but do not have direct redemption rights with the Company.
nodes.note: BOTH APPROXIMATE. Rd asserts a right the attestation expressly denies to non-account holders. Aw is a CORPUS DEPARTURE, added on the corpus's own USDC reasoning (Clients in Good Standing versus Users). CORPUS CORRECTION to the Rd marker: the corpus says 'institutional-only, contractual, discretionary'. Contractual and discretionary are right; 'institutional-only' is NOT stated -- the terms say registered customers in Good Standing, which is a KYC and sanctions test, not an institutional test. Law L16 is not satisfied: transfers are permissionless.

nodes.label: F4 No redemption minimum, fee schedule or settlement time is published: t
nodes.text: No redemption minimum, fee schedule or settlement time is published: the governing terms describe only submission through the issuer's platform, compliance review, and settlement timing.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Minimum, fee and latency are UNKNOWN from the primary documents reachable in stage 1, and are not repaired from press or aggregators. The gap matters for the same reason it matters at USDT: the three parameters that decide whether the peg holds under stress are neither in the model nor, here, in the public record.

nodes.label: F5 The reserve at 2026-06-30 is US$4,634,586,966 against 4,634,410,387 re
nodes.text: The reserve at 2026-06-30 is US$4,634,586,966 against 4,634,410,387 redeemable tokens outstanding -- a surplus of US$176,579 -- held as US$1,178,613,044 in demand deposit accounts and US$3,455,973,922 in a government money market fund at NAV under CUSIP 31607A703, with zero in the issuer's own bank account.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, with a qualification the corpus gets backwards. USD1's reserve is NARROWER than the corpus implies -- 'reserve portfolio (custodied at BitGo)' suggests a portfolio; it is bank deposits plus one government money market fund, with no directly held Treasuries, no repo, no gold and no loans. The vocabulary cannot express that USD1's reserve is nameable in one line where Tether's takes a table, and that difference is the difference between a boring instrument and an interesting one. CUSIP 31607A703 resolves to the Fidelity Investments Money Market Government Portfolio per third-party securities reference; the fund is NOT named in the attestation and this identification is not an issuer claim.

nodes.label: F6 Cash sits in demand-deposit and money-market-deposit accounts at US co
nodes.text: Cash sits in demand-deposit and money-market-deposit accounts at US commercial banks regulated by the Federal Reserve, in segregated accounts titled to BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. for the benefit of USD1 stablecoin holders, with the attestation noting that balances at times may exceed the FDIC limit of US$250,000; no bank is named.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Two unnameable facts in one sentence: which banks hold the cash (UNKNOWN), and that the deposit insurance which is the retail reader's mental model of 'a bank account' does not reach the balance. The FDIC-limit caveat is the issuer telling you, in the attestation, that the segregation is legal rather than insured -- and At has no slot for a caveat.

nodes.label: F7 Eligible reserve assets are contractually limited to cash, cash equiva
nodes.text: Eligible reserve assets are contractually limited to cash, cash equivalents, short-term US Treasuries, fully Treasury-collateralised reverse repurchase agreements and government money market funds.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. A rule that FORBIDS the issuer from holding certain assets is a constraint on the reserve, and the reserve has no representation, so the constraint has nothing to bind. This is the single largest design difference between USD1 and USDT -- an enforceable eligible-asset list against a discretionary portfolio containing gold, bitcoin, equities and secured loans -- and both decompose with At.

nodes.label: F8 The issuer is also the custodian: BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. issues, red
nodes.text: The issuer is also the custodian: BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. issues, redeems and holds the reserve.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, and a CORRECTION to the corpus's framing. The corpus records custody as a distinct residue on the ground that no element distinguishes 'issuer holds reserves' from 'custodian holds reserves for issuer'. True -- and here the distinction COLLAPSES, because one entity is both, which is a third case the vocabulary also cannot record. Compare USDC, where manager (BlackRock) and custodian (BNY) are two further separate parties.

nodes.label: F9 Assurance is a monthly examination by KPMG LLP, San Francisco, of the
nodes.text: Assurance is a monthly examination by KPMG LLP, San Francisco, of the issuer's management assertion, signed 2026-07-31, under AICPA attestation standards against the AICPA 2025 Criteria for Stablecoin Reporting: Specific to Asset-Backed Fiat-Pegged Tokens, Part I, at two report dates per month, with reports published back to April 2025.
nodes.note: The best L27 fit of the five, and still incomplete: named attester yes, independence yes, stated assurance yes, and uniquely a NAMED PUBLIC CRITERIA SET against which the assertion is examined. Staleness bound: cadence by practice, not covenant. Recourse: none. At cannot record that this examination is against the AICPA 2025 stablecoin criteria while USDT's is an ISAE 3000R engagement on a bespoke schedule and USDG's is under Singapore ISCA standards -- three incomparable subject matters under one symbol.

nodes.label: F10 The seizure machinery is armed and, at the report date, unused: the Ju
nodes.text: The seizure machinery is armed and, at the report date, unused: the June 2026 report records that with respect to USD1 there are no time-locked tokens, test tokens, or access-restricted tokens in the reporting period.
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Fz is a capability predicate and cannot record exercise. 'The power exists and has never been used' and 'the power exists and 2,000 addresses are frozen' produce identical decompositions, and USD1 and USDT are respectively those two cases. This is the same defect as USDT F17's latent fee dial seen from the other side: the vocabulary cannot say armed-and-unused any more than it can say installed-but-dormant.

nodes.label: F11 A freezer may immobilise an address, and the freeze predicate is check
nodes.text: A freezer may immobilise an address, and the freeze predicate is checked in _transfer and _approve against from, to AND msg.sender, so freezing an address also disables it as a spender of other people's allowances.
nodes.note: CANDIDATE REGISTER, used with a note. RESIDUE WITHIN THE ASSIGNMENT: no symbol distinguishes freezing a BALANCE from freezing an ACTOR. Freezing a relayer or a market-maker contract here disables it for every counterparty who has approved it, which is a blast radius Fz cannot express.

nodes.label: F12 The owner may seize a frozen balance in full: drain(address) requires
nodes.text: The owner may seize a frozen balance in full: drain(address) requires the account to be frozen and moves its entire balance to owner(), emitting FrozenAccountDrained.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE. This is confiscation, not freezing. Fz names it identically to USDT's destroy (which annihilates rather than seizes) and to USDC's blacklist (which does neither). Three consequences for a holder -- immobilised, annihilated, transferred to the issuer -- one symbol.

nodes.label: F13 The owner may forcibly re-assign a frozen balance to a different addre
nodes.text: The owner may forcibly re-assign a frozen balance to a different address: reallocate(address _from, address _to, uint256 _amount) requires _from to be frozen and transfers to a replacement account, emitting FrozenFundsReallocated.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and the sharpest instance of Fz's collapse. The intended use is key-loss recovery -- re-issuing a holder's own position to a new address -- which is a FORCED TRANSFER WITH A BENIGN PURPOSE, and it is indistinguishable in the vocabulary from confiscation. USD1 holds all three powers (freeze, drain, reallocate); PYUSD holds two (freeze, wipe); USDT holds two (freeze, destroy); USDC holds one. Fz is present on all four.

nodes.label: F14 A pauser may halt all transfers: pause() and unpause() are present in
nodes.text: A pauser may halt all transfers: pause() and unpause() are present in the verified implementation and held by PAUSER_ROLE and UNPAUSER_ROLE in the governor; paused() reads false at 2026-08-04.
nodes.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Gp is ADDED. Verified in the implementation ABI on 2026-08-04 (pause, unpause both present) and separated into two roles in the governor, which is finer than any other member of the five. Adding Gp here and at USDT is what breaks the corpus's claimed identity USDT = USD1 against USDC's set.

nodes.label: F15 The token is an EIP-1967 transparent proxy at 0x8d0D000Ee44948FC98c9B9
nodes.text: The token is an EIP-1967 transparent proxy at 0x8d0D000Ee44948FC98c9B98A4FA4921476f08B0d with implementation StablecoinV2 at 0x694aA534BdeF8Ed63244eb902E7914e527891F08 (solc 0.8.24, fully verified 2026-04-05) and a separate ProxyAdmin at 0xa032Fe6C496732bdfc0d235066F55f171FA4aecE.
nodes.note: Firm fit. There is no public source repository for StablecoinV2 or TokenGovernor and neither declares a license; the canonical artefact is the fully verified deployed source, matched by metadata hash. 'Deployed matches a repo' is not applicable -- there is no repo -- which is a third case beside 'matches' and 'does not match' that no element records.

nodes.label: F16 Upgrade authority and token authority are held by two different quorum
nodes.text: Upgrade authority and token authority are held by two different quorums with no delay on either: the ProxyAdmin's owner is a Gnosis Safe at 0x6a8dc6dbf909f542f2536edf8676d52630cf59e1 with 5 owners and threshold 3, while the token's owner is TokenGovernor at 0xEE9b1a09aEdaCED9dCDa74964EA447FEB93861c2 whose DEFAULT_ADMIN is a different Safe at 0x0d190b74308669e8f4fe7dbce3466169b285289d with 6 owners and threshold 3.
nodes.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xee9b1a09aedaced9dcda74964ea447feb93861c2 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call of the EIP-1967 admin slot at 0x8d0D000Ee44948FC98c9B98A4FA4921476f08B0d, owner() on the ProxyAdmin, and getThreshold()/getOwners() on both Safes (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Tg is correctly ABSENT -- neither Safe has a timelock -- so law L15 is NOT satisfied, exactly as at USDC and PYUSD. The separation of upgrade authority from token authority into two distinct 3-of-N quorums is a real and deliberate control-plane design and the carrier has no party sort in which to state it. Prohibition X9 does not fire on a 3-of-N, so the tables again treat a three-signature immediate upgrade as unremarkable.

nodes.label: F17 Token authority is decomposed into nine named roles in TokenGovernor -
nodes.text: Token authority is decomposed into nine named roles in TokenGovernor -- MINTER_ROLE, BRIDGE_MINTER_OR_BURNER_ROLE, BURNER_ROLE, FREEZER_ROLE, UNFREEZER_ROLE, PAUSER_ROLE, UNPAUSER_ROLE, RECOVERY_ROLE and CHECKER_ADMIN_ROLE -- with DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE reserved for drainFrozenAccount, batchDrainFrozenAccounts and executeTokenFunction; minters and burners are the admin Safe plus two further addresses, freezers the admin Safe plus one, pausers the admin Safe plus one.
nodes.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xee9b1a09aedaced9dcda74964ea447feb93861c2 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getAdmins(), getMinters(), getBurners(), getFreezers(), getPausers(), getBridgeMintersOrBurners(), getChecker() at 0xEE9b1a09aEdaCED9dCDa74964EA447FEB93861c2 (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. This is the finest-grained control plane of the five -- freeze and unfreeze are separate roles, pause and unpause are separate roles -- and the model records exactly Fz and Gp for it, the same two symbols it records for USDT's single 3-of-6 key. The vocabulary's resolution on the control plane is one bit per facility, and the category's real variation is entirely inside that bit.

nodes.label: F18 A compliance checker can be installed at any time and is not installed
nodes.text: A compliance checker can be installed at any time and is not installed: TokenGovernor exposes setChecker() for an IChecker, and getChecker() reads the zero address at 2026-08-04.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, new -- not in the corpus. A transfer-time permission gate is ABSENT BUT ONE TRANSACTION AWAY. Aw is correctly not assigned for this (the gate does not exist today), and the vocabulary has no way to record that it is armed. The same shape recurs three times in this category: USDT's zero-valued but owner-settable transfer fee, this null-but-installable checker, and USDG's capabilities that exist only while an admin-controlled dispatch table maps their selectors. That is a category-level gap: THE VOCABULARY DESCRIBES WHAT IS, NOT WHAT IS ARMED.

nodes.label: F19 Ownership cannot be dropped: renounceOwnership() reverts.
nodes.text: Ownership cannot be dropped: renounceOwnership() reverts.
nodes.note: RESIDUE of the kind the options lane named: this is a guarantee discharged BY CONSTRUCTION -- the state 'no owner' cannot arise -- and the requirement language admits only discharge by naming a satisfying element. A deliberately permanent control plane and an unexamined one produce the same record.

nodes.label: F20 USD1 moves between chains by burning and minting under Chainlink CCIP,
nodes.text: USD1 moves between chains by burning and minting under Chainlink CCIP, corroborated on-chain by a dedicated BRIDGE_MINTER_OR_BURNER_ROLE held by two addresses, 0xf9e47d3720d5142930444ae6773c7f6d05696228 and 0x36a72ed0096b414521c45e3ddc9ed657d1d9c141, over native issuance on Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, Tron, Aptos and Tempo and eleven documented deployments.
nodes.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Xf and Xm are ADDED. The corpus says explicitly 'the token is deployed natively on multiple chains by the issuer, again not Xf'. That is now wrong on both the documentation and the chain: burn-and-mint over a message-verifying protocol is Xf plus Xm, and the code itself agrees -- a bridge mint/burn role would not exist if bridge-driven supply were not a distinct authority. This is genuine MECHANISM and it is the second refutation of the claim that every symbol these five use is control-plane or attestation.

nodes.label: F21 Bridge-driven supply is a different authority from treasury-driven sup
nodes.text: Bridge-driven supply is a different authority from treasury-driven supply: BRIDGE_MINTER_OR_BURNER_ROLE is separate from MINTER_ROLE and BURNER_ROLE and is held by different addresses.
nodes.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xee9b1a09aedaced9dcda74964ea447feb93861c2 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call getMinters(), getBurners(), getBridgeMintersOrBurners() at 0xEE9b1a09aEdaCED9dCDa74964EA447FEB93861c2 (accessed 2026-08-04)
nodes.note: RESIDUE. Xf does not distinguish supply created against an incoming cross-domain message from supply created against an incoming wire, and this deployment separates them explicitly in code because they are different risks. The corpus's cross-domain group names the movement and not the authority behind it.

nodes.label: F22 A holder may authorise transfers by signature: the implementation expo
nodes.text: A holder may authorise transfers by signature: the implementation exposes EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization, receiveWithAuthorization, cancelAuthorization and batchCancelAuthorization together with EIP-2612 permit.
nodes.note: APPROXIMATE, and a NEW ASSIGNMENT the corpus codes for none of the five. Law L17's four terms are satisfied exactly -- bounded scope (one amount, one payee), revocation (cancelAuthorization, and uniquely a batch form), expiry (validAfter/validBefore) and nonce plus EIP-712 domain separation. Approximate only against Au's 'session policy' gloss: this is single-shot delegation. Verified from the implementation ABI on 2026-08-04.

nodes.label: F23 The token has 18 decimals rather than the category's usual 6, and Ethe
nodes.text: The token has 18 decimals rather than the category's usual 6, and Ethereum supply is 1,529,515,526.739243049392059492 at 2026-08-04 against attested all-chain outstanding of 4,634,410,387 across six chains, of which BNB Smart Chain is the larger leg at 1,802,654,137.
nodes.note: RESIDUE, as at USDT F12: no element names a fixed-unit balance. RANKING BASIS NOTE: attested outstanding is 4,634,410,387 against the corpus's DefiLlama US$4.00B; the Ethereum leg alone is 1.53bn, so a single-chain reading understates by roughly three times. Decimals differ from every other member of the five and nothing in the model records the unit.

nodes.label: 12-prediction
Azuro
F1 a bettor's position is a transferable NFT carrying a payout struck aga
nodes.text: a bettor's position is a transferable NFT carrying a payout struck against the pool; no operation splits pool collateral into complementary outcome claims and none recombines them
nodes.note: residue, and the third answer this category gives to the first structural claim. Polymarket implements a state partition (polymarket.json F1), Kalshi implements a price identity (kalshi.json F3), and Azuro implements neither: the contingent claim is one-sided and unitary, the pool holds the other side implicitly, and there is no object to split or merge. `Py` splits along time and does not apply; nothing in the 58 names a one-sided tokenised contingent claim on a pool either.

nodes.label: F2 a single protocol-wide liquidity pool is the counterparty to every bet
nodes.text: a single protocol-wide liquidity pool is the counterparty to every bet, writing a non-linear event-contingent payoff, so no bettor ever faces another bettor
nodes.note: residue, confirming the corpus. `Pl` is lending; `Cv` requires adjudicated claims against pooled premium; `Op` requires a strike and an expiry. Note the relation to the category's second structural claim: this is the third clearing form in five applications — a pool that is principal to every trade with no novation and no substitution — and the vocabulary names none of the three.

nodes.label: F3 the price of an outcome is the normalised inverse of the pool's virtua
nodes.text: the price of an outcome is the normalised inverse of the pool's virtual fund for that outcome, loaded with a spread allocated inversely to the outcome's probability under a total-margin constraint, and every bet moves the virtual funds so the odds worsen against incoming flow
nodes.note: residue, confirming the corpus. The closed form is published: o_i = sum(F)/F_i, p_i = 1/o_i, s_i = 1 - p_i*o_i with s_i/s_j = p_j/p_i, and the update F_i <- F_i - a with the other funds scaled by their share. None of `Cp`, `Wg`, `St`, `Cl` or `Pm` describes it, because all five price an ASSET against another asset or against an external reference and this prices a STATE against the pool's own exposure. The virtual funds are pricing parameters deliberately decoupled from the pool's real balance, so the curve is not even a function of the inventory it claims to represent.

nodes.label: F4 the odds struck at the moment of the bet are locked for that bettor an
nodes.text: the odds struck at the moment of the bet are locked for that bettor and fix the payout, while the curve continues to move for everyone after
nodes.note: residue. payout = o_i * (1 - s_i) * a, fixed at bet time. There is no symbol for a quoted-and-locked payoff drawn from a continuously repriced pool; `Rf` (request for quote) names a signed maker quote in a bilateral trade, not a quote struck against a pool's own moving curve, and `Op` requires a strike and an expiry rather than a struck price.

nodes.label: F5 each Condition reserves a fixed Reinforcement of pool liquidity at cre
nodes.text: each Condition reserves a fixed Reinforcement of pool liquidity at creation, immutable thereafter, which both seeds the outcome pricing and bounds the pool's worst-case loss on that Condition so simultaneous events cannot oversubscribe the same capital
nodes.note: approximate; the corpus marker is right that this is the closest good fit in the whole vocabulary, and stage 1 sharpens why it is still not exact: `Rl` reserves a RESOURCE against a fulfilment, whereas Reinforcement reserves a WORST-CASE LOSS computed across an entire outcome vector, and it doubles as the price prior. It is a risk budget and a pricing seed in one object, and `Rl` carries neither role. Azuro's own marketing calls this 'concentrated liquidity', which would have made `Cl` an attractive and completely wrong choice: naming collision, not mechanism match.

nodes.label: F6 bets enter through a relayer that is the execution entry point for the
nodes.text: bets enter through a relayer that is the execution entry point for the whole protocol, taking the bettor's signed order and drawing sponsored fees and freebet amounts from a paymaster
nodes.note: departure from the corpus, which records neither element; both are V3 components absent from the V2 public repository. `Gs` (sponsored-fee liability, paymaster) is an exact fit, down to the contract's name. `Au` is approximate: the relayer executes authority the bettor delegated by signing, which is the shape `Au` describes, but the scope is protocol-defined rather than user-configured. This pairing also warrants `Rl` (F5) under the tables and satisfies L20 and L21, which the corpus's Azuro element set could not.

nodes.label: F7 each liquidity deposit is a separate leaf of a segment tree over a 2K+
nodes.text: each liquidity deposit is a separate leaf of a segment tree over a 2K+1 array, a Condition's profit and loss is distributed across a leaf range, and the updates are lazy — annotated at parent nodes and pushed down only when a provider withdraws
nodes.note: residue, and a departure from the corpus, which recorded `Sh` (stage-1 delta 4). A provider's claim is not a pro-rata share of one pot: it is a leaf with an entry position, and its value depends on WHICH Conditions resolved during its residence. That is neither `Sh` (proportional claim on a pool), nor `Ix` (a single global index), nor `Rb` (nominal rescaling). The LiquidityTree is a third accounting form the vocabulary does not have. The token standard of the provider's position is UNKNOWN — the docs do not say whether it is fungible, an NFT, or a bare accounting entry.

nodes.label: F8 a liquidity provider is locked for seven days from deposit and may wit
nodes.text: a liquidity provider is locked for seven days from deposit and may withdraw at will thereafter
nodes.note: residue. `Wq` is a queue of claimants waiting for liquidity that has not arrived; this is a per-deposit minimum holding period with no queue and no rationing. `Ep` gates transitions at shared epoch boundaries and this lock is dated from each deposit individually. Azuro's own documentation warns that positions held under a week will most likely be in the red, so the lock is economically load-bearing rather than administrative.

nodes.label: F9 one permissioned party creates and cancels events, seeds and reprices
nodes.text: one permissioned party creates and cancels events, seeds and reprices the sell-side odds, sets the reinforcement and margin, and then declares which outcome won
nodes.note: residue, and a departure from the corpus, which recorded `Ex` AND `Sv` for this role; stage 1 finds both wrong. `Ex` misrepresents a single trusted party as an oracle — there is no feed, no aggregation and no medianizer; `Sv` is written for servicing a loan and does not reach 'sets the price and also decides who won'; `Oa` needs an assertion, a bond and a dispute window and there is none. Azuro's docs say Data Providers resolve 'in good faith' citing a bookmaker's published settlement rules, with AzuroDAO 'acting as the arbiter of last resort in case of disputes' — so the corpus's flat claim of 'no dispute path' is wrong as documented (stage-1 delta 1), but the arbitration MECHANISM is not specified on-chain anywhere stage 1 could find and is marked UNKNOWN. Dropping `Ex` and `Sv` leaves this application with no expressible resolution mechanism at all, which is the category's finding, not a gap in the spec.

nodes.label: F10 a Data Provider must post collateral up to the total Reinforcement it
nodes.text: a Data Provider must post collateral up to the total Reinforcement it expects to use across all its active markets
nodes.note: residue, and a stage-1 finding the corpus records no bond for at all (stage-1 delta 2). `Bs` is the nearest shape and does not fit: nothing in the documentation describes a slashing condition, so this is a bond against MISPRICING — capital sized to the exposure the party is allowed to create — rather than slashable first-loss capital against insolvency or against a false report.

nodes.label: F11 a Condition may be paused, and cancelling it refunds every bettor's st
nodes.text: a Condition may be paused, and cancelling it refunds every bettor's stake instead of paying out
nodes.note: `Gp` fits the pause. `Rd` is approximate for the refund: it names an unconditional right to draw a fixed amount back, but the act here unwinds an already-struck contingent claim at par, and no element names the annulment of a live claim as distinct from its settlement.

nodes.label: F12 a winning bettor claims the payout struck at bet time after the Condit
nodes.text: a winning bettor claims the payout struck at bet time after the Condition is resolved
nodes.note: good fit for the claim itself; the amount claimed is fixed by F4, which is residue.

nodes.label: F13 the pool quotes a price to buy back an open bet before the event concl
nodes.text: the pool quotes a price to buy back an open bet before the event concludes, extinguishing a live contingent claim early
nodes.note: residue, and absent from the corpus record entirely — Cashout is a V3 feature (stage-1 delta 5). It is not `Rd` (there is no resolved payout to redeem against), not `Ob` (there is no counterparty), and not `Op` (there is no strike). A pool that will repurchase its own written liability at a quoted price before the state is known is a distinct mechanism with no symbol.

nodes.label: F14 a combination bet multiplies the odds of several legs into one payout
nodes.text: a combination bet multiplies the odds of several legs into one payout while the pool's exposure to the combination is not the product of its exposures to the legs
nodes.note: residue, confirming the corpus. A whole risk-management object — correlated exposure across simultaneously-priced conditions underwritten by one pool — with no representation in the vocabulary.

nodes.label: F15 pool revenue is divided among four named claimants: liquidity provider
nodes.text: pool revenue is divided among four named claimants: liquidity providers take 20% and the Data Provider 10% of the pool's profit or loss on each completed Condition, apps take a share, and AzuroDAO takes the residual computed by deducting all other rewards from monthly pool revenue
nodes.note: `Fd` (candidate register) fits the distribution with a named residual claimant. Departure from the corpus on a neighbouring point: the corpus records `Em` (protocol-funded emissions) and stage 1 could not confirm at a primary source that protocol-funded emissions are currently paid (stage-1 delta 3). What is verifiable is a share of pool profit and loss and of spread revenue, which is `Fd`, not `Em`; a `RewardPool` repository exists but its live use is UNKNOWN. `Em` is therefore dropped from the construction. The split itself is mutable at AzuroDAO's discretion.

nodes.label: F16 an app's share is the LESSER of 70% of the revenue it generated and a
nodes.text: an app's share is the LESSER of 70% of the revenue it generated and a monthly cap of 50% of the spread times the bet size summed over its bets
nodes.note: residue. `Fd` (F15) names the fact of distribution but not a share capped by a DIFFERENT quantity from the one it is a share of, and there is no symbol for a frontend as a first-class revenue claimant of the protocol it fronts.

nodes.label: F17 when the pool loses, the liquidity providers', Data Provider's and DAO
nodes.text: when the pool loses, the liquidity providers', Data Provider's and DAO's rewards go negative, while an app's share can only ever be positive or zero
nodes.note: residue. This is a declared order of loss-bearing across claimant classes, published in a fee schedule rather than encoded as a structure. `Tr` names declared seniority over a loss event and is the nearest, but there are no tranches, no principal and no waterfall — only a sign rule on a reward rate; `Sl` assigns a realised deficit to a claim class and there is no deficit here, just a negative share of a period's result. Neither is honest, so neither is used.

nodes.label: F18 protocol roles are tokenised by an Access contract and granted by the
nodes.text: protocol roles are tokenised by an Access contract and granted by the pool owner, so only permissioned parties may create Conditions, reprice odds or resolve them
nodes.note: approximate, and a departure from the corpus, which records no access element for Azuro. `Aw` is a permission/identity gate and the function matches — a party without the role token cannot act — but `Aw` is written for gating holders of a claim, and here what is gated is an office, with the role itself being transferable as a token.

nodes.label: F19 pools are deployed by a factory behind beacon proxies, and the pool ow
nodes.text: pools are deployed by a factory behind beacon proxies, and the pool owner may attach new betting engines to a live pool
nodes.note: good fit for the beacon-proxy upgradeability. Note two facts stage 1 established that bear on any check of this construction: no timelock is documented, so L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is unsatisfied; and the deployed system is V3 while the only public contract repository covers V2 and has not been touched since 2025-01-29, so the source for the live system is UNKNOWN and every element above is grounded in documentation rather than in code (stage-1 delta 6).

nodes.label: Grove Finance (Onchain Capital Allocator)
F1 a strategy may be funded only after Sky governance approves it through
nodes.text: a strategy may be funded only after Sky governance approves it through the Atlas Edit weekly cycle following a public forum round in which Grove answers voter questions; only approved strategies move to on-chain deployment
nodes.note: residue, confirming corpus claim (c), and the harder case than Steakhouse because the discretion and the capital sit in DIFFERENT governance domains: the capital is Sky's, the discretion is Grove's, and the depositor in the economically meaningful sense is a DAO rather than a user. Nothing names the authorisation, its size limit, its revocability, or the standing of the authorising body.

nodes.label: F2 the capital enters by minting USDS against a Sky allocation vault rath
nodes.text: the capital enters by minting USDS against a Sky allocation vault rather than by any user transferring assets in — the deposit is a governance-authorised credit line
nodes.note: residue. `Cd` (collateralized-debt minting) requires collateral posted against the liability and none is; `Uc` (undercollateralized credit) requires identity, underwriting and recourse against an obligor, and what stands in their place is a governance vote by the creditor's own token holders in favour of a counterparty they part-own. No element expresses a credit line whose underwriting is a ballot.

nodes.label: F3 the allocator converts between USDS, DAI and USDC at par through the m
nodes.text: the allocator converts between USDS, DAI and USDC at par through the mainnet peg-swap module
nodes.note: good fit and a departure from the corpus, which records no stability element for Grove. `Ps` is exactly a 1:1 reserve-backed swap module and the PSM is the named mechanism.

nodes.label: F4 every asset the allocator controls sits in one minimal stateless proxy
nodes.text: every asset the allocator controls sits in one minimal stateless proxy that holds no logic, and every movement of those assets is a call the proxy makes on a controller's instruction; funds never leave it
nodes.note: residue. Custody separated from logic, with arbitrary call, call-with-value and delegatecall forwarding. `Up` names a mutable implementation behind a fixed address and this is the inverse arrangement — a fixed custodian in front of replaceable logic — and the two have opposite risk profiles. No element names custody at all.

nodes.label: F5 only holders of a relayer role may invoke a fund-moving function, and
nodes.text: only holders of a relayer role may invoke a fund-moving function, and the role is exercised by an off-chain planner that submits the transactions
nodes.note: residue. `Au` (delegated execution scope) is the nearest and stage 1 declines it: `Au` is written for a principal's user-configured session policy, and this is an institution's operations bot acting on an authority no user granted. Declined here for the same reason as steakhouse-financial.json F12, and in deliberate contrast with azuro.json F6 and polymarket.json F4, where a user does sign the authority the relayer exercises.

nodes.label: F6 a freezer role can revoke the relayer role and thereby halt every auto
nodes.text: a freezer role can revoke the relayer role and thereby halt every automated operation of the allocator
nodes.note: approximate; corpus retained `Gp` and stage 1 marks the mismatch. `Gp` names a pause of a SYSTEM — a flag that suspends functions and is later cleared. This is the revocation of an ACTOR's authority: the system is not paused, it is left with nobody able to act, and restoring it requires re-granting a role rather than unsetting a flag. The emergency stop and the authority model are the same object here, which no single element expresses.

nodes.label: F7 every controller operation is bounded by a rate limit that refills lin
nodes.text: every controller operation is bounded by a rate limit that refills linearly at a configured slope up to a maximum, keyed per asset, per destination or per domain
nodes.note: residue, and stage 1's most consequential addition to the corpus record (delta 7): this is the single most load-bearing on-chain risk control in the allocator and the corpus element set has nothing for it. The formula is explicit — current = min(slope * (now - lastUpdated) + lastAmount, maxAmount) — and it is not a delay (`Tg`), not a pause (`Gp`), not an epoch (`Ep`) and not a cap on a position: it is a FLOW constraint on a privileged actor, bounding how fast rather than how much. The vocabulary has no flow limiter at all, and stage 1 notes the gap is general — Spark, Grove and several bridges all use one.

nodes.label: F8 the value of an off-chain allocation enters the on-chain accounting as
nodes.text: the value of an off-chain allocation enters the on-chain accounting as the fund manager's own reported net asset value
nodes.note: approximate; corpus marker confirmed and now with a mechanism to point at (stage-1 delta 6). `At` presupposes L27's shape — a named attester, independence, a stated assurance level, a staleness bound and recourse — and here the attester is the manager whose performance is being attested, with no independence and no recourse.

nodes.label: F9 positions are taken in vaults whose deposits and redemptions do not se
nodes.text: positions are taken in vaults whose deposits and redemptions do not settle synchronously: a request is made on-chain now and the claim is fulfilled later out of an off-chain process
nodes.note: residue. The ERC-7540 async vault is the interface across which an unverifiable NAV enters the accounting (F8), and it is a request/claim protocol with an off-chain fulfilment step. The vocabulary assumes settlement is synchronous or queued; `Wq` names a queue of claimants inside one system, not a two-phase claim across a system boundary, and `Of` (optimistic fill and reimbursement) presupposes a filler who is made whole on a verified message.

nodes.label: F10 capital moves between Ethereum, Avalanche and Plume through cross-chai
nodes.text: capital moves between Ethereum, Avalanche and Plume through cross-chain transfer protocols
nodes.note: good fit; corpus retained. CCTP and LayerZero are the named routes.

nodes.label: F11 the economically decisive transfer is not between chains but from a ch
nodes.text: the economically decisive transfer is not between chains but from a chain into a fund administrator's register of record, where the subscription becomes an entry in a Cayman or Luxembourg vehicle's books
nodes.note: residue, confirming the corpus marker. `Xf` (F10) describes movement between chains and its law demands debit(source) = credit(destination); the hop that matters crosses out of every ledger the formalism can see, and no symbol reaches it.

nodes.label: F12 the credit the capital ultimately buys is a tranche of a collateralise
nodes.text: the credit the capital ultimately buys is a tranche of a collateralised loan obligation, which from the allocator's position is a single opaque net asset value with no visible waterfall
nodes.note: residue, confirming the corpus. `Tr` would name the waterfall if the waterfall were visible; what the allocator holds is a share of a fund that holds tranches, so the seniority the price depends on is one level below anything the construction can reach. The initially approved size was $1 billion into JAAA via Centrifuge, later extended to JTRSY and to a $250M Avalanche target.

nodes.label: F13 a retail user supplies USDS or USDC to the savings product and receive
nodes.text: a retail user supplies USDS or USDC to the savings product and receives sUSDS, an ERC-4626 share with no lock-up whose exchange rate updates at the Sky Savings Rate, a parameter set by Sky governance
nodes.note: departure from the corpus, which recorded `Sh` without siting it (stage-1 delta 3), and the correction that matters most for anyone building on this spec: the retail user is NOT buying Grove's credit book — the share is a claim on the Sky Savings Rate, issued by Sky, and Grove's TVL is Sky-sourced allocated capital, not retail deposits. Any construction that treats Grove as a deposit-taking vault is wrong. `Sh` names the share and `Ix` the accrual of its exchange rate; neither names that the accrual RATE is a governance parameter of a different protocol, which is the whole content of the product.

nodes.label: F14 users also accrue Grove Points in proportion to their activity, which
nodes.text: users also accrue Grove Points in proportion to their activity, which are non-transferable, have no monetary value and confer no claim or entitlement
nodes.note: residue. `Em` (protocol-funded emissions) presupposes that the emitted thing has value and that emitting it is a cost to the protocol. A pure record of contribution with no claim attached is neither an emission nor a security nor a share, and it is one of the most widely deployed objects in DeFi with no symbol.

nodes.label: F15 GROVE holders stake into stGROVE and vote directly or by delegate, but
nodes.text: GROVE holders stake into stGROVE and vote directly or by delegate, but the token contract's only authorised admin is Sky's pause proxy, so administrative authority over the governance token belongs to another protocol's governance
nodes.note: residue. A governance system whose root of authority is another governance system is a distinct object; `Tg` names a delay and nothing names SUBORDINATION. Stage 1 found no evidence that GROVE holders can veto an allocation, so the votes that decide are Sky's and the votes that are sold are Grove's. Ten billion tokens at genesis, split 70% Sky ecosystem / 25% team and contributors / 5% foundation over ten years, with 21% still unassigned by future Sky governance decisions.

nodes.label: F16 the Basin facility commits up to $1 billion a day of immediate stablec
nodes.text: the Basin facility commits up to $1 billion a day of immediate stablecoin liquidity to eligible holders of tokenised funds, without purchasing or taking ownership of the underlying assets and without changing the fund's own redemption procedures, settlement cycles or transfer restrictions
nodes.note: residue, entirely absent from the corpus, and stage 1 calls it the single most interesting unnameable object in the category (delta 1). The corpus's own residue list names the redemption LAG between an on-chain instant-liquidity promise and a slow off-chain fund as a structural maturity transformation; Basin is a purpose-built facility that SELLS that transformation, to counterparties who are not the protocol's depositors, for a fee, warehousing the timing risk itself while the fund's T+2/T+3 workflow continues unchanged behind it. `Wq` names a queue of claimants; `Fl` names atomic borrow-and-repay inside one settlement scope; neither is a standing committed facility against a slow claim.

nodes.label: F17 an eligible counterparty may use Basin only if it already holds the to
nodes.text: an eligible counterparty may use Basin only if it already holds the tokenised fund, whose transfer eligibility is enforced by the issuer
nodes.note: approximate; corpus retained `Aw`. The gate is the underlying fund's own investor-eligibility régime, enforced by the issuer and its transfer agent rather than by Grove, so the permission the construction depends on is administered outside it. Launch partners are BlackRock and Janus Henderson as managers, Securitize and Centrifuge as tokenisers, and Anchorage, Galaxy and FalconX for institutional access.

nodes.label: F18 administrative changes to Basin execute only after a mandatory timeloc
nodes.text: administrative changes to Basin execute only after a mandatory timelock delay
nodes.note: good fit; an OpenZeppelin TimelockController is the named mechanism.

nodes.label: F19 in that timelock the external issuer holds the proposal right, Grove g
nodes.text: in that timelock the external issuer holds the proposal right, Grove governance executes after the delay, and a security multisig may cancel
nodes.note: residue. `Tg` (F18) names the delay and the execution but not a proposal right held by an EXTERNAL COMMERCIAL COUNTERPARTY, which is what makes this three-party arrangement unusual: the party whose commercial interests the change serves initiates it, and the protocol's own governance is reduced to executing or being overridden by a multisig veto.

nodes.label: F20 Basin fees accrue on-chain and are immediately claimable by authorised
nodes.text: Basin fees accrue on-chain and are immediately claimable by authorised issuers, the only function exempt from the timelock delay
nodes.note: approximate, and a departure from the corpus, which records no fee element for Grove. `Fd` (candidate register) names accrual and distribution to a named claimant; the carve-out from the delay — the one privileged action nobody has to wait for is the one that moves money to the counterparty — is a structure `Fd` does not carry. What Grove itself earns on the Sky mandate is not published at any primary source stage 1 could reach and is UNKNOWN; it is not guessed at here and no element is claimed for it.

nodes.label: Kalshi
F1 a person may not trade until an account is opened at the regulated exc
nodes.text: a person may not trade until an account is opened at the regulated exchange and passes identity and geographic eligibility screening
nodes.note: approximate: `Aw` names a permission/identity gate, but this is an account-opening process at a regulated broker-exchange, enforced off-chain and continuously by a compliance function, not a transfer-time eligibility check on a claim. Corpus marker retained.

nodes.label: F2 orders rest in a continuous two-sided limit order book operated by the
nodes.text: orders rest in a continuous two-sided limit order book operated by the exchange, quoted in sub-penny dollar prices and published as bids only
nodes.note: residue. `Ob` is an ON-CHAIN order book and nothing here is on-chain: the book, the matching engine and the record of positions are proprietary rows in Kalshi's system (KalshiEX Rule 6.2). The corpus reached the same conclusion by the wrong route — it called this 'a conventional off-exchange matching engine'; it is in fact an on-exchange CLOB run by the DCM with a documented public API (stage-1 delta 2). The conclusion survives the correction.

nodes.label: F3 the long and short of one contract are complementary claims on one esc
nodes.text: the long and short of one contract are complementary claims on one escrowed dollar, and that complementarity exists only as a price identity — a YES bid at X is a NO ask at $1.00 minus X — with no object that can be split into or merged out of the pair
nodes.note: residue, and the negative half of the category's first structural claim. Nothing in the 58 splits collateral into complementary contingent claims along a state partition; `Py` splits a claim along time and takes no partition argument. Kalshi shows that the primitive can be dispensed with entirely — the complement is an identity in the price domain, not an object — and the vocabulary cannot name that arrangement either, because it has no symbol for a position that exists only as a venue's bookkeeping row.

nodes.label: F4 no trade is accepted unless the account already holds the collateral f
nodes.text: no trade is accepted unless the account already holds the collateral for it: an event contract is collateralised against its Maximum Downside Exposure before clearing, and a margined contract against initial margin computed over a regulatory liquidation horizon with anti-procyclicality measures
nodes.note: approximate: `Ct` names the margin/LTV/health computation, and this is exchange-rule margin computed off-chain by the DCO under CFTC Reg. 39.13(g), gross per member with no netting across FCM customers. The pre-trade refusal branch — the clearing house declines the transaction rather than opening a position that can later fail a test — has no separate symbol.

nodes.label: F5 on acceptance of a matched trade the clearing house is substituted as
nodes.text: on acceptance of a matched trade the clearing house is substituted as seller to the buying participant and buyer to the selling participant, the original bilateral contract is extinguished, and the parties are released from their obligations to each other
nodes.note: residue, and the category's second structural claim stated precisely (Klear DCO Rule 6.1(E)(1); KalshiEX Rule 6.1(c)). Nothing in the 58 is a counterparty-substitution operator. `Rd` names a $1 payment right but carries no obligor identity, and the identity of the obligor is the entire content of novation. Consent is constructive on both sides — participants consent by entering orders, the clearing house by accepting the trade — which no delegation symbol (`Au`) reaches either.

nodes.label: F6 open margined positions are marked and settled in cash at least once e
nodes.text: open margined positions are marked and settled in cash at least once each business day, with unscheduled intra-day calls available
nodes.note: residue. Klear Rules 6.2(A), 7.2, 7.4. `Ct` names the test that triggers the call, not the periodic cash transfer that realises the mark. `Pf` is the nearest transfer in the vocabulary and is a funding payment tethering a perpetual to an index, not a daily realisation of profit and loss on a dated contract. Nothing names periodic mark-to-market settlement.

nodes.label: F7 at expiration a binary contract pays the $1.00 Settlement Value to the
nodes.text: at expiration a binary contract pays the $1.00 Settlement Value to the side whose Payout Criterion is met, by the clearing house debiting its settlement account and crediting member accounts
nodes.note: approximate, and the corpus marker is now citable rather than asserted (stage-1 delta 3: Klear Rule 6.2(C), KalshiEX Rule 6.3(d)(b)). `Rd` names an unconditional right to be paid, but the payment is a clearing-house bookkeeping entry against a segregated settlement account, not a redemption against a reserve, and the right is against an institution `Rd` cannot name (see F5).

nodes.label: F8 a scalar contract apportions the $1.00 between long and short as a fun
nodes.text: a scalar contract apportions the $1.00 between long and short as a function of where the Expiration Value falls, rather than paying it wholly to one side
nodes.note: residue. The apportionment rule — a continuous division of one unit of collateral between two counterparties as a function of an observed value — is not `Op`: there is no premium, no writer, no strike and no uncollateralised leg, and the two sides are symmetric. `Rd` (F7) names each side's right to collect but not the rule that decides how much.

nodes.label: F9 members fund a mutualised guaranty fund sized so the clearing house su
nodes.text: members fund a mutualised guaranty fund sized so the clearing house survives the default of the member creating the largest exposure in extreme but plausible conditions, cash only, at least $1,000,000 for a new member
nodes.note: approximate but sound; stage 1 confirms the mapping (Rule 12.4). `Bs` is slashable first-loss capital and the guaranty fund is applied to another member's default rather than slashed for the depositor's own fault, and the deposit requirement is recomputable by a risk committee at any time — a discretionary sizing `Bs` does not carry.

nodes.label: F10 the operator commits two capped tranches of its own capital to the def
nodes.text: the operator commits two capped tranches of its own capital to the default waterfall, one ahead of the mutualised fund and one behind it, each capped at the greater of $20 million or 10% of the guaranty fund
nodes.note: residue; stage-1 finding beyond the corpus record (Rule 12.5(C)(2)-(5)). Operator first-loss is structurally unlike `Bs`: it is not staked by a third party, not slashable by rule, and not a pool — it is a capped contractual obligation of one named firm, and it appears TWICE in the ordering, sandwiching the mutualised layer. Nothing in the 58 names a first-loss commitment by the venue itself, and nothing names a loss-absorption ORDER over heterogeneous sources.

nodes.label: F11 when the fund is exhausted the clearing house may call assessments on
nodes.text: when the fund is exhausted the clearing house may call assessments on every surviving member, pro rata to their deposit requirement over the preceding three months, capped at 200% for one default and 550% for multiple defaults in six months, and refundable pro rata out of later recoveries
nodes.note: residue; stage-1 finding beyond the corpus record. Callable capital is neither pre-posted collateral (`Bs`) nor loss socialisation (`Sl`): it is a contingent claim the clearing house holds AGAINST its members, unfunded until called, capped, and reversible on recovery. No element expresses an obligation to pay that does not yet exist.

nodes.label: F12 if resources remain short after assessments, unpaid variation-margin g
nodes.text: if resources remain short after assessments, unpaid variation-margin gains owed to members are haircut
nodes.note: Rule 12.5(D). Good fit: a residual loss is assigned to a defined claim class (members owed gains this cycle). Note the rulebook's own carve-out — haircutting and tear-ups 'are not Assessments and are therefore not subject to the Assessment limits' — so the uncapped tail sits in `Sl` and `Ad`, not in the capped instruments.

nodes.label: F13 as the last resort the clearing house tears up open contracts to close
nodes.text: as the last resort the clearing house tears up open contracts to close the book
nodes.note: Rule 12.5(E). `Ad` (rank-ordered forced close) is the intended reconstruction and fits: tear-ups extinguish the winning side's contracts to match the shortfall.

nodes.label: F14 the mutualised default fund is partitioned by Contract Segment between
nodes.text: the mutualised default fund is partitioned by Contract Segment between the fully-collateralised and margined product classes, and the collateral of non-defaulting customers in each account class may not be applied to a defaulting member's obligations
nodes.note: residue (Rules 12.4, 12.5(C)(1)(a)). Two distinct fences, neither named. `Im` fences an isolated LENDING market; there is no symbol for segmenting a mutualised default fund by product class, and none for a legal ring-fence around one claimant class's collateral inside a single custodian.

nodes.label: F15 the outcome of a contract is determined by an internal committee of th
nodes.text: the outcome of a contract is determined by an internal committee of the exchange with full discretion, within 24 hours, and its determination is final and not subject to review
nodes.note: residue (KalshiEX Rules 6.3(c), 7.1). This is a tribunal and the vocabulary has no symbol for one. `Oa` requires an assertion, a bond and a dispute window and there is none of the three; `Ex` requires a data feed and a medianizer and there is neither; `Sv` is written for servicing a loan, not for adjudicating a fact with finality. Disagreement about an outcome here is not adjudicated, it is decided.

nodes.label: F16 where the Expiration Value is indeterminable the contract may be settl
nodes.text: where the Expiration Value is indeterminable the contract may be settled at its own last traded price
nodes.note: residue (Rule 6.3(c)(a)). A self-referential settlement: the market's own final price becomes the payout, so the order book is the oracle. `Tp` (on-chain time-weighted price) is the nearest shape and is not it — no time weighting, no on-chain series, and the price being consulted is the price of the very claim being settled.

nodes.label: F17 after the first day of trading the venue may designate a new Source Ag
nodes.text: after the first day of trading the venue may designate a new Source Agency and Underlying for a listed contract and change its specifications
nodes.note: residue (KalshiEX Rule 7.2(a)). A mutable oracle DESIGNATION, distinct from `Up` (a mutable implementation) and from `Ex` (a feed). The instrument's settlement source is a venue parameter, so what the contract means can change while it is open.

nodes.label: F18 a new market exists because the venue self-certified its terms with th
nodes.text: a new market exists because the venue self-certified its terms with the regulator under CEA 5c(c) and the regulator did not object within the window
nodes.note: residue, confirming the corpus. `Aw` gates USERS; this is an authority gate on INSTRUMENTS, and it is a negative permission — listing succeeds by the absence of an objection. The listed product itself is a natural-language Payout Criterion plus a named Source Agency, i.e. a rulebook, for which there is also no symbol.

nodes.label: F19 the venue charges a taker fee of ceil(M x 0.07 x C x P x (1-P)) and a
nodes.text: the venue charges a taker fee of ceil(M x 0.07 x C x P x (1-P)) and a maker fee of ceil(M x 0.0175 x C x P x (1-P)) per trade, debited from member accounts into a clearing-house proprietary account, with no settlement fee
nodes.note: approximate, and a departure from the corpus element set, which recorded no fee element for Kalshi. `Fd` (candidate register) names the taking and distribution of a fee; here the whole surplus accrues to one residual claimant, the operator. The pricing rule itself — a fee proportional to P(1-P), i.e. to the variance of the contract — has no analogue in any fee element.

nodes.label: F20 the venue lists perpetual futures on crypto prices with leverage up to
