nodes.text: the venue lists perpetual futures on crypto prices with leverage up to 5.8x and a funding rate rebalanced three times a day on an eight-hour cycle against a reference price the exchange selects
nodes.note: departure from the corpus, which recorded Kalshi as a purely binary, purely fully-collateralised venue (stage-1 delta 1). `Pf` names the funding transfer and the shape is right, but the framing is not: the rate is computed by the venue, the leverage caps are set by the venue, and the reference price is selected by the venue with no feed, no aggregation and no medianizer. That leaves L1a and L4 unsatisfiable for this construction — both demand a truth element (Ex|Tp|Oa|At) beside `Pf`, and Kalshi has none, because its truth source is a committee (F15). The unsatisfied law is the finding, not a defect in the spec. Whether the perpetuals clear in the margined tier rather than the fully-collateralised one is an inference from the existence of leverage, not a documented mapping; stage 1 marks it UNKNOWN.

nodes.label: F21 the exchange and the clearing house may invoke Emergency Rules to susp
nodes.text: the exchange and the clearing house may invoke Emergency Rules to suspend or modify trading and clearing
nodes.note: approximate (Klear Rule 2.12; KalshiEX Rule 2.8). `Gp` names an emergency guardian or pause and the function matches, but the guardian is a corporate board acting off-chain under a rulebook with no enumerated trigger set and no on-chain effect, and its powers are broader than halting — it may modify terms.

nodes.label: F22 customer funds are held in United States dollars only, segregated by a
nodes.text: customer funds are held in United States dollars only, segregated by account class under CFTC Reg. 1.20 or Part 22 with the clearing house holding a continuing first-priority security interest and UCC control over them, investable only in US Treasuries, agency securities, reverse repo on those and government money-market funds up to two-year maturity — and the clearing house retains all profit from that investment not paid to members
nodes.note: residue (Rules 7.6, 7.7, 7.9); stage 1 records segregation and the float as one finding — assets held for a claimant whose income belongs to the custodian. Nothing in the 58 names custody at all, `Fz` (freeze / forced transfer) names a seizure event rather than a standing lien, and `Sh` and `Ix` both assume the yield on pooled assets accrues to the claim, which here it explicitly does not. This is the venue's float business.

nodes.label: Polymarket
F1 one unit of collateral is partitioned into one YES and one NO outcome
nodes.text: one unit of collateral is partitioned into one YES and one NO outcome token, and returning both recombines them into that unit, under an enforced invariant that the partition is pairwise disjoint, that no index set is empty and that none is the whole state space
nodes.note: residue, and the category's first structural claim stated precisely. `splitPosition`/`mergePositions` partition collateral along the STATE SPACE of a condition; `Py` is the only splitting element in the 58 and it partitions a claim along TIME, taking no partition argument at all. Two facts make the gap wider than the corpus recorded: the primitive is RECURSIVE — a position may be split again against a second condition through `parentCollectionId`, building a lattice of joint-state claims rather than a pair — and positions are not stored but DERIVED, a position id being a hash of (collateral token, condition, index set) used as an ERC-1155 id, so the claim space is defined intensionally. No element names any of it, and this is the operation that makes the venue fully collateralised without a counterparty.

nodes.label: F2 two of the three settlement modes of the matching engine are that prim
nodes.text: two of the three settlement modes of the matching engine are that primitive: two crossing buy orders mint a complementary pair out of collateral, and two crossing sell orders merge a pair back into collateral, with only a crossing buy against a sell settling by transfer
nodes.note: residue, and the sharpest form of the structural claim. The corpus's `Ob` marker ('off-chain signed-order matching with on-chain settlement') is true but incomplete (stage-1 delta 2): the matching engine and the state partition are the same machine, so a vocabulary with no state-partition symbol cannot name Polymarket's ORDER MATCHING either, not merely its collateral representation.

nodes.label: F3 users sign orders off-chain and an exclusive operator matches them and
nodes.text: users sign orders off-chain and an exclusive operator matches them and calls the exchange with one taker order and an array of maker orders, which validates the signatures and cross-prices before settling on-chain
nodes.note: approximate; corpus marker retained. `Ob` is an on-chain order book and only the settlement is on-chain here. The exclusivity of the operator — a single party with the right to decide which orders match and in what order — is a censorship and reordering surface that `Ob` conceals and no element names.

nodes.label: F4 a user's orders are executed through an operator-deployed proxy wallet
nodes.text: a user's orders are executed through an operator-deployed proxy wallet acting on the user's signed authority rather than by the user's own account
nodes.note: approximate; corpus marker retained (corpus records `Au` as derived). `Au` is delegated execution scope written for user-configured session policy; here the scope, the deployment and the revocation path are all operator-defined, and the user configures nothing.

nodes.label: F5 the user pays no gas: transaction fees for trading and settlement are
nodes.text: the user pays no gas: transaction fees for trading and settlement are sponsored on the user's behalf
nodes.note: candidate register, and load-bearing for the product as the corpus records. Sponsorship is what makes a $1-scale contingent claim economically tradeable at all.

nodes.label: F6 an outcome is proposed to an optimistic oracle under a $750 bond and s
nodes.text: an outcome is proposed to an optimistic oracle under a $750 bond and stands if undisputed for roughly two hours; a first dispute resets the question and re-requests a price, and a second escalates to a token-holder vote that resolves in 48 to 72 hours
nodes.note: approximate, per the corpus marker: `Oa` is structurally right (assert, bond, dispute, escalate) but the escalation terminates in a token-holder vote with no objective referent, and what is being asserted is an interpretation of prose rather than an observation of data. Stage 1 did not re-verify the WSJ voter-conflict statistics the corpus marker cites; they are UNKNOWN in this lane and are not restated here.

nodes.label: F7 only addresses on a per-request proposer whitelist may propose an outc
nodes.text: only addresses on a per-request proposer whitelist may propose an outcome, while any address may dispute one
nodes.note: partial. `Aw` names the gate on the proposing role, so the obligation is not pure residue; what it cannot express is the ASYMMETRY, which is the structurally interesting half (stage-1 delta 6). `Oa`'s whole shape is permissionless assertion, and after UMA's MOOV2 / UMIP-189 the assertion is permissioned while the challenge remains open. No element composes a gated assertion with an ungated dispute.

nodes.label: F8 the question being resolved is prose: a natural-language resolution cr
nodes.text: the question being resolved is prose: a natural-language resolution criterion posted under the order book, against which every dispute is a dispute about text
nodes.note: residue, confirming the corpus. `Oa` (F6) names the wrapper around the answer and says nothing about what question is being answered. The rulebook is the product being sold and it is invisible to the formalism. The market's ancillary data is bounded at 8139 bytes, so even the size of the unnameable object is a checkable constant.

nodes.label: F9 an admin role may pause and unpause resolution of a market, and may re
nodes.text: an admin role may pause and unpause resolution of a market, and may reset a question to re-issue a price request when the oracle callback failed
nodes.note: good fit for the pause; the reset branch (re-requesting truth after a failed callback) is a recovery path `Gp` does not name.

nodes.label: F10 an admin may flag a market, which pauses it and starts a fixed one-hou
nodes.text: an admin may flag a market, which pauses it and starts a fixed one-hour safety period, after which the admin writes the payout vector directly, overriding the oracle entirely
nodes.note: residue, and now a checkable constant rather than the corpus's governance narrative (stage-1 delta 5): flag() sets manualResolutionTimestamp = block.timestamp + SAFETY_PERIOD, unflag() cancels inside the window, resolveManually() writes the payout. `Tg` names a delay on GOVERNANCE execution; this is a delay on an operator's determination of FACT, the delay is one hour rather than a governance cycle, and the act delayed is unilateral. The escalation ladder is therefore proposer to disputer to token vote, and orthogonally to this write at any point.

nodes.label: F11 on resolution the oracle's payout numerators are reported to the condi
nodes.text: on resolution the oracle's payout numerators are reported to the conditional-token contract, winning shares redeem for one unit of collateral each and losing shares become worthless
nodes.note: good fit: an unconditional right to draw a fixed amount of the escrowed collateral against a reported payout vector. Unlike Kalshi's F7 the obligor is the contract holding the collateral, so `Rd` carries the whole obligation here.

nodes.label: F12 for a family of binary markets of which exactly one resolves true, a h
nodes.text: for a family of binary markets of which exactly one resolves true, a holder may exchange a bundle of NO positions for collateral plus the residual YES, financed before resolution out of a wrapped-collateral buffer the adapter holds itself; if the family's mutual-exclusivity constraint is violated the family cannot fully resolve and funds are frozen
nodes.note: residue, and stronger than the corpus's 'constraint-imposing wrapper'. It is an arbitrage-free-completion operator over a family of conditions, and it does two unnameable things at once: it converts N-1 complementary claims into collateral plus a claim on the residual outcome, and it releases that collateral BEFORE resolution out of a privately held buffer, giving the adapter liquidity control independent of the underlying accounting. No element names the conversion, the constraint it enforces, or the buffer.

nodes.label: F13 collateral is pUSD, an ERC-20 on Polygon backed one-for-one by USDC wi
nodes.text: collateral is pUSD, an ERC-20 on Polygon backed one-for-one by USDC with the backing enforced on-chain and no algorithmic peg or fractional reserve, convertible in either direction at par with no fee
nodes.note: departure from the corpus, whose canonical form omits it (stage-1 delta 1). Since the 2026-04-28 cutover the collateral is pUSD, not bridged USDC.e, and `Ps` (peg-swap module, 1:1 reserve-backed) is a genuine fit rather than an approximation: fixed parity, full reserve, no fee, on-chain enforcement.

nodes.label: F14 the exchange wraps that collateral a second time as PMCT through a col
nodes.text: the exchange wraps that collateral a second time as PMCT through a collateral adapter with dedicated onramp and offramp contracts, so an adapter can hold liquidity outside the conditional-token accounting
nodes.note: residue. A wrapper whose purpose is to place value outside the accounting system that would otherwise govern it. `Ps` (F13) names a par-convertible representation backed by a reserve; it does not name a re-wrap whose function is accounting escape, and the failure mode of the second wrap is different from the first.

nodes.label: F15 a fee up to an admin-settable maximum of 500 basis points is charged p
nodes.text: a fee up to an admin-settable maximum of 500 basis points is charged per order in USDC, calculated at match time rather than at placement, validated before execution and collected during settlement
nodes.note: approximate, and a departure from the corpus element set, which recorded no fee element. `Fd` (candidate register) names the taking of a fee; the destination of the collected fees is not stated at a primary source in stage 1's evidence, so the residual claimant is UNKNOWN and the distribution half of `Fd` is unverified.

nodes.label: F16 the exchange and the collateral token are deployed behind upgradeable
nodes.text: the exchange and the collateral token are deployed behind upgradeable proxies with admin-settable parameters
nodes.note: good fit. Corpus retained. Note that L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is not satisfied by any documented timelock in stage 1's evidence; the only delay found anywhere in the system is the one-hour safety period of F10, which is not a governance delay.

nodes.label: F17 on the US venue a participant must be onboarded to a designated contra
nodes.text: on the US venue a participant must be onboarded to a designated contract market before trading, and contracts are quoted in minimum increments of $0.001 and tradeable in fractional units
nodes.note: approximate: a regulated participant-onboarding process, off-chain, not a transfer-time gate. Same shape as Kalshi F1.

nodes.label: F18 on the US venue every matched trade is novated: the clearing house is
nodes.text: on the US venue every matched trade is novated: the clearing house is immediately substituted as seller to the purchaser and purchaser to the seller
nodes.note: residue, and the category's second structural claim, now shared by two of the five (stage-1 delta 3; Polymarket US Rulebook Rule 6.1(d), QCX designated 2025-07-09). The twist WEAKENS the corpus's framing: QC Clearing states publicly that it clears only fully collateralised positions, employs no margin methodology and maintains NO financial resource package — no guaranty fund at all. So the `Bs`/`Sl`/`Ad` trio that reconstructs Kalshi's waterfall (kalshi.json F9, F12, F13) reconstructs nothing here. A fully-collateralised central counterparty is pure novation plus custody, and against that institution the vocabulary has even less to say: there is no default waterfall to name because the whole institution is the unnameable part.

nodes.label: F19 on the US venue the clearing house checks that the account holds the f
nodes.text: on the US venue the clearing house checks that the account holds the full collateral before accepting the trade, and refuses it otherwise
nodes.note: approximate, and a departure from the corpus element set. `Ct` names a collateral-sufficiency computation; this one is an off-chain rulebook check performed by the clearing house before novation (Rule 6.1(c)), with no ongoing health factor because a fully-collateralised position cannot become undercollateralised.

nodes.label: F20 on the US venue a company officer runs a Contract Outcome Review Proce
nodes.text: on the US venue a company officer runs a Contract Outcome Review Process, determines the final outcome at sole discretion, and may reverse a determined outcome in the case of obvious error, with company liability to any one participant capped at $2,500 a day, $5,000 a month and $50,000 a year
nodes.note: residue (Rule 10.4, Chapter 11), and the finding that sharpens the corpus's category residue (stage-1 delta 4). The same tribunal identified for Kalshi (kalshi.json F15), inside the same brand as F6: the same market question resolves by bonded assertion on Polygon and by officer discretion in New York, with a reversal power the on-chain leg does not have and a monetary cap on the operator's liability for getting it wrong. Counting venues rather than brands, only Polymarket-on-Polygon has an expressible resolution mechanism at all.

nodes.label: Steakhouse Financial (Risk Curators)
F1 a depositor puts a stablecoin into an ERC-4626 vault and receives shar
nodes.text: a depositor puts a stablecoin into an ERC-4626 vault and receives shares representing a proportional claim on the vault's assets
nodes.note: good fit; one vault per loan asset, with ERC-2612 permit on the V1 vaults.

nodes.label: F2 the vault does not lend: it deploys the deposit into isolated lending
nodes.text: the vault does not lend: it deploys the deposit into isolated lending markets on a base protocol, so the depositor holds the credit and oracle risk of markets they did not choose
nodes.note: approximate; corpus marker retained. `Im` names the per-market risk fence, which is the SUBSTRATE the vault allocates across — the vault neither creates the fence nor operates the market. There is no symbol for the client relation itself: a vault that is a customer of a market rather than a market. Stage 1 corrects the corpus's substrate list (delta 2): the documented platforms are Morpho V1, Morpho Vaults V2 and Kamino on Solana, plus a Coinbase distribution channel; no Steakhouse documentation names Euler.

nodes.label: F3 a named firm decides which markets the capital may enter, in what orde
nodes.text: a named firm decides which markets the capital may enter, in what order they fill and drain, and rebalances at will, for a share of the interest generated
nodes.note: residue, confirming corpus claim (c). This is the entire product: what the depositor buys is a manager. `Sv` (servicing and determination discretion) is written for servicing a loan and does not reach EXPOSURE SELECTION; `Im` (F2) describes the substrate the mandate allocates across, not the mandate. Nothing in the 58 names the delegation of investment discretion over other people's capital.

nodes.label: F4 each market carries a supply cap defaulting to zero, so no market may
nodes.text: each market carries a supply cap defaulting to zero, so no market may receive any capital until the curator explicitly caps it up, and a vault may enable at most thirty markets
nodes.note: residue. The supply cap is the vault's own risk instrument and it is a portfolio-construction limit on a MANAGER, whereas `Ct` (F7) is a per-position solvency test on a BORROWER: different object, different subject, opposite direction of enforcement. The default-to-zero is the load-bearing detail — a market is unusable until an affirmative act makes it usable — and no element expresses a permission that must be granted per venue and per amount.

nodes.label: F5 deposits fill along an ordered supply queue up to each cap and withdra
nodes.text: deposits fill along an ordered supply queue up to each cap and withdrawals drain along an ordered withdraw queue, so the identity of the market receiving the next dollar is a curator-set ordering
nodes.note: residue, and a departure from the corpus, which recorded `Wq` for Steakhouse. `Wq` is a queue of CLAIMANTS waiting for liquidity; these are queues of VENUES in priority order, and no claimant ever waits in them. Stage 1 calls the corpus fit partial at best; on inspection it is not a fit at all, because the queued objects are of a different kind. `Wq` is therefore dropped from the construction.

nodes.label: F6 a depositor may redeem shares at any time, but only to the extent the
nodes.text: a depositor may redeem shares at any time, but only to the extent the underlying markets can be drained; there is no queue and no pro-rata gate, so a redemption that outruns available liquidity simply fails
nodes.note: approximate, and a departure: the corpus recorded no redemption element. `Rd` names an unconditional right to draw against the vault's assets, and the right IS unconditional in the contract — what is conditional is its exercise. Nothing names a redemption right that can fail for want of liquidity without queueing, which is the shape L14 (illiquid backing implies a queue or a bounded liquidity reserve) is reaching for; see F7.

nodes.label: F7 capital not deployed into a market sits as idle supply in a market wit
nodes.text: capital not deployed into a market sits as idle supply in a market with null oracle and null collateral addresses, immediately withdrawable
nodes.note: residue. This is the only liquidity reserve behind F6, and it is expressed as a degenerate instance of a lending market rather than as a reserve: a market whose oracle and collateral are the zero address. No element names an uninvested buffer, and the encoding — a market that is not a market — is exactly the kind of object a mechanism vocabulary should be able to name and cannot.

nodes.label: F8 capital is lent only against collateral subject to a liquidation-loan-
nodes.text: capital is lent only against collateral subject to a liquidation-loan-to-value test, computed by the underlying markets rather than by the vault
nodes.note: approximate; corpus records `Ct` as derived and stage 1 confirms and tightens the marker. The vault performs no solvency computation of its own; it inherits one. Carried in the construction because the obligation is genuinely discharged, but the discharging mechanism belongs to a protocol the vault does not control.

nodes.label: F9 raising a cap, adding a market or an adapter, and (on Vaults V2) chang
nodes.text: raising a cap, adding a market or an adapter, and (on Vaults V2) changing a fee take effect only after a timelock, while lowering a cap takes effect immediately; Steakhouse sets seven days for new-market onboarding on its Prime line and three on High Yield, above the protocol minimum of twenty-four hours
nodes.note: good fit, and the asymmetry (delay to increase risk, immediate to reduce it) is expressible as two `Tg` settings. The delay is explicitly sized 'to provide depositors time to withdraw or exercise veto rights before capital deployment', which makes it the enabling half of F10.

nodes.label: F10 vault users become vault guardians in proportion to the size of their
nodes.text: vault users become vault guardians in proportion to the size of their deposit, and may veto a critical curator action inside the timelock window
nodes.note: residue, and the correction that reframes the corpus's residue line (stage-1 delta 1). The corpus says depositors have 'no on-chain recourse'; they have PREVENTIVE recourse — an Aragon DAO guardian weighted by deposit — and no COMPENSATORY recourse (F14). That distinction is the sharper finding, and neither half is nameable: `Tg` is the delay not the veto, `Gp` is a designated pauser not a weighted electorate, and `Ve` (vote-escrow, contested register) is a lock-for-weight scheme, not governance weight derived from an economic exposure inside a single vault.

nodes.label: F11 a guardian or sentinel may revoke a pending timelocked action, decreas
nodes.text: a guardian or sentinel may revoke a pending timelocked action, decrease caps instantly and deallocate, and the vault owner is a five-of-five multisig
nodes.note: good fit, with one carve-out `Gp` cannot express: on Morpho V1 the guardian explicitly CANNOT revoke a fee change, so exactly the action that transfers value to the curator is outside the emergency power. On Vaults V2 fee changes became timelocked instead.

nodes.label: F12 authority is split four ways — an appointer, a strategy-setter who set
nodes.text: authority is split four ways — an appointer, a strategy-setter who sets caps and fees, bounded executors who may only move funds within the strategy-setter's limits, and sentinels who may only reduce
nodes.note: residue. `Au` (delegated execution scope) is the nearest and is declined here for the same reason stage 1 declines it for Grove's relayer: `Au` describes a principal delegating their OWN authority under a bounded session policy, and this is an institution's internal separation of duties, where no principal has delegated anything and the depositor is not a party to the arrangement. The monotone directionality of the sentinel and allocator roles — powers that can only reduce exposure — has no symbol either. (Contrast azuro.json F6 and polymarket.json F4, where a user does sign the authority the relayer exercises, and `Au` is used.)

nodes.label: F13 the curator takes a performance fee of up to 50% of generated interest
nodes.text: the curator takes a performance fee of up to 50% of generated interest and, on Vaults V2, a management fee of up to 5% a year on assets, accruing on interaction
nodes.note: `Fd` (candidate register) names the fee take; corpus marker retained. Steakhouse's High Yield line charges typically 10% with temporary waivers. Accrual only on interaction means a fee recipient who never transacts cannot actually receive underlying assets, which `Fd` does not express. The corpus notes but does not name the incentive this creates to reach for yield.

nodes.label: F14 the fee is paid by minting new vault shares to the fee recipients, so
nodes.text: the fee is paid by minting new vault shares to the fee recipients, so it is borne as dilution of every other holder rather than as a transfer of assets
nodes.note: residue, and a stage-1 sharpening of the corpus's `Fd` marker (delta 3). `Fd` names a distribution out of a surplus; dilution takes nothing out of the vault and has a different failure mode — it cannot fail for want of assets, it cannot be revoked by a guardian on V1, and it is invisible in the asset accounting.

nodes.label: F15 the curator disclaims being a broker, intermediary, agent, custodian o
nodes.text: the curator disclaims being a broker, intermediary, agent, custodian or advisor, disclaims any fiduciary relationship or obligation, caps total liability at $1,000, and routes disputes to Cayman arbitration with a class-action waiver
nodes.note: residue, and the single most important fact about the instrument. The manager takes a share of the upside and disclaims the downside; the depositor's loss from an allocation decision has no addressee. There is no symbol for the absence of recourse, and — worse for the formalism — no way to DISTINGUISH a mandate with recourse from one without, so two economically opposite products decompose identically.

nodes.label: F16 before a market may be listed at all, at least two members of the risk
nodes.text: before a market may be listed at all, at least two members of the risk team run a quality-control review across six named risk vectors, and every vault passes a due-diligence questionnaire with at least two internal and one external reviewer
nodes.note: residue. An off-chain listing gate on instruments, structurally the same object as Kalshi's self-certification (kalshi.json F18) in a different sector: a market becomes eligible because a named process was performed by named humans. `Aw` gates parties, not instruments.

nodes.label: F17 where the capital goes is a function of a published, versioned three-l
nodes.text: where the capital goes is a function of a published, versioned three-layer rating — an asset rating over issuer, credit and operational pillars, a platform rating, and a market rating over oracle, liquidity, price fluctuation, LLTV and credit-enhancement criteria — which is entirely off-chain
nodes.note: residue, and the finding that joins the two halves of this category. The allocation is a function of a DOCUMENT — exactly the shape of the prediction-market rulebook (polymarket.json F8, kalshi.json F18) in a completely different sector. What is verifiable on-chain is the role assignments, the enabled markets and caps, the queue ordering, the timelock and the fee; what is not verifiable is why any of those values were chosen.
